Overall, MP migration and retention were jointly controlled by pore-network accessibility, hydrodynamics, and interfacial interactions, providing a mechanistic basis for assessing potential MP transfer toward deeper soils and shallow groundwater.

title: Particle collision synergistic ultrasonic oxidation (PCUO) for oil-sludge treatment: Mechanisms of boundary film disruption and process optimization
abstract: Oil-sludge treatment is hindered by stable multi-layer boundary films formed by heavy oil components. This study investigates the synergistic particle collision-ultrasonic oxidation (PCUO) method for disrupting these films. Single ultrasonic treatment achieves 49.85% total oil removal but fails to remove resins and asphaltenes (removal 50 = 15-50 μm balancing ultrasonic penetration and re-adsorption risks. XDLVO confirms PCUO reduces oil-sludge interaction energy, enhancing treated sludge stability. Box-Behnken design optimization yields parameters: 10.15 min, 42.42 °C, pH 3.15, achieving 64.71% total oil removal with 82.0% heavy oil removal, significantly outperforming traditional technologies. In short, PCUO effectively disrupts complex boundary films, enhancing oil removal efficiency and providing a novel purification approach for oily solid waste.

title: Microplastic degradation and organic acids recovery via homogeneous catalytic wet air oxidation: Role of redox and Lewis acidity of metal ions
abstract: The pervasive accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems poses a growing threat to environmental and human health, yet current advanced oxidation technologies are constrained by inefficiency or reliance on excess oxidants. Here, a homogeneous catalytic wet air oxidation (CWAO) system using Cu 2 + ions was developed to degrade polyethylene (PE) MPs and simultaneously recover value-added carboxylic acids. The system enables 98.7% weight loss of PE (1.0 g/L) and a liquid-phase total organic carbon of 489 mg/L at 170 °C, substantially outperforming non-catalytic WAO. About 57.1% of the PE carbon is transformed into carboxylic acid species, with a total dicarboxylic acid concentration reaching 186.9 mg/L. The catalyst functions through a synergistic dual-mechanism pathway, consisting of a Cu 2+ /Cu + redox cycle that activates O 2 to generate •OH radicals for C-C bond scission, and Lewis acidity that polarizes C-H and C-C bonds to lower the activation energy for oxidative cleavage, which enables controlled polymer chain scission and stepwise oxidation, including hydroxylation, carbonylation, and carboxylation. The system also exhibits applicability to other MPs or real-world PE-rich plastic waste, with more than 97.7% weight loss. This work establishes CWAO as a promising route that integrates environmental remediation with resource recovery for MPs treatment.

title: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter constituents and lung cancer risk in Chinese never-smokers
abstract: Although long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) has been linked to lung cancer incidence in never-smokers (LCINS), evidence for PM 2.5 constituents remains limited. This study included 262,785 never-smokers from the China Kadoorie Biobank, among whom 2646 LCINS cases were identified. Annual average concentrations of PM 2.5 and its major constituents during 2004-2018 were obtained from the ChinaHighAirPollutants database. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models estimated constituent associations with LCINS incidence, and Quantile-based g-computation assessed the importance of each constituent. The polygenic risk score (PRS) was constructed to explore the multiplicative and additive interactions between genetic risk and pollutant constituents. Per interquartile range increase, exposure to nitrate (NO 3 - ), ammonium (NH 4 + ), and chloride (Cl - ) was associated with higher LCINS risk, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.35 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.23-1.48), 1.22 (95% CI, 1.13-1.31), and 1.20 (95% CI, 1.12-1.28), respectively. Mixture analyses consistently identified NO 3 - and NH 4 + as the largest positive contributors to the overall PM 2.5 -related risk, with an overall mixture HR of 1.13 (95% CI, 1.07-1.19). Significant additive and multiplicative interactions between NO 3 - exposure and PRS were observed. These findings suggest that long-term exposure to specific PM 2.5 constituents, particularly NO 3 - , was associated with higher LCINS risk, especially among genetically susceptible individuals.

title: Bisphenol A exacerbates chronic non-bacterial prostatitis by upregulating ITGAX and promoting M1 macrophage polarization
abstract: Chronic non-bacterial prostatitis (CNP) is a common urological disease, whereas the effects of bisphenol A (BPA) on CNP remain unclear. We systematically evaluated the associations between BPA and CNP by combining dietary exposure assessment, urinary BPA detection, and animal model validation, and performed integrated multi‑omics analyses to decipher the underlying molecular mechanisms. Dietary questionnaire data from 1256 individuals showed that BPA exposure was associated with increased CNP risk (OR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.08-1.98), particularly among individuals with BMI < 24 kg/m². Consistently, a case-control study of 120 participants further revealed elevated urinary BPA levels in patients with CNP and positive correlations with inflammatory cytokines. Such epidemiological observations were further recapitulated in the BPA‑exposed CNP animal model. Multi-omic integration identified ITGAX as a hub gene with increased expression in CNP and predicted binding affinity for BPA. Within BPA‑aggravated CNP lesions, M1 macrophages constituted the expanded immune subpopulation, wherein ITGAX colocalized with M1 macrophages and contributes to M1 macrophage polarization. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed that Itgax⁺ macrophages exhibited an M1-like phenotype and enhanced inferred communication with CD8⁺Gzmk⁺ effector-memory T cells. Collectively, these results suggest that BPA exposure may exacerbate CNP through ITGAX-associated macrophage inflammation, highlighting a potential mechanism linking BPA exposure to prostatitis.

title: Integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses provide insights into zinc-doped carbon quantum dot-mediated alleviation of cadmium toxicity in lettuce
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in crops seriously threatens agricultural productivity and food safety, highlighting the need for effective strategies to mitigate Cd toxicity. Uniformly dispersed zinc-doped carbon quantum dots (Zn-CQDs; 2.67 ± 0.36 nm) were synthesized in this study. The synthesized dots demonstrated enzyme-mimetic activities in vitro and potent radical-scavenging capacity. Foliar application of Zn-CQDs markedly alleviated Cd-induced growth inhibition in lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.), increasing shoot fresh and dry biomass by 30.8% and 23.9%, respectively. Moreover, Zn-CQDs treatment reduced the Cd concentration in lettuce shoots by 44.7% while elevating the Zn concentration by 167.9%. Photosynthetic performance was also substantially restored, as evidenced by a 61.0% increase in total chlorophyll content. Concurrently, Zn-CQDs mitigated Cd-triggered oxidative damage, reducing H 2 O 2 and MDA levels by 31.4% and 38.9%, respectively, and lowering the activities of the antioxidant enzymes POD, SOD, and CAT by 23.3%, 71.5%, and 44.3%, respectively. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that Zn-CQDs modulate stress-responsive signaling networks involving MAPK cascades, Ca 2 + , and phytohormone signaling, as well as their associated transcription factors, thereby regulating downstream genes involved in ROS detoxification and metal transport. Metabolomic analysis further demonstrated that Zn-CQDs extensively reprogram Cd-responsive metabolic pathways, particularly those related to phenylpropanoid, lipid, amino acid, and phytohormone metabolism, accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid, flavonoids, and organic acid derivatives. The above-mentioned findings offer mechanistic insights into Zn-CQD-mediated alleviation of Cd stress and lay a theoretical basis for functional carbon nanomaterials' application to reduce heavy metal risks in agricultural systems.

title: Bimetallic synergy-driven generation of high-valent metal-oxo species in a nanoconfined catalytic ceramic membrane for efficient antibiotic-containing water treatment
abstract: Efficient purification in complex waters requires catalytic membranes with high selectivity and interference resistance, a need addressed by nanoconfinement through steering reactive species toward nonradical oxidation. Herein, a cobalt-nickel layered double hydroxide (CoNi-LDH) catalyst was synthesized via hydrothermal conversion of a CoNi metal-organic framework self-sacrificing template and deposited onto a ceramic substrate. In a continuous flow-through system with peroxymonosulfate (PMS), the membrane achieved 97.6% sulfadiazine degradation. The nanoconfined effect increased the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constant of sulfadiazine degradation to 4.916 s -1 , three orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional batch system (2.433 × 10 -3 s -1 ). Mechanistic investigation showed that the O-O bond heterolysis of PMS generated high-valent cobalt-oxygen species as the dominant reactive species, endowing high resistance and oxidation selectivity. The degradation efficiencies exceeding 95% for various organic micropollutants and performed stably in actual surface water and secondary effluent. It also exhibited permeate flux recovery efficiency exceeding 80% after multiple cycles of cleaning and fouling caused by humic acid, indicating excellent antifouling properties. This work provides a theoretical foundation and instructive demonstration for nonradical catalytic membrane reactors toward practical water treatment.

title: OH and 1O2 mediated oxidative reduction of antibiotic-resistant bacteria cultivability and tetA abundance in a 3D electro-Fenton system
abstract: The proliferation of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) in aquatic environments necessitates efficient remediation strategies. This study developed a three-dimensional electro-Fenton (3DEF) system employing a novel MnO 2 /Pd(Ⅱ)@CA particle electrode to simultaneously inactivate tetracycline-resistant Escherichia coli (TR E. coli) and mitigate antibiotic resistance dissemination. Under optimal conditions (1.5 V, 12 mM Fe 2+ , 1.5 g L -1 particle electrode, pH 5), complete inactivation of TR E. coli (> 7-log reduction) was achieved within 4 min. The particle electrode promoted in-situ H 2 O 2 generation, subsequently activated to produce •OH and 1 O 2 as dominant reactive species, with reactive chlorine species also contributing. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed extensive membrane disruption, accompanied by substantial leakage of intracellular K + and proteins. Both intracellular and extracellular tetracycline resistance genes (tetA) were detected, while residual extracellular DNA lost transformation capability, indicating reduced dissemination potential. Proteomic analysis revealed suppression of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump, disrupted DNA repair pathways, and impaired energy metabolism, ultimately leading to complete loss of viability and regrowth capacity. This work highlights the 3DEF system as a promising technology for mitigating environmental risks posed by ARB.

title: Sequential reduction-oxidation degradation of alkaline nitrophenol wastewater by a novel Al0/O2 system
abstract: Alkaline nitrophenol (NP) wastewater is highly toxic and resistant to direct oxidation. Although reductive treatment can enhance NP degradability, the alkaline environment complicates remediation, especially for zero-valent iron (Fe 0 ) that readily undergoes passivation. To address these challenges, this study developed a sequential reduction-oxidation system employing carbon nanotube-modified micron-sized zero-valent aluminum (CNTs@mAl 0 ) to activate O 2 for p-nitrophenol (PNP) degradation under alkaline conditions. In the reduction stage, CNTs@mAl 0 achieved complete conversion of PNP to p-aminophenol (PAP). Upon subsequent O 2 sparging, the generated PAP underwent further oxidation and mineralization by •OH and 1 O 2 derived from O 2 activation, achieving > 99.9% overall PNP removal and 66.1% TOC removal. Electrochemical analyses and material characterizations (SEM-EDS and XPS) revealed that CNTs not only act as conductive bridges to facilitate electron transfer in mAl 0 , but also facilitate O 2 diffusion and activation through their high specific surface area, hydrophobic porous structure, and π*-electron-rich carbon framework, boosting reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and enhancing PAP mineralization. Notably, this method effectively removed 98.3% of diazodinitrophenol (DDNP) from real alkaline NP explosive wastewater, while also removing 49.5% TOC, confirming its practical efficacy. Overall, this study offers a promising strategy for the treatment of alkaline wastewater contaminated with refractory nitroaromatic pollutants.

title: Lateral flow strip biosensor for visual detection of heavy metal ions based on feedback circuit with trigger DNA regeneration strategy and its logic gate applications
abstract: The on-site and visual detection of trace levels of heavy metal ions in resource-limited settings is still a big challenge. Herein, using chromium ions (Cr 3 + ) as a model target, we developed a lateral flow strip biosensor for visual detection of Cr 3+ on the basis of a feedback circuit with trigger DNA regeneration strategy. Cr 3+ -specific DNAzyme was used to recognize Cr 3+ . The free trigger DNA (T) after the cleavage reaction can initiate the assembly of hairpin probes H1, H2, and H3. The resulting H1-H2-H3 products contain a freshly regenerated T fragment, which can continuously drive the operation of feedback DNA circuit, thereby yielding abundant H1-H2-H3 assemblies. Compared with the no T regeneration strategy, the feedback circuit with T regeneration method exhibits superior signal amplification capability. The strip biosensor achieves a visual detection limit of 10 pM. Moreover, the sensing platform exhibits favorable robustness and performs reliably when applied to practical water samples. Using Cr 3+ and cadmium ion (Cd 2+ ) as two inputs, we further constructed INHIBIT and XOR strip logic gates that open new avenues for intelligent detection of different heavy metal ions in resource-poor environments.

title: Structure-dependent cellular mechanisms of PFAS regulating antibiotic resistance genes conjugation through membrane remodeling and energy metabolism reprogramming
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) widely coexist with antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic systems, posing ecological risks. However, how environmentally relevant concentrations and structural differences of PFAS regulate ARGs dissemination remains unclear, limiting structure-informed management of PFAS substitutes. Here, conjugation assays, transcriptomics, molecular dynamics simulations, and molecular docking were integrated to systematically investigate the structure-dependent effects of four representative PFAS (PFOA, PFBA, PFOS, and PFBS) on RP4 plasmid conjunction. At 0.01-10 μg·L -1 , short-chain PFAS significantly enhanced RP4 plasmid conjunction, with PFBS showing the strongest promotion (up to 5.8-fold), followed by PFBA（3.8-fold）, whereas long-chain PFAS showed minor effects (PFOA, 1.4-fold; PFOS, 1.1-fold). Notably, PFBS exhibited relatively weak yet dynamic interactions with membrane proteins, facilitating porin accessibility and intracellular transport. Mechanistic analyses revealed that PFAS, especially PFBS, promote ARGs conjunction through coordinated modulation of membrane properties and cellular energy metabolism at environmentally relevant concentrations. Integrated molecular simulations and transcriptomic analyses suggested a structure-dependent mechanism, highlighting the overlooked risk of short-chain sulfonate PFBS. Overall, these findings demonstrated that PFAS-induced ARGs transfer was strongly structure-dependent and identify PFBS as a higher-risk short-chain substitute, with implications for targeted environmental regulation.

title: Urban–rural disparities in antibiotic and disinfectant use and their socioeconomic associations by wastewater surveillance
abstract: Understanding urban-rural and socioeconomic disparities in antibiotic and disinfectant consumption is important for effective antimicrobial resistance management. In this study, we applied wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) to systematically assess per capita antibiotic and disinfectant consumption across 22 wastewater treatment plants in Dalian, China. The results revealed marked urban-rural disparities in both total consumption and medication structures across the monitored periods. Total antibiotic and disinfectant consumption in urban areas was significantly higher than in rural areas. Urban populations showed greater use of higher-cost, broad-spectrum antibiotics such as azithromycin, whereas rural populations relied more heavily on lower-cost and more accessible antibiotics such as phenoxymethylpenicillin. Although antibiotic consumption increased markedly during certain observation periods, these peaks subsequently returned toward baseline levels. Socioeconomic analysis showed that urban total antibiotic consumption was negatively correlated with the Composite Development Index (CDI), indicating higher antibiotic consumption in economically disadvantaged communities, potentially associated with differences in healthcare resources and diagnostic capacity. In contrast, rural disinfectant use was positively associated with the CDI, highlighting that routine sanitation in rural contexts remains strongly constrained by local economic infrastructure. These findings suggest that population-level antimicrobial use may be associated with socioeconomic disparities and differences in healthcare accessibility.

title: Au-loaded ZnO immobilized cellulose-derived carbon beads for enhanced photocatalytic degradation of tetracycline
abstract: The elimination of tetracycline antibiotics from aqueous environments remains a significant challenge. In this work, Au-loaded ZnO immobilized cellulose-derived carbon beads (Au/ZnO@C) composite materials, with varying Au molar ratios, were synthesized through a one-pot approach. The Au/ZnO@C composite featured a metal-semiconductor architecture built from Au nanoparticles deposited on ZnO. The introduction of Au nanoparticles can modify the interfacial electronic structure of ZnO and promote charge transfer between Au and ZnO. Meanwhile, using cellulose-derived carbon beads as a carrier effectively suppressed the aggregation of Au/ZnO particles, addressing a key limitation in ZnO-based photocatalysts. Compared to bare carbon beads and ZnO@C, Au/ZnO@C exhibited better photocatalytic degradation performance. Among all samples, Au(1%)/ZnO@C showed the best catalytic performance, achieving a degradation efficiency of 87.62% for tetracycline. The degradation kinetics were well described by the Langmuir-Hinshelwood model, exhibiting a first-order behavior and an optimal apparent rate of 0.00729 min -1 . Mass spectrometry analysis revealed that tetracycline was progressively transformed into small-molecule intermediates during the degradation process.

title: The construction of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu oxidase for multivariate identification of acetylcholinesterase, organophosphorus pesticides and tannic acid supported by machine learning
abstract: The widespread abuse of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) threatens human health and ecological sustainability. The development of a portable, intelligent, and prompt detection strategy poses a key priority in both environment and human health, but remains a significant challenge. Here, visual detection of OPs was achieved based on its inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE), using the constructed metal-organic framework (MOF) composite UiO-66(Ce)/Cu as a catalyst in the 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) oxidation process. The coexistence of Cu 2 + /Cu + and Ce 4+ /Ce 3+ redox pairs synergistically promoted electron transfer and oxidase-mimicking (OXD-mimicking) catalysis. Based on the oxidation capability of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu and reversible colorimetric response, the AChE, OPs, and tannic acid (TA) can be detected assisted by the smartphone integrating with the machine learning algorithm. The limits of detection for TA, AChE, and OPs were determined to be 0.344 μM, 0.102 mU mL⁻¹ , and 0.0891 μg mL⁻¹ , respectively. In addition, satisfactory recoveries of 91.95-106.04% were obtained from real water and food samples, further corroborating the applicability of the intelligent and visual readout system for the portable analysis of OPs and TA. This work presented a practical strategy for constructing MOF-based OXD-mimicking nanozyme toward cascade biosensing and food safety applications.

title: Rapid assessment of the intrinsic hazard potential of different types of plastic additives using machine learning (RF-MLP)
abstract: As plastic pollution becomes increasingly severe, the additives released during its degradation have attracted widespread attention. How to effectively assess the potential hazards of plastic additives and identify candidates with relatively lower predicted intrinsic hazard potential for further evaluation has become an urgent issue. Experimental hazard assessment is costly and time-consuming, and the limited availability of baseline data prevents comprehensive screening of the large number of plastic additives in use. Currently, most additives lack sufficient baseline data, making it difficult for existing risk assessment methods to provide effective predictions under conditions of data scarcity. This paper proposes an intrinsic hazard potential assessment method based on the random forest-multilayer perceptron (RF-MLP) model to address this challenge. By combining the powerful nonlinear modeling capabilities of RF with the deep feature learning capabilities of Multi-Layer Perceptrons, this method can effectively capture the complex relationships between plastic additives and intrinsic hazard potential, thereby improving the accuracy of intrinsic hazard potential predictions. To further enhance the model's robustness and predictive capability, an Out-of-Fold (OOF) combination strategy was incorporated into the model. Linear regression analysis was performed on the outputs of the RF and MLP, thereby improving the accuracy of intrinsic hazard potential predictions. This model was used to conduct intrinsic hazard potential assessments on 7267 plastic additives. The RF-MLP model achieved an R 2 of 0.68 on the independent test set, reflecting the degree of agreement between the predicted and observed Hazard_score_sum values. Additionally, the performance of the RF-MLP model was compared with that of commonly used machine learning models (such as RF, MLP, SVR, and XGBoost) and other hybrid models. Validation was conducted on 60 plastic additives across different predicted intrinsic hazard potential intervals, incorporating toxicity or intrinsic hazard potential results reported in the literature and data from the T.E.S.T. software developed by the U.S. EPA. The results indicate that the RF-MLP model outperforms the comparison models in predictive performance. Comparisons with literature reports and T.E.S.T. outputs provided complementary evidence for interpreting the predicted hazard patterns. The constructed RF-MLP model partially mitigates the practical limitations caused by the prediction challenges caused by insufficient baseline data and can be applied not only to the intrinsic hazard potential assessment of plastic additives but also serve as a reference for chemical intrinsic hazard potential prediction in other data-scarce scenarios.

title: FTO mediates benzo[a]pyrene-induced lung cancer progression through regulating ferroptosis via lactylation-driven YTHDF2-KEAP1-NRF2 axis
abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification and histone lactylation are important regulators of gene expression and cancer progression, but their interplay in lung cancer associated with benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) remains unclear. Integrating clinical bioinformatics with cellular and in vivo analyses, we found that BaP enhanced migration and invasion while inducing a ferroptosis-resistant phenotype in lung cancer cells. Pharmacological modulation with Erastin and Ferrostatin-1 further supported ferroptosis involvement. BaP decreased FTO and increased YTHDF2 expression. FTO overexpression and YTHDF2 knockdown enhanced ferroptosis-associated lipid oxidation and suppressed migration and invasion, while their combined intervention attenuated BaP-associated experimental metastatic progression in vivo. Mechanistically, FTO overexpression reduced m 6 A enrichment on KEAP1 mRNA, whereas YTHDF2 associated with KEAP1 transcripts and accelerated their decay. Disruption of the A2108 RRACH motif attenuated YTHDF2-responsive repression of the KEAP1 reporter. KEAP1 knockdown attenuated FTO effects under BaP exposure. Upstream analyses supported AHR-dependent FTO regulation and a glycolysis-associated lactate-H3K18la contribution to YTHDF2 upregulation. Collectively, these findings support an m 6 A-sensitive FTO/YTHDF2-KEAP1-NRF2 framework contributing to ferroptosis defense and BaP-associated lung cancer malignant progression.

title: Battery-type-associated pollutant fingerprints and cytotoxicity of firefighting wastewater from full-scale electric vehicle fires
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased concern over fires, whose suppression generates chemically complex wastewater. However, the temporal evolution and toxicity of EV fire wastewater remain poorly understood. In this study, we conducted full-scale fire and suppression tests on EVs powered by nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, using time-resolved sampling to characterize firefighting runoff and residual wastewater retained after suppression. By integrating chemical profiling and in vitro cytotoxicity assays, we resolved battery-type-associated wastewater hazards. Runoff wastewater exhibited distinct metal-release fingerprints: NMC-runoff carried substantially higher battery-derived ionic loads, with early-stage Li + reaching 4.26-4.59 mg·L -1 , approximately one order of magnitude higher than that in LFP-runoff (averaging 0.36 mg·L -1 ). Residual pallet wastewater acted as a concentrated pollution reservoir, with NMC samples becoming strongly alkaline (pH>11). Li + and fluoride in residual wastewater reached about 7.21 × 10 2 mg·L -1 and 3.85 ×1 0 2 mg·L -1 , respectively, generally more than two orders of magnitude higher than in runoff wastewater. Cytotoxicity tests revealed that residual wastewater induced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with human neuroblastoma cells being the most sensitive and viability decreasing to 5.7%. These findings identify residual or immersion-type suppression water as a secondary EV fire hazard and support battery-type-specific strategies for emergency management. SYNOPSIS: Full-scale NMC and LFP battery EV fire tests reveal distinct wastewater pollutant fingerprints, sludge properties, and cytotoxic profiles, underscoring the need for chemistry-specific environmental standards and emergency protocols.

title: Salinity–regulated interfacial interactions of asphaltene subfractions: Mechanistic insights into petroleum emulsion stability and destabilization
abstract: Asphaltenes are problematic petroleum components that contribute to persistent oil-water emulsions and complicate produced water treatment. However, how asphaltene subfractions with distinct interfacial activities respond to brine salinity and regulate emulsion stability remains insufficiently understood. Here, the salinity-dependent adsorption, interfacial film formation, and intermolecular interactions of interfacially active asphaltenes (IAA) and interfacially non-active asphaltenes (INAA) were investigated at different NaCl concentrations using dynamic interfacial tension measurements, interfacial film characterization, surface force measurements, and emulsion stability tests. With increasing NaCl concentration, the extrapolated equilibrium interfacial tension of INAA-containing systems increased monotonically, whereas that of IAA-containing systems initially decreased and then increased. Apparent diffusion coefficients and crumpling ratios increased with NaCl concentration up to 1 M and decreased at 3 M, whereas compression energies remained elevated or increased further at 3 M. Droplet adhesion increased at 1-100 mM NaCl but declined sharply at 1-3 M. Bottle tests using a steam-assisted gravity drainage emulsion showed greater stability at low salinity and pronounced oil-water separation at high salinity. These results reveal a salinity-dependent transition from interfacial film strengthening to emulsion destabilization, providing mechanistic insights into the salinity-regulated interfacial interactions of asphaltene subfractions in stabilizing petroleum emulsions.

title: Integrated modelling framework for predicting microplastic build-up on urban surfaces
abstract: Urban impervious surfaces are major accumulation zones for microplastics, with deposited urban dust as a key carrier matrix facilitating their retention, redistribution, and transport from terrestrial to aquatic environments. However, processes governing microplastic build-up and the ability to predict its spatial distribution remain poorly understood. This study quantified the key factors influencing microplastic build-up and created a catchment-scale spatial predictive framework. Using dust samples from typical urban land uses in Brisbane, Australia, five influential predictors were identified, including dust loading, mineralogical composition, wind speed, land use, and population and were integrated using principal component analysis, multivariate regression, and spatial response surfaces modelling. Population was defined as the number of residents within a 1 km radius of each sampling site. Site-based observations combined with spatial predictor layers generated a continuous microplastic build-up surface across the study area. The resulting model has strong explanatory and predictive performance (R² = 0.91; cross-validated R² = 0.84). The novelty of this work lies in the integration of dust mineralogy and environmental drivers within a spatially explicit predictive framework, enabling identification of microplastic build-up at unsampled locations. The proposed framework improves understanding of terrestrial microplastic dynamics, providing a practical tool to support targeted monitoring and mitigation.

title: Enhanced removal of sulfamethoxazole by tourmaline-modified iron‑carbon substrate in constructed wetlands and underlying microbial metabolic mechanisms
Physical bioturbation coupled with gut-substrate cross-inoculation: A dual-pathway mechanism for enhanced acetochlor degradation in vermifilters
abstract: To mitigate acetochlor (ACT) diffuse pollution in the black soil region of Northeast China, a black soil-gravel biofilter was constructed to investigate how earthworm (Eisenia fetida) bioturbation enhances ACT degradation through coupled physical remodeling and micro-ecological regulation. At an HRT of 72 h, the vermifilter achieved 85.3% aqueous ACT removal and 66.4% solid-phase ACT removal rate, significantly outperforming planted and blank biofilters. In situ Micro-CT showed that earthworm burrowing increased matrix pore connectivity to 20 times that of the blank biofilter, reducing mass transfer resistance and maintaining pollutant bioavailability. High-throughput sequencing revealed that the earthworm gut functioned as a mobile incubator for key degrading bacteria, selectively enriching dechlorinating and dealkylating taxa such as Pseudomonas and Chryseobacterium and reinoculating them into the substrate. Under micro-acidic and nitrogen-rich conditions, the abundance of key transformation genes were higher, enabling complete ACT degradation to the molecular weight product N-(2-ethylphenyl) formamide.

title: The GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 module coordinately regulates soybean root development and cadmium tolerance through the ethylene signaling
abstract: Soybean (Glycine max) is a critical oil crop and a key source of fat and protein for both humans and animals. Cadmium (Cd) stress is a severe heavy metal stresses limiting root growth and yield. Significant variations exist in Cd tolerance among different soybean varieties. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying Cd-induced root growth inhibition and Cd accumulation remain elusive. Here, we identified that the GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 module in the ethylene signal transduction pathway coordinately regulates soybean root growth and Cd accumulation. We found Cd stress positively regulates the expression of GmEIN3.1 (Glyma.13G076700), which inhibits root development but reduces Cd accumulation and enhances Cd tolerance. Multiple lines of experimental evidence demonstrate that GmEIN3.1 represses the expression of GmERF3 (Glyma.14G050100), a transcription factor that promotes root development. In turn, GmERF3 binds to and suppresses the expression of the ABC transporter GmABCI17 (Glyma.08G055000), a Golgi-localized protein with Cd efflux transporter activity. Overexpression of GmABCI17 promotes Cd efflux, thereby reducing intracellular Cd accumulation and enhancing Cd tolerance. Collectively, the GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 transcriptional cascade coordinates Cd-induced root growth inhibition, restricts Cd accumulation, and Cd tolerance in soybean. It provides exploitable targets for breeding low-Cd soybean cultivars and addresses critical food safety concerns.

title: Dynamic release of phthalate esters from pristine and aged microplastics in indoor environments and their potential lung health impacts
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in indoor environments are a significant source of phthalate ester (PAEs) release, posing potential health risks. This study investigated PAEs release kinetics from polyethylene (PE) and polylactic acid (PLA) in indoor air, and from four common MPs (polyamide, polycarbonate, polyethylene, and polylactic acid) at multiple aging stages (0, 7, 14, 21, and 28 days) in simulated lung fluids (ALF and GS) through simulation experiments. Results demonstrated that light, temperature, and aging degree significantly influence PAEs release. Aging altered surface properties (increased specific surface area and hydrophilicity), causing non-monotonic release trends of PAEs. Both light exposure and elevated temperature significantly promoted PAEs release (p < 0.05), with kinetics following a pseudo-second-order model, governed by surface desorption and intraparticle diffusion. PAEs release was significantly higher in ALF than in GS (p < 0.05). Aged MPs exhibited elevated relative concentrations of ·OH and ·O₂⁻ in lung fluids, indicating a potential oxidative burden. This study elucidates the dynamic release behavior of additives during aging of microplastics, and highlights the dynamic aging process of MPs as well as the potential health impacts.

title: Zinc differentially modulates resistome responses to ciprofloxacin and sulfamethazine in activated sludge
abstract: Antibiotics and metals frequently coexist in wastewater, but whether metals uniformly intensify antibiotic-driven resistome selection remains unclear. Here, activated sludge reactors were exposed to zinc (Zn), ciprofloxacin (CIP), sulfamethazine (SMZ), and their combinations across four stepwise exposure stages. Read-based, assembly-based, and genome-resolved metagenomics were integrated to characterize antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) abundance, composition, mobility-associated genetic contexts, and putative hosts. Antibiotics primarily drove resistome restructuring, whereas Zn alone had limited effects. CIP strongly enriched ARGs, while Zn co-exposure attenuated this response and caused late-stage declines in total ARG abundance and the relative abundance of ARG-hosting metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). In contrast, ARG abundance remained comparatively stable under SMZ but increased progressively under Zn+SMZ. Because antibiotic concentrations increased sequentially over time, these patterns represent stage-dependent responses rather than independent concentration effects. Antibiotic-related treatments showed higher contributions of ARGs on predicted plasmid-like contigs and more frequent ARG-mobile genetic element co-localization. Pseudomonadota dominated putative ARG hosts, and CIP showed broader ARG-host profiles. Approximately 67% of ARG-hosting MAGs carried virulence factor genes, indicating co-occurring resistance and virulence-associated genomic potential. These findings demonstrate that Zn altered activated sludge resistome in an antibiotic-dependent manner, highlighting that mixture effects cannot be inferred from single-contaminant responses alone.

title: Functional characterization of PeNRAMP5 implies its potential role in controlling cadmium accumulation in plants
abstract: Reducing cadmium (Cd) accumulation in plants by disrupting transporter genes involved in Cd uptake or transport often compromises normal plant growth due to the co‑transport of essential elements. Therefore, identifying genes that specifically reduce Cd accumulation without impairing micronutrient uptake remains challenging. Here, we identified and functionally characterized two duplicated Moso bamboo genes, PeNRAMP5-1 and PeNRAMP5-2. Both genes are predominantly expressed in roots, downregulated by Cd, and encode plasma membrane‑localized transporters. Immunostaining revealed non polar distribution of PeNRAMP5 proteins in all root cells. Yeast assays demonstrated their ability to transport both Cd and Mn. Expression them in rice mutant osnramp5 increased root Cd uptake but reduced Cd accumulation in shoots and grains. In contrast, root Mn uptake and accumulation in shoots and grains were largely restored. When expressed in the mutant atnramp1 or wild‑type Arabidopsis, these genes markedly enhanced root Mn uptake and its accumulation in shoots. Conversely, although Cd accumulation in roots increased, shoots Cd accumulation was strongly inhibited. These results suggest that PeNRAMP5 can limit Cd accumulation in shoots while restoring Mn uptake in plants. This work identifies PeNRAMP5 as a promising genetic resource for inter‑species application to minimize Cd accumulation and maintain Mn nutrition in plants.

title: Formulation-dependent pulmonary disposition and secondary hepatic responses of the household insecticide hydramethylnon following respiratory tract delivery
abstract: Hydramethylnon (HM) is a household-use insecticide whose inhalation hazard remains poorly characterized. We combined whole-body disposition analysis with mechanistic assessment in pulmonary and hepatic systems. Structurally identical 18 F-labeled HM enabled dynamic positron emission tomography/computed tomography after intratracheal instillation in mice. Pulmonary clearance was rapid, with predominant redistribution to the liver and a fourfold longer half-life for the polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based than the ethanol-based dispersion (26.92 versus 6.59 min). In an air-liquid interface model, HM was cytotoxic to Calu-3 and H441 epithelial cells, whereas barrier-related responses reflected both PEG and HM in Calu-3 cells but predominantly HM in H441 cells. In HepG2 hepatocytes, differentiated THP-1 macrophages, and primary alveolar macrophages, HM induced apoptosis, adenosine triphosphate depletion, mitochondrial loss, impaired respiration, and reactive oxygen species generation without altering glycolysis. In vivo, hepatic apoptosis increased after both three-dose intratracheal instillation and 28-day repeated pharyngeal aspiration, whereas reduced hepatic mitochondrial content and elevated serum transaminases emerged only after 28 days, indicating duration- and cumulative dose-dependent hepatic responses. This study identifies the liver as the principal secondary exposure compartment after respiratory delivery of HM and shows that formulation modifies pulmonary retention, providing route-specific disposition data for hazard identification rather than quantitative risk assessment.

title: Machine learning-assisted ratiometric Zr-MOF-based fluorescent probe for intelligent detection of uranyl ions
abstract: Uranium contamination in aquatic environments poses potential threats to ecosystems and human health due to the high radioactive and chemical toxicity of uranyl ions (UO 2 2 + ), necessitating the development of accurate and rapid detection strategies for the monitoring of UO 2 2+ . Herein, a zirconium-based metal-organic framework (NH 2 -PCN-134) was constructed through a one-pot hydrothermal method and employed as a ratiometric fluorescent probe for the detection of UO 2 2+ . The ratiometric fluorescence response of NH 2 -PCN-134 toward UO 2 2+ featured emission quenching at 655 nm and enhancement at 515 nm, enabling quantitative analysis based on the I 515 /I 655 intensity ratio. Furthermore, the probe exhibited a broad linear response range of 0-200 μM with a low detection limit of 1.23 μM, and excellent selectivity toward UO 2 2+ in the presence of various interfering ions. The ratiometric fluorescence response was attributed to the synergistic effects of photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and molecular interactions between NH 2 -PCN-134 and UO 2 2+ . Moreover, the color features extracted from fluorescent images were integrated with multiple machine learning models for quantitative prediction, which exhibited strong agreement between the predicted and experimental values even in the presence of interfering ions, demonstrating their effectiveness for quantitative analysis. This study provides a machine learning-assisted ratiometric fluorescence sensing strategy for intelligent detection of UO 2 2+ , highlighting its potential for environmental monitoring.

title: Kinetic mismatch drives tetrachloroethene (PCE) rebound in Fe(II)/persulfate in situ chemical oxidation
abstract: Ferrous iron-activated persulfate (Fe(II)/PDS) is widely used for in situ chemical oxidation (ISCO) of chlorinated solvents, yet aqueous rebound complicates treatment evaluation. Phase-resolved mass balances were combined with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and surface characterization to examine tetrachloroethene (PCE) redistribution and removal. In homogeneous aqueous systems, PCE removal was rapid within 2 h, with rapid dissolved Fe(II) consumption. Among evaluated Fe(II):PDS ratios, 1:1 yielded the highest removal, with > 30% PDS persisting beyond the initial stage. Following Fe(II)/PDS addition to pre-equilibrated soil-water systems, aqueous PCE increased while soil-associated PCE decreased and total PCE mass declined monotonically. SEM-EDS, FTIR, and XRD indicated Fe-rich surface deposition and altered organic functional groups, supporting interfacial changes that weaken PCE retention. Soil addition attenuated EPR spin-adduct responses. In pre-equilibrated systems, the fitted sulfate-adduct response in soil extracts exhibited negligible variation between 10 and 120 min, consistent with continued soil-associated activation as intensive aqueous oxidation subsided. These observations support a kinetic mismatch between declining effective oxidative capacity and continued soil-to-water PCE release, allowing aqueous accumulation despite net removal. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for coordinating reagent transport and local activation with delayed contaminant release through alternating PDS and Fe(II) injection in groundwater circulation well (GCW) systems.

title: Lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide particles may impair cognitive function via CTCF-associated suppression of NMDAR-dependent synaptogenesis
abstract: Lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide (NCM) is the predominant cathode material for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs); however, its occupational health risks remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we found that in occupationally NCM‑exposed workers, urinary levels of Li, Ni, Co, and Mn were negatively associated with Mini‑Cog test scores and positively associated with serum neurofilament light chain (NfL, as neuronal injury marker). In an intratracheal instillation rat model, NCM-exposed rats exhibited learning and memory deficits, neuronal injury, and reduced synaptic complexity. RNA‑seq analysis revealed suppression of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDAR)‑dependent synaptogenesis pathways in rat hippocampus, along with downregulation of NMDAR subunits (GluN2A and GluN2B) and postsynaptic proteins such as CaMKII‑α, MAP2, PSD‑95, and Synapsin‑1. In SH-SY5Y cells, treatment with NCM-derived metals recapitulated these gene expression changes. Bioinformatics analysis identified CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) as a potential regulator of NMDAR. Cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) identified the binding of NCM-derived metals to CTCF. Based on in vivo data, human equivalent concentrations (HECs) derived from BMDL 10 of Ni and Mn were below the current OELs of China and America. Collectively, these findings indicate that NCM may induce neurotoxicity and impair learning and memory by disrupting synaptogenesis, and CTCF is implicated in this process.

title: Polyaniline-modified sea sand suppresses phase-change-driven microplastic transport via regenerable interfacial retention for long-term solar desalination
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation (SIE) provides a low-carbon route for seawater desalination, but its nonequilibrium phase-change interface may facilitate microplastic transfer from seawater to condensate. To mitigate this water-quality risk, a low-cost, regenerable photothermal interface was constructed by modifying natural sea sand with polyaniline (PANI@SS). The PANI coating enhanced broadband solar absorption and promoted interfacial water activation, achieving an evaporation rate of 2.20 kg·m -2 ·h -1 . Adsorption, spectroscopy, thermodynamic analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations showed that PANI converted the weak physical retention of pristine sea sand into stable interfacial anchoring, counteracting phase-change-driven microplastic transport. Reversible protonation/deprotonation enabled pH-regulated interfacial affinity, supporting facile regeneration and sustained antifouling performance. PANI@SS effectively retained seven representative microplastics with different structures and polarities, indicating broad applicability. In a 30-day outdoor test using natural seawater from the Yellow, Yangtze, and Pearl River estuaries, cumulative freshwater production exceeded 220 kg·m -2 , while major ion concentrations met drinking-water guideline limits. Evaporation performance, microplastic retention, and material structure remained stable after repeated evaporation-regeneration cycles. This study reveals the competition between phase-change transport and interfacial retention as a key mechanism governing microplastic migration and product-water safety in SIE, providing a practical strategy for efficient, durable, and regenerable solar desalination.

title: Nanoplastics and thermal stress induce synergistic toxicity in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) through epithelial barrier damage, immuno-metabolic dysregulation, and cancer-associated transcriptional signatures
abstract: Marine organisms are increasingly exposed to nanoplastics (NPs) and rising temperatures due to climate change, yet their combined effects remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the interactive toxicity of polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs, 80 nm) and elevated temperature (32 °C vs 25 °C) in marine medaka larvae (Oryzias melastigma) using integrated bioaccumulation analysis, histopathology, and transcriptomic profiling. Our results revealed that the digestive tract served as the primary tissue for NPs bioaccumulation, with elevated temperature significantly accelerating particle bioaccumulation (1.20-6.27-fold increase) and exacerbating shedding of intestinal villi. Transcriptomic analysis identified temperature as the dominant driver of transcriptional remodeling, while co-exposure induced unique synergistic effects not observed under individual stressors. Specifically, combined exposure amplified immuno-inflammatory responses through complement cascade and phagosome pathways, with NPs perceived as pseudo-pathogenic threats triggering respiratory burst and apoptosis. Concurrently, antagonistic interactions suppressed critical protective responses including heat shock protein hsp90α1 and immune regulators (e.g., il2rg and ptx3). Most concerning, co-exposure uniquely enriched multiple cancer-related pathways absent from individual stress conditions, with synergistic upregulation of the proto-oncogene myc-2. These findings demonstrated that elevated temperature fundamentally altered NPs toxicity from localized intestinal stress to broad immuno-inflammatory dysregulation, creating a transcriptional state associated with cancer-related pathways. Additionally, a phenotypic interaction analysis on catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA), reduced glutathione (GSH) and intestinal villus morphometry (length and width) showed that the standardized Cohen's d interaction indices followed a consistent trend matching transcriptome-level predictions of synergistic antioxidant induction and barrier impairment. Our results highlighted that current single-stressor risk assessments underestimate NPs threat under climate change scenarios, emphasizing the urgent need for multi-stressor frameworks in environmental protection.

title: Comparative studies of hydroxyl radical and sulfate radical-mediated degradation of aromatic compounds: Changes in electron-donating moieties and disinfection byproduct formation potential
abstract: Aromatic compounds contribute the majority of UV 254 , electron-donating moieties (EDM), and disinfection byproduct formation potential (DBP-FP) for natural organic matter (NOM). This study selected 4-ethylphenol (4-EP), 1-(4-hydroxyphenyl)ethanol (4-HPE), 1-(4-hydroxyphenyl)ethenone (4-HPA), and 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid (4-HPAA) as model compounds representing aromatic hydrocarbons, alcohols, ketones, and carboxylic acids, respectively. 4-HPA behaves differently from the other three: its electron-withdrawing carbonyl group substantially increases UV 254 while decreasing EDM. During oxidation, 4-HPA uniquely shifts from a negative to a positive EDM-UV 254 correlation, whereas the other three maintain negative correlations. SO 4 •- oxidation removed more EDM but generated higher UV 254 products than • OH. Both radical oxidations enhanced representative DBP-FP (6-108-fold), with • OH showing 1.5-4.4-fold higher DBP-FP than SO 4 •- . 4-HPA exhibited the highest trichloromethane and 1,1,1-trichloropropanone formation potential before and after oxidation. For • OH, 4-HPE was the primary chloral hydrate precursor, while for SO 4 •- , multiple compounds contributed comparably. EDM removal serves as a better surrogate for DBP-FP when applied to aromatic hydrocarbons, alcohols, and carboxylic acids, while UV 254 change is more suitable for aromatic ketones. These correlations were extended to Suwannee River NOM, providing a potential mechanistic basis for understanding DBP formation from complex NOM during radical-based water treatment.

title: Alkaline cementitious matrix effects on the fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in recycled plastic aggregates
abstract: Recycled plastics, including polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) and high-density polyethylene (rHDPE), are increasingly used as construction materials in response to sustainability and circular-economy goals, to repurpose waste streams and reduce natural-resource demand. This study provides the first assessment of PFAS adsorption by recycled plastic aggregates (rPA) and subsequent desorption in simulated cement pore solution (SCPS) by evaluating sorption-desorption mechanisms as functions of polymer type, surface chemistry, exposure duration, and perfluoroalkyl chain length (C4-C11). Batch experiments quantified indicative multi-analyte PFAS loading under neutral pH and PFAS desorption under construction-relevant exposure to high pH (>12.5) and ionic strength (0.85-1.0 M) SCPS. PFAS with carbon chain lengths >C8 showed strong adsorption affinity for rHDPE over rPET (6.2-106.5% greater mass-normalised adsorption (pg/g)), with competitive uptake increasing with chain length and contact time up to 28 days. Desorption into near-neutral ultrapure water was negligible (<LOD), confirming rPA as effective short-term sinks for PFAS. However, SCPS induced substantial PFAS desorption from rPA, particularly of short-chain perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) from rPET, and (less so) rHDPE. These findings challenge the long-term viability of rPA in concrete, highlight their potential as transient PFAS sinks or enduring leaching sources, and emphasise the need for risk-based guidelines for rPA use in cementitious matrices.

title: Occurrence features, source apportionment, and exposure risks of organic ultraviolet absorbers in surface dust, soil, and PM2.5 in a semi-arid industrial city of Xi'an, China
abstract: Organic ultraviolet absorbers (OUVAs) are widely used in personal care and industrial products, which have attracted increasing concerns due to their adverse health effects. However, the occurrences, sources, and exposure risks of OUVAs in urban environments remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a total of 167 samples, encompassing surface dust, topsoil, and atmospheric PM 2.5 , were collected from the largest city of Xi'an in Northwest China. Twelve OUVAs were analyzed in these samples for their pollution characteristics, potential sources, and exposure risks. The results showed that OUVAs were widely detected in the three media. In the surface dust, topsoil, and PM 2.5 , the total concentration of 12 OUVAs (Σ12OUVAs) averaged as 369 ng/g, 86.6 ng/g, and 9.81 ng/m³ . OUVAs were dominated by 3-(4-methylbenzylidene) camphor (4-MBC), homosalate (HMS), and benzophenone (BP); ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate and 2-ethylhexyl 4-(dimethylamino) benzoate; and 4-MBC. Higher Σ12OUVAs were mainly distributed in the urban east-west axis and the northeastern and southern of Xi'an; the western, southwestern, and northwestern of Xi'an; and summer (13.7 ng/m³) rather than winter (5.77 ng/m³). OUVAs mainly originated from usages of sunscreen and personal care products, construction-related emissions, mixed sources, domestic wastewater. Human exposure levels to OUVAs followed ingestion > dermal contact > > inhalation and children > adolescents > youths > adults. The contributions of environmental media to the total exposure followed surface dust > topsoil > > PM 2.5 . Among OUVAs, 4-MBC was the major contributor to human exposure, followed by HMS and BP. The hazard quotient (HQ) and hazard index (HI) for individual and all OUVAs were below the threshold of 1, suggesting insignificant non-carcinogenic health risks.

title: Smart pH-regulated foams with tunable wettability and photothermal enhancement for controllable recovery of oil-contaminated water
abstract: Oil contamination in water poses persistent environmental risks, making the efficient removal and recovery of oil pollutants a pressing challenge. Materials capable of adapting their interfacial properties in response to environmental stimuli are highly desirable for oil pollution control. Herein, we develop a pH-responsive smart composite foam (SCF) that integrates reversible wettability switching, controllable oil absorption-desorption, and photothermal-assisted oil recovery within a single porous architecture. The SCF exhibits pronounced pH-dependent wettability switching (0°∼155°), enabling controllable separation of various immiscible oil-water mixtures. In acidic media, the SCF surface displays superhydrophilicity and underwater superoleophobicity, while it transitioned to hydrophobic/oleophilic state under neutral or alkaline conditions, with oil-water separation efficiency exceeding 99%. The SCF demonstrates reversible pH-regulated oil uptake and release, with high uptake capacity under alkaline conditions and desorption efficiency above 80% upon acidification. Integrated with a dissolved oxygen probe, the SCF enables real-time oil spill monitoring, and its photothermal conversion effectively reduce oil viscosity and accelerate absorption. Unlike traditional responsive materials relying mainly on wettability transitions, this study establishes a strategy for efficient oil recovery by exploiting pH-dependent interfacial energy changes to regulate the capillary driving force, thereby providing new mechanistic understanding of controllable oil transport and recovery in porous materials.

title: Polymerizable viscous additive-assisted interfacial polymerization enables superior micropollutant/mineral selective separation in nanofiltration membranes for sustainable water purification
abstract: Selective removal of hazardous organic micropollutants (OMP) while preserving beneficial mineral ions (e.g., Ca 2 + and Mg 2+ ) remains challenging for conventional nanofiltration (NF) membranes, which commonly reject both OMP and mineral salts. Herein, we developed a sulfonated poly(vinyl alcohol)-incorporated nanofiltration (SINF) membrane through a polymerizable viscous additive-assisted interfacial polymerization strategy. By using sulfonated poly(vinyl alcohol) (SPVA) as a multifunctional aqueous-phase additive, the diffusion of piperazine was retarded and additional -SO 3 H groups were incorporated into the polyamide (PA) layer, creating a thin, loose, and highly negatively charged selective layer with ring-shaped surface topographies and nanovoid-enriched substructures. The optimized SINF membrane achieved an OMP/mineral (eltrombopag/Ca 2+ ) separation factor of 652.0, 41.2 times higher than that of the control membrane, while maintaining a high water permeance of 29.2 L m -2 h -1 bar -1 and an uncompromised Na 2 SO 4 rejection of 98.7%. In real surface water, the SINF membrane also maintained high OMP rejection (≥90.9%) and favorable Ca 2+ permeation (65.8%). Enhanced OMP rejection was attributed to strengthened electrostatic exclusion of negatively charged OMP and enhanced hydration layer interaction of hydrophobic OMP. This work provides a robust strategy for designing NF membranes that integrate rapid water transport, strong OMP rejection, and mineral ion preservation for high-quality reclaimed water production.

title: Deciphering cross-scale spatiotemporal mapping and metabolic signatures of aflatoxins accumulation in Aspergillus-infected peanuts
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination in peanuts poses carcinogenic risks, yet conventional detection methods provide limited rapid, non-destructive assessment and insight into the dynamic spatiotemporal progression and associated metabolic changes. This study integrated near-infrared hyperspectral imaging (NIR-HSI), mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (uHPLC-MS/MS) with machine learning (ML) to elucidate the cross-scale spatiotemporal mapping and metabolic signatures associated with aflatoxin accumulation in Aspergillus-infected peanuts. The NIR-HSI-based predictive model achieved 100% classification accuracy in discriminating control, toxigenic, and nontoxigenic strains. Quantitative models achieved Rcv/Rpre values of 0.94/0.84 and 0.87/0.90 for AFB1 and AFB2, respectively. MSI combined with ML analysis resolved the microscale spatiotemporal metabolic dynamics of aflatoxins and their metabolites across various infection stages. The early stage (0-24 h) was characterized by lipid oxidation and synthesis of flavonoid antimicrobials; the mid-stage (24-48 h) was accompanied by fungal carbohydrate plundering; and the later stage (48-72 h) exhibited systemic metabolic disorder. NIR-HSI and MSI collectively demonstrated that Aspergillus flavus infection typically initiates spatially on the surface near the hypocotyl and progressively advances inward, consistent with the aflatoxins' accumulation dynamics. In conclusion, this work established a cross-scale spatiotemporal framework, providing a foundation for early warning and prevention of aflatoxin contamination.

title: Interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds and organic foulants in ultrafiltration processes
abstract: In this study, we systematically investigated the fundamental interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) and organic fouling layers during ultrafiltration (UF) processes. Two representative PhACs, propranolol (PRP) and naproxen (NPX), were filtered through polyethersulfone membranes fouled with natural organic matter surrogates, including humic acid, bovine serum albumin, and sodium alginate. The results suggested that electrostatic interactions contributed substantially to the association of ionic PhACs with organic fouling layers under the investigated UF conditions. Electrostatic attraction likely promoted the association of cationic PRP with negatively charged fouling layers, whereas electrostatic repulsion likely limited the association of anionic NPX with these layers under neutral and alkaline conditions. Experiments conducted at high ionic strength (1 M NaCl) further supported these mechanisms by suppressing electrostatic interactions, resulting in decreased PRP and improved NPX association with fouling layers. When electrostatic contributions were reduced, the observed PhAC retention was consistent with hydrophobic interaction, with possible additional contributions from π-π interactions and hydrogen bonding. These findings highlight the influence of foulant chemistry on pharmaceutical association.

title: Ag and Cu partitioned on SSZ-13/γ-Al2O3 composites: Synergistic enhancement of NH3-SCO
abstract: SSZ-13 and γ-Al 2 O 3 were composited by ball milling, and the Ag/Cu-A l S 3 catalyst was successfully prepared, exhibiting excellent catalytic performance and high economic efficiency. Introducing γ-Al 2 O 3 effectively modulated the reaction mechanism of the Ag/Cu-SSZ-13 catalyst. More importantly, a significant synergistic effect between Ag and Cu was observed across different temperature regions. At low temperatures ( 3 to generate NO x , thereby lowering the reaction energy barrier, while Cu species within the pores served as the primary active centers, dominating the internal-selective catalytic reduction (i-SCR) mechanism and endowing the catalyst with excellent low-temperature activity. When the reaction temperature exceeded 200 °C, the reaction mechanism switched to the N 2 - mechanism , which was dominated by the Ag/Al 2 O 3 component. Meanwhile, Cu species further lowered the reaction energy barrier through synergy, ensuring a smooth transition of the N 2 - mechanism after the i-SCR process and achieving efficient NH 3 elimination over a wide temperature range.

title: Hydrodynamic forcing controls denitrification-DNRA competition and groundwater-derived nitrate contaminant attenuation
abstract: River stage fluctuations regulate river aquifer interactions and subsurface biogeochemistry in upstream and midstream rivers. Nevertheless, how diel river-groundwater stage fluctuations impact surface subsurface mixing and the fate of groundwater derived nitrate remains poorly understood in downstream gaining rivers, critical hotspots for nitrogen accumulation and ecological risks. This study develops a coupled hydro-biogeochemical numerical model to evaluate how diel stage fluctuations govern nitrate attenuation via denitrification and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) competition. The model represents a typical dune-shaped streambed, where nitrate-polluted groundwater discharges into organic-carbon-rich stream. Diel surface water fluctuations propagate into the aquifer, inducing groundwater responses with 10-90% amplitude attenuation and 3-24 h time lags. Diel hydrological fluctuations expand surface-groundwater mixing zones, regulate in-situ C/N stoichiometry, alter nitrate reduction rates, and govern denitrification-DNRA competition. Under C/N ratios of 0.5-2, moderate hydraulic-head offsets (30-50%) and 6-18 h out-of-phase subsurface fluctuations favor DNRA, whereas large head differences (>70%) shift competition toward denitrification. Baseline simulations reveal that hydrological fluctuation regimes exert stronger control over this competition than C/N ratios, although biogeochemical kinetic properties may mask these fluctuation‑driven signals and limit the generalizability of such patterns. These results indicate targeted hydrodynamic‑regime regulation can enhance nitrate attenuation and mitigate nitrogen pollution risks in lowland rivers.

title: Tunable pore architectures in programmable DNA hydrogels for ultrasensitive magnetic relaxation sensing of Pb²⁺ over a wide dynamic range
abstract: Magnetic relaxation switch (MRS) sensors are widely used in analytical applications due to their excellent performance. Gel-MRS offers enhanced stability, making it particularly advantageous. However, existing stimuli-responsive hydrogel-based MRS sensors are often limited in detection range and limit of detection (LOD) by the physicochemical constraints of the gel network. Herein, we demonstrate wide-range, ultrasensitive MRS detection of Pb²⁺ using programmable DNA hydrogels with tunable pore architectures. By systematically varying the crosslinking linker design, three hydrogels with pore sizes of 0.72, 1.12, and 4.28 μm were fabricated. As pore size increased, the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) decreased from 2.03 × 10⁻³ to 1.65 × 10⁻³ mm²/s, while the transverse relaxation time change (ΔT₂) increased proportionally, establishing a quantitative structure-property relationship among pore size, ADC, and T₂ response. Leveraging this relationship, the optimized MRS-DNA hydrogel biosensor achieves a detection limit of 8.4 pg/mL and a linear range spanning four orders of magnitude (0.01-100 ng/mL) with a correlation coefficient of 0.99. Validation in complex matrices yields spike recoveries between 95.21% and 109.21%, underscoring the method's robustness. This programmable pore-engineering strategy offers a new pathway toward reliable, decentralized screening of hazardous contaminants.

title: Risk assessment of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in global lakes and their hotspots
abstract: Freshwater lakes are crucial hotspots that have fueled the global antimicrobial resistance crisis. However, the distribution patterns and health risks of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) in lakes remain largely unexplored at the global scale. In this study, we comprehensively examined 1268 metagenomic samples from lakes globally and identified 12,866 ARBs spanning 28 phyla. Furthermore, based on the co-carriage of resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, and virulence factors, we developed a three-tiered risk framework. This framework distinguishes a critical-risk group comprising six species (belonging to Enterobacteriaceae, Aeromonadaceae, and Pseudomonadaceae) that are phylogenetically closely related to known pathogens, exhibiting the highest resistance, mobility, and pathogenic potential. Geographically, these critical-risk ARBs are primarily concentrated in low-latitude lakes (Amazon Basin, Central Africa, South/Southeast Asia, and Central America). Using machine learning, we identified temperature and wind speed as the primary driving factors. From a One Health perspective, our results inform a clear action plan and pinpoint low-latitude lakes as the priority targets for surveillance. This highlights the urgent need to include ARB risk stratification in security frameworks for global aquatic ecology.

title: Targeted capture of thallium by cerium sulfate enables efficient NOx reduction in poisoned SCR catalysts
abstract: Severe thallium (Tl) contamination released from cement kiln flue gas profoundly deactivates commercial selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalysts, restricting their long-term service stability. Highly volatile Tl species preferentially bind to essential V=O redox active sites to form inert V-O-Tl structures, aggressively disrupting surface acidity and redox synergy. Herein, we report a targeted modification strategy where surface sulfate groups on a Ce(SO 4 ) 2 -modified vanadium-based catalyst act as sacrificial sites. Even under conditions of severe Tl poisoning, this modified catalyst maintains the NO x conversion rate exceeding 95% within the high-temperature window, in contrast to the catalytic failure of the unmodified catalyst. Tl species preferentially bind and immobilize onto surface sulfate sites of the catalyst, and this targeted capture mechanism spatially and electronically isolates toxic Tl from V active centers. The DFT calculations indicate that the formation of thallium sulfate is thermodynamically more favorable, and this sacrificial trapping mechanism restores surface acid and redox sites, maintaining intact NOₓ adsorption intermediates and unobstructed SCR reaction pathways. This study provides new mechanism regarding the Tl tolerance of SCR catalysts, and these insights for the rational design of highly stable catalysts for industrial NO x removal under complex flue gas conditions.

title: PM2.5 exposure and retinal neurovascular dysfunction: Clinical and mechanistic evidence for complement C3/C3aR pathway involvement
abstract: PM 2.5 is a pervasive environmental toxicant associated with retinal neurodegeneration, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. This study combined clinical, animal, and cellular approaches to investigate whether C3/C3aR signaling mediates PM 2.5 ‑induced retinal neurovascular damage. In retrospective longitudinal glaucoma cohort, a linear mixed‑effects model analyzed PM 2.5 effects on inflammatory markers. In mice, we examined PM 2.5 effects on retinal complement, microglia activation, neurovascular function, and vision. The protective effect of the C3aR blocker SB290157 was also evaluated. BV2 and retinal endothelial cells were used to study C3‑dependent microglial polarization and its vasoregulatory effects. In clinical experiment, we identified a significant association between short-term PM 2.5 exposure and systemic complement dysregulation, characterized by a decrease in serum C3c. In mice, PM 2.5 exposure induced marked retinal C3 activation. This change was characterized by microglial activation, vascular dysfunction, and retinal structural and functional impairment. In vitro, PM 2.5 directly induced C3/C3aR-dependent microglial M1 polarization and stimulated endothelial vasoconstrictor secretion via microglial crosstalk. Treatment with C3aR inhibitor attenuated the vicious cycle, preserving retinal structure and visual function. In conclusion, C3/C3aR axis serves as a key mechanistic link between PM 2.5 exposure and retinal neurodegeneration. Targeting this pathway may offer a therapeutic strategy for mitigating pollution-related retinal damage.

title: Soil nanoparticles and agricultural ligands remobilize cadmium sulfide colloids through composition–dependent heteroaggregation in saturated porous media
abstract: Cadmium sulfide (CdS) formation can attenuate dissolved Cd mobility in reducing or sulfur-enriched agricultural soils, yet the remobilization risk of CdS nanoparticles (CdS-NPs) by natural soil nanoparticles and agricultural ligands remains poorly understood. Here, we show that soil-derived nanoparticles (SNPs) and common ligands can remobilize CdS as colloidal particles rather than dissolved Cd 2 + , creating a potentially overlooked pathway for Cd transport in saturated porous media. Saturated quartz sand column experiments, effluent speciation, colloidal characterization, fluorescence microscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, XDLVO calculations, and two-site kinetic attachment modeling were integrated to determine how nanoparticle size, soil-derived composition, humic acid, and phosphate regulate CdS transport. Smaller SNPs promoted CdS breakthrough by forming smaller, more negatively charged, and more stable CdS-nanoparticle heteroaggregates. Nanoparticle composition exerted contrasting effects: organic matter-rich black soil nanoparticles and paddy soil nanoparticles enhanced CdS mobility, with black soil nanoparticles producing the highest transport percentage of 58.27%, whereas loessial soil nanoparticles reduced CdS transport to 35.45% by promoting aggregation and retention, likely through Ca-mediated cation bridging. Humic acid and phosphate further increased CdS-nanoparticle transport, with humic acid showing the stronger effect by enhancing colloidal stability and increasing interaction energy barriers. XDLVO calculations and kinetic attachment modeling linked enhanced CdS breakthrough to higher repulsive energy barriers and lower irreversible retention. These findings demonstrate that naturally occurring soil nanoparticles and agricultural ligands can convert immobilized CdS into mobile colloidal carriers, highlighting an important colloid-facilitated pathway for Cd migration and groundwater contamination risk in agricultural soils.

title: Biogenic maturation of mineral-encrusted plastispheres overrides ecological drift to orchestrate multi-kingdom assembly and nitrogen reprogramming in agroecosystems
abstract: The quantitative assembly rules and multi-kingdom functional gateways of the soil plastisphere remain poorly resolved. We integrated multi-omics with high-resolution surface deconvolution to decode the ecological signatures of weathered polyethylene (PE) films in intensive agroecosystems. Surface characterization revealed an interfacial metamorphosis where biogenic maturation facilitated the formation of a dense mineral organic crust, transforming inert polymers into reactive metabolic islands. Ecological modeling identifies a distinct departure from neutral assembly, demonstrating that niche-based selection driven by polymer surface remodeling overrides ecological drift in shaping microbial consortia. Machine learning and structural equation modeling identify ammonia oxidizing archaea as the primary functional keystone taxa orchestrating the global interactome. This archaeal-bacterial axis, regulated by protistan assemblages that exhibit significant topological densification, catalyzes a cross-kingdom metabolic relay synchronized with nitrogenous biomarker accumulation and intensified enzymatic mineralization. Functional decoupling across taxonomic domains reveals a metabolic lag where rapid deterministic recruitment outpaces steady-state nutrient stabilization. While promoting local alpha-diversity, the bacterial core exhibits structural fragmentation and elevated antagonistic interactions, signaling an asynchronous regime shift that may trigger positive priming effects on native soil organic carbon. These findings establish a mechanistic blueprint for how weathered PE residues redirect terrestrial nutrient fluxes via deterministic multi-kingdom assembly, pinpointing specific organo-mineral signatures and archaeal keystone taxa as critical targets for precision microbiome engineering in the Anthropocene.

title: Emerging contaminants in microalgae-based sustainable foods: occurrence patterns and dietary risk implications
abstract: Microalgae-based foods are gaining attention as sustainable protein sources, but information on the occurrence of emerging contaminants in commercial products remains limited. Here, we investigated the occurrence patterns and dietary risk implications of three classes of emerging contaminants, including parabens, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and p-phenylenediamine antioxidants (PPDs), in 77 commercially available microalgae-based food samples from China, including spirulina powder, chlorella powder, and microalgae-processed food products. Target analytes were quantified using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry, and probabilistic dietary exposure was assessed using Monte Carlo simulation. Parabens, PFAS, and PPDs were widely detected across the analyzed samples, with methylparaben and butylparaben dominating the paraben profiles, PFBA dominating the PFAS profiles, and 6PPD overwhelmingly dominating the PPD profiles. Despite their frequent occurrence, parabens and PPDs posed limited dietary risks through microalgae consumption, with hazard index values far below 1. Moreover, PFAS showed relatively higher dietary risk. This risk was not driven by the most abundant PFAS, but by trace-level PFDA, PFHxS, and PFOA, whose extremely low reference doses made them the dominant contributors to overall risk. These findings document the co-occurrence of three contaminant classes in microalgae-based foods and provide evidence-tiered priorities for screening-level dietary risk management. SYNOPSIS: Dietary risk estimates for microalgae-based foods were low for parabens and PPDs but sensitive to the toxicity benchmarks selected for trace PFAS congeners.

title: Fluorine mass balance, precursor transformability, and screening-level inhalation prioritization of PFAS-containing firefighting foam concentrates
abstract: Ten PFAS-containing firefighting foam concentrates from South Korea were characterized by LC-MS/MS target analysis, IMS-HRMS suspect screening with CCS-supported confidence assignment, the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay, total organofluorine (TOF) analysis, and screening-level inhalation prioritization. PFOS and PFOA were not detected, whereas C6 fluorotelomer-derived PFAS dominated all eight AFFF-related products. 6:2 FTAB accounted for 97.5-98.6% of quantified PFAS in five products and 6:2 FTS for 92.3-96.3% in the remaining three. Suspect screening identified 16 PFAS classes, including four candidate classes previously unreported in firefighting foams. TOP results indicated unknown oxidizable PFCA precursor pools. Apparent target-plus-suspect fluorine recovery averaged 45 ± 52% across all ten products, including LOQ-bound estimates for two SS products without directly quantifiable TOF, indicating unresolved organofluorine. Under a conservative indoor scenario without self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) protection, the toxicity reference value (TRV)-normalized hazard index (HI) was dominated by 6:2 FTS and reached 18.1 for H-AFFF at 450 L/min. Although 6:2 FTAB had the largest target-PFAS burden, it was excluded from the main HI because only an exploratory 28-day oral provisional TRV was available; therefore, the HI should be interpreted as a screening-level prioritization metric rather than a definitive inhalation risk estimate.

title: Microbial necromass carbon links soil carbon sequestration to heavy metal stabilization under long-term fertilization
abstract: Long-term fertilization sustains soil productivity but concurrently introduces heavy metals (HMs) into agroecosystems. The mechanisms by which soil carbon pools regulate HM speciation, however, remain inadequately understood. Based on a 15-year field experiment, this study investigated the influence of fertilization on HM accumulation and speciation in relation to microbial necromass carbon (MNC), soil aggregation, and microbial community reorganization.
