Fertilization increased soil carbon pools, soil organic carbon increased by 44% under mineral fertilization and by 101-140% under organic amendments, while MNC rose by 92% and 304-342%, respectively. Sequential extraction revealed a consistent redistribution of HMs toward oxidizable fractions, particularly under organic fertilization where the proportion of this fraction increased by 7-26% relative to the unfertilized control. Shifts in microbial community composition toward copiotrophic taxa accelerated microbial turnover and promoted necromass accumulation. Aggregate-scale analyses further demonstrated that MNC was preferentially enriched in macroaggregates > 0.25 mm, whereas HMs were preferentially enriched in the 0.25-2 mm fraction. Random forest highlighted MNC as a primary predictor of Cu and Cd partitioning, whereas PLS-PM indicated that necromass accumulation and direct HM inputs jointly regulate HM speciation. These findings identify MNC as a previously underappreciated biogeochemical interface linking soil carbon stabilization with long-term HM retention in fertilized agricultural soils.

title: Impacts of aged nanoscale zero-valent iron on the weathering of arsenopyrite: Arsenic transformation and environmental implications
abstract: Arsenopyrite, an arsenic-bearing sulfide mineral, is highly susceptible to weathering, causing contamination with toxic arsenic and hydrogen ions. Nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI), which is widely employed in environmental remediation, is gradually oxidized into iron hydroxides accompanied by aging phenomena after being applied to soil or groundwater, thereby affecting the oxidation process of arsenopyrite. In this study, electrochemical measurements, immersion experiments and various characterization techniques were employed to explore the effects of aged nanoscale zero-valent iron (A-nZVI) on the oxidation mechanism of arsenopyrite. Experimental results indicate that within the low concentration range (0-1.0 g·L -1 ), A-nZVI accelerates the oxidation rate of arsenopyrite and raises arsenic concentration. The corrosion current density reaches its peak at 1.0 g·L -1 . A-nZVI can adsorb and reduce arsenic in the solution, markedly decreasing the concentration of As(V). This inhibits the formation of ferric arsenate passivation products and reduces the charge transfer resistance at the mineral-solution interface. As A-nZVI concentration increase from 1.0 to 1.5 g·L -1 , excess A-nZVI covered the mineral surface, increasing the adsorption layer resistance and charge transfer resistance, which in turn inhibited the oxidation of arsenopyrite. Characterization results verified that A-nZVI surface consists of lepidocrocite (γ-FeOOH) and magnetite/maghemite (Fe 3 O 4 /γ-Fe 2 O 3 ). A-nZVI increases As(III) levels and total arsenic release without aggravating proton pollution originating from arsenopyrite. This work offers data and scientific evidence for evaluating A-nZVI performance in environmental/industrial uses and its large-scale application near mining sites.

title: Water-washing pretreatment enhanced co-smelting of MSWI fly ash and copper slag: Metals extraction, slag vitrification and silicate network evolution mechanism
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA) is a typical hazardous waste that needs urgent detoxification and resource utilization. However, existing treatment methods typically suffer from high energy consumption, low metal yield, and unclear microstructure evolution mechanisms. This study proposes a novel, energy-efficient water-washing pretreatment enhanced co-smelting strategy utilizing copper slag (CS) as a co-treatment feedstock to simultaneously recover high-value Cu/Zn and achieve slag vitrification. A water-washing pretreatment was implemented to mitigate chlorination-induced Cu volatilization. Under optimal conditions, Cu and Zn extraction ratios reach 96.41% and 85.84%, respectively, with 91.40% glass content in the residual slag. Crucially, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to quantitatively decode the microstructural evolution of the silicate network. The results establish a precise multiscale linkage between atomic-level [SiO 4 ] 4- depolymerization, melt fluidity, and macroscopic metal-slag separation. This co-treatment strategy offers an efficient and economical solution for simultaneous resource extraction and hazardous waste detoxification.

title: Proteomics as an emerging tool for understanding biotransformation and toxicological impacts of contaminants
abstract: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics is rapidly advancing, becoming fast, affordable, and increasingly accessible to environmental scientists. This perspective outlines how proteomics can illuminate biotransformation processes and sublethal organism-level effects, and highlights future opportunities enabled by emerging technologies. Our goal is to give a concise overview on realistic expectations of current capabilities while inspiring scientists to adapt and develop novel proteomic approaches addressing fundamental questions in contaminant science.

title: Urbanization-driven pathways of soil metal resistance genes across three park types in a karst mountainous city
Determination of specific kinetic parameters for different ionization states of enrofloxacin during UV/chlorine treatment: A pH-independent kinetic modelling method
abstract: The UV/chlorine process has demonstrated superior efficacy in micropollutant degradation. However, the strong pH dependence of second-order rate constants between contaminants and reactive species poses a fundamental challenge to the accuracy and generalizability of kinetic models. In this study, a comprehensive kinetic investigation was conducted on the degradation of enrofloxacin (ENR) by UV/chlorine across its three ionic speciation states (ENR + , ENR 0 , and ENR - ). Key mechanistic insights were obtained through systematic differentiation of degradation pathways, including direct UV photolysis, oxidation by free chlorine, HO • and reactive chlorine species. The specific photolysis rate constants were calculated to be 1.51 × 10 -3 , 15.09 × 10 -3 , and 9.57 × 10 -3 cm 2 Ein -1 for ENR + , ENR 0 , and ENR - , respectively. The specific second-order rate constants for the reaction toward ClO • for ENR + , ENR 0 , and ENR - were calculated to be 5.46 × 10 9 , 1.11 × 10 9 and 4.66 × 10 9 L mol -1 s -1 , respectively. Based on species-specific kinetic parameters, a pH-independent kinetic model for ENR degradation by UV/chlorine were construct, enabling reliable prediction of degradation kinetics at any pH within the selected range. This model provides a robust framework for predicting and optimizing treatment performance, thereby offering critical guidance for the design and engineering application of UV/chlorine processes.

title: Unexpected higher emissions of nitrogenous compounds and formaldehyde during DPF regeneration in real driving emission test of China VI heavy-duty diesel trucks
abstract: Heavy-duty diesel vehicles are important sources of air pollutants, yet gaseous emissions during diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration remain insufficiently characterized under real-world driving conditions. In this study, a portable emissions measurement system (PEMS) was used to quantify gaseous emissions from a China VI heavy-duty diesel truck during an on-road regeneration event. The instantaneous emissions and regeneration contributions of NO, NO 2 , N 2 O, and HCHO were systematically evaluated. All four pollutants exhibited pronounced emission peaks during regeneration, substantially exceeding those observed during non-regeneration driving. Emissions during regeneration accounted for 37%, 66%, 71%, and 78% of the total test emissions of NO, NO 2 , N 2 O, and HCHO, respectively. Elevated HCHO and nitrogenous compound emissions showed strong correlations with DPF inlet temperature during the heating and cooling phases. Assuming a 500-km regeneration interval, regeneration was estimated to occur over only 4.66%-5.99% of the vehicle's useful-life mileage, with scenario-based lifetime contributions reaching up to 38.36% and 25.76% of lifetime HCHO and NO 2 emissions, respectively. These findings highlight that regeneration-related emissions can represent a substantial fraction of gaseous emissions for our tested vehicle, underscoring the importance of further considering such events in emission characterization and inventory development.

title: Eco-genotoxicity assessment of carbamazepine, diclofenac, fluoxetine and propranolol in the marine crustacean Artemia franciscana: A multi-endpoint approach
abstract: This study evaluates the eco-genotoxic effects of four widely detected pharmaceuticals, carbamazepine (CBZ), diclofenac (DCF), fluoxetine (FLX), and propranolol (PRP), in the marine crustacean Artemia franciscana, a non-target marine organism. Acute toxicity was assessed throught mortality, immobility and swimming behavioural alteration showing no significant effects at concentrations up to 10 mg/L. Genotoxicity, oxidative stress, and neurotoxicity were subsequently investigated as sublethal responses. DNA damage was induced by FLX, PRP, and DCF at 0.001 mg/L, whereas CBZ required 0.010 mg/L to produce significant effects. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) production was significant starting from 1 mg/L for CBZ, 0.01 mg/L for DCF and PRP, while FLX induced ROS already at lower concentrations (0.001 mg/L). Neurotoxicity, evaluated through acetylcholinesterase activity, emerged at 10 mg/L for CBZ, FLX, and PRP. Based on the concentrations inducing significant DNA damage, a preliminary exploration of environmental risk using genotoxicity endpoints revealed DCF and PRP as compounds of potential concern, followed by FLX and CBZ. Overall, the findings suggest that standard acute endpoints may underestimate early sublethal biological effects and highlight the potential value of genotoxicity endpoints for risk characterization of pharmaceuticals in aquatic organisms.

title: Design and fabrication of boric acid functionalized covalent organic framework with sea urchin-like structure and its application for efficient enrichment of bisphenols
abstract: The morphology and functional groups of materials have equally important effects on their properties. In this paper, a boric acid functionalized covalent organic framework with sea urchin-like structure (SU-COF-V-B(OH) 2, where V denotes the vinyl groups derived from 2,5-divinylterephthalaldehyde) was prepared as a solid phase extraction (SPE) sorbent for bisphenols (BPs). The unique morphology provided enhanced analyte capacity, delivering 1.15-1.49 times higher enrichment than the solid spherical material. The prepared sorbent showed high removal performance (536.77 ± 37.04-833.69 ± 47.52 mg g -1 ). Binding energy calculations revealed the relative adsorption affinity of BPs at different sites, and together with Hirshfeld surface analysis and 2D fingerprint plots, the atomic-level interaction contributions between SU-COF-V-B(OH) 2 and BPs were further elucidated. Moreover, a new detection method was established by SPE-high-performance liquid chromatography-diode array basing on SU-COF-V-B(OH) 2 , and exhibited the wide linear range (0.10-200 ng mL -1 ) and low detection limits (0.02-0.04 ng mL -1 ). The established method had been successfully used for detection of BPs in tap water and milk samples with satisfactory recoveries (80.1-111.8%). The material showed potential for pollutant removal and enrichment detection, with broader applications of sea urchin-like COFs expected in the future.

title: Comparative assessment of the behaviour and potential ecological risks of pretilachlor and its metabolites in contrasting soil environments
abstract: A comparative evaluation of degradation behaviour and possible ecological risks associated with pretilachlor and its metabolites was conducted. Five metabolites (M1-M5) were synthesized and characterized. Pretilachlor and the metabolites were applied at 0.25 and 0.50 µg/g in different soils. Despite having shorter half-lives (t 1/2 = 1.18.1 days) than pretilachlor (t 1/2 = 5.313.7 days), metabolites residues persisted in soil from 3 to 45 days. Based on the conservative and first-tier screening of measured soil residues, some compounds showed risk quotients, RQ > 1 for earthworms, fish and honeybees; whereas the RQ for algae, birds and rats ranged from moderate to negligible. M2 and M3 reduced soil dehydrogenase activity by 1.11.5 times, while pretilachlor and remaining metabolites enhanced it. M2 and M3 bound strongly to the catalytic site of the dehydrogenase near Zn 2 + ion with docking scores of -5.45 and -5.22 kcal/mol, respectively. The overall stability of the docked complexes was also established through 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. The root mean square deviation (RMSD) and root mean fluctuations (RMSF) remained within the acceptable limits (less than 2.5 Å), indicating stable protein-ligand interactions. In summary, pretilachlor metabolites may persist in the environment with potential risk implications to different non-target species.

title: Interactive effects of tyre wear particles and oxytetracycline on a marine polychaete-sediment ecosystem
abstract: Tyre wear particles (TWPs) and antibiotics are co-occurring contaminants in coastal sediments, yet their combined effects on polychaete-associated sediment processes remain under reported. This study provides new evidence on the joint effects of TWPs and oxytetracycline (OTC) on a polychaete-sediment ecosystem. Polychaete-sediment systems were exposed to TWPs (1% of sediment dry weight), OTC (2.0 mg·L -1 ), and their combined treatment for 16 days. In polychaete-containing sediments, OTC-TWP co-exposure was associated with higher OM (1.74%) relative to the polychaete group, consistent with a reduced sediment-reworking effect. Co-exposure also altered inorganic nitrogen profiles and increased alkaline phosphatase activity to 184.37 nmol·g -1 . Microbial analysis showed that OTC-TWP co-exposure was associated with lower Chao1 and ACE indices, and Desulfobacterota showed a higher relative abundance in TWP groups. OTC and TWP co-exposure triggered oxidative stress and physiological alterations in P. aibuhitensis, reflected by increased MDA levels and changes in antioxidant responses. Moreover, exposure to these pollutants resulted in the suppression of AChE and LZM activities. Given the global occurrence of TWPs and antibiotics in coastal environments, this study provides insights into the ecological risks of emerging contaminant mixtures and highlights the need to incorporate particle-antibiotic co-pollution into sediment risk assessment.

title: Coal gasification fine slag activates dual oxidants for PFOA degradation: Synergy of reactive species and C-F cleavage mechanisms
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is highly recalcitrant, necessitating degradation strategies that go beyond phase-transfer adsorption. Here, we constructed a synergistic "waste-treating-waste" system that uses coal gasification fine slag (CGFS) to dually activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and H 2 O 2 . Under optimal conditions, the CGFS/PMS/H 2 O 2 system removed 75.34% of PFOA within 4 h via radical (SO 4 •- and O 2 •- ) and non-radical ( 1 O 2 and electron transfer) pathways. Combining LC-MS and DFT calculations, we identified the electron-rich carboxyl terminus of PFOA as the primary nucleophilic site for single-electron oxidation. DFT calculations revealed that SO 4 •- -driven Kolbe decarboxylation was barrierless and exergonic, whereas O 2 •- -mediated decarboxylation (+3.49 eV) and direct C-F bond cleavage (>3.0 eV) were endothermic in the homogeneous phase. Nevertheless, LC-MS confirmed that all three pathways operated concurrently, which we attributed to the heterogeneous CGFS interface. Localized O 2 •- pools and substrate pre-polarization lower activation energies, unlocking theoretically constrained routes. The CGFS/PMS/H 2 O 2 system effectively removed C6-C10 perfluorocarboxylic acids from real water samples, reducing toxicity and improving biodegradability after treatment. This study provides in-depth mechanistic insight and a practical, environmentally friendly approach for PFOA remediation.

title: Enhanced electro-peroxone degradation of fluoroquinolones using quinone-enriched carbon cathodes via kinetic suppression of O–O bond cleavage
abstract: The electro-peroxone (EP) process is a promising advanced water treatment technology that couples in situ H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis with ozone activation. However, its efficiency is severely limited by low two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e - -ORR) selectivity and poor three-phase mass transfer. Here, we address these bottlenecks by integrating a quinone-enriched carbon cathode with tailored interfacial microenvironment into a flow-through EP reactor. The quinone functionalities kinetically suppress O-O bond cleavage instead of merely tuning *OOH adsorption, thus steering ORR toward selective H 2 O 2 production. Meanwhile, these groups facilitate rapid H 2 O 2 desorption, achieving a high yield of 96.6 mmol g -1 h -1 . The optimized EP system enables fast kinetics and highly efficient degradation of multiple fluoroquinolone antibiotics (3.86 min -1 ), far outperforming standalone ozonation and electrolysis. Mechanistic investigations confirm that the boosted ·OH flux from the peroxone reaction drives deep oxidation of ozone-resistant intermediates. The system exhibits excellent matrix adaptability and reusability, and enables effective antibiotic removal, antibacterial activity reduction, and multidrug resistance gene mitigation in real aquaculture wastewater. This work demonstrates that interfacial microenvironment engineering provides a reliable and scalable strategy for boosting EP performance toward sustainable antibiotic pollution control.

title: Nanoscale magnesium oxide reduces the accumulation and toxicity of micro/nanoplastics by accelerating root lignification and alleviating endoplasmic reticulum stress
abstract: The risk to agricultural production and human health from micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) exposure cannot be ignored, making it imperative to find effective mitigation strategies. Nanoscale magnesium oxide (MgO·NP) has been widely demonstrated to enhance plant stress resistance by activating defense pathways. However, its ability to mitigate MNPs stress remains unexplored. A greenhouse soil culture experiment was conducted by co-adding five predominant soil MNPs (polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), polystyrene (PS), polypropylene (PP), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC)) at 1 g·kg⁻¹ each. After 30 days, pyrolysis gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) analysis of tomato leaves revealed a distinct absorption profile for MNPs: PET > PE > PS > PP > PVC. Soil amendment with 40 mg·kg⁻¹ MgO·NP significantly inhibited MNPs accumulation in tomatoes, reducing PET, PS, and PVC by 57.44%, 76.14%, and 31.82%, respectively. Multi-omics analyses revealed that MgO·NP upregulates phenylpropanoid biosynthesis genes (PAL, 4CL, CCR). This upregulation elevated lignin content by 26.7% and stimulated root lignification, a response that may be linked to the observed reduction in apoplastic uptake and transport of MNPs. Furthermore, MgO·NP was associated with changes in ERAD‑related gene expression and may have contributed to mitigating protein misfolding and organelle stress under MNPs exposure. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that exogenous application of 40 mg·kg⁻¹ MgO·NP significantly inhibits the accumulation and mitigates the toxicity of MNPs in tomato plants. These findings may offer a feasible strategy for alleviating the adverse impacts of MNPs contamination on agricultural production.

title: Water quality disruptions following an extreme flood: Microbial and geochemical responses to the 2024 DANA in a Mediterranean wetland
abstract: In late October 2024, an extreme Isolated Depression at High Levels (DANA) caused widespread flooding and the failure of wastewater treatment and sewerage systems across several municipalities in the Valencia region (Spain). Researchers from several Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) institutes conducted a six-month monitoring program in Albufera Natural Park and in the Poyo and Picassent gullies, which drain into the lagoon. Microbiological fecal indicators (Escherichia coli, somatic coliphages, and viral markers) showed an immediate and pronounced response to the flooding, indicating substantial inputs of untreated wastewater. Although most indicators gradually declined over subsequent months, several remained above pre-event levels, suggesting incomplete recovery and the persistence of contamination hotspots. Geochemical analyses revealed elevated concentrations of major and trace elements, marked increases in carbon and nitrogen fractions, and significant post-event enrichment of key anions in sediment samples. In water samples, variations in nutrient and anion concentrations were attenuated but clearly distinguishable, reflecting the combined influence of runoff and wastewater overflows. Multiple contamination indices were applied to evaluate changes in water and sediment quality. Differences among indices highlighted their relative nature and the critical role of reference values in interpretation. Integrative indices based on geometric means and relative toxicity (PLI and PERI) indicated moderate to low levels of current geochemical contamination. These findings demonstrate that the 2024 DANA caused significant and persistent microbiological and geochemical disturbances, underscoring the vulnerability of Mediterranean wetlands to extreme hydrometeorological events and the need for improved wastewater management and flood-resilient infrastructure under climate change.

title: Self-limiting stibnite weathering in suboxic humic sediments triggers Sb2O3-like-dominated passivation and decoupled genotoxic-phytotoxic damage in Elodea canadensis
abstract: Antimony (Sb) is a priority pollutant whose mobility and toxicity are linked to the environmental weathering of stibnite (Sb 2 S 3 ). This study combined a 10-week hydrochemical investigation (Sb T , SO 4 2- , pH, Redox) with surface (AFM, SEM, Raman, XPS, Zeta-potential (ζ)), electrochemical (EIS, CV, CA, Tafel plots), and ecotoxicological (genotoxicity, phytotoxicity) analyses to elucidate weathering mechanisms under suboxic humic sedimentary conditions. A critical Sb release pulse peaked at 2 weeks (∼60 μg·L -1 ), followed by progressive passivation. Raman and XPS confirmed the formation of an Sb 2 O 3 -dominated layer, while Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy showed charge-transfer resistance (R ct1 ) increasing from 782.8 to 20,069 Ω 2 . Negative surface charge (-33 to -53 mV) indicated that OH - (and SO 4 2- ) ions competitively occupied reactive surface sites, electrostatically repelling humic polyanions and confining Sb species to the solution. Ecotoxicological assays on Elodea canadensis (1-2000 mg·kg -1 Sb 2 S 3 ) revealed an asynchronous recovery phenomenon: while chlorophyll a exhibited physiological recovery after 21 days (3.05 μg·g⁻¹ at 50 mg·kg -1 ), comet assays demonstrated cumulative genotoxicity (35.66 ± 16.63-244.50 ± 5.92 A.U. at 2000 mg·kg -1 Sb 2 S 3 ). This decoupling proves that physiological recovery can mask persistent genomic damage, highlighting the limitations of single photosynthetic biomarkers for evaluating long-term ecological risks.

title: Seasonally structured diazotrophic communities and potential biological nitrogen fixation in a eutrophic urban lake replenished with reclaimed water
abstract: Reclaimed water recharge introduces nutrients and dissolved organic matter into urban lakes, sustaining enrichment under seasonal variability. Biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) is often assumed to be limited by long-term external nitrogen (N) enrichment and may therefore be underestimated in eutrophic systems. A year-long investigation was conducted in eutrophic Xi'an Lake. Total nitrogen (TN) remained high (1.09-7.53 mg L -1 ), yet acetylene reduction assay (ARA)-derived potential nitrogen fixation rates (NFRs) reached 2.65-4.36 nmol N L -1 h -1 in summer, whereas winter values ranged from below detection to 1.5 nmol N L -1 h -1 . Correlation and random forest analyses indicated that NFR variation was associated with C/N stoichiometry (the TOC/TN molar ratio), water temperature, and dissolved oxygen. Lomb-Scargle analysis identified seasonally recurrent nifH-bearing OTUs, indicating temporal structuring of the potential diazotrophic community. Null model analysis implicated Proteobacteria in multiple community assembly processes, suggesting their involvement in structuring the potential diazotrophic community. Alga-diazotroph co-cultures under a TN gradient (0, 1, 3, and 5 mg L -1 ) exhibited higher C/N stoichiometry, potential NFRs, and nifH gene abundance than monocultures. These findings suggest that BNF may be an underestimated internal N process in eutrophic lakes receiving reclaimed water and highlight algae-diazotroph associations in seasonal N cycling and eutrophication.

title: Multi-functional poly(fluorinated-aniline) nanofibrous mat for highly efficient remediation of PFAS in water through synergistic chemical and physical adsorption
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are carcinogenic and environmentally persistent contaminants, necessitating efficient removal to protect environmental and human health. Although numerous adsorbents have been fabricated, there remains strong demand for materials that are facile-to-synthesize, highly efficient, and practically viable. Here, we present a surface-localized growth strategy to functionalize electrospun nanofibers with poly(fluorinated-aniline) moieties, yielding poly (fluorinated-aniline) nanofibrous mat (PFA NFM). Unlike previous adsorbents, PFA NFM achieves dual-functionalization via a single-step reaction. This tailored synergy endows PFA NFM with high PFAS uptake capacities in both static/dynamic adsorption scenarios. Compared to the polyaniline counterpart (PA NFM), PFA NFM showcases significantly accelerated adsorption kinetics (11-52 times faster) and outstanding anti-interference performance. Its interfacially derived mesoporous structure further promotes physical adsorption and affords an exceptionally high PFAS uptake capacity. Multiple mechanisms were confirmed via FT-IR, XPS, solid-state ¹ ⁹F NMR, and DFT calculations. Notably, PFA NFM enables efficient removal of both long‑ and short‑chain PFAS across diverse environmental water matrices over a broad concentration range, indicating its applicability to both point- and non-point-source PFAS-polluted water samples. Additionally, the monolithic PFA NFM retains superior removal efficiency even after 10 regeneration cycles in multiple PFAS-spiked environmental water. Its robust recyclability and reusability render PFA NFM practically valuable.

title: Contrasting cross-media distributions of parent neonicotinoids and their transformation products in paired farmland–fishpond systems
abstract: Small fishponds embedded within rural farmland are directly affected by surrounding agricultural activities and may therefore serve as important interfaces for the input, transformation, and redistribution of pesticides. However, the occurrence, transformation-product patterns, and cross-media distribution of parent neonicotinoid insecticides (pNNIs) and their transformation products (TPNNIs) among environmental media in farmland-fishpond systems (FFS) remain poorly understood. In this study, pNNIs and TPNNIs were simultaneously analyzed in farmland soil, fishpond water, and sediment collected from FFS. Results showed that both pNNIs and TPNNIs were detected in all three media. The median concentrations of pNNIs were 66.9 ng/L in fishpond water, 46.2 ng/g in farmland soil, and 0.6 ng/g in sediment, while the corresponding concentrations of TPNNIs were 44.2 ng/L, 2.4 ng/g, and 0.3 ng/g, respectively. The compositional profiles of pNNIs were broadly similar among the three media and were dominated by clothianidin, thiamethoxam, and imidacloprid, whereas the compositional profiles of TPNNIs and TPNNIs/pNNIs ratios differed markedly among media. Environmental factors, including pH and total organic carbon, were significantly associated with residue levels of pNNIs and TPNNIs, relationships between pNNIs and their TPNNIs, and partitioning among media. Ecological risk screening indicated that clothianidin may pose risks to non-target organisms in both soil and water, while imidacloprid may also pose risks in water at some sites.

title: Photodegradation of triclosan in SiO2-water heterogeneous systems: Mechanisms coupled with adsorption effects
abstract: Triclosan (TCS) is a hydrophobic and endocrine-disrupting contaminant that poses significant ecological risks. Suspended particulate matter (SPM) is ubiquitous in natural waters and can simultaneously influence both photolysis and adsorption of TCS. However, the mechanistic understanding of this dual modulation remains limited. In this study, we systematically investigated the phototransformation of TCS in SiO 2 -water heterogeneous systems. Results demonstrated that SiO 2 particles generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) under irradiation, leading to accelerated photodegradation kinetics and an enhanced contribution of indirect photolysis. Adsorbed TCS exhibited slower degradation kinetics and markedly reduced pH sensitivity relative to dissolved TCS, suggesting that the adsorbed species existed in a form distinct from the ionized aqueous species. Dissolved organic matter (DOM) influenced TCS photolysis via light shielding, ROS quenching, and enhanced adsorption onto SiO 2 ; however, the effect of DOM was attenuated in the heterogeneous system, likely due to the increased dominance of ROS-mediated indirect photolysis, which diminished the relative importance of DOM's light-shielding effect. Notably, the solid-phase yield of 2,8-dichlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (2,8-DCDD) was lower than its aqueous-phase yield, confirming the modulating effect of SiO 2 on dioxin formation. Collectively, these findings suggested that SPM and its adsorptive interactions critically regulate TCS persistence, byproduct production, and phase-dependent transport.

title: Enhanced Fenton-like degradation over defect-rich bimetallic catalysts: Interfacial electron transfer triggered by coupled FeMn dual-atom–nanocluster sites
abstract: Controllable synthesis of dual-atom-nanocluster (DA-NC) coupled structures offers a new strategy to construct effective catalytic sites and enhance degradation performance in Fenton-like catalysts. In this work, the heteronuclear FeMn DA-NC was fine constructed in a defect-rich Fe/Mn co-doped biochar matrix (Fe/Mn-NABC). Accordingly, Fe/Mn-NABC can effectively activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) to degrade persistent organic pollutants and generate abundant non-radical species, thereby achieving superior selective degradation (97.9%) with a rate constant of 0.264 min -1 , 1.8 times higher than that of Fe monometallic system (Fe-N-C). Electrochemical measurements and DFT calculations reveal that FeMn DA-NC generated via introducing Mn species into Fe-N-C facilitates the interfacial reaction of PMS on the catalyst surface. The electronic modulation shifts the Fe d-band center upward, promotes PMS adsorption, and decreases the reaction energy barrier of PMS activation (1.53→1.11 eV). Furthermore, this system exhibits excellent long-term stability (nearly 100% over 100 h) and prominent economic advantages ($ 0.22/m 3 ). This research offers insights into developing stable Fe-based bimetallic catalysts, revealing the role of structural defect in non-radical catalysis, and optimizing high-efficiency water purification systems.

title: Chlorine-bromine coexistence redirects hazardous dioxin formation from phenolic precursors under post-combustion conditions
abstract: Chlorine and bromine coexist in industrial thermal processes and can alter the formation of hazardous halogenated dioxins. This study investigated the formation of chlorinated, brominated and mixed-halogenated dioxins from phenolic and naphtholic precursors under different Cl/Br molar ratios. Tube furnace experiments, in situ electron paramagnetic resonance and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were combined to evaluate the effects of halogen identity, precursor structure and radical-mediated reactions. In single-halogen systems, polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins/dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) were formed in higher yields and dominated by highly chlorinated congeners. In contrast, polybrominated dibenzo-p-dioxins/dibenzofurans (PBDD/Fs) favored lower-brominated products, reflecting stronger steric constraints and less favorable bromination. In mixed systems, brominated precursors suppressed PCDD/Fs formation, whereas chlorinated precursors promoted selected PBDD/Fs congeners and mixed-halogenated dioxins (PXDD/Fs). Br2Cl2-DD was the dominant PXDD congener group, indicating that cross-coupling between chlorinated and brominated precursor-derived radicals contributes to mixed-halogenated product formation. DFT calculations supported the greater thermodynamic favorability of chlorination over bromination and the feasibility of radical-coupling pathways, although product selectivity should be interpreted together with precursor availability, radical abundance and kinetic constraints. These findings show that Cl-Br coexistence redirects hazardous dioxin formation and highlights the need to include PBDD/Fs and PXDD/Fs in risk assessment and control strategies for mixed-halogen thermal processes.

title: Molecularly imprinted polymer/boronic acid carbon dots/bismuth vanadate-cofunctionalized Janus particles for the integrated function of adsorption-degradation-detection of tetracycline
abstract: To mitigate water pollution, current approaches include removal, degradation, and monitoring. Tetracycline (TC) poses resistance and health risks, so material integrating adsorption, detection, and degradation is needed. In this study, Janus particles with asymmetric structure were used as carriers to achieve multi-functional partition modification. Janus particles, with epoxy groups on one side and halogen groups on the other side, were prepared by our proposed photo-initiated seed swelling polymerization. Based on the chemical structure of TC, on the rough halogen surface, the high-density TC-imprinted polymer (TMIP) was formed by SI-ATRP for specific recognition. On the smooth epoxy surface, boric acid functionalized carbon dot (CD) was grafted by epoxy-ammonia reaction to achieve sensitive fluorescence detection. Finally, a visible-light-responsive bismuth vanadate (BVO) photocatalytic layer was grown in situ on the surface of Janus particles by the hydrothermal method, endowing the Janus with photocatalytic degradation performance. With an adsorption capacity of 148.6 mg g⁻¹ , 97.5% degradation in 90 min (83.9% after 5 cycles), and a detection limit of 1.99 μg L⁻¹ over 0-45 μg L⁻¹ , the TMIP/CD/BVO@Janus effectively achieves sensitive detection, selective adsorption, and efficient degradation for TC in real water, with no side effects by LC-MS/MS, providing a new strategy for develop multi-function material for antibiotic pollution treatment.

title: Nitrogen cycling regulates arsenic mobilization in alluvial-lacustrine aquifer systems: DOM molecular signatures and thermodynamic constraints
abstract: High arsenic (As) groundwater commonly co-occurs with elevated ammonium (NH 4 + ) in aquifers worldwide. However, the underlying nitrogen cycling processes regulating As mobilization in groundwater remain elusive. Here, hydrochemistry, stable isotopes, FT-ICR MS, and thermodynamic modelling were integrated to investigate the NH 4 + production pathways and their impacts on As mobility within the alluvial-lacustrine aquifer. Hydrochemical and isotopic data indicated that groundwater NH 4 + was primarily produced through OM mineralization and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), and both processes contributed to As enrichment which reached up to 1603 μg/L. FT-ICR MS analysis revealed that OM mineralization depleted CHON2 and highly unsaturated compounds, while DNRA preferentially consumed labile aliphatic compounds. Thermodynamic potential factors (F T ) further evidenced that OM mineralization faced thermodynamic constraints (0.26 T T > 0.97). Notably, thermodynamically favorable organic compounds such as highly unsaturated compounds and N-containing OM could promote OM mineralization, during which NH 4 + is produced and the reductive dissolution of Fe(III) oxides is simultaneously facilitated, thereby releasing As into groundwater. These findings could provide novel insights into the role of coupled C-N-Fe cycling in As mobilization within alluvial-lacustrine aquifer systems.

title: An assessment of the annual effective dose rate due to radon inhalation from Phosphogypsum stacks in the SW of Spain
Micro-nanobubbles as interface regulators to enhance electron transfer on mackinawite for promoting natural attenuation
abstract: Naphthalene (NAP), a representative polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), is a hazardous groundwater contaminant because of its persistence, toxicity, and potential carcinogenicity. Although naturally occurring mackinawite (FeS) contributes to pollutant attenuation through reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation during oxygen perturbation, its reactivity is limited by inefficient interfacial electron transfer. Here, micro-nanobubbles (MNBs) were introduced as a chemical-free interfacial regulation strategy to activate FeS, significantly enhancing hydroxyl radical (•OH) production and NAP degradation. Results revealed that the strong interfacial electric field of MNBs could regulate the FeS interface and generate Fe(II) active sites, leading to approximately 7.4-fold and 1.5-fold increases in the electron utilization efficiency of ion-exchangeable and structural Fe(II), respectively. Meanwhile, MNBs accelerated the initial oxidation of S(-II) in the early reaction stage, thereby preventing prolonged competition with Fe(II) for O 2 and ultimately improving Fe(II) utilization efficiency and •OH production. Furthermore, DFT calculations and ECOSAR toxicity predictions indicated that the MNB-mediated pathway drove NAP toward more reactive intermediates, reducing the risk of toxicity amplification and enhancing mineralization. Overall, this study demonstrates that MNBs effectively unlock the natural attenuation potential of FeS, providing a clean and sustainable strategy for in-situ groundwater remediation.

title: Legacy mercury emissions and vegetation-mediated Hg cycling in the world's largest Hg mining district
abstract: The Almadén district (Spain), the world's largest historical mercury (Hg) mining area, remains a major legacy source of atmospheric Hg driven by soil re-emissions and nocturnal boundary layer stability. This study evaluates the role of Stone pine (Pinus pinea L.) as both a biomonitor and an active interface in the Hg cycle by integrating spatial modelling, mobile total gaseous mercury (TGM) measurements, and pyrolytic speciation across soil, and bark matrices in managed and unmanaged environments. A strong spatial coupling (ρ = 0.69, p < 0.01) was identified between nocturnal atmospheric TGM concentrations and the spatial distribution of soil Hg. Under these conditions, Hg⁰ is likely taken up by vegetation through combined cuticular and residual stomatal pathways. Once internalized, the pyrolytic signatures are compatible with the transformation of Hg⁰ into more stable Hg species, including Hg-OM and β-HgS. Our results suggest that P. pinea may function as an active biogeochemical interface, potentially promoting Hg transformation, contributing to Hg stabilization. These results highlight vegetation as a potential key driver of Hg transformation and attenuation in legacy mining environments and identify urban biomass management as a possible, previously overlooked control on Hg cycling.

title: In situ measurement of thallium in acid mine drainage-impacted waters using the diffusive gradients in thin-films technique embedded with a copper(II) ferrocyanide functionalized mesoporous silica gel layer
abstract: Thallium (Tl) contamination in groundwater and surface water poses serious ecological and human health risks. This study developed a diffusive gradients in thin-films (DGT) technique using a copper(II) ferrocyanide-functionalized mesoporous silica (CFC-SBA) binding gel for in situ measurement of DGT-labile Tl in acid mine drainage (AMD)-impacted waters. The CFC-SBA gel achieved near-quantitative elution with 5 mol L -1 HNO 3 and had a binding capacity of 48.2 μg cm -2 . Diffusion coefficients in agarose gel at 25 °C were 15.30 × 10 -6 cm 2 s -1 for Tl(I) and 8.01 × 10 -6 cm 2 s -1 for Tl(III). Laboratory tests supported Tl(I) measurement across pH 2-12 and Tl(III) measurement across pH 2-7. Performance was independent of ionic strength (1.0-500 mmol L -1 NaNO 3 ), and dissolved organic matter (0-30 mg L -1 humic acid). Method detection limits were 2.2 ng L -1 for Tl(I) and 3.2 ng L -1 for Tl(III), and the gel remained stable after 240 days of controlled storage. The method was further validated in quiescent solutions mimicking groundwater conditions. Field deployments at five AMD-impacted sites (24-72 h) demonstrated the feasibility of measuring DGT-labile Tl. Relative to TP-DGT, CFC-SBA-DGT showed an advantage under the strongly acidic and high-ionic-strength conditions tested, but the comparison does not demonstrate universal analytical superiority.

title: Environmental aging alters the toxicity profiles of nanoplastics and generates biologically active soluble products
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) health risks are widely recognized, yet assessments largely regard particles as the principal toxic entity and overlook soluble aging products generated during environmental exposure. Here, we examine how environmental aging alters NP toxicity profiles and generates biologically active soluble products. Polystyrene (PS) and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) NPs were subjected to long-term (365 days) solar-relevant UV aging (315-400 nm) to provide an environmentally realistic framework for evaluating transformation-driven effects. By physically separating aged particles from low-molecular-weight aging products, we found that aging attenuated particle-associated toxicity while generating products that retained substantial biological activity. Integrated histological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses of blood, gut, liver, and brain revealed distinct patterns of tissue injury and metabolic disruption across aged particle and aging product exposures. Aged particles induced fewer and weaker hepatic transcriptional changes than pristine particles, whereas soluble fractions mainly affected circulating metabolism, with 70 and 30 differential serum metabolites for PMMA and PS, respectively. Multi-omics integration and targeted manipulation of gut bacteria linked both components to microbiome-dependent modulation of host metabolism. Environmental aging therefore altered NP toxicity profiles and generated biologically active soluble fractions, highlighting the importance of evaluating residual particles and soluble aging-associated fractions separately.

title: Quantitative source apportionment of soil heavy metals on a regional scale: Integrating input inventory, dual-isotope analysis and spatial decomposition modeling
abstract: Quantifying the sources of soil heavy metal (HM) contaminants in mining-affected agricultural land is vital for effective pollution control and preventing food security issues. However, over large-scale agricultural regions, geogenic inputs, diffuse agricultural pollution (e.g., from fertilisation and irrigation), and discrete industrial sources often overlap spatially, making them difficult to resolve with conventional receptor models such as Positive Matrix Factorisation (PMF). Here, we develop a Spatial Frequency Decomposition (SFD) model that integrates a multi-pathway agricultural flux inventory with HM spatial distribution and validate it using an independent isotope mixing model. Applying the SFD model to a representative agricultural region with a long history of metal mining, we find that Cd inputs are characterised by multiple pathways, whereas Pb loading is predominantly derived from irrigation-borne fluvial sediments. We also note that proximity to river channels amplifies Cd accumulation levels, suggesting large-magnitude inputs associated with historic episodic flood deposition or rainfall-driven surface runoff. The model further identifies industrial point-source clusters for Cd and Pb contamination that spatially coincide with known mining and smelting activities. Arsenic (As) contamination yielded no significant point-source anomalies, consistent with a predominantly diffuse component. Cross-validation confirmed that SFD-derived industrial fractions closely matched isotope benchmarks, whereas the conventional PMF model systematically overestimated the industrial fraction, conflating geogenic enrichment with direct emissions. Our SFD framework provides a spatially explicit method to complement existing source apportionment tools, enabling quantification of HM flux and detection of potential point sources, thus supporting more precise and spatially differentiated sustainable land management strategies.

title: Geochemical controls on the fate and mobility of coal combustion product-derived elements in a dolomitic aquifer
abstract: Coal combustion products (CCPs) can release elements of concern into groundwater, posing risks to drinking water and ecosystems, yet their behavior in carbonate aquifers remains poorly understood. This study investigated the fate and mobility of seven elements (As, B, Cd, Cu, Cr, Mo, Ni) at a CCP disposal site overlying a dolomitic aquifer in the southeastern United States. CCP-impacted wells showed Ca-Mg-SO4 type waters with elevated sulfate concentrations (460-635 mg/L) compared to background Ca-Mg-HCO3 waters. Boron (0.13-4.5 mg/L) and Mo (0.10-2.9 mg/L) were the most mobile elements and exceeded groundwater protection standards. Sequential extraction showed that ~76% of leachable Mo was associated with water-soluble and amorphous oxide fractions, indicating weak sorption. In contrast As, Cd, Cr, Cu, and Ni were predominantly associated with aquifer solids and occurred as low dissolved concentrations. Geochemical speciation models predicted HAsO42-, B(OH)3, and MoO42- as the dominant aqueous species under the site’s alkaline and oxidizing conditions. However, SEM-EDS identified As-Ca-Mg-O associations and sequential extraction showed that ~95% of the leachable As was associated with carbonate-dominated fractions, indicating that As attenuation occurs through adsorption and/or structural incorporation onto carbonate minerals, rather than Fe-oxide attenuation pathways. Chromium was predominantly associated with resistant residual fractions, consistent with precipitation/co-precipitation of Cr(III) oxide or spinel phases. Cadmium, Cu, and Ni showed no plume enrichment and were interpreted as predominantly geogenic. Overall, the empirical and modeling results suggest B and Mo are the major CCP-derived hazards in this carbonate aquifer, whereas As is likely immobilized by carbonate adsorption and/or structural incorporation.

title: Reductive dechlorination resilience to oxygen intrusion: dehalogenase-dependent differential recovery and community-mediated redox homeostasis
abstract: Oxygen intrusion in chlorinated solvent-contaminated aquifers frequently compromises organohalide-respiring bacteria (OHRB)-driven in-situ bioremediation. This study examined the dechlorination dynamics of a tetrachloroethene (PCE)-respiring consortium for 72 days after exposure to 0-4 mg/L dissolved oxygen (DO). Although DO fell below 0.2 mg/L within 36 h, recovery differed among dechlorination steps. At an initial DO of 4 mg/L, PCE-to-dichloroethene (DCE) dechlorination was retained at up to 3.8 μmol Cl - ·L -1 ·d -1 , whereas vinyl chloride (VC) detoxification ceased above 2 mg/L. By day 72, the 4 mg/L treatment contained 39.6% DCE and 9.4% VC, with less than 1% of the supplied PCE dechlorinated to ethene. Integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses attributed this differential resilience to functional redundancy among diverse PceA-carrying OHRB (Dehalobacter, Dehalococcoides, and other taxa) for upstream steps, versus the confinement of vcrA to a single oxygen-sensitive Dehalococcoides population, whose depletion coincided with delayed VC-to-ethene recovery. Facultative aerobes, particularly Pseudomonas, rapidly depleted O 2 through aerobic respiration. These findings identify the terminal VC-to-ethene step as the most vulnerable link in PCE attenuation. Oxygen intrusion therefore shifts attenuation end products from ethene towards the more mobile DCE and VC, prolonging contaminant persistence at oxygen-disturbed sites.

title: Thallium retention in sulfide-rich mine wastes associated with jarosite formation
abstract: Thallium (Tl) is an emerging contaminant of concern in mining-impacted environments because of its high toxicity and mobility, yet the mineralogical processes controlling its retention during mine-waste weathering remain poorly constrained. The sulfide-rich mine wastes investigated here contain up to 200 mg kg -1 Tl and abundant secondary jarosite-group minerals. We combined synchrotron-based µXRF, µXRD, and Tl L 3 -edge XANES analyses to determine Tl distribution, speciation, and mode of occurrence. Elemental mapping shows that Tl is concentrated in discrete particles (∼70-110 µm) rather than being diffusely distributed throughout the mine waste. Tl L 3 -edge XANES analyses indicate that Tl occurs predominantly as Tl(I) (95-100% according to LCF results), with no detectable contributions from Tl(III) species. Linear combination fitting and cluster-based analysis, supported by µXRF and µXRD data, reveals systematic compositional zoning from Tl-rich jarosite cores toward Tl-poorer jarosite rims. Lattice expansion observed by µXRD, together with the spatial association of Tl with As, Se, and Ni, is consistent with possible trace-element co-hosting and/or structural incorporation within Tl-bearing jarosite particles. Overall, our results demonstrate that Tl is retained predominantly through structural incorporation into jarosite-type minerals and highlight the importance of these phases as secondary Tl hosts in sulfide-rich mine wastes.

title: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and metabolic transformation of Flonicamid in rats: Insights from radiotracing, metabolite profiling and multi-scale analysis
abstract: Understanding flonicamid (FLO) disposition is important for interpreting its potential health implications. We investigated FLO metabolism in male Sprague-Dawley rats using 14 C-radiotracing, high-resolution mass spectrometry, hepatic transcriptomics, density-functional-theory calculations, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. FLO was rapidly absorbed, widely distributed, and detected in the brain and testes. Parent FLO predominated in the radiochromatographic profiles, accounting for 70.3% of the total integrated radioactive peak area. TFNA-AM was the predominant metabolite, representing 72.3% of the total metabolite peak area. Its formation was consistent with cyanomethyl oxidative cleavage and computational predictions of molecular reactivity. Within 192 h, urinary recovery accounted for 84.1% of administered radioactivity, indicating predominantly urinary elimination. Integrated transcriptomic and molecular-simulation analyses further prioritized CYP2B2 as a candidate enzyme for subsequent biochemical evaluation of its potential role in the oxidative metabolism of FLO. FLO exposure was also associated with transcriptional changes in several hormone-related pathways in male rat liver. Collectively, these findings complement existing FLO studies by quantifying the recovery of FLO-derived material across excretion routes and the contributions of parent FLO and major metabolites to the recovered components. This information supports the interpretation of FLO disposition and the selection of analyses for subsequent exposure and toxicological studies.

title: Co-expression of alnA and bphC in alfalfa enhances PCB phytoremediation by coupling bioavailability modulation and intracellular detoxification
abstract: Phytoremediation of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)-contaminated soils is hindered by low PCB bioavailability and insufficient plant detoxification. Here, we engineered transgenic alfalfa co-expressing alnA (encoding an emulsifying protein) and bphC (encoding a ring-cleavage dioxygenase) to address these barriers. Five representative congeners spanning a range of chlorination degrees were selected to evaluate the system's efficacy. The transgenic AB lines achieved sustained rhizosecretion of AlnA, enhancing PCB solubility by 2.0- to 3.2-fold relative to wild-type (WT) plants. While enhanced bioavailability typically exacerbates phytotoxicity, endogenous BphC cleaved the biphenyl ring, preventing toxic intermediate accumulation. This extracellular solubilization-intracellular detoxification synergy enabled AB alfalfa to maintain improved growth under PCB stress, increasing root accumulation by 3.7-fold and overall removal by 2-fold compared to WT alfalfa. Metagenomic and structural equation modeling revealed that while microbial genes act as "proximate executors" directly degrading PCBs, the transgenic plant functions as the "primary driver". The AB lines enriched specific degraders (Pseudomonas and certain genera within the order Burkholderiales) and assembled a functional network for aerobic PCB degradation. This integrated plant-microbiome system offers a low-maintenance strategy for in situ remediation of PCB-contaminated sites.

title: Sustainable electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination of chlorinated aromatic acids in groundwater-saturated porous media using an optimized Ru-TiO2 cathode
abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination (ECH) offers a reagent-free approach for groundwater remediation, but its application in porous media is constrained by uncertain reaction pathways and transport limitations. Here, a low-loading Ru-TiO 2 cathode was developed for the removal of 2,4-dichlorobenzoic acid (2,4-DCBA) under batch and flow-through conditions. The cathode achieved 98% removal with a k obs of 0.0160 min -1 . Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, product, and computational results indicate that interfacial electron transfer and adsorbed-hydrogen-mediated processes may coexist during C-Cl cleavage, while surface hydrogen also participates in subsequent hydrogenation. In porous media, 2,4-DCBA removal reached 85-87% over 16 h. Moderate flow improved transport reaction matching, whereas further acceleration produced diminishing kinetic gains because of shortened residence time. Treatment reduced phytotoxicity. One factor TEA/LCA sensitivity analyses identified electricity price, current utilization, grid carbon intensity, and electrolyte management as the principal scale-up variables. These results demonstrate the potential of Ru-TiO 2 catalyzed ECH for groundwater remediation.

title: Cadmium–tetracycline complexation enhances interfacial reactivity on Fe0@γ-Fe2O3/carbon for coupled contaminant removal
abstract: The coexistence of heavy metals and antibiotics in water poses unique remediation challenges, because their interactions can alter adsorption and redox reactivity. Here, resorcinol-formaldehyde carbon sphere-supported Fe 0 @γ-Fe 2 O 3 nanoclusters (RFCS-Fe 0 @γ-Fe 2 O 3 ) were employed to elucidate the interactions between cadmium (Cd) and tetracycline (TC). Binary-system experiments further revealed that concentration, pH, and addition sequence regulated the competitive and synergistic interactions. Quantum chemical calculations revealed that Cd-TC complexation narrowed the frontier orbital gap of TC and strengthened its interaction with Fe 0 @γ-Fe 2 O 3 . The adsorption energy of Cd-TC complex was -3.92 eV, compared with -2.79 eV for Cd(II) and -2.92 eV for TC, indicating a stronger affinity of the complex for the reactive interface. Multimodal characterization indicated the synergy of surface hydroxyls and oxygen vacancies (O V ) in Fe 0 @γ-Fe 2 O 3 clusters: hydroxyl-rich iron sites favored Cd(II) coordination, whereas O V facilitated electron transfer and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation for TC oxidation. Moreover, effective treatment performance was maintained over a broad pH rang, in the presence of competing ions, natural organic matter, in real water samples, and over repeated reuse cycles. These findings suggest that the Cd-TC complexation enhances interfacial reactivity and provides a mechanistic basis for designing defect-rich iron-carbon interfaces for co-contaminant remediation.

title: Effects of dry–wet alternation patterns on PFAS fate in sediments amended with microplastics
abstract: The accumulation of PFASs in sediments is influenced by both dry-wet alternation (ADW) patterns and microplastic (MP) pollution, yet their combined effects on PFAS fate in water-sediment systems remain unclear. In this study, we investigated PFAS accumulation in sediments under three ADW patterns (1ADW, 2ADW, 3ADW) and continuous submergence (CS), combined with or without polypropylene (PP) MPs (1% w/w). The results showed that, relative to CS, ADW generally inhibited the accumulation of PFOA & substitutes, whereas its effect on PFOS & substitutes was pattern-dependent, with 3ADW even showing elevated accumulation. For individual compounds, HFPO-TA and PFHxS varied most across ADW treatments; Gen-X and PFBS least. MPs presence altered this trend: MPs promoted PFAS accumulation under ADW (with the highest increment of 44.68 μg/kg for PFOS & substitutes under 1ADW), but exhibited inhibition (for PFOA & substitutes) or weak (for PFOS & substitutes) effects under CS, indicating that the direction of MP-mediated regulation is highly dependent on hydrological conditions. Based on sediment physicochemical property differences and multiple linear regression (MLR) model results, compared to CS, ADW primarily inhibited PFAS accumulation by disrupting sediment flocculent structures and altering the role of DOM, whereas MPs presence enhanced PFAS retention by intensifying surface fragmentation, modulating key parameters (e.g., Zeta potential, BIX, and DOC), and serving as an additional sorption phase, thereby altering the original inhibition pattern imposed by ADW.

title: A multi‑target adverse outcome pathway network for sub-chronic ketamine‑induced cognitive impairment in adult zebrafish
abstract: Ketamine (KET), an emerging contaminant, is increasingly detected in aquatic environments, yet its sub-chronic neurocognitive effects at environmentally relevant concentrations remain largely unknown. We exposed adult zebrafish to KET for 40 days and integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, behavioral assays, and molecular simulations to investigate these effects. Sub-chronic KET exposure impaired spatial learning and memory at 0.4 μg/L, while anxiety‑like and social behavior were altered only at 40 μg/L. Intersecting transcriptomics with network toxicology yielded 9 candidate genes and 15 shared KEGG pathways, which were mainly associated with neurocognitive function. SHAP prioritized hmox1, camkk2, and trem2 and molecular simulations predicted stable binding of KET to these proteins, supporting their role as candidate molecular initiating events. Gene expression changes correlated with altered glutamate, and GABA levels. Based on these multi‑level findings, we constructed a proposed adverse outcome pathway (AOP) network in which KET is predicted to bind to HMOX1, CAMKK2, and TREM2, which may contribute to oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and synaptic dysfunction converging on cognitive decline. This study provides evidence in adult zebrafish that sub-chronic exposure to environmentally relevant KET impairs cognition and proposes a multi‑target AOP network based on zebrafish data, supporting ecological risk assessment of KET as an emerging contaminant.

title: An ultra-sensitive flexible room-temperature H2S sensor enabled by PANI/MXene/Cu2O ternary nanocomposites for meat spoilage monitoring
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), a highly toxic gas released during meat spoilage, necessitates room-temperature real-time detection for accurate freshness assessment and potential health hazards mitigation. In this work, an ultra-sensitive flexible H 2 S sensor was developed by depositing a polyaniline/MXene/cuprous oxide (PANI/MXene/Cu 2 O) ternary nanocomposite onto a flexible substrate, and it operates reliably at room temperature. The sensing material was synthesized via in-situ polymerization of PANI on titanium carbide (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) MXene, followed by the strategic integration of Cu 2 O microparticles to construct a hierarchical heterostructure. The sensor exhibits a high response sensitivity of 24.72% ppm -1 , a low theoretical detection limit of 0.456 ppb, and fast response/recovery times of 55 s and 35 s. It also delivers good selectivity, repeatability, long-term stability, and mechanical flexibility. A signal acquisition circuit integrating an OPA333 precision amplifier and a microcontroller was assembled for real-time quantitative detection of H 2 S release during shrimp spoilage, enabling effective tracking of H 2 S accumulation and discrimination of freshness stages. The enhanced gas-sensing performance stems from the synergistic combination of the highly conductive Ti 3 C 2 T x network, the p-p heterojunction between PANI and Cu 2 O, and the reduction reaction of PANI with H 2 S, which facilitates rapid charge transport and effectively modulates the interfacial energy band alignment upon H 2 S exposure. This study provides an effective strategy for designing high-performance room-temperature flexible gas sensors for real-time meat freshness assessment.

title: Response to the commentary on “trace cisplatin adsorption by thiol-functionalized sponge (TFS) and Sn/SnO₂-coated TFS: Adsorption study and mechanism investigation”
abstract: This response addresses the Commentary by Lima et al. on our study "Trace cisplatin adsorption by thiol-functionalized sponge (TFS) and Sn/SnO₂-coated TFS: Adsorption study and mechanism investigation". The discussion focuses on three main issues: the interpretation of the Dubinin-Radushkevich mean adsorption energy, the treatment of equilibrium constants in adsorption thermodynamics, and the use of three temperature points in the van't Hoff analysis. We clarify that the D-R parameter E was not used as a standalone proof of chemisorption, but as supporting evidence interpreted together with adsorption behavior, surface chemistry, and spectroscopic observations. We further discuss why conversion of adsorption constants into thermodynamic equilibrium constants must depend on the assumptions of the underlying adsorption model, particularly for systems that are not well described by the Langmuir model. Finally, we acknowledge the statistical limitations of a three-temperature van't Hoff analysis, while arguing that limited statistical power should not be equated with mathematical invalidity. Overall, we emphasize that adsorption thermodynamic parameters should be interpreted within the physical and model-specific context of the investigated system.

title: Manganese-oxidizing Priestia sp. Z-MLHA-1 drives biogenic Fe–Mn mineralization for synergistic As(V)/Cd(II) co-immobilization in groundwater: Experimental and DFT mechanisms with sustainability implications
abstract: Arsenic (As) and cadmium (Cd) frequently co-occur in contaminated groundwater, yet their distinct geochemical behaviors make simultaneous immobilization challenging. Here, a newly isolated Mn-oxidizing bacterium, Priestia sp. Z-MLHA-1, drives the formation of biogenic Fe-Mn minerals (BFMMs) through microbial Mn(II) oxidation involving a transient Mn(III) intermediate. The resulting bacteria-mineral composites, comprising poorly crystalline Fe-Mn oxides and microbial organic components, provide hydroxyl, carboxyl, and metal-oxygen groups as binding sites. In binary As(V)-Cd(II) systems, BFMMs achieve immobilization efficiencies of 97% and 98%, substantially outperforming single-component systems (82% and 91%), with single-component Langmuir capacities of 94.33 and 120.16 mg/g for As(V) and Cd(II), respectively. Combined characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal that heterogeneous electrostatic interactions and surface complexation govern contaminant binding, while Cd(II) acts as a bridging cation to stabilize ternary As-Cd-surface complexes. This mechanism accounts for the synergistic, rather than competitive, immobilization of As(V) and Cd(II) on BFMM surfaces. Sustainability assessments confirm low phytotoxicity and identify optimization pathways for production costs and environmental impacts, supporting the practical applicability of BFMMs as adsorbents in fixed-bed systems for active remediation, while the underlying bacteria-mediated mineralization process can be harnessed for passive in-situ natural attenuation, offering a nature-based solution for co-contaminated groundwater remediation.

title: Urine metabolomics analysis of construction painters with complex chemical exposures
abstract: Construction painters involved in metal structure coating experience complex chemical exposures, including epoxy resins, amine cross-linkers, isocyanates, organic solvents and flame retardants. These exposures induce oxidative stress and downstream metabolic perturbations, yet integrative metabolomic evidence in this workforce remains scarce. This study aimed to characterize urinary metabolomic alterations associated with distinct construction-related exposure scenarios including painting workers applying epoxy-based mid-coat and isocyanate-based top-coat. Untargeted urinary metabolomics was performed using liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) in pre- and post-shift samples collected from professional construction painting workers. Daily exposure effects were assessed using pre- versus post-shift urinary metabolomic comparisons, while exposure biomarker-associated metabolomic alterations were evaluated using tertile exposure stratification based on established urinary exposure biomarkers. The association of metabolic responses related to heat stress/dehydration was assessed using urinary specific gravity values. Statistical analyses included Student's t-testing, pathway enrichment analysis, and correlation analysis. Solvent-related metabolites, including hippuric and methylhippuric acids, were markedly elevated among coating workers. Both exposure groups showed significant alteration of amino acid metabolism and glutathione metabolism. In addition, mid-coat workers showed exposure effects on vitamin B6 metabolism, riboflavin metabolism, and catecholamine biosynthesis specifically. Top-coat workers demonstrated the exposure effects of nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism. These findings demonstrate that distinct coating-related exposures mixtures could yield unique metabolic signatures, despite complex mixtures exposures with overlapping chemical signatures.

title: Wireless portable detection of hazardous triethylamine vapor at near-room temperature via ZnO nanoflowers functionalized with titanium-oxo cluster
abstract: Triethylamine (TEA) is a widely used industrial solvent, yet its high volatility and toxicity pose significant risks to occupational safety and environmental air quality, with a recommended workplace exposure limit of 10 ppm. Real-time, low-temperature monitoring of TEA remains challenging for metal oxide semiconductor sensors, which require elevated operating temperatures. Herein, we report a ZnO nanoflower sensor functionalized with a classical titanium-oxo cluster [Ti 8 O 8 (OMc) 16 ]·2CH 3 CN (Ti 8 ) that enables sensitive and selective TEA detection at near-room temperature. The ZnO/5% Ti 8 sensor achieves a response (R a /R g ) of 5.29 toward 100 ppm TEA, a 4.3-fold enhancement over pristine ZnO, with a low detection limit of 0.39 ppm. The sensor exhibits a response to TEA at least 3 times higher than that to common interfering vapors and retains 90% of its initial response over 30 days. The enhanced performance is attributed to the Ti 8 -induced increase in chemisorbed oxygen on the ZnO surface, which provides more active sites for TEA oxidation. As a proof-of-concept demonstration for portable TEA detection, the sensor was integrated into a compact Bluetooth-enabled device capable of wirelessly transmitting response data to a smartphone. This work provides a material design strategy for low-power, portable detection of hazardous TEA for workplace and environmental safety.

title: Tracing contamination sources and geochemical processes in groundwater of industrial complex using multiple isotopes (Zn, Cr, S-O of sulfate, and H-O of water), PCA, and PMF
abstract: A multi-tracer framework combining rank-based principal component analysis (PCA), positive matrix factorization (PMF), and four stable-isotope systems was applied to 26 groundwater samples from three industrial zones and a residential reference area in South Korea. Trace metals were elevated in the industrial zones, with Cr reaching 17,324 and Zn 2026 µg L⁻¹ . PMF resolved four sources: sewage (Factor 1, NO₃⁻-dominant) at residential and Zone 2 wells, industrial SO₄²⁻ (Factor 2) at Zone 3 wells, reduction of Mn-Fe (oxy)hydroxides (Factor 3), and Zn alloy/plating (Factor 4). Three roadside wells showed low deuterium excess (d-excess, down to -1.7‰), suggesting characteristics of sewage. Among the 10 samples analyzed for sulfate isotopes, DS-11 showed increased δ³⁴S-SO₄ indicating bacterial sulfate reduction, with stable Δ¹⁸O(SO₄-H₂O) values suggesting oxygen exchange. δ⁶⁶Zn (n = 26; -0.32-1.04‰) was inversely related to dissolved Zn (R² = 0.60, p < 0.001), suggesting in-aquifer Zn sulfide (ZnS) precipitation. δ⁵³Cr (n = 3; 1.14-1.84‰) exceeded the industrial electroplating range (≈0‰), suggesting Cr(VI) reduction at those wells. The framework thus separated contaminant sources from in-aquifer attenuation. This separation, unattainable from dissolved concentrations alone, supports targeted remediation.

title: Interfacial capture of microplastics by a superhydrophobic COF–zeolite medium: Performance and multiscale mechanisms
abstract: Urban stormwater runoff is an important pathway for microplastics entering aquatic environments, while conventional bioretention media have limited interfacial capture capacity for hydrophobic microplastics (MPs). To construct a medium with a superhydrophobic surface and enhanced MP capture ability, this study fabricated a superhydrophobic medium, HDA@COF-LZU1@PDA@Zeolite, through polydopamine anchoring, in situ growth of COF-LZU1, and hexadecylamine hydrophobic modification. Its structural composition, wetting stability, MP removal performance, and interfacial interaction mechanism were systematically investigated. The results showed that the modified material achieved a WCA of 160° and retained superhydrophobicity under saline, acidic/alkaline, and mechanical abrasion conditions. Compared with pristine zeolite, the modified medium increased PP, PE, and PET removal from 3.27%, 5.63%, and 6.89-83.06%, 96.52%, and 99.16%, respectively. Kinetic data were best described by the PSO model, while the Langmuir model provided the best fit to the isotherm data, with capture capacity tending toward saturation at higher MP concentrations. The material also maintained effective MP removal at lower initial concentrations and under different ionic conditions. AFM, XDLVO, DFT calculations, and AIMD simulations were further used to explain the origin of the different capture behaviors from the perspectives of interfacial mechanics and molecular interactions. The differentiated capture behavior was associated with hydrophobic interactions, van der Waals interactions, local polar interactions, and possible π-π interactions. Among them, PET exhibited the highest capture efficiency, possibly due to additional contributions from its benzene rings and ester groups to interfacial interactions with the COF-LZU1 framework. This study suggests the differentiated capture mechanism of different MPs by the superhydrophobic COF-zeolite medium and provides guidance for the interfacial design of media in bioretention systems.

title: Integrated mechanisms of progestogen degradation and stress resistance in Novosphingobium sp. ES2-1
abstract: Environmental progestogens (Ps), precursors of various steroid hormones (SHs), can potentiate the endocrine-disrupting effects of SHs. Novosphingobium spp. are highly promising candidates for mitigating Ps contamination. Targeting progesterone (PGT), we found that N. sp. ES2-1 alleviated PGT-induced oxidative stress through metabolic glutathione synthesis, rerouting of electron transport entry points, and reduction of reactive oxygen species targets. PGT degradation initially proceeds via hydroxyprogesterone, following a metabolic pattern analogous to testosterone degradation. Through β-oxidation, this pathway ultimately yielded ring-cleavage products secophenol and 3aα-H-4α(3'-propanoate)-7aβ-methylhexahydro-1,5-indanedione. Cytochrome P450 and extradiol dioxygenase were identified as pivotal enzymes responsible for PGT structural modification and steroid skeleton cleavage. Proteins involved in iron acquisition, vitamin B6/B2 (VB6/VB2) biosynthesis interacted with β-oxidation-related proteins, suggesting that enzymes facilitating PGT skeleton cleavage required iron as an essential cofactor, while the necessary coenzymes and electron carriers relied on VB6/VB2. Seven putative PGT degradation genes encoding hydroxylases, dioxygenases, and dehydrogenases were proposed and harbored across four gene clusters that were significantly upregulated under PGT induction. These findings, for the first time, uncover the synergistic mechanisms in N. sp. ES2-1 where oxidative stress mitigation and optimized resources allocation supported PGT degradation, providing a theoretical framework for the rational engineering of SHs bioremediation strategies.

title: Index-based pollution and environmental risk assessment of microplastics: Handbook for a mindful practice
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is a major environmental issue due to its potential impacts on ecosystems and human health. After more than 20 years of research and over 7000 publications, sufficient knowledge is now available to support the first ecological risk assessments. In this context, risk indices have emerged as tools for evaluating environmental quality and MP contamination. This review analyzed 361 studies investigating MP pollution and risk assessment indices, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and future development needs. Since the first publication in 2018, research activity has grown exponentially. Initially dominated by studies from Asia, the topic has recently expanded into a global research field. Most studies have been published in high-impact journals, reflecting the importance of risk indices in MP monitoring and assessment. However, this growth has led to the proliferation of numerous and highly similar indices (31 metrics proposed), sometimes applied with methodological inconsistencies, creating confusion among researchers and practitioners. The most widely used are the Pollution Load Index (PLI), the Polymer Hazard Index (PHI), and the Potential Ecological Risk Index (PERI), mainly applied to water samples, with 73.9% of studies used in combination. Overall, MP indices can be classified into three groups: those based on MP abundance, those focusing on a single MP characteristic, and multidimensional indices integrating multiple traits, such as size, shape, and polymer type. We conclude that multidimensional approaches should be prioritized, supported by a shared assessment framework and the consistent application of existing indices rather than the continued development of new overlapping metrics.

title: Design of a highly active interfacial catalyst based on synergistic S/Se dual vacancies for the degradation of the highly hazardous emerging pollutant octogen (HMX): Interfacial PMS activation mechanism and electron pathway optimization
abstract: To address the urgent threat of energetic pollutants to soil and water, this study proposes a controllable dual-defect hydrothermal assembly strategy to anchor CoS and FeSe₂ onto phenolic resin-derived carbon spheres (PC), fabricating a 3D interfacial catalyst PC@CoS-FeSe₂ with abundant S/Se vacancies. The catalyst efficiently activates PMS over a wide pH range, achieving complete removal of HMX from aqueous solution within 10 min, with a maximum k of 0.5048 min⁻¹ . Synchrotron radiation and DFT calculations reveal that synergy between S/Se dual vacancies and the highly active CoS/FeSe₂ interface optimizes electron migration, significantly enhancing catalytic performance; band structure analysis confirms that the CoS-FeSe₂ interaction markedly improves electron filling efficiency near the Fermi level, accelerating charge transport across the heterojunction interface. EPR and quenching experiments verified the contributions of ROS to both radical and non-radical pathways during HMX degradation. MD simulations compared the dynamic evolution and bonding tendencies of PMS and HMX interacting with the catalyst and its individual components. HPLC-MS identified degradation intermediates, and four novel degradation pathways for HMX were proposed. Intermediates' toxicity was assessed using T.E.S.T. System practicality was evaluated by continuous-flow column experiments. The dual-defect-rich 3D catalyst PC@CoS-FeSe₂ shows promise for degrading hazardous nitramine pollutants and environmental remediation.

title: Semantic-guided adaptive dual-stream inference for marine floating litter detection
abstract: Marine floating litter detection on autonomous edge platforms, such as Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs), faces a fundamental scale-compute conflict: downsampling can obscure the fine-grained features of micro-scale targets, while native high-resolution inference often exceeds the computational budgets of edge platforms. Uniform slicing recovers small-scale target recall but exhaustively processes empty sea surfaces, amplifying false positives from sun glint and sea foam and substantially increasing inference latency. We propose GL-DSI, a Global-Local Dual-Stream Inference framework that replaces blind slicing with semantic-guided adaptive extraction: a low-resolution global stream localizes suspect regions, triggering high-resolution local inference only where small-scale targets likely exist. A Size-Aware Gaussian Attenuation (SAGA) module suppresses boundary artifacts, while the Scale-Semantic Consistency Filter (SSCF) removes environment-induced pseudo-targets. On our marine floating litter dataset (MFL-Dataset), GL-DSI with YOLOv11s reaches an F1-score of 93.4% at 44.6 frames per second (FPS) on the desktop benchmark.
