Compared to its standard baseline, it improves the detection of highly degraded small-scale targets, boosting recall for targets with areas below 256 px 2 by 11.0 %age points and lifting nano-scale target recall from 13.5% to 27.0%, while remaining substantially less computationally intensive than exhaustive slicing.

title: Heavy metal accumulation, lability and ecological risk in sediments across contrasting depositional settings within a surface-flow wetland: Associations with organic carbon fractions and porewater biogeochemistry
abstract: Contrasting depositional settings can generate differences in heavy metal accumulation, ecological risk, and lability, but their relationships with organic carbon (OC) fractions and porewater biogeochemistry remain unclear. We investigated inlet, interior, and outlet sediments of the Luoshijiang constructed surface-flow wetland, Southwest China, integrating 210 Pb-based depositional characterization, metal and risk assessments, diffusive gradients in thin films, porewater measurements, diffusive fluxes, modeled speciation, OC fractions, and bacterial indicators. Most total metal contents decreased from inlet to outlet, while OC, readily oxidizable carbon, and total glomalin-related soil protein increased. Co showed the strongest contamination, whereas Cd contributed 52.7-58.0% of potential ecological risk. Contemporary metal lability did not consistently parallel total metal accumulation. Cd, Cu, and Pb showed net diffusive influx into sediments, whereas Mn showed net efflux and Zn shifted between source and sink behavior. Modeled Cd was dominated by S-bearing inorganic complexes, Co, Mn, Ni, and Zn by free ions and carbonate/hydroxide complexes, and Cu and Pb by fulvic-acid-bound forms. Associations of OC fractions, total phosphorus, Anaeromyxobacter abundance, and Cd S-bearing complexes with metal accumulation or lability varied among depositional settings. These findings show that accumulated metal burden, ecological risk, and contemporary lability provide complementary information for wetland sediment assessment.

title: T-2 toxin induces glycometabolic reprogramming in chondrocytes via a MALAT1/p38‑mediated ceRNA regulatory axis
abstract: T-2 toxin is a widely distributed dietary mycotoxin and a key environmental driver of Kashin-Beck disease (KBD), yet the molecular events linking exposure to cartilage injury remain incompletely defined. We examined the chondrotoxic mechanism of T-2 toxin through a MALAT1/miR-15b-5p/MAP2K3 competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) axis across cellular, animal and human levels. Rat models of graded T-2 toxin exposure, combined with mRNA and miRNA sequencing identified affected pathways and candidate non-coding RNAs. In C28/I2 human chondrocytes, dual-luciferase and rescue experiments characterized the targeting relationships and functional consequences of the axis. The p38 inhibitor BIRB796 and exogenous insulin were administered to rats, and a 1:1:1 frequency-matched case-control study in a KBD-endemic area assessed clinical relevance. T-2 toxin increased chondrocyte MALAT1, which sponged miR-15b-5p and relieved its repression of MAP2K3, leading to sustained p38 MAPK hyperactivation and concurrent extracellular matrix degradation and glycometabolic reprogramming. p38 inhibition or insulin supplementation attenuated T-2 toxin-induced cartilage degeneration and glucose dysregulation in rats. In humans, elevated serum lactate and peripheral-blood MALAT1 were independently associated with both KBD and osteoarthritis. These findings expand the molecular network underlying T-2 toxin chondrotoxicity and provide candidate biomarkers for the health-risk assessment of mycotoxin exposure and prevention of environment-related osteoarthropathy.

title: Do alternative PFAS reduce risk or shift it? A critical comparative review of persistence, mobility, bioaccumulation, toxicity, exposure, and safer substitution criteria
abstract: Regulatory restrictions on legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (L-PFAS), including perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), and related long-chain compounds, have accelerated the global adoption of alternative and emerging PFAS (A-PFAS, functional umbrella term rather than structural class). Many A-PFAS were introduced to reduce selected legacy concerns, particularly bioaccumulation and long human retention. However, lower bioaccumulation alone does not establish lower overall risk, because several A-PFAS remain highly persistent, mobile, treatment-resistant, or capable of transforming into persistent terminal products. Here, we present a critical comparative review and analysis of eleven L-PFAS and eighteen A-PFAS across physicochemical properties, environmental fate, global occurrence, bioaccumulation, trophic transfer, toxicity, and exposure, with particular attention to whether substitution reduces risk or shifts it among endpoints. The evidence indicates that PFAS substitution has often reduced some hazard dimensions while preserving or intensifying others, but the direction and confidence of risk shifting differ markedly among compounds. Risk shifting is demonstrated for several chlorinated, fluorotelomer-derived compounds, and perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) that show documented increases in persistence, mobility, bioaccumulation, trophic magnification, or transformation potential. Mixed evidence applies to most short- and ultra-short-chain perfluoroalkyl acids (PFAA) and the hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO) compounds, which reduce bioaccumulation or human retention but shift concern toward high mobility, treatment difficulty, diffuse exposure, or toxicity. The evidence is insufficient for several fluorotelomer-based precursors and N-(Methyl) nonafluorobutanesulfonamide (N-MeFBSA), for which bioaccumulation, toxicity, and exposure data remain too limited to characterize the direction of risk shifting. No compound met the criteria for reduced concern across all dimensions. These patterns indicate that many current substitution pathways shift risk from bioaccumulation and long human retention toward persistence, mobility, diffuse exposure, treatment difficulty, secondary-waste generation, and end-of-life uncertainty. Avoiding further regrettable substitution requires moving beyond molecule-by-molecule replacement toward function-based alternatives assessment, transparent production and use information, monitoring beyond conventional target PFAS, evaluation of treatment removability and destruction feasibility, end-of-life release control, and class-or subgroup-based management where justified.

title: Self-adaptive starch-based flocculant enabling irreversible stimulus-mediated phase separation: Achieving ultralow residual and simultaneous demulsification/decolorization for textile wastewater reclamation
abstract: Treating complex wastewater containing coexisting oily emulsions and dyes via flocculation technology encounters extremely intractable challenges, such as poor simultaneous removal efficiency and high residual flocculant level, which severely impede the closed-loop reuse of reclaimed water. Herein, we fabricated a novel multifunctional starch-based flocculant (ST-GPMDES-BDAT) to address key challenges in treating oil-dye composite wastewater. ST-GPMDES-BDAT exhibits multi-stimuli-responsive phase transition behavior. The extent of reversibility of ST-GPMDES-BDAT (reversible, semi-reversible and irreversible) was regulated by varying the environmental stimulus. As a result, irreversible stimulus-mediated phase separation of resulting polymer enables ultralow residual levels of the flocculant in the filtrate. This residual level significantly outperforms conventional commercial flocculants, thereby overcoming the key bottleneck of flocculant interference in closed-loop water reuse. Leveraging the synergistic effects of charge neutralization and hydrophobic bridging, ST-GPMDES-BDAT achieves highly efficient simultaneous removal of emulsified oil and anionic dyes (exceeding 99%). It also demonstrates exceptional versatility across various oil-dye composite systems, indicating broad applicability for treating diverse complex wastewaters. Furthermore, closed-loop reusability tests further confirm that the treated wastewater can be stably used for fabric dyeing over three consecutive cycles. Notably, no significant decline in dyeing performance is observed, which validates the practical feasibility of ST-GPMDES-BDAT for sustainable wastewater treatment.

title: Multidimensional risk assessment of yield-enhancing plant growth regulators in medicinal plants: A case study of paclobutrazol in Ophiopogon japonicus with metabolomics, bioactivity, and regulatory implications
abstract: The illicit use of plant growth regulators in medicinal plant cultivation poses potential environmental and public health risks, exemplified by paclobutrazol (PBZ) application on Ophiopogon japonicus (OJ). The new Chinese Pharmacopoeia establishes the first mandatory standard limiting PBZ residues in OJ. This study aimed to evaluate the agronomic benefits, residue risks, metabolomic alterations, and preliminary biological consequences of PBZ application in OJ under field conditions to support the new standard's implementation. PBZ increased OJ yield by 43.7%-47.7% at medium concentrations but posed residue risks, with levels reaching 1.3- to 5.4-fold of the limit at medium-to-high concentrations. PBZ differentially regulated metabolite profiles, promoting representative homoisoflavonoids (8.9%-98.8% increase) while suppressing steroidal saponins (7.6%-32.8% decrease). PBZ enhanced anti-inflammatory activity (up to ∼40%) but attenuated antioxidant capacity (>20% reduction), exploratory correlation analysis suggested potential associations between activity changes and metabolite levels. In conclusion, PBZ impacts beyond residue concerns, inducing substantial alterations in metabolites, with preliminary observations suggesting that these changes may potentially affect the bioactivity and safety of the medicinal material. This study provides baseline data and directions for subsequent ecotoxicological and safety assessments, and may offer references to inform the potential development of evidence-based management policies regarding PGRs.

title: Mineral-contaminant interactions in the presence of polystyrene microplastics: Implications for contaminant adsorption in aqueous environments
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), particularly polystyrene microplastics (PSMPs), are emerging contaminants of global concern that can alter contaminant dynamics in aquatic systems. This study investigates how Polystyrene MPs influence the adsorption behaviour of three representative environmental contaminants-Cd(II), Cr(VI), and tetracycline (TC) onto natural clay and mineral substrates (goethite, kaolin, and bentonite). Batch adsorption experiments showed that all three minerals effectively adsorb these contaminants. However, the presence of PSMPs reduced their overall adsorption capacities by ∼13-45% for Cd(II), ∼7-11% for Cr(VI), and ∼9-12% for TC, depending on the mineral system. Kinetic modelings revealed distinct behaviours between pollutant classes. The adsorption of Cd(II) and Cr(VI) followed a mixed kinetic control governed by both surface reaction and intraparticle diffusion. In contrast, tetracycline uptake was best described by a revised pseudo-second-order mechanism sensitive to both solute and surface site availability. Markedly, the addition of PSMPs altered apparent adsorption rates in a highly system-specific manner, inducing, either suppression or minimal variation through a complex interplay between steric hindrance arising from site masking and a concurrent transition toward rapidly forming outer-sphere complexes. The XPS analyses suggested that, while contaminant binding in MP-free systems involved a greater contribution from inner-sphere complexation, PSMP-amended systems exhibited an increased contribution from weaker outer-sphere interactions. Although PSMP-only controls showed negligible direct contaminant uptake under the tested conditions, the presence of PSMPs altered mineral surface reactivity and aggregate structure, thereby reducing mineral-mediated contaminant retention. These findings demonstrate that PSMPs can modify contaminant partitioning and mobility in aquatic environments and highlight the importance of incorporating MP-mineral interactions into contaminant transport and environmental risk assessment frameworks.

title: Combination-specific effects of antibiotic and disinfectant co-contamination on the enrichment of antibiotic resistance genes in sediments
abstract: The environmental co-occurrence of disinfectants and antibiotics has emerged as a typical multi-pollutant issue, with river sediments serving as critical sinks and accumulation media. However, whether their combined exposure accelerate antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) dissemination in sediments remains unclear. Here, we systematically evaluated the effects of single and combined exposures to sodium hypochlorite and representative antibiotics on the sediment resistome and microbial communities. The results demonstrated that combined exposure generally increased the relative abundances of ARGs (1.83- to 3.57-fold) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs, 2.39- to 22.28-fold). Notably, sodium hypochlorite-gentamicin combination exhibited the most pronounced synergistic effect, consistent with toxicological model prediction. Combined exposure also reshaped bacterial community structure and enriched potential ARG-host taxa, while co-occurrence network analysis identified Limosilactobacillus as a candidate genus associated with multiple ARGs. Mechanistically, partial least squares path modeling indicated that MGE-mediated horizontal gene transfer was the dominant pathway driving ARGs enrichment. Plasmid conjugation assays further showed that NaClO + gentamicin increased conjugation frequency by 3.81-fold, supporting enhanced horizontal gene transfer. Overall, this study elucidates the intrinsic mechanisms by which complex pollution drives ARGs propagation in sediments, highlighting the overlooked ecological risks associated with disinfectant-antibiotic co-contamination in aquatic environments.

title: Stage-wise far-UVC/chlorine process curbs antimicrobial resistance in hospital wastewater: Short-burst inactivation and sustained suppression of recovery and resistance transfer
abstract: Conventional UV 254 /chlorine can leave incomplete genetic damage and create a low-dose window that promotes horizontal gene transfer (HGT), limiting reliable antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) control. Here, UV 222 /chlorine (1 mg/L free chlorine) was evaluated in 0.22-μm-filtered hospital wastewater inoculated with E. coli DH5α-RP4 and compared with UV 222 , UV 254 , and UV 254 /chlorine. During UV 222 /chlorine treatment in hospital wastewater, free available chlorine (FAC) declined rapidly and approached the detection limit at approximately 35 mJ/cm 2 , whereas UV 254 /chlorine retained measurable FAC at 100 mJ/cm 2 . Chloride promoted conversion of Cl· to selective Cl 2 · - , whereas tert-butanol quenching indicated a smaller contribution from ·OH. Accordingly, the process comprised an initial chlorine-enhanced phase (0-35 mJ/cm 2 ), which delivered ∼2.5-log greater ARB inactivation than UV 222 alone, followed by a UV 222 -dominated phase after FAC depletion. Membrane permeabilization largely saturated during Stage 1, supporting an acute rather than dose-proportional envelope attack. At 100 mJ/cm 2 , UV 222 /chlorine prevented regrowth, reduced intracellular antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) by 76.6-88.3%, and drove RP4 conjugation toward zero. In contrast, UV 254 /chlorine transiently increased conjugation to ∼150% of the control at low doses. Transcriptomics showed concurrent suppression of envelope maintenance, DNA repair, protein homeostasis, and metabolism. Thus, UV 222 /chlorine combines a short RCS shock with sustained multi-target damage to control ARB, ARG persistence, and plasmid-mediated HGT in complex wastewater.

title: Retention of source microbial signals in plastispheres of fibrous plastic debris after translocation
abstract: While numerous studies have explored microbial hitchhiking on aquatic plastics, the fate and interpretability of residual source signals after translocation remain unclear. Here, disposable face masks were used as model fibrous plastic debris to examine source conditioned plastisphere formation, post transfer signal retention, and mask part specific exposure history signals. Masks were conditioned in two freshwater systems and transferred to autoclaved deionized water as a simplified receiving medium to reduce source water input. Before transfer, mask surfaces developed plastispheres that differed from surrounding water in overall composition and dominant bacterial assemblages, and the two source waters produced distinguishable original plastispheres. At transfer weeks 2, 4, and 6, whole mask plastispheres remained distinguishable by their source origin; PERMANOVA explained 20.9%, 18.9%, and 19.5% of variation across Bray Curtis, Jaccard, and Aitchison CLR distances. Similarity contrast based affinity indices were further used to distinguish water-source carryover from affinity to the original plastisphere state. Whole mask water source affinity was weak and non-significant (mean = -0.0015, p = 0.728), whereas plastisphere source affinity was marginal at the whole mask scale (mean = 0.0033, p = 0.074) and significant under part matched comparisons (mean = 0.0015, p = 0.014), and source separation was clearer in inner and outer layers than ear loops. Overall, these findings indicate that source-history-associated compositional information remained detectable during post-transfer reassembly, supporting further exploration of plastisphere profiles for source tracing.

title: Multimodal deep learning for species-aware prediction of chemical toxicity to aquatic plants
Characterization of PM10 sources in the Riotinto copper mining district (SW Spain) using multi-time-resolution receptor modelling
authors: Ana M. Sánchez de la Campa
abstract: Mining activities significantly contribute to the emission of heavy metals and metalloids to the atmosphere. This year-long study (July 2024–July 2025) aimed to comprehensively characterize PM10 sources in the Riotinto copper mining district (southwestern Spain) using a highly time-resolved X-ray fluorescence monitor and an Aethalometer, and a high-volume sampler sampling daily on quartz fiber filters. Filters were chemically analyzed for multiple pollutants. High-time-resolution (1-h) and low-time-resolution (24-h) data subsets were integrated within a multi-time-resolution positive matrix factorization approach. The source apportionment analysis identified seven major PM10 sources: Waste Rock (4.9 µg·m-3), Regional + Traffic (3.6 µg·m-3), Dust (1.1 µg·m-3), Open Pit (1.6 µg·m-3), Aged Marine (1.2 µg·m-3), Copper Concentrate (0.7 µg·m-3), and Combustion (1.2 µg·m-3). The incorporation of species measured at daily resolution enabled the identification of traffic tracers and secondary organic aerosol in several factors, which was not possible using only the hourly-resolution data subset. During the study period, As represented the main geochemical anomaly because of its elevated concentration. This work highlights the advantages of combining data with different temporal resolutions in source apportionment analyses for a better characterization of emission sources in environmentally vulnerable areas.

title: Systematic insights into 6PPD-quinone biotransformation by acclimated aerobic sludge: Kinetics, pathways, toxicity, and enzymatic mechanisms
abstract: This study acclimated aerobic (AeS), nitrifying (NS), and denitrifying (DS) sludge systems to N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q) at 1-20 mg·L⁻¹ . Within an environmental to high concentration range (1 μg·L⁻¹ to 5 mg·L⁻¹), acclimated AeS removed 88.9%-95.2% of 6PPD‑Q within 14 days, significantly outperforming the NS and DS systems. The first-order degradation rate constant of the aerobic sludge ranged from 0.175 to 1.006 d⁻¹ . Based on the Haldane kinetic model, its substrate inhibition constant was 29.3 mg·L⁻¹ , demonstrating the broadest substrate tolerance range. This study proposed 13 biotransformation products (7 of which were reported for the first time), and constructed a complete degradation pathway accordingly. Ecological Structure-Activity Relationship modeling and in vitro bioassays jointly confirmed that AeS treatment significantly reduced the acute toxicity of 6PPD-Q. Metagenomic binning identified Sphingopyxis, Achromobacter, and Pseudomonas as the dominant genera, while molecular docking further implicated cytochrome P450 and peroxidase may serve as key enzymes in the catabolism of the parent compound. A 40‑day experiment showed that combining acclimated aerobic sludge with activated sludge significantly reduced 6PPD‑Q concentrations in real wastewater effluents. This study systematically elucidated the degradation pathway, toxicity evolution, and enzymatic mechanisms of 6PPD-Q in activated sludge, providing new insights for its bioremediation.

title: Flyway-scale lead and multielement exposure in globally threatened Cinereous vultures (Aegypius monachus) wintering on the Korean Peninsula: Insights from tissue burdens and stable lead isotopes
abstract: Lead (Pb) is a major toxicant in avian scavengers, but its ecological role and exposure pathways along the East Asian flyway remain unclear. Immature Cinereous vultures (Aegypius monachus) migrate from Mongolia through China to winter on the Korean Peninsula, where they mostly congregate near the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), creating a potential flyway-scale bottleneck where local hazards may affect much of the population. This study investigates Pb and multielement exposure in 74 immature vultures recovered near the DMZ by quantifying Pb concentrations in liver and muscle, measuring hepatic Cd, Cu, Zn, Ni, As, V, and Fe, and analyzing stable Pb isotope ratios ( 206 Pb/ 207 Pb, 208 Pb/ 206 Pb, 208 Pb/ 207 Pb) in tissues to assess potential exposure sources. Hepatic Pb concentrations ranged from 1.17 to 33.4 μg/g dw, and 16.2% of individuals reached levels consistent with Pb-induced mortality. Hepatic Pb burdens did not differ among probable causes of death (gunshot, trauma, emaciation, electrocution, suspected poisoning, and unknown), indicating pervasive Pb exposure across the wintering cohort. Muscle Pb concentrations were generally low, except in one gunshot-injured bird, which had an extreme level of 120.9 μg/g dw. In contrast, other hepatic elements showed comparatively moderate concentrations, identifying Pb as the primary toxicological concern. Tissue Pb isotope signatures overlapped with ammunition-related and other anthropogenic Pb sources, supporting a mixed-source exposure scenario in which Pb-based ammunition likely contributes. These findings indicate that immature Cinereous vultures wintering on the Korean Peninsula are widely and persistently exposed to Pb, highlighting the need for flyway-scale monitoring and targeted mitigation across the Mongolia-China-Korea flyway.

title: Super-stable mineralization materials for long-term remediation of heavy metal contaminated soil: Triple criteria, research progress and design of materials
abstract: The remediation of heavy metal contaminated soil is a common challenge faced worldwide. Solidification/stabilization technology has been widely applied. In particular, the concept of super-stable mineralization proposed in recent years offers a promising approach for the long-term and stable remediation of soil heavy metal contamination. A large number of studies on super-stable mineralization (SSM) materials have been reported. However, there is still a lack of comprehensive evaluation system for super-stable mineralization. Combined with the research frontiers and achievements in related fields through a multidisciplinary approach, this paper proposes a triple evaluation framework for SSM based on reaction stability, structural stability, and environmental stability. At the same time, CatBoost machine learning model is used to preliminarily assess the proposed framework. The research status, super-stable mineralization ability and application prospects of hydroxyapatite, silicates, metal oxides, and layered double hydroxides (LDH) were systematically reviewed. Finally, the design strategies for super-stable mineralization materials are proposed. This review aims to provide insights for the future exploration of materials for long-term heavy metal fixation, and to promote the establishment of a unified standard for evaluating material performance in heavy metal stabilization.

title: Solar-photoaged maize leaf residues reshape soil physicochemical–biological processes and Fe–Cd biogeochemistry
abstract: Solar photoaging endows maize leaf residues with persistent redox activity through the spontaneous generation of oxygen-centered environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs). Upon soil incorporation, these long-lived radicals and their derived dissolved organic matter (DOM) act as electron donors that promote Fe(III) reduction to Fe(II), followed by Fe(II) reoxidation and reprecipitation, thereby promoting reduction-initiated Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox cycling. This process profoundly shapes soil properties by expanding the organic carbon pool, yet it accelerates soil acidification and triggers root-localized oxidative stress, which induces lipid peroxidation and partially offsets the growth-promoting effect of biomass amendment. Concurrently, the persistent oxidative pressure and oxygen consumption reshape the indigenous soil microbiome, shifting it toward iron-reducing consortia (e.g., Gammaproteobacteria and Bacillus circulans). Crucially, this radical-Fe process is associated with the conversion of labile ion-exchangeable Cd into more stable Fe/Mn oxide-bound fractions. Consequently, heavy metal translocation in the soil-plant system is effectively blocked, mitigating root and shoot Cd accumulation in Ipomoea aquatica by up to 50%. This study demonstrates a novel nature-based strategy coupling organic waste recycling with sustainable in-situ heavy metal remediation.

title: Integrated post-closure safety assessment of radioactive waste containing hazardous chemicals: A screening framework for radiological–chemical risk
abstract: Disposal of radioactive waste containing hazardous chemicals can generate post-closure radiological cancer risks, chemical cancer risks, and chemical non-cancer hazards. Existing assessments often treat radiological and chemical endpoints separately. This study develops an integrated post-closure assessment and screening framework that combines United States Environmental Protection Agency risk methods with AMBER dynamic compartment modeling, using the International Atomic Energy Agency Trench Case as a reference disposal system. A normalized generic assessment of selected metallic elements was used to compare radiological and chemical risk behavior and derive two endpoint-specific screening metrics: a critical radioactivity concentration for identifying when chemical cancer risk is small relative to radiological cancer risk, and a preliminary non-cancer trigger based on maximum leachate concentration relative to the drinking-water standard. A case-study application using documented mixed-waste inventory data from nuclear facilities evaluated complex waste types with associated radionuclides under normal-evolution and human-intrusion scenarios. Several cases triggered total cancer risk screening criteria under human intrusion, indicating the need for detailed assessment. The results are reference-scenario screening outcomes, not site-specific predictions. The framework supports prioritization of radioactive mixed waste for constituent-specific, pathway-specific, and site-specific assessment. This structure links time-dependent transport outputs with endpoint-specific decisions for waste management and regulation.

title: Cometabolic and nutrient-driven defluorination and transformation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances by metabolically versatile bacteria
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are emerging contaminants of great concern. Yet, current knowledge of PFAS-degrading microorganisms is limited. Here, we report novel bacterial strains, Cupriavidus sp. CuC1, Pseudomonas sp. PsB, and Variovorax sp. VaC1, capable of defluorinating diverse C1-C6 fluorinated PFAS and using nitrogen (N)- and sulfur (S)-containing PFAS as nutrients. These bacteria exhibited broad metabolic versatility toward various sugar, carboxylates, alcohols, alkanes, aromatic, hydrocarbon surfactants, and organic solvents. In particular, 1-butanol (BuOH)-grown CuC1 effectively defluorinated C1-C6 fluorinated PFAS. Strain PsB significantly removed 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonamidoalkyl betaine (FtSaB) and N-ethyl perfluorooctane sulfonamide as sole N-sources. All three strains removed 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonate (FtS) as a sole S-source and accumulated various PFAS (suspect) metabolites when grown from selective carbon source types. Strains CuC1 (ethylene glycol-, BuOH-, or octanoate-grown) and VaC1 (glucose-grown) achieved > 95% 6:2 FtS removal. Strain VaC1 uniquely accumulated a novel metabolite, α-OH 6:2 FtS, that corresponded with higher accumulation of 6:2 fluorotelomer unsaturated carboxylic acid. Furthermore, CuC1 demonstrated 6:2 FtS removal when grown on sodium octyl sulfate under S-rich conditions and showed potential removal in 6:2 FtSaB and undecafluoro-2-methyl-3-oxahexanoic acid (commercial name GenX) under S-limited conditions. These findings significantly expand the portfolio of PFAS degraders and provide new mechanistic insights into nutrient-driven PFAS biotransformation.

title: Chronic heavy metal exposure drives mitochondrial remodeling and metabolic reprogramming to enhance sperm velocity in wild tree sparrows
abstract: Environmental pollution is widely assumed to impair reproductive performance, yet whether organisms can sustain reproductive function under chronic stress remains poorly understood. Here, using natural populations of tree sparrows from a heavy metal-contaminated site and a reference site, we reveal a paradoxical increase in sperm velocity despite clear physiological costs. Males from the polluted population exhibited reduced body condition and elevated cadmium and lead accumulation in reproductive tissues, but their sperm velocity parameters were significantly enhanced. Mechanistically, sperm from exposed birds showed coordinated mitochondrial optimization, including elevated mitochondrial membrane potential, enhanced complex I activity, and higher ATP content. In the testis, genes associated with mitochondrial biogenesis (TFAM) and mitophagy (BNIP3) were upregulated, indicating enhanced mitochondrial quality control during spermatogenesis. Functional inhibition using the oxidative phosphorylation uncoupler carbonyl cyanide 4-(trifluoromethoxy) phenylhydrazone (FCCP) confirmed that elevated sperm velocity depends on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses further revealed a systemic metabolic reprogramming from glycolysis toward OXPHOS, characterized by upregulation of OXPHOS-related proteins and suppression of glycolytic pathways. Together, our findings demonstrate that chronic heavy metal stress can enhance sperm performance through mitochondrial and metabolic remodeling, revealing a key mechanism by which avian reproductive behavior responds to long-term environmental stress.

title: Spatiotemporal distribution and rainfall-runoff transport characteristics of microplastics in a typical agricultural watershed
abstract: Rainfall runoff is one of the key drivers of microplastic transport from sources to sinks, but the dynamic changes of microplastics remain insufficiently quantified. This study systematically investigated the spatiotemporal distribution of microplastics in a typical agricultural watershed from April to December 2025 through soil sampling and monthly water monitoring, combined with high-frequency monitoring of 13 rainfall events to quantify the impact of rainfall on microplastic transport. Results showed that soil microplastic abundance was higher near residential areas. The water microplastic abundance in the downstream was higher than that in the upstream, and elevated concentrations in ponds may serve as both sinks and export sources of microplastics. The mean of event mean concentrations (EMC MP ) during rainfall events was significantly higher than that of baseflow, representing a 1.9-fold increase (p < 0.05). The predominance of counter-clockwise hysteresis (62% of events) supported the hypothesis that microplastic transport may be influenced by proximal supply limitation and distal-source delayed delivery as hydrological connectivity increases. Microplastic load was significantly correlated with most of the hydrological variables examined. Load-discharge model estimated that the 23.2% of rainfall time contributed 54.1% of the annual load, highlighting the necessity of incorporating high-frequency rainfall event monitoring into watershed microplastic load assessment frameworks.

title: Resuscitation-promoting factor enhances PFOA biodegradation and modulates cellular stress responses in two PFOA-degrading bacterial strains
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a highly persistent and toxic per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), poses significant environmental and health risks. Microbial degradation offers a promising remediation strategy but is limited by the scarcity and low efficiency of known degraders. Here, two PFOA-degrading strains, Alcaligenes sp. MT1 and Pseudomonas sp. MT3, were isolated and characterized. Whole-genome analysis identified multiple genes potentially involved in fluorinated compound transformation. Supplementation with resuscitation-promoting factor (Rpf) significantly enhanced PFOA degradation, with an optimal dosage of 1.5% (v/v), increasing removal efficiencies by 16.8% (MT1) and 18.7% (MT3) relative to controls. Rpf improved cellular performance by elevating antioxidant enzyme activities (peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, catalase) and Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity while reducing malondialdehyde levels, indicating enhanced oxidative stress tolerance and energy metabolism. Consistently, key genes associated with decarboxylation and dehalogenation pathways were markedly upregulated. LC-MS/MS analysis revealed that PFOA degradation involved sequential decarboxylation and defluorination, with Rpf affecting metabolite abundance but not the core degradation pathways. These findings demonstrate that Rpf-mediated activation effectively enhances microbial PFOA degradation and provides a promising strategy for PFAS bioremediation.

title: Compound-specific porewater-surface water relationships of taste and odor compounds under contrasting water-level conditions in a reservoir drawdown zone
abstract: Elevated odorant concentrations in sediment porewater may not correspond to surface-water occurrence. This study examined four taste-and-odor compounds (odorants), β-cyclocitral (CYC), β-ionone (ION), 2-methylisoborneol (2-MIB), and geosmin (GSM), in paired sediment porewater and surface-water samples from 11 sites in Xiangxi Bay, Three Gorges Reservoir, China. Sampling on 2 July 2025 and 6 January 2026 captured contrasting low- and high-water conditions. CYC and ION showed positive site-level porewater–surface water associations during the July campaign. In January, 2-MIB and GSM generally exhibited higher concentrations in porewater than in surface water, without corresponding site-level associations between compartments. These contrasts show that porewater enrichment and cross-compartment covariation provide different evidence about odorant distribution. Because each condition was sampled once, the differences are interpreted as campaign-specific rather than replicated seasonal or water-level effects. Joint analysis of porewater and surface water may therefore improve the assessment of odorant occurrence in regulated reservoir bays.

title: Detection of degradation products of chemical warfare agents in Halabja soil: In vitro genotoxicity and effects in exposed humans
abstract: The town of Halabja in Iraqi Kurdistan remains a symbol of the devastating impact of chemical weapons. Almost four decades after the attack, inhabitants continue to suffer from increased cancer rates and severe respiratory, neurological, and psychiatric disorders. While the acute effects of chemical warfare agents have been widely studied, their long-term environmental persistence and associated health impacts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the presence of chemical warfare agent residues in the environment and assessed their potential genotoxic effects. Soil and water samples collected in Halabja in 2021 were analyzed for chemical warfare agents, including sulfur mustard, sarin, and their degradation products using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry with dual flame photometric detection and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, selected for their sensitivity toward sulfur- and phosphorus-containing compounds. In soil samples, we detected thiodiglycolic acid and methylphosphonic acid, degradation products of sulfur mustard and organophosphorus nerve agents, respectively. To evaluate biological relevance, soil-derived extracts were tested in vitro using Western blotting to assess markers of DNA damage and inflammation, revealing elevated levels of both endpoints. Because some soil samples also contained the persistent organic pollutant p,p'-DDE, the observed genotoxic effects were interpreted as potentially reflecting contributions from both CWA-related degradation products and other environmental contaminants. To complement these findings, plasma and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from individuals exposed in 1988 were analyzed in 2025, by flow cytometry and ELISA, demonstrating increased levels of the same markers compared with controls. Together, these findings indicate long-term environmental persistence of chemical warfare agent degradation products and their genotoxic potential, while also highlighting that other environmental contaminants may contribute to the biological effects observed in complex soil extracts, alongside sustained biological effects in exposed individuals.

title: Residual polyethylene film loading alters soil quality and maize productivity, with distinct bacterial communities in plastisphere soil
abstract: Residual polyethylene (PE) film can alter soil resources and crop production, but its effects across loading levels and at the soil-film interface remain poorly resolved. In a maize field experiment established in 2011 in northwestern China, we assessed soil properties, bacterial communities, nitrogen cycling indicators, and crop performance across five PE loadings (0-600 kg ha -1 ). Soil firmly adhering to residual film was pooled across the four film treatments to characterize plastisphere soil. Soil quality and maize performance responded nonmonotonically to loading. Grain yield was 20% higher at 150 kg ha -1 and 22% lower at 600 kg ha -1 than in the control. At the highest loading, lower nutrient levels and root biomass coincided with greater soil water content after harvest and lower bacterial network connectivity. Pooled plastisphere communities showed greater diversity and contrasting assembly patterns. Their higher connectivity did not consistently correspond to greater simulated robustness. Plastisphere soil had higher nitrification potential than bulk soil, despite lower summed nitrification gene abundance than at 300 and 450 kg ha -1 . Structural equation modeling linked yield positively to total nitrogen and available phosphorus. These findings identify loading and microbial differentiation at soil-film interfaces as complementary dimensions of residual-film impacts.

title: Descriptor-informed oxidant selection in pulsed electrochemical AOPs: Cathode-favored periodate activation enables selective sulfamethoxazole oxidation
abstract: Oxidant selection in electrochemical advanced oxidation processes remains largely empirical because molecular and interfacial factors governing activation are not quantitatively linked to degradation performance. Here, a descriptor-informed framework was developed to rationalize oxidant-dependent activation in pulsed electrochemical AOPs. Six oxidants or redox-active precursors were evaluated using sulfamethoxazole degradation, and four descriptors-the LUMO-HOMO gap, vertical electron affinity, adsorption energy, and Bader charge transfer-were correlated with apparent rate constants. The preliminary descriptor-informed analysis captured the oxidant-dependent activation trend and identified periodate (PI) as the most favorable oxidant. Under identical conditions, pulsed electrolysis/periodate (PE/PI) achieved 95.43% sulfamethoxazole (SMX) removal with a rate constant of 0.10631 min -1 , outperforming pulsed electrolysis/peroxymonosulfate (PE/PMS) and PE/H 2 O 2 . Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that the superior PE/PI performance arose from stronger cathodic adsorption, more efficient interfacial electron transfer, and contributions from 1 O 2 -mediated non-radical oxidation and IO 3 • -associated radical oxidation, while freely diffusing • OH contributed only marginally. Matrix tests further indicated that PE/PI is better suited to relatively clean waters, whereas PE/PMS offers greater robustness in complex matrices. This work extends empirical oxidant comparison toward descriptor-informed interpretation of oxidant-dependent activation.

title: Capturing the dual organic-metal hazard of fire smoke: Material-dependent passive sampling of PAHs and battery-derived metals
abstract: Wildland-urban interface and battery-involved fires emit chemically complex smoke containing carcinogenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and metal-rich aerosols. However, the comparative performance of passive sampler materials under these conditions remains poorly defined. This study evaluated six chemically and structurally distinct materials: silicone wristband (SWB), polyurethane foam (PUF), activated carbon felt (ACF), thermoplastic polyurethane nanofiber (TPU), cotton fabric (CF), and cotton ball (CB) under controlled smoke from pine, pine + polystyrene (PS), and pine + battery scenarios. The 16 priority PAHs listed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, along with battery-derived elements, were quantified and benchmarked against active sampling. Active sampling showed clear source-dependent profiles: total PAHs increased from 10.2 µg m⁻³ in pine smoke to 167.8 µg m⁻³ in pine + PS smoke, while pine + battery smoke was dominated by metal-rich aerosol, especially nickel (∼840 µg m⁻³). Passive uptake was strongly material dependent. Under the high-PAH pine + PS scenario, PUF retained the highest total PAHs (∼1.50 µg cm⁻²), followed by TPU (∼1.24 µg cm⁻²) and SWB (∼1.11 µg cm⁻²). ACF showed selective naphthalene enrichment, whereas SWB retained the highest battery-derived metal loading (∼46 µg cm⁻²), followed by PUF (∼38 µg cm⁻²) and TPU (∼30 µg cm⁻²). Scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy indicated that PAH uptake was governed mainly by sorption and partitioning, while metal retention reflected particle deposition and surface adhesion. These findings highlight the need for complementary, multi-material sampling strategies matched to the target exposure metric.

title: Influence of root morphology and salinity on PFAS uptake by ten Australian wetland plant species
abstract: Constructed Floating Wetlands (CFWs) show promise as nature-based technology for attenuating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in surface water. However, few studies have investigated plant morphological and physiological characteristics that promote PFAS uptake. This study assessed ten wetland plant species exposed to PFAS-spiked stormwater (PFBS, PFPeA, PFHxS, PFOA, PFOS, 30 µg/L each), for 28 days, under two salinity conditions (200 and 1000 mg/L). At low salinity, all species accumulated PFAS, with variation according to species. T. triandra, P. labillardieri, and S. validus were most effective for short-chain compounds (5740-6610 ng PFBS, and 4330-5290 ng PFPeA), whereas E. acuta, C. fascicularis, P. labillardieri, and B. caldwellii accumulated more long-chain compounds (2040-2390 ng PFHxS, 6100-6590 ng PFOS, and 2320-2830 ng PFOA). Plants with thin, branched roots showed greater PFAS accumulation. Bioaccumulation data highlighted that PFAS carbon chain length influenced PFAS partitioning, with PFOS showing limited shoot translocation compared with PFBS and PFPeA (translocation factors: 0.2-2.8 vs 0.4-34.0 vs 0.5-24.6). Elevated salinity significantly suppressed the uptake and translocation of short-chain PFAS (particularly PFPeA), while long-chain compounds were less affected. Results suggest that species selection for CFW must consider plant morphology and site-specific water parameters for optimum removal of complex PFAS mixtures.

title: MOF-on-MOF-derived Co3O4@ZnO@Hemin peroxidase-like nanozyme for ultrasensitive detection of organophosphorus pesticides in vegetables and lake water
abstract: To address threats of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) residues to food safety and environmental health, this study developed a core-shell-shell nanozyme (Co 3 O 4 @ZnO@Hemin) for sensitive OPs detection in multiple real samples. The nanozyme integrates nanocatalyst electronic effects with biomimetic hydrophobic microenvironment functionality, fabricated by pyrolyzing a ZIF-67@ZIF-8 metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF precursor, followed by Hemin loading. Remarkably, this nanozyme exhibits specific peroxidase-like activity, attributed to the mesoporous Co 3 O 4 @ZnO structure that promotes electron transfer and provides bimetallic mixed-valence active sites. Meanwhile, Hemin incorporation further increases oxygen vacancies through electronic regulation and enhances hydrophobicity, synergistically boosting catalytic performance. Therefore, this nanozyme sensor platform achieved ultrasensitive acetylcholinesterase (AChE) detection with a detection limit (LOD) of 0.07 mU mL⁻¹ and quantitative trichlorfon detection (1-5 ng·mL -1 , LOD 0.10 ng·mL -1 ), successfully applied to detect trichlorfon in lettuce, cucumber, bok choy, and lake water, with 90.21-105.91% recoveries and RSDs below 4.62%. This study provides a bioinspired nanozyme strategy for sensing.

title: Corrigendum to “Regenerable Cu2S-CuO heterostructure nanoarray electrode for efficient electrochemical iodate reduction” [J Hazard Mater 516 (2026) 143304]
vToxiNet: An interpretable deep learning framework for hepatotoxicity prediction and mechanism exploration
abstract: Hepatotoxicity remains a leading cause of drug attrition and post-marketing withdrawal, resulting from diverse and complex toxicity mechanisms. Traditional in vitro models can only capture a limited subset of toxicity pathways, and animal studies face translational and ethical limitations. Regulatory agencies have therefore promoted new approach methodologies, including human-relevant assays, omics technologies, and computational models to improve predictive toxicology and support evidence-based decision-making. However, most machine learning models for hepatotoxicity either rely solely on chemical structure or operate as black boxes, limiting mechanistic interpretability and broader applicability. Here, we introduce the virtual toxicity network (vToxiNet), a biologically constrained deep learning framework that embeds systems toxicology knowledge directly into neural network architecture for interpretable hepatotoxicity prediction. vToxiNet integrates chemical descriptors, high-throughput assay responses, transcriptomic signatures, and Reactome pathway hierarchy to construct a virtual adverse outcome pathway network. Across cross-validation and external validation, vToxiNet demonstrates promising predictive performance. Importantly, interpretation of vToxiNet enables gene and pathway-level attribution, supporting mechanism-informed hazard characterization and chemical prioritization. By integrating multimodal data and biological hierarchy as architectural constraints, this study provides a framework that combines prediction with mechanistic interpretation and supports further development of mechanism-informed approaches for chemical hazard assessment.

title: Spatiotemporally adaptive optimization of groundwater remediation: Well-network system design and multi-stage operation
abstract: Groundwater remediation under stringent resource and time constraints requires coordinated decisions on where extraction infrastructure is deployed and how pumping is operated over time. Conventional pump-and-treat optimization often addresses strategic well-network design and dynamic pumping operation separately, limiting the coordinated use of evolving hydraulic and concentration fields in heterogeneous aquifers. Here, we developed an optimization framework incorporating mixed-variable well-network design and multi-stage pumping optimization under concentration and hydraulic-head constraints. Mixed-variable NSGA-II identifies Pareto-optimal combinations of well number, location, pumping rate and remediation duration, after which the selected solution is refined by reallocating pumping between stages according to simulated plume evolution. The framework was evaluated using two-dimensional and three-dimensional heterogeneous aquifer models and applied to a chromium-contaminated field site initialized from monitoring data. In the three-dimensional case, multi-stage operation reduced estimated pumping energy cost by 35.3% relative to the selected single-stage solution. At the field site, multi-objective optimization reduced cumulative pumping by 27.3% using existing wells, and multi-stage operation achieved a further 2.8% reduction while maintaining modeled contaminant mass removal within 1.6% of the single-stage solution. This work shifts groundwater management from experience-led heuristic designs toward model-driven, precision decision-making, providing a resource-efficient approach for pump-and-treat remediation of groundwater contamination.

title: Weathering chemistry shapes the gut microbiome–metabolome–transcriptome response of adult zebrafish to aged polyethylene microplastics
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquatic environments undergo continuous weathering, yet most toxicological studies still rely on pristine commercial particles, leaving biological consequences of distinct aging chemistries poorly resolved. Here, polyethylene (PE) MPs were aged through oxidative and hydrolytic pathways (UV+H₂O, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, and NaOH), characterized by FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy) and SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy), and administered to zebrafish to link surface chemistry with the multilayered gut microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome responses. Weathering chemistry governed surface oxidation and morphological damage, with strong-acid treatment (H₂SO₄ ≫ HNO₃) causing the most severe fragmentation. These surface differences propagated into chemistry-specific effects: an abundance-driven restructuring of the gut microbiota, including suppression of the core commensal Cetobacterium under alkaline aging and expansion of stress-tolerant environmental taxa; weathering-specific remodeling of the metabolome (NAD⁺/nicotinamide and glycosphingolipid); and low but treatment-specific transcriptional changes (6-13 DEGs per treatment, including a shared ∼800-fold induction of lhfpl5b under NaOH and UV+H₂O). Multi-omics integration resolved into three chemistry-specific cross-omics axes, with the metabolome and transcriptome showing the strongest cross-layer concordance (Procrustes 1-M 2 = 0.38, p < 0.01). Weathered MPs from different degradation pathways cannot be aggregated into a single "aged-MP" category, as their hazards are chemistry-specific at every molecular layer.

title: VOC evolution during petrochemical abnormal operations and vertical characteristics during shutdown: Evidence from ground and tower observations
abstract: Petrochemical shutdown, maintenance, and start-up operations emit substantial amounts of reactive volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, the vertical distribution of these emissions within the lower boundary layer remains poorly characterized. This study combined full-cycle online monitoring with shutdown-stage multi-height tower sampling (10, 50 and 90 m) and receptor-site observations to investigate VOC evolution, vertical profiles, and spatial transport in a large petrochemical park. After meteorological normalization, mean TVOC concentrations during shutdown, maintenance, and start-up were 97.59, 106.62 and 85.36 ppbv, respectively. VOC composition showed more pronounced stage-dependent changes. Alkenes increased by 53.69% during maintenance, with ethene reaching 32.13 ppbv. Propylene and 1,3-butadiene increased markedly during start-up. During shutdown, TVOC showed a non-monotonic vertical profile and peaked at 146.29 ppbv at 50 m, 1.52 times that at 10 m. The difference between 10 and 50 m was significant (p OH ) and ozone formation potential (OFP) also peaked at 50 m, reaching 32.07 s⁻ 1 and 1160.73 μg m⁻ 3 , respectively. After normalization, L OH /TVOC was similar at 10 and 50 m, while OFP/TVOC increased with height. Near-ground observations within the park and at the tower during the shutdown stage showed reduced VOC concentration fluctuations during transport, accompanied by a shift from alkane- and alkene-dominated composition toward greater OVOC contributions. Combined near-ground and multi-height tower observations during shutdown highlighted the potential limitations of single-height near-ground monitoring in characterizing vertical variations in elevated plumes. These measurements support the value of height-resolved observations for characterizing reactive VOCs during petrochemical shutdown.

title: An explainable machine learning framework for predicting colloid-mediated release of potentially toxic elements from Pb/Zn smelter contaminated soils
abstract: To date, how the physicochemical properties of soil colloids contribute to the prediction and explanation of PTEs release remain unclear. Therefore, the machine learning (ML) model framework was developed and optimized to accurately predict PTEs concentrations in soil colloid solutions. The results indicated that colloid concentrations were within the order of 10 10 particles/mL, with the zeta potential ranging from -49.5 to -5.60 mV, and the median particle sizes (D50) ranging between 190 and 200 nm. The mean PTEs concentrations followed the decreasing order of Zn (68.23 mg/L) > Cd (2.98 mg/L) > Pb (0.78 mg/L) > As (0.12 mg/L). A two-stage model coupled with random forest (RF) classification and gradient boost regression tree (GBRT) regression could greatly improve As and Pb prediction accuracy (R 2 >0.85). The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model combining with logarithmic transformation achieved the higher predictive performance for Cd (R 2 =0.97). XGBoost further incorporating Winsorize processing and logarithmic transformation demonstrated the better predictive performance for Zn (R 2 =0.97). Relative importance analysis further indicated that soil types and colloid properties were the most influential factors for PTEs release. Collectively, these findings could provide the technical support for the risk prediction and management of PTEs in contaminated sites.

title: Enhanced phytoremediation of Cd- phenanthrene co-contaminated soil through the combined application of electric field and chemical additives
abstract: Electric fields and chemical additives can enhance phytoremediation, but their synergistic mechanisms in cadmium (Cd)-phenanthrene (PHE) co-contaminated soils remain unclear. Here, a greenhouse pot experiment was conducted to investigate the combined effects of a direct‑current electric field and chemical additives (citric acid + ammonium nitrate) on the phytoremediation of Cd-PHE co‑contaminated soil using marigold (Tagetes patula L.). The combined treatment (Phy‑CN‑EK) achieved the highest PHE removal (82.3%) and total shoot Cd uptake (41.443 μg pot -1 ), and simultaneously increased the relative abundance of potential PHE-degrading functional bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Saccharimonadaceae. The results suggested that the chemical additives accelerated the initial oxidative degradation of PHE, while the electric field subsequently promoted the complete mineralization of its intermediates. For Cd uptake, the chemical additives directly enhanced phytoextraction but indirectly suppressed it via a shift toward Pseudomonas dominance; conversely, the electric field promoted Cd uptake by enhancing plant biomass and facilitating intermediate mineralization, thereby counteracting the microbial-driven suppression. Their integration achieved synergistic enhancement of both PHE degradation and Cd phytoextraction. These findings deepen the understanding of the combined enhancement mechanisms in phytoremediation of Cd-PAH co-contaminated soils and provide a mechanistic basis for future field-scale validation and optimization.

title: Tracing 3D printing emissions: Micro- and nanoplastic formation and the trade-off of mass-based mitigation
abstract: The widespread adoption of fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printing introduces undocumented inhalation risks from airborne micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) in indoor microenvironments. While prior studies have focused on non-specific nanoparticles and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), the precise chemical identity, emission mechanisms, and respiratory fate of printing-emitted MNPs remain critical knowledge gaps. This study systematically quantified MNP emissions across five commercial filament types using size-resolved monitoring, morphological analysis and pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (Py-GC-MS). Substantial MNP emissions were observed for ASA and ABS filaments (2.3 ± 1.0 and 0.6 ± 0.3 mg kg -1 , respectively). Crucially, morphological evidence of droplet condensation combined with chemical characterization revealed that these emitted MNPs predominantly comprised polyethylene (PE) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) not originating from the parent polymer matrices. Furthermore, respiratory dosimetry modeling unveiled a mitigation trade-off: while standard FDM enclosures removed > 90% of total nanoparticle mass, they selectively allowed ultrafine nanoparticles to escape, inadvertently driving the pulmonary deposition fraction of inhaled mass from 10.3% to 19.8% in adults, and up to 29.5% in children. These findings highlight that mass-based metrics alone do not fully capture changes in inhalation exposure and respiratory deposition patterns. We advocate for integrating particle number concentrations into indoor air quality standards and requiring disclosure and regulation of all filament constituents to reduce potential MNP exposure at the source.

title: Sustained hydrogen delivery enhances microbiome-associated cadmium and copper immobilization in co-contaminated soils
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H₂) is an important energy source for soil microbes and has been implicated in biogeochemical regulation; however, whether-and how-exogenous H₂ inputs promote Cd and Cu immobilization in co-contaminated soils remains unclear. We engineered MgH₂-biochar granules capable of sustained H₂ release for up to 448 h. The granules exhibited high adsorption capacities in aqueous Cd-Cu systems (Cu: 59.76 mg g⁻¹; Cd: 35.76 mg g⁻¹). In soil, MgH₂-biochar treatment was associated with enhanced microbial hydrogenase activity, reduced oxidative stress, and enrichment of functional taxa, together with significant reductions in available Cd (10.9-22.5%) and Cu (14.2-30.1%) (P < 0.05). Notably, Mg-associated alkalization elevated soil pH and contributed to physicochemical immobilization. Microbial community analyses further revealed H₂-associated shifts in community structure and significant associations between H₂ metabolism and metal resistance (Cd: P < 0.001; Cu: P < 0.03). Genome-resolved metagenomics identified 10 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) that co-harbour [NiFe]-hydrogenases (Groups 1 and 4) and Cd/Cu resistance genes (e.g., actS, czcA, and copC). Exploratory pathway modeling further indicated associations of Cd/Cu immobilization with H₂-associated microbial processes and Mg-associated physicochemical effects. This work provides integrated material, geochemical, and microbial evidence supporting an H₂-associated contribution to heavy-metal immobilization in soils.

title: Ag-SnO2 nanofibers with lattice oxygen activation for high performance triethylamine gas sensor
abstract: TEA is a highly flammable and neurotoxic volatile organic compound; prolonged exposure can lead to emphysema and even immediate death, making the development of rapid, highly responsive TEA gas sensors an urgent priority. Although tin dioxide (SnO 2 )-based sensors have been extensively studied, they suffer from low sensitivity and high operating temperatures. In this study, silver-loaded tin dioxide nanofibers (Ag-SnO 2 NFs) with a porous hollow structure were fabricated using electrospinning combined with in-situ reduction technology. The Schottky junction at the Ag-SnO 2 interface triggers interfacial electron redistribution, thereby activating lattice oxygen (O L ) in SnO 2 and converting it into adsorbed oxygen species, which enhances the gas-sensing performance for TEA. At 200℃, the AS-2 sensor exhibited a response value of 2163.6 for 100 ppm of TEA, which is 79 times that of pure SnO 2 , and demonstrated fast response and recovery times (48 s/44 s). In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated this mechanism. This study provides a new mechanistic insight into how noble metal modification activates lattice oxygen and converts it into adsorbed oxygen to enhance gas sensing performance, offering rational design principles for advanced gas sensors targeting harmful volatile compounds.

title: Facet-dependent activation of chlorine dioxide over Mn2O3 for benzo[a]pyrene degradation
abstract: Benzo[a]pyrene (Bap) is a representative highly recalcitrant and extremely toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon. Although chlorine dioxide (ClO 2 ) oxidation technology can be employed for Bap treatment, it often suffers from incomplete oxidation and the residual accumulation of highly toxic intermediate products. In this study, a series of Mn 2 O 3 catalysts with different exposed facets are synthesized to regulate ClO 2 activation pathways for deep Bap degradation. The cubic Mn 2 O 3 exposing predominantly (001) facets possesses more oxygen vacancies and facilitates the adsorption of ClO 2 species. These adsorbed ClO 2 species subsequently undergo coupling disproportionation to generate singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) and chlorine radical species (•ClO), while concurrently enabling the formation of transient high-valent Mn V (O) + species. The synergistic interaction between 1 O 2 and Mn V (O) + establishes a non-radical-dominated oxidation regime, leading to an efficient Bap degradation rate exceeding 97.6% and excellent stability. In contrast, Mn 2 O 3 exposing (111) facets with fewer oxygen vacancies shows lower activity because Bap degradation proceeds mainly via hydroxyl radical (•OH)-dominated pathways. This work demonstrates that the facet engineering of Mn 2 O 3 can be tuned to regulate the activation pathways of chlorine dioxide, providing fundamental mechanistic insight and a rational design strategy for the efficient and deep oxidation of persistent polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: Viral regulation of N2O emissions depends on soil acidity
abstract: Acidification generally enhances N 2 O emissions from soils. Yet, the adaptive responses of denitrifiers and the regulatory roles of soil viruses in denitrifier-mediated N 2 O emissions under persistent acidity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined D 2 O-labeled single-cell Raman spectroscopy, 15 N tracing, metagenomics, machine learning, and virus-addition experiments to examine virus-denitrifier interactions across soils with contrasting long-term acidity conditions maintained for > 17 years. Acidic soils showed the highest N 2 O emissions despite the lowest potential denitrification rate and highest microbial anabolic activity. Denitrifiers and viral populations in acidic soils exhibited reduced microdiversity, stronger purifying selection, and distinct functional specialization, while viruses showed a lower virulent-to-temperate ratio and greater genetic potential for host interaction and persistence. Host antiviral defense capacity was the strongest genomic predictor of abundance responses to active virus. In acidic soils, active viruses increased N 2 O reductase level by 33.2% without altering nosZ abundance and reduced N 2 O accumulation by up to 62.5%, indicating an efficiency-optimized response. Neutral soils showed a quantity-driven response, whereas alkaline soils showed no significant reduction in N 2 O accumulation. These findings reveal acidity-dependent viral regulation of N 2 O emissions, strongest in long-term acidic soils.

title: PFAS removal from drinking water and semiconductor wastewater by microbubble foam fractionation
abstract: Efficient separation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from complex water matrices remains challenging because treatment performance depends on both PFAS concentration and matrix composition. This study evaluated microbubble foam fractionation (FF) in simulated waters, drinking water source waters, and real semiconductor wastewater, with and without coagulant addition. In simulated wastewater, adding 2000 mg/L NH₄Cl enhanced PFAS removal, consistent with an ionic-strength contribution. Within 20 min, FF removed 91-98% of PFOA, PFOS, and PFHxS and approximately 91% of PFBS from a natural source water with individual PFAS concentrations of 2-19 μg/L. Removal was lower in a second source water containing 0.4-1.2 μg/L PFAS but improved with coagulant addition. In semiconductor wastewater containing 0.1-0.6 μg/L PFAS, removal reached 94-99% for PFOA, PFOS, and PFHxS and approximately 90% for PFBS. These contrasting results highlight the importance of water matrix composition in enabling effective separation at low PFAS concentrations. To explore potential downstream treatment, UV/sulfite reduction was separately evaluated using a model concentrate containing 20 mg/L total PFAS. Complete parent-compound removal was achieved for PFOA, PFOS, and PFHxS within approximately 30 min, 110 min, and 7 h, respectively, whereas PFBS removal reached approximately 63% after 8 h. These findings support matrix-specific application of microbubble FF as a PFAS concentration pretreatment and provide a basis for developing multistage FF coupled with downstream UV/sulfite treatment.

title: Comparative fate and risk of microplastics in sanitary landfills versus open dumping sites: A multidimensional assessment framework
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills are critical terrestrial reservoirs of microplastics (MPs), yet how disposal methodology governs MP fate remains poorly constrained, hindering accurate risk assessment and management. Here, we systematically compared MP pollution between an engineered sanitary landfill (SL) and an open dumping site (OD) in East China through field investigation and laboratory simulation. We analyzed spatial distribution, physicochemical characteristics, and release potential of MPs, and developed a novel Index (MDAI) that integrates soil species sensitivity distribution (SSD), abundance, size, shape, and polymer hazard to assess ecological risk. Results revealed that MP abundance in SL (5340-12,670 particles/kg soil) markedly exceeded that in OD (2100-5620 particles/kg soil), with SL exhibiting a distinct vertical accumulation gradient absent in OD. MP abundance on plastic waste were substantially higher, reaching 29,740 particles/kg plastic on deeply buried SL plastics. MPs in SL were predominantly small-sized fragments and films dominated by polypropylene, whereas OD contained more fibers and medium-sized fragments dominated by polyethylene. Surrounding soils of the OD showed higher MP levels and extremely high potential ecological risk (PERI), whereas those of the SL exhibited only Level III risk. Plastic waste from both sites demonstrated ongoing MP release potential, most pronounced for deeply buried SL waste. The MDAI indicated a higher comprehensive risk within SL (Level III) versus moderate but spatially dispersed risk around OD (Level II). This spatial disparity highlights distinct management priorities: for SL, ensuring long-term containment to prevent release of internally accumulated MPs; for OD, implementing immediate source control and migration barriers to limit off-site dispersion. This study provides a critical, multidimensional framework for assessing and managing MP pollution from these predominant waste disposal pathways.

title: Biochar and drilosphere soil synergistically form a low-cadmium, high-nutrient remediation hotspot: Insights from microbial functional gene and enzymatic stoichiometry analyses
abstract: The drilosphere is a biogeochemical hotspot, but its role in biochar-assisted remediation of cadmium (Cd)-contaminated soil remains unclear. Comparisons were made between fresh (RS) and aged rice straw (ARS) biochar treatments at different Cd contamination levels to assess their effects on the drilosphere microenvironment. The results showed that ARS biochar was more effective in forming a low‑Cd, high‑nutrient hotspot, reducing total Cd in burrow wall soil (BWS) by 13.42% and increased TOC, TN, and TP by 17.89%, 76.16%, and 132.36% (P lightly disturbed soil > undisturbed soil. Under low Cd, ARS biochar decreased microbial C limitation by 5.21% but increased N limitation by 8.81% (P < 0.05); no effect at high Cd. RS biochar increased bacterial α-diversity (Chao1) (2.41%, P < 0.05), decreased archaeal (14.00%) and fungal (2.16%) diversity, enriched Myxococcota, Gemmatimonadota, Acidobacteriota (72.64%-216.67%), and reduced Firmicutes (47.83%). ARS biochar decreased drilosphere pH and altered eco-enzymatic stoichiometry, making archaeal and fungal α-diversity significantly correlated with C-N-P enzyme activities. It enriched Acidobacteriota (116.30%) and increased Firmicutes, Actinobacteriota, Planctomycetota (60.08%-75.52%), showing a distinct pattern (Acidobacteriota, Firmicutes) contrasting with RS biochar (Myxococcota, Gemmatimonadota). Under low Cd, both RS and ARS biochar promoted C fixation (AA/GT genes, 3.98%-5.75%) and inhibited C decomposition (PL/GH genes, 4.00%-11.37%); compared to RS biochar, ARS biochar significantly enhanced denitrification (4.47%) and nitrification (14.41%), inhibited anammox (45.17%), and upregulated P metabolism pathways (2.54%-6.73%). Under high Cd, both RS and ARS biochar shifted to promoting C decomposition and inhibiting C fixation; ARS biochar maintained N fixation capacity (19.8%) and enhanced organic P hydrolysis (9.99%) (P < 0.05), indicating that ARS biochar retains key nutrient cycling potential under Cd stress. Thus, biochar aging status is crucial for synergistic drilosphere remediation, offering a strategy for simultaneous Cd immobilization and soil fertility improvement.

title: CBP inhibition and histone H3K18 hypoacetylation induced by the hematotoxic benzene metabolite 1,4-benzoquinone
abstract: Benzene (BZ) is a pervasive environmental and occupational carcinogen whose leukemogenicity depends on metabolic activation into reactive intermediates, notably 1,4-benzoquinone (BQ). While genotoxic effects such as DNA damage and chromosomal instability have been extensively documented, growing evidence highlights a central role for epigenetic dysregulation in BZ-induced hematotoxicity. In this study, we identify a novel molecular mechanism linking BZ metabolism to epigenetic dysfunction. We demonstrate that BQ irreversibly inhibits the histone H3K18 acetyltransferase activity of CREB-binding protein (CREBBP/CBP), a key epigenetic regulator essential for normal hematopoiesis and tumor suppression. Mechanistically, BQ rapidly forms covalent adducts with critical cysteine residues, notably within the RING and PHD Zn²⁺-finger domains of CBP, thereby impairing its catalytic activity. Both in vitro and cellular models show that BQ exposure markedly reduces CBP acetyltransferase activity, accompanied by decreased levels of the epigenetic mark H3K18Ac. These findings identify CBP as a direct molecular target of benzene metabolites and reveal an epigenetic mechanism that may contribute to the hematotoxic and leukemogenic effects of BZ.

title: Emerging plastic additives in umbilical cord serum, metabolomic profiles, and fetal growth restriction: A case-control study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with substantial perinatal and long-term health risks. As traditional plasticizers are being restricted, exposure to emerging plastic additives is increasing, yet their associations with FGR and related metabolic profiles remain poorly characterized. METHODS: This case-control study included 90 FGR cases and 100 controls from the "Early Life Plan" cohort. A total of 117 plastic additives were measured in umbilical cord serum, and untargeted metabolomics was performed using UHPLC-HRMS. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and quantile g-computation were used to evaluate the effects of single and mixed exposures of these chemicals on fetal growth outcomes. Meet-in-the-middle (MITM) analysis and pathway enrichment analysis were performed to identify associated metabolic features. RESULTS: UV-360 was positively associated with FGR (OR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.11-1.64), while 2,6-DtBEP was negatively associated with FGR (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.61-0.84). Neither BKMR nor quantile g-computation provided clear evidence of an overall association between the 21-chemical mixture and FGR. Exploratory class-specific BKMR analyses suggested positive and negative associations for UV stabilizers and antioxidants, respectively. Differential metabolites were mainly enriched in amino acid, lipid, and one-carbon metabolism. MITM analyses suggested that six metabolites, including Valine, Proline, Palmitoylcarnitine, Ornithine, Xanthine, and (25 R)-Delta(4)-dafachronic acid, may be involved in the associations of UV-360 and DiBA/DnBA with FGR. CONCLUSIONS: Concentrations of selected plastic additives in umbilical cord serum were associated with FGR, with UV-360 being consistently associated with higher odds of FGR. Metabolomic findings suggest that amino acid and lipid metabolism may be involved in these associations, warranting further validation in future studies.

title: Solar-hydrodynamic energy coupling enables round-the-clock algal inactivation in natural waters
abstract: Sustainable mitigation of harmful algal blooms in natural waters remains constrained by intermittent energy supply, quenching of reactive species (RS) in complex matrices, and limited recoverability of conventional nanocatalysts. Here, we report a piezo-photocatalytic strategy integrating ambient solar and hydrodynamic energy harvesting with floating catalyst deployment and selective RS regulation, enabling round-the-clock in situ algal control under realistic aquatic conditions. A Bi 4 O 5 I 2 /Bi 2 O 2 S (6BIS) heterojunction couples light and mechanical energy harvesting, extending catalytic activity across illuminated and dark conditions when the corresponding energy input is available. In the dark, weak mechanical agitation yields ∼50% algal inactivation within 4.5 h via limited piezoelectric activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS), increasing to 90% under ultrasonic stimulation. Under combined ultrasound and low-intensity visible light, complete algal inactivation is achieved within 2.5 h. Microcystin-LR (0.5 mg L -1 ) is degraded within 5 min. Mechanistic investigations reveal that PMS adsorption at Bi sites selectively promotes superoxide radicals and singlet oxygen, mitigating quenching by humic substances. Field tests using a floating-supported catalyst achieved 55% algal inactivation within 8 h under natural sunlight and ambient hydrodynamic conditions. This work provides a strategy for improving the temporal continuity of environmental remediation by coupling ambient renewable energy harvesting with selective RS regulation.

title: Accumulation mechanisms and source-specific risks of PAHs across indoor and outdoor environments in a typical petrochemical industrial park
abstract: Prolonged petrochemical activities severely exacerbate polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in surrounding areas; however, the differential accumulation mechanisms and source-specific risks of these pollutants across off-site indoor and outdoor environments remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated PAH occurrence and risks in soil, road dust, and indoor dust surrounding a typical petrochemical industrial park to elucidate their divergent multimedia accumulation pathways. The mean concentrations of ∑ 16 PAHs (μg/kg) in soil, road dust, and indoor dust within the study area were 5.94 × 10 2 , 4.66 × 10 3 , and 5.28 × 10 3 , respectively, with a mixed combustion-related source identified as the largest contributor to regional PAH contamination. An integrated analysis combining gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT) and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) indicated that multimedia PAH accumulation was shaped by the complex interplay between intrinsic matrix properties and external inputs. Specifically, total organic carbon (TOC) may directly influence PAH retention across the three matrices, while petrochemical sources and wind direction may indirectly affect PAH accumulation through matrix carbon content; traffic emissions likely intensify PAH loading in roadside environments. Additionally, source-specific assessments showed that road and indoor dust had higher PAH pollution and greater health risks than soil, with petrochemical-associated sources contributing most to both. This study advances understanding of PAH accumulation and distribution across multimedia environments under intensive industrial activities, providing a scientific basis for targeted PAH mitigation in industrial areas.

title: Rhizospheric phosphorus activation drives microbial degradation of tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate
abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs), such as tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP), undergo accelerated microbial degradation in the rhizosphere, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Given their structural similarity to natural organophosphorus compounds, we hypothesized that rhizospheric phosphorus cycling contributes to OPE degradation. Using DNA-stable isotope probing, we identified active TCEP degraders and linked them to soil phosphate fractions.
