Plant cultivation reshaped degrader communities, increasing their relative abundance by 80.7% and predicted functional gene content by 20.8%, while reducing interactions between degraders and non-degraders. Rhizospheric TCEP degraders exhibited a lower average phylogenetic distance than those in non-rhizosphere soils (0.58 vs. 0.64). This contrasts with the greater phylogenetic breadth observed for rhizospheric PAH and PCB degraders. The reduced phylogenetic breadth suggests that TCEP degradation may be more functionally conserved and dominated by specialized taxa, potentially reflecting phosphatase-mediated processes rather than cooperative, multi-taxon degradation networks. TCEP degradation correlated negatively with total phosphorus but positively with bioavailable phosphorus, indicating a key role of plant-mediated phosphorus solubilization in regulating degrader composition and activity. Increased alkaline phosphatase activity further supported this interpretation. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which rhizospheric nutrient cycling regulates TCEP degradation, advancing our understanding of phosphorus-microbe interactions in pollutant biotransformation within plant-soil systems. SYNOPSIS: Plant-mediated phosphorus cycling in the rhizosphere selectively enriches TCEP-degrading microbes, uncovering a novel link between nutrient availability and pollutant biotransformation in soil ecosystems.

title: Mechanisms of biochar derived from chicken manure or rice straw that effectively immobilizes cadmium do not apply to sewage-sludge biochar
abstract: In order to explore immobilization characteristic and its possible mechanism of various feedstocks-based biochars, deriving from chicken manure (CMB), rice straw (RSB) and sewage sludge (SSB), the effect of three biochars on speciation transformation of Cd in soil was compared, and soil properties, microbial community diversity were also examined. The treatment of CMB and RSB reduced significantly the content of acid-extractable Cd by 53.62% and 41.18%, respectively, but this available fraction was increased by 23.44% after SSB treatment. Simultaneously, CMB and RSB treatment significantly increased the soil pH, CEC, TOC, AN, AP, TK, microbial biomass carbon, dehydrogenase, phosphatase, catalase and urease enzyme activity, while SSB treatment slightly increased AP and TK content, only decreased urease enzyme activity. Lower bacterial alpha diversity was observed at the initial sampling of day 0, whereas treatment differences in bacterial Shannon diversity were not significant at day 225, it suggested that their effects on microbial alpha diversity were dependent on sampling stage and microbial kingdom. Partial least squares modelling (PLS-PM) speculated that CMB and RSB treatment decreased available Cd through direct effect of biochar and indirect effect of soil, whereas SSB treatment elevated available metal by indirect effect. This increase might be due to the decrease of urease activity indirectly affected by SSB, thus decelerating Cd precipitation and enhancing available Cd. These results deepen our understanding on the degree of immobilization and underlying mechanisms for Cd in soil that is critical for evaluating the application of effective biochar treatments.

title: Molecular transformation of dissolved black carbon during photobleaching and its enhanced role in goethite-mediated 17α-ethinylestradiol anaerobic biotransformation
abstract: Dissolved black carbon (DBC) is an important component of dissolved organic matter, which undergoes continuous photobleaching in the sunlit surface water. The resulting photobleached DBC (P-DBC) can subsequently be transported across the sediment-water interface into sediments rich in minerals and microbes, thereby regulating the transformation of organic contaminants. This study investigated photobleaching-induced molecular transformation of DBC and the mechanism of P-DBC in goethite-mediated 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2) anaerobic biotransformation. The results showed that photobleaching promoted the oxidation and decarbonization of DBC, driving its molecular composition toward a higher oxidation state and lower energy density. Intensity and H content were the key molecular features governing the photochemical reactivity of DBC. P-DBC was enriched in oxygen-containing functional groups that could enhance electron transfer with goethite. Additionally, the higher bioavailability of P‑DBC enriched aromatic‑degrading bacteria. Species associated with iron reduction and organic matter transformation in the presence of goethite were increased. As a result, P-DBC combined with goethite significantly promoted the anaerobic biotransformation of EE2, achieving a removal efficiency of 73.0%. EE2 transformation involved de-ethynylation and decarboxylation to yield more oxygenated products, contrasting with co‑metabolism alone. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the natural attenuation of estrogens in iron-rich aquatic environments.

title: Overlooked Pb–(Sn)–(Sb)–(As) oxide particles in incineration bottom ash: Particle-scale occurrence, alteration and potential relevance to antimony and arsenic mobility
abstract: Antimony (Sb) is a critical metal and an emerging hazardous pollutant, chemically akin to arsenic (As), and is widely used as antimonial lead in Pb–(Sn)–Sb–(As) alloys. A substantial fraction of the Sb fed to municipal solid waste (MSW) incinerators remains in incineration bottom ash (IBA), where Sb leaching, together with that of As, restricts IBA reuse. We document, at the particle scale, the occurrence of Pb–(Sn)–(Sb)–(As) oxide particles in the 0.25–2 mm fractions of IBA from several facilities in France. Seven particles were characterized in detail by optical microscopy, SEM–BSE–XEDS, PXRD, and S/TEM–XEDS with dual-range EELS. The particles span a continuum of apparent alteration states, from Pb–(Sn)–(Sb) metallic cores with incipient oxide crusts to hollow, fully oxidized, brittle polycrystalline shells with distinctive yellow to brown-reddish colours. EELS features are consistent with Sb(III) and higher Sb oxidation states and XEDS phase maps show that As is concentrated together with Sb in Ca-bearing Pb–Sb–As oxide domains of the alteration rims. The assemblages constitute an overlooked, dense host of Sb and As in IBA that complement the calcium-antimonate framework; Because these particles are much denser than the silicate-carbonate ash matrix, density-based separation of IBA fines is a natural candidate for their removal.

title: Machine learning-driven high-throughput prediction of Hg0 capture in MOFs and decipherment of structure-property relationships
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show potential for Hg 0 adsorption via tunable pore structures and chemical functionalities. However, efficient screening of MOF adsorbents remains challenging due to vast material space and unclear structure-property relationships. Herein, a Hg 0 adsorption database of 6528 MOF samples was established, and machine learning models were developed for predicting adsorption performance. Among tested models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) exhibited the best prediction on the independent test set, achieving a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.893. SHAP analysis revealed that energy descriptors, including logarithmic Henry coefficient (log(K H )) and adsorption enthalpy (ΔH ads ), dominated Hg 0 adsorption, while structural descriptors further regulated adsorption behavior. Combined model interpretation revealed a condition-dependent interaction between adsorption affinity and pore characteristics. High-throughput screening revealed characteristic descriptor intervals for high-performing MOFs, including log(K H )=-3.62 to -2.61, ΔH ads = -34.60 to -25.21 kJ·mol -1 , and VF = 0.67-0.78. MOFid-based structural analysis identified significant enrichment of Cr, Fe, Co nodes and nbo topology, alongside preferred acs and tbo topologies, as well as nitrogen-containing aromatic conjugated heterocyclic ligands in high-performing MOFs. These findings clarify the roles of metal nodes, topology, and ligand chemistry in Hg 0 adsorption and provide a machine learning-driven strategy for rational design of MOF-based mercury removal adsorbents.

title: Substrate-dependent attenuation of antibiotic and metal resistance genes during acidogenic fermentation of titanium-flocculated sludge
abstract: Titanium-based coagulation enables efficient wastewater purification and sludge recovery, yet the fate of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and metal resistance genes (MRGs) during downstream sludge valorization remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated how food waste-derived substrates affected fermentation performance and ARGs/MRGs profiles during 7-day acidogenic co-fermentation of Ti-flocculated sludge. Substrate composition resulted in distinct fermentation characteristics and resistome responses. Compared with refractory fiber-rich substrates, readily hydrolysable starch promoted organic solubilization and acidogenesis, producing the highest soluble chemical oxygen demand and volatile fatty acid (VFA) concentrations. These fermentation characteristics were accompanied by the enrichment of polysaccharide-degrading and VFA-producing microorganisms, together with an increased representation of genes associated with glycolysis and carbohydrate-active enzymes. Concurrently, the relative abundance of mobile genetic element-associated genes decreased, accompanied by a reduction in total ARG abundance after fermentation. Protein-rich substrates showed distinct microbial and functional profiles, with higher relative representation of genes associated with proteolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and VFA-related metabolism. This treatment also markedly decreased the relative abundance of transposase-related genes, suggesting reduced mobility-associated potential of resistance genes. This study lays the foundation for evaluating resistance gene dynamics during co-fermentation of Ti-flocculated sludge.

title: Migration mechanism of PAH4 into cooking fume particles during frying: Driving role of lipid oxidation and the carrier effect of carbonyl compounds
abstract: The cooking fumes from frying carry highly toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), which pose a serious threat to human health. This study utilized the stable isotope PAH4-d 12 to simulate the migration of PAH4 from frying oil into cooking fumes, and characterized the process through physicochemical analysis of oils, single particle aerosol mass spectrometry, GC-MS, and quantum chemical calculations. The results indicate that the concentration of PAH4-d 12 in cooking fumes increases linearly with cooking time, and that it accumulates preferentially in fine particles with an aerodynamic diameter of less than 1.1 μm. The migration of PAH4-d 12 increases significantly with the degree of lipid oxidation. The radical-mediated oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids is the key driving force behind PAH4 migration. The abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups on the surface of cooking fume particles further enhances the carrier capacity. Carbonyl compounds are key components responsible for carrying PAH4, their binding to PAH4 is primarily governed by intermolecular van der Waals forces, while the strength of π-π stacking and C-H-π interactions depends on the structure. These findings reveal that lipid oxidation and particle properties jointly regulate the migration of PAHs, and provide insights at molecular level for pollution control.

title: Species-specific adaptations to cadmium or zinc stress in the pseudometallophytes Arabidopsis halleri and Arabidopsis arenosa
Paenibacillus polymyxa L62 synergistically regulates Pb2+ speciation and reconstructs soil microecological networks via surface complexation and PbS mineralization
abstract: The adsorption activity of Paenibacillus polymyxa L62 toward Pb 2+ was evaluated in aqueous systems. Strain L62 achieved a Pb 2+ removal efficiency of 95.97%. Its cell surface was enriched with functional groups such as -OH and -COO⁻, which promoted Pb 2+ adsorption via complexation and ion exchange. In aqueous systems, XRD, FTIR, and EDS analyses suggested the possible formation of stable PbS crystalline precipitates on the cell surface. In soil incubation experiments, strain L62 was inoculated into Pb-contaminated soil at 1% (L1) and 3% (L3). Both treatments significantly promoted Pb transformation among different fractions, with L3 showing greater efficacy. Compared with the control, L3 increased soil cation exchange capacity and soil organic matter by 55.24% and 5.26%, respectively. Microbial community analysis showed that L1 and L3 enriched key bacterial genera, including Marinobacterium and Photobacterium, and significantly enhanced soil acid phosphatase, urease, and dehydrogenase activities. Collectively, P. polymyxa L62 removed Pb 2+ in aqueous systems mainly through surface complexation and possible PbS mineralization. In soil, L62 promoted Pb transformation toward more stable fractions and reshaped the microbial community and enzyme activities.

title: A study on the characteristics of soil heavy metal pollution and risk assessment resulting from particulate matter erupted during thermal runaway of ternary lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Ternary lithium-ion batteries can release heavy-metal-containing particulate matter during thermal runaway, posing potential risks to soil after deposition. In this study, overcharge-induced thermal runaway tests were conducted on a 117 Ah NCM811 prismatic battery at 100% SOC in a sealed chamber. Particulate matter was collected by particle size and characterised using SEM, EDS and ICP-MS. The results showed clear particle-size-dependent characteristics. As particle size decreased, particle morphology changed from fused spherical agglomerates to loose, porous and flake-like structures, while the contents of Cr, Mn, Ni and Co and the proportions of exchangeable and carbonate-bound forms generally increased. A quantitative indicator system integrating particle migration, pollutant load and chemical speciation was established to assess potential soil heavy metal pollution risk. The comprehensive pollution index increased with decreasing particle size, and the 200-500 μm fraction exhibited the highest risk. These results identify 200-500 μm particles as the key fraction requiring priority attention and provide a quantitative basis for pollution risk assessment and control following battery thermal runaway.

title: Functional complementarity in a heavy oil-degrading consortium through cross-feeding, detoxification, pH stability, and transcriptional relief
authors: José Aparecido de Sousa Bernardino Leite
abstract: Heavy oil bioremediation is challenged by hydrocarbon recalcitrance and toxicity, requiring synergistic microbial consortia. This study formulated a tripartite biodegradation microbial consortium (BMC) comprising Micrococcus luteus BD1, Acinetobacter baumannii subsp. oleum ficedula BD54, and Ochrobactrum oleinvorans BD61, guided by genomic screening and Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). In microcosms, the BMC achieved 77% degradation of heavy oil (16° API) in 15 days, significantly outperforming monocultures. Initially, all strains attack aliphatic fractions, with BD1 operating via monooxygenases and adh, while BD54 and BD61 secrete biosurfactants (80% emulsification). In late stages, as BD54 and BD61 shift to complex aromatic cleavage (benD and pcaH), BD1 transitions into a detoxifying "metabolic sink" supporting pH stability. FBA and Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) provided a testable hypothesis of proton-associated metabolism. In vitro assays validated that the consortium maintains neutral pH, mitigates toxic phenol accumulation, and displays bidirectional exudate cross-feeding. This detoxification prevents enzyme inhibition and triggers systemic transcriptional relief, as evidenced by RT-qPCR and total oil and grease (TOG) analysis. Social coordination is supported by quorum sensing networks (LuxI/LuxR and RiPP-like). Integrating in silico modeling with in vitro validation reveals functional complementarity through cross-feeding, detoxification, pH buffering, and bioavailability enhancement, sustaining continuous heavy oil mineralization.

title: Phosphate rock drives greater arsenic accumulation in Pteris vittata than calcium carbonate by enhancing arsenic metabolism and reshaping rhizosphere microbiome
abstract: Poorly-soluble phosphate rock (PR) and CaCO 3 can enhance arsenic accumulation in calcicolous As-hyperaccumulator Pteris vittata, but their mechanisms under soil conditions remain unclear. P. vittata was grown for two months in As-contaminated soil (100 mg kg -1 ) receiving 2.0 g kg -1 Ca as PR, CaCO 3 , or soluble CaCl 2 . Plant nutrients, rhizosphere chemistry and bacterial communities, and As-metabolism genes were examined. Compared with CaCO 3 , PR increased frond As and P by 35% and 28% to 3128 and 3158 mg kg -1 , while CaCO 3 produced slightly greater biomass and 10-15% higher rhizosphere available As and P. PR upregulated P-transporter PvPht1;3, arsenate reductase PvHAC2, and arsenite antiporters PvACR3 and PvACR3;3 by 2.0-2.3 fold, whereas CaCO 3 induced PvPht1;3, PvPTB1;2, and PvACR3;1/3;2 by 1.7-3.3 fold relative to the soil control. PR retained a more diverse bacterial community (Shannon: 4.20) containing taxa associated with P cycling and As tolerance, whereas CaCO 3 showed lower diversity (3.76) under elevated pH. These findings link superior As accumulation under PR to P acquisition, distinct As-metabolism transcriptional responses, and rhizosphere restructuring, providing a mechanistic basis for selecting PR to enhance As accumulation during phytoremediation of As-contaminated soils.

title: An overlooked source of inhalational and dermal exposure to bisphenol A and its chlorinated derivatives in disposable face masks
abstract: The presence of emerging and toxic chlorinated bisphenol A derivatives (Cl x BPA) in disposable face masks (DFMs) remains unconfirmed. A total of 123 DFMs of various types, sourced primarily from China with additional samples from other Asian regions, North America, and Europe were analyzed. The results illustrated bisphenol A (BPA) was detected in all samples, while 3-monochloro bisphenol A (MCBPA) and 3,3',5,5'-tetrachloro-bisphenol A (TCBPA) were found in over 65% of DFMs. BPA exhibited the highest concentrations (geometric mean: 11.6 ng g -1 ), followed by TCBPA (0.0446 ng g -1 ), MCBPA (0.0234 ng g -1 ), 3,3'-dichlorobisphenol A (DCBPA-1, 0.0179 ng g⁻¹), 3,3',5-trichloro-bisphenol A (TriCBPA, 0.0169 ng g -1 ), and 3,5-dichloro bisphenol A (DCBPA-2, 0.0142 ng g -1 ). Notably, the proportion of DFM samples in which at least one Cl x BPA congener was detected reached 92.7%, indicating the widespread occurrence of Cl x BPA in DFMs. The concentration levels of BPA and Cl x BPA varied by mask material but not between adult and toddler masks or across production regions. Exposure assessment indicated that occupational users and toddlers face higher BPA and Cl x BPA exposure risks, particularly when using N95 and disposable activated carbon masks. Given the reported toxicological effects of Cl x BPA, the health risks posed by these emerging contaminants deserve further attention.

title: Precursor-dependent reconstruction of iron-carbon interface for high-efficiency removal of Cr(VI)
abstract: Using kitchen waste digestate as the feedstock, we assessed the impacts of precursor carbonization degree on modified chars' characterization, compared their Cr(VI) removal behavior, and clarified the high-efficiency Cr(VI) removal mechanisms. K 2 FeO 4 promoted pore development, surface oxygen-containing group enrichment, and in-situ anchoring of iron species in torrefied chars and hydrochars, whereas it mainly introduced iron-based active sites in pyrolysis chars. K 2 FeO 4 modification effectively improved the Cr(VI) removal performance of the chars. The equilibrium adsorption capacity increased by 83.8-100.8% from 39.46 to 54.29 mg·g -1 to 79.24-100.20 mg·g -1 . Isotherm results suggested monolayer adsorption for modified torrified char and heterogeneous multilayer adsorption for modified pyrolysis char and hydrochar. The maximum adsorption capacity of modified torrified char increased from 90.91 to 96.91 mg·g -1 , whereas the Freundlich adsorption coefficient of modified pyrolysis char and hydrochar increased markedly by 467% and 39%, respectively. The thermodynamic driving force, heat‑absorbing property, and randomness at solid‑liquid interface of Cr(VI) removal were evidently promoted. Cr(VI) was removed by K 2 FeO 4 -modified chars via several mechanisms, including surface electrostatic accumulation, inner-layer complexation capture, reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III), and Fe/Cr co-precipitation. These findings lay a solid scientific foundation for optimizing the preparation and usage of the K 2 FeO 4 modified chars for Cr(VI) removal.

title: Threshold-like transitions of microbial community states and functional reorganization in petroleum hydrocarbon-contaminated soils
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon (PH) contamination alters soil microbial communities, yet whether microbial responses to PH contamination occur gradually or exhibit threshold-like transitions remains poorly understood. Here, soils collected along a PH contamination gradient surrounding an oil well were analyzed to identify microbial community states and their associations with environmental factors, community assembly, interactions, and functional potential. Bacterial communities exhibited a bimodal distribution, indicating two distinct states: State A was predominantly associated with higher PH contamination, whereas State B was associated with lower contamination. Random forest analysis identified PH contamination, particularly n-alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), together with inorganic nitrogen (N), as the environmental factors most strongly associated with state differentiation. Potential landscape analysis identified intermediate contamination ranges where both states occurred (2.50 ≤lg(n-alkanes)≤ 3.21; 1.61 ≤lg(PAHs)≤ 1.69), indicating threshold-like differentiation. State A exhibited lower diversity, stronger deterministic assembly, more modular co-occurrence networks, enrichment of hydrocarbon-degrading taxa, and greater predicted functional potential for hydrocarbon activation, aromatic ring cleavage, denitrification, and N assimilation. State B showed greater network connectivity and stronger predicted potential for downstream carbon assimilation, nitrification, and more balanced N transformation. These findings demonstrate that PH contamination is associated with nonlinear reorganization of microbial community structure and functional potential across different community states.

title: Dual-functional Bacillus cereus X1 drives hydrocarbon biodegradation and carbon sequestration via glnQ-mediated metabolic rewiring
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination poses dual environmental challenges: direct ecosystem pollution and indirect exacerbation of greenhouse gas emissions via microbial mineralization, while natural carbon fixation pathways (e.g., the RuBisCO-mediated Calvin cycle) are insufficient at offsetting CO₂ release due to RuBisCO's inherent catalytic limitations. To address this, we engineered a dual-functional Bacillus cereus X1 strain capable of coupled hydrocarbon degradation and enhanced CO₂ fixation through optimization of a glnQ-centered metabolic network. Starting from oil-contaminated sludge, 40 carbon-fixing strains were isolated, with B. cereus X1 as the top performer, exhibiting the highest RuBisCO level (74.4 ± 2.8 U/g) together with confirmed n-alkane-degrading activity. Using Atmospheric Room-Temperature Plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, we generated mutant derivatives (X1-Mut13/29) displaying a 1.29-1.34-fold elevation in RuBisCO level to the wild type that was stably inherited over ten serial passages. Whole-genome resequencing identified a shared nonsynonymous variant in glnQ (c.836 C>T; p.Ala279Val), encoding the ATP-binding subunit of a glutamine ABC transporter. Expression of the mutant glnQ A279V allele in wild-type X1 generated X1-glnQ, which exhibited 2.13 times the RuBisCO level of the empty-vector control and the lowest mean residual TPH concentration among the inoculated treatments in oily-residue microcosms (690 ± 62.23 mg kg -1 dry residue). Transcriptomics profiling revealed that glnQ overexpression upregulated key enzymes of the Calvin cycle (e.g., fbaA, glpX, tktA), glycolysis (gapA, pgk), and tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, thereby enhancing NADPH/ATP supply to support carbon fixation particularly for RuBP regeneration. Mechanistically, glnQ overexpression influenced cellular C/N status, redirecting glutamine-derived α-ketoglutarate to replenish TCA cycle intermediates and fuel anaplerotic CO₂ assimilation. Collectively, this study establishes a novel "degrade-and-sequester" biocatalyst that enables synergistic pollution remediation and carbon fixation, providing a blueprint for engineering microbial carbon loops in oil-contaminated ecosystems. SYNOPSIS: This study engineers a hydrocarbon-degrading Bacillus cereus X1 strain with enhanced CO₂ fixation capacity via glnQ-mediated metabolic reprogramming, offering a novel bioremediation strategy for petroleum-contaminated environments. By leveraging glnQ-a key regulator of nitrogen and carbon metabolism-as a metabolic hub, the strain is designed to couple hydrocarbon catabolism with CO₂ sequestration, addressing the dual challenges of environmental pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. These findings support partial CO₂ reassimilation as a potential route to improve carbon-use efficiency during bioremediation, advancing sustainable solutions for contaminated ecosystem restoration.

title: HumanToxPredict: An interpretable data-driven framework for human oral TDLo prediction and toxicity assessment of pharmaceuticals and bioactive compounds
abstract: Predicting the human toxic dose low (TDLo) is critically important for pharmaceutical safety assessment and regulatory toxicology. A global computational toxicology framework that integrates toxicity data for children, infants, men, and women was developed using indicator-variable-based demographic encoding. Initially, Partial Least Squares (PLS)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) and quantitative read-across structure-activity relationship (q-RASAR) models were developed using interpretable molecular descriptors and similarity-based descriptors. A structure-level group-wise partitioning strategy was adopted. The q-RASAR model demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with the corresponding QSAR model. Additionally, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models were explored to investigate non-linear relationships. To further improve practical applicability, classification models were also developed, with RF showing the strongest overall performance among the evaluated models based on multi-metric analysis. Model interpretation suggests that pTDLo values are influenced by substituted nitrogen environments, topological arrangements, and similarity-driven toxicological information. The final model was further applied to 3660 investigational drugs, with most compounds falling within the applicability domain. We also developed a user-friendly software tool, HumanToxPredict, to enable rapid toxicity prediction. Overall, the present study introduces an interpretable, population-integrated human toxicity prediction framework that integrates q-RASAR, machine learning, and large-scale chemical screening.

title: Flow-through filter divided electrolytic cell enables highly efficient water purification via spatiotemporal alteration in electrocatalytic ozonation processes
abstract: Emerging contaminants with contrasting electronic structures respond differently to molecular ozone (O 3 ) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH), yet conventional electro-peroxone systems mainly exploit cathodic O 3 activation while leaving the acidic anodic chamber underutilized. Here, a hydrophilic carbon-fiber-membrane-divided, single-pass flow-through GF/EP reactor was developed to convert the anodic chamber into an active O 3 -preserving oxidation zone and regulate oxidant exposure by reversing the influent direction. In the cathode-to-anode (C-A) configuration, upstream H 2 O 2 /HO 2 - -mediated O 3 activation increased the apparent •OH exposure to 0.59 × 10 -10 M s, achieving 96.0% ibuprofen (electron-deficient contaminant) removal with a k obs of 0.101 min -1 , compared with 82.3% and 0.076 min -1 in A-C. Conversely, the upstream acidic anodic region in A-C preserved molecular O 3 and promoted selective electrophilic oxidation of electron-rich contaminants, yielding 99% benzotriazole removal with a k obs of 0.103 min -1 . Product identification and DFT calculations revealed configuration-dependent pathways and toxicity evolution. Matching influent direction with contaminant reactivity reduced the specific energy consumption for ibuprofen mineralization to 0.16 kWh g -1 . The system also maintained over 80% ibuprofen removal and achieved 47% COD removal in secondary effluent. These results establish flow-direction-regulated oxidant sequencing as a simple and energy-efficient strategy for treating chemically diverse contaminants.

title: Synergistic enhancement of quinoline degradation and nitrogen removal in a coupling FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis and partial denitrification-anammox system: performance and mechanisms
abstract: Quinoline in coal chemical wastewater severely inhibits the performance of partial denitrification-anammox (PD/A) process. This study innovatively developed a FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis coupled PD/A system to simultaneously enhance quinoline degradation and nitrogen removal under quinoline stress. The coupled system achieved quinoline and nitrogen removal efficiencies of 92.0 ± 2.4% and 81.7 ± 1.7%, respectively, outperforming the control (32.8 ± 6.0% and 17.8 ± 9.5%), FeS (73.3 ± 6.8% and 53.8 ± 5.4%), and ZVI (75.3 ± 9.3% and 51.6 ± 5.6%) groups. Mechanistically, the FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis facilitated reactive species generation, thereby enhancing the abiotic removal of quinoline (30.0 ± 0.7%). Meanwhile, FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis maintained higher microbial electron transport and energy metabolism, with electron transport system activity, electron-donating capacity, and ATPase activity being 31.9-133.1%, 30.4-116.5%, and 104.1-771.3% higher, respectively, than those in the other groups. Crucially, quinoline degradation into chain compounds and the release of Fe 2 + /S 2- via FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis, enhanced heterotrophic and autotrophic partial denitrification, respectively, ultimately supporting anammox. Metagenomics analysis revealed enrichment of the electroactive bacteria (Pseudomonas), quinoline-degrading bacteria (Exiguobacterium), and genes involved in carbon (Ior A/B, PcaD, LigC), nitrogen (hdh, hzs, narB), and sulfur (Sox) metabolism. Therefore, the FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis-PD/A system achieved synergistic carbon and nitrogen removal under quinoline stress.

title: Chemical composition and toxicological properties of particulate emissions from lithium-ion battery fires
abstract: This study assessed the physical, chemical, and toxicological properties of particulate emissions produced from lithium-ion battery fires. Commercially-available nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) battery modules were overcharged to trigger thermal runaway. The first experiment allowed the battery modules to burn without engaging any suppression system, while two additional experiments were performed with water and a potassium-based aerosol to suppress the battery fires. Results showed the formation of large diameter particles with geometric mean diameters of ∼360 nm, with their majority be below 1 μm. Depending on the experimental conditions, particle morphology revealed the generation of more spherical complex particles, while particle composition showed a mix of organic and inorganic agglomerates. Particle metallic composition was dominated by Li, Ni, Mn, Co, O, and Al, consistent with the chemistry of the battery modules. Medium and high molecular weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) showed higher concentrations than lighter PAHs. Small-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) dominated the particle emissions, with the presence of legacy PFAS suggesting that these compounds are still used in the manufacturing of lithium-ion batteries. All particle samples induced elevated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and correlation analysis identified relationships between particle composition and toxicological outcomes.

title: Interpretable QSPR modeling of PFAS endpoints via transformer-driven SMILES-to-molecular descriptor learning
abstract: A data-centric and interpretable Quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) framework was developed for four Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) endpoints (i.e., LC 50 , log BCF, log K OA , and log K OW ) with molecular- and descriptor-level interpretation of prediction behavior. First, PFAS endpoint datasets were collected while molecular descriptors and tokenized SMILES sequences were integrated for descriptor imputation. Descriptor redundancy was then reduced through statistical feature selection, and MissTransformer reconstructed missing descriptor values from latent structural information encoded in SMILES. Finally, explainable AI (XAI) analysis was applied to interpret chemical descriptor contributions to PFAS endpoint prediction. As a result, MissTransformer increased the number of descriptor-complete compounds available for QSPR modeling by 133.71% for log BCF data. Among the endpoint prediction models, the data-centric XGB model showed the best performance for log K OW prediction, with R 2 and Q 2 LMO values of 0.976 and 0.775, respectively. Interpretation results showed that hydrophobicity-related descriptors and fluorine atoms strongly contributed to log K OW prediction, whereas global structural descriptors related to molecular size and steric effects were important for log BCF prediction. The proposed framework can be used to prioritize data-poor PFAS compounds for further testing, monitoring, and risk-based environmental management.

title: Thiamphenicol decouples acidogenesis from methanogenesis and redirects carbon flux toward volatile fatty acids in sludge anaerobic digestion
abstract: Antibiotic residues in waste activated sludge (WAS) may disrupt anaerobic carbon conversion, yet how phenicol antibiotics redistribute carbon between acidogenesis and methanogenesis remains unclear. At 10 mg/g TSS, methane production decreased by 63.2% while VFAs reached 131-fold the control. This functional decoupling was underpinned by microbial fates: hydrolytic-acidogenic bacteria were largely retained or enriched, whereas methanogenic archaea and syntrophic bacteria were severely depleted. Concurrently, bacteria-archaea ecological networks underwent reorganization, with positive correlations partially rebounding at moderate TAP exposure. The network collapsed at high TAP, with substantial loss of connector taxa mediating inter-module metabolite exchange. Metagenomic evidence further revealed a functional asymmetry: genes involved in substrate transport and amino acid metabolism were maintained or showed increased relative abundance, while methanogenic genes and AI-2-associated communication genes exhibited decreased relative abundance. PLS-PM revealed that TAP was positively associated with the acidogenic bacterial community (β = 0.960) but negatively with methanogenic potential (β = -0.998). Accordingly, the methane share dropped from 98.7% to 18.1%, while VFAs increased to 81.9% of the COD-equivalent product pool. This work advances the understanding of antibiotic-driven functional imbalance and carbon flux redirection in sludge anaerobic digestion, providing a mechanistic basis for managing antibiotic-laden sludge prior to energy recovery.

title: Atmospheric deposition as a substantial source of lead in wheat grain: Between-year variation and uptake-pathway contributions
abstract: Atmospheric deposition is a critical pathway for lead (Pb) entry into agroecosystems; however, the patterns of its between-year accumulation and the contributions of foliar and root uptake to Pb levels in crops remain unclear. In this study, we combined a two-year factorial field exposure with a foliar-exposure trial in wheat to elucidate these mechanisms. Pb concentrations in wheat varied in accordance with the interannual deposition flux of Pb, decreasing synchronously as the flux declined from the first to the second year, demonstrating that crop Pb levels tracked annual atmospheric inputs. Extending soil exposure to atmospheric deposition from one to two years did not increase Pb concentrations in soil solution or wheat tissues. This suggested that, under the conditions of this study, newly deposited Pb during the current growing season-rather than Pb previously deposited in the soil-may be the primary source of Pb in wheat, as its bioavailability decreased markedly with soil aging. Quantitative pathway partitioning further revealed a sustained high contribution from foliar uptake to grain Pb accumulation (24.7%-68.8%), highlighting aboveground exposure as the key target for intervention. Collectively, these findings challenge conventional soil-centric management frameworks and emphasize the importance of reducing atmospheric Pb deposition and regulating foliar uptake to ensure the safe production of crops.

title: Reconciling mass and number emissions through particle size: Implications for urban ultrafine particle modelling
abstract: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) contribute only a small fraction of particulate mass but dominate atmospheric particle number, making size-resolved particle-number (PN) emissions essential for urban exposure modelling. This study evaluates how methodologies for estimating size-resolved UFP emissions affect simulated PN concentrations over Greater Paris, from regional background to street level. Simulations were performed for summer 2021 with the WRF-CHIMERE/MUNICH/SSH-aerosol modelling framework. A mass- and number-conserving algorithm was implemented to consistently combine PM mass emissions with PN emission factors in a sectional aerosol model. Sensitivity scenarios examined traffic exhaust emissions constrained by COPERT or on-board-measurement PN factors, traffic non-exhaust emissions, and the sector related to industrial processes without combustion, which includes construction activities. The reference simulation, based on PM mass emissions and prescribed representative diameters by activity sector, reproduced total PN concentrations well at background and traffic stations, showing that a simple mass-based methodology can estimate total PN concentrations across scales. However, uncertainties remained in the simulated size distribution, particularly for particles around 10 nm. Non-exhaust traffic emissions had a limited but non-negligible influence, contributing to about a third of total traffic PN. More detailed size-resolved PN emission factors, including particles below 10 nm, are needed to improve UFP exposure modelling.

title: Simultaneous valorization of nitrate and formaldehyde waste streams to hexamethylenetetramine via photo-electro-thermo-catalysis
abstract: To remediate nitrate (NO 3 - ) pollution and recover resources from formaldehyde wastewater, this work presents a waste valorization strategy integrating photoelectrocatalytic nitrate reduction (PEC NO 3 RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) with downstream chemical upgrading. Herein, a hollow MoO 2 @CuFe 2 O 4 @MnFe 2 O 4 Z-scheme-Schottky dual heterojunction nanoreactor array is developed to spatially separate proton and nitrate adsorption sites. The MoO 2 @CuFe 2 O 4 @MnFe 2 O 4 improves photogenerated charge separation and retaining robust redox capability, while the oxygen vacancy-rich MoO 2 layer exhibits favorable photothermal features to extend light harvesting, accelerate carrier migration and produce localized heating through localized surface plasmon resonance for reduced reaction energy barriers. Interfacial built-in electric field combined with spatial confinement jointly promote nitrate capture and enrichment. Fast hydrogen intercalation/deintercalation within MoO 2 create a dynamically *H-enriched surface to boost NO 3 RR-to-NH 3 conversion efficiency. This system resolves kinetic incompatibility between NO 3 - reduction and hydrogen supply, effectively suppressing NO 2 - accumulation and hydrogen evolution. It delivers an NH 3 yield rate of 5.96 mM h -1 cm -2 at -0.6 V vs. RHE with high selectivity and stability over 24 h. The in-situ generated NH 3 further transforms formaldehyde wastewater into high-value hexamethylenetetramine. This process enables simultaneous detoxification of two waste-streams and nitrogen/carbon feedstock upgradation, providing a closed-loop pathway for integrated pollution abatement and resource reclamation.

title: Oxidative conversion of HEDP to phosphate in charged water microdroplets
abstract: Organophosphonates are persistent anthropogenic phosphorus compounds because of their stable carbon-phosphorus bonds. Whether such compounds can be oxidatively converted to inorganic phosphate at dynamic air-water interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, using 1-hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid (HEDP) as a model organophosphonate, we show its stepwise oxidation in charged water microdroplets under mild conditions. Online mass spectrometry revealed a marked decrease in the deprotonated HEDP signal and the appearance of H 2 PO 4 - at m/z 96.9685, while ion chromatography and CO 2 analysis independently confirmed phosphate formation and carbon oxidation. Charge measurements and high-speed imaging showed atomization-induced charge separation, and simulations indicated possible local electric-field enhancement between oppositely charged droplets. Electron paramagnetic resonance, melatonin oxidation, H 2 18 O labeling, and tert-butyl alcohol scavenging experiments further showed that water-derived hydroxyl radicals are generated during atomization and participate in HEDP oxidation. Time-resolved product profiles identified transient phosphorus-containing intermediates and small organic acids, followed by the accumulation of phosphate and CO 2 . Detected carbon and phosphorus recoveries further constrained the elemental redistribution during the reaction. These results establish charged microdroplets as a model interfacial system for HEDP-to-phosphate conversion and support a mechanism involving water-derived hydroxyl radicals, with possible contributions from localized electric fields and oxygen-involved radical chemistry.

title: Natural variation in BjuB05.IRT1 is associated with cadmium accumulation in Brassica juncea
abstract: Phytoremediation of cadmium (Cd)-contaminated agricultural soils requires suitable germplasm and an improved understanding of the genetic factors underlying Cd accumulation. Here, we evaluated a genetically diverse panel of 165 Brassica juncea accessions and identified BJ20 as a high-Cd-accumulating genotype. Across two years, two sites, and two developmental stages, BJ20 consistently accumulated more Cd than the low-accumulating genotype BJ25. Mean shoot Cd accumulation reached 111.21 μg plant⁻¹ in BJ20, compared with 55.07 μg plant⁻¹ in BJ25. However, BJ20 had a lower root-to-shoot translocation factor than BJ25 (1.68 versus 2.30). Thus, its greater shoot Cd accumulation was not accompanied by greater proportional root-to-shoot transfer. Population resequencing and structure-adjusted association analysis identified an A/G SNP at the fourth coding nucleotide of BjuB05.IRT1, resulting in a Thr-to-Ala substitution at residue 2. The haplotype association with shoot Cd concentration was significant at flowering (P = 0.048), but not at maturity (P = 0.155). Differences in transcript abundance at flowering did not explain the contrasting phenotypes. In heterologous yeast assays, the BJ20-type allele increased Cd accumulation in the Cd-sensitive Δycf1 mutant to 455.76 ± 47.09 μg g⁻¹ , approximately 9.5-fold that of yeast expressing the BJ25-type allele. Together, the field, population-association, expression, and yeast results support BjuB05.IRT1 as a candidate contributing to natural variation in Cd accumulation-related traits. BJ20 therefore warrants site-specific evaluation as a phytoextraction resource. Low-accumulating germplasm may provide candidates for low-Cd breeding, subject to direct measurement of Cd concentrations in edible tissues.

title: Integrated fate of organic emerging contaminants and antibiotic resistance genes in biosolid-amended soils: effects of composting, biochar addition, and soil texture in wheat crops.
abstract: Land application of biosolids can introduce a complex mixture of emerging contaminants (ECs), antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and heavy metals into agricultural soils, yet their combined fate and the effectiveness of mitigation strategies remain poorly understood. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of ECs, ARGs, heavy metals, and bacterial community responses within a biosolid-soil-wheat system under controlled greenhouse conditions. Two mitigation strategies, biosolid composting and biochar co-application with biosolid (BB), were evaluated relative to unamended biosolid in sandy and silty clay loam (SCL) soils. Fifty-eight ECs, nine target genes (ARGs and mobile genetic elements), seven heavy metals, and the soil bacterial community were monitored over 140 days. Biosolids contained ECs at concentrations up to 793 ng g⁻¹, whereas compost substantially reduced the abundance of most ARGs and several ECs before soil application. Organic amendments approximately doubled wheat seed yield in sandy soil relative to the untreated control (139–142 vs. 69 g), whereas treatment effects on crop productivity were limited in SCL soil. Median EC half-lives remained similar among amendments in sandy soil (26–28 days), but compost increased EC persistence in SCL soil from 28 to 124 days. Compost also promoted greater accumulation of Zn, Cu and Cr while biochar reduced EC persistence, clinically relevant β-lactam resistance genes, and ARG transfer to straw under the same soil conditions. Bacterial community analyses showed that soil type exerted a stronger influence on community composition than amendment type after 140 days, suggesting that the resident soil microbiota contributed to ARG persistence. No target ECs or ARGs were detected in wheat grain under the experimental conditions evaluated, suggesting limited transfer to the edible fraction following a single biosolid application. Overall, the results indicate that mitigation strategies should be selected according to the receiving soil: organic amendments are particularly beneficial for improving crop productivity in nutrient-poor sandy soils, whereas biochar-amended biosolids provided the most balanced environmental performance in SCL soils.

title: Comparative ecotoxicity of aluminium-based galvanic anodes and impressed current on the Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) larvae: A dose-response study
abstract: ABSTRACT Cathodic protection through aluminium-based galvanic anodes (Al-GACP) or impressed-current cathodic protection (ICCP) are widely used to prevent corrosion of submerged steel structures in seawater. These processes release cocktail of compounds, whose impact on the surrounding environment remains poorly documented. In this study, the effects of the metal cocktail released by Al-GACP and of by-products formed by the ICCP system were assessed in Crassostrea gigas oyster D-larvae. The ICCP released chlorination and bromination by-products, such as trihalomethanes, haloacetonitriles, and haloaldehydes. Both cathodic protection systems induced dose-dependent responses on embryonic development and larvae unable to develop normally at concentrations above thresholds of 117 to 187 μg L⁻¹ for Al-GACP, and with the slightly diluted (1.6-fold) stock solution of by-products for the ICCP produced after 4 h under non-renewed water conditions. Embryotoxicity tests further demonstrated interindividual variability in the sensitivity of C. gigas broodstock to Al-GACP, with an EC 50 ranging from 63.4 to 110 μg L -1 . These preliminary results highlight the need for further research on the ecological effects of chlorination byproducts (generated by the ICCP system) in ecotoxicological studies, in order to strike the right balance between decisions regarding the protection of offshore structures against corrosion and the conservation of marine wildlife.

title: Empowered electron transfer behavior mediated by iron/sulfur cycling drives synergistic transformation of nitrogen and PFOA in constructed wetlands: Overlooked abiotic and biotic mechanisms
abstract: In this study, enhanced dynamic ammonium, nitrate (NO 3 - -N), and total nitrogen (TN) removal reaching 85.87-99.35%, 61.31-99.45%, and 74.61-98.48% were observed in biochar-pyrite (BCP) amended constructed wetland. Among them NO 3 - -N and TN were significantly higher than both control and individual biochar (BC) group. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) removal efficiency was 74.05-92.58% by BCP amendment, with higher defluorination rate and lower short-chain products accumulation. Increased activity of nitrate/nitrite reductase caused improved denitrification process in BCP system, which could result from enrichment of autotrophic denitrifying bacteria (like Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus, and Gallionella) and promotion of most genes involved in nitrogen/iron/sulfur metabolism. Facilitated redox cycles of iron/sulfur increased electron transfer system activity by 14.03-261.60% and 9.06-93.53% compared to control and single BC system, with higher activity of enzymes related to electron transport chain and encoding genes. Meanwhile, 1.72-3.79 folds enrichment of electroactive bacteria in BCP layer increased extracellular electron transfer (EET) efficiency. In mechanism, both reactive oxygen species mediated degradation and accelerated EET might enhance PFOA mineralization. This work offered a promising technique for synergic removal of nitrogen and PFOA in secondary effluent of WWTPs, which supplied novel insights on abiotic/biotic PFOA degradation mechanisms mediated by iron/sulfur cycling.

title: Combined exposure to polyethylene microplastics, copper, and Di(2-Ethylhexyl) phthalate reconfigures component-specific internal exposure profiles and triggers cross-level biological responses in earthworms
abstract: Microplastics, metals, and plastic additives commonly coexist in soils, but how their interactions reconfigure internal exposure and relate to biological responses across multiple levels We exposed Eisenia fetida to polyethylene microplastics (PE), copper (Cu), and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) singly and in binary and ternary combinations, integrating internal exposure, organismal phenotypes, redox biomarkers, histopathology, gut microbiota, and untargeted metabolomics. Combined exposure reconfigured rather than uniformly increased internal exposure: under ternary exposure, whole-body Cu decreased from 17.96 to 10.34 mg kg⁻¹ , whereas DEHP increased from 2735.76 to 8523.19 μg kg⁻¹ , while gut-retained PE varied among mixtures. Ternary exposure produced the strongest organismal effects, with mortality reaching 34%, body-weight loss 18.16%, reproductive and locomotor impairment, and ROS increasing 4.9-fold over the control. Gut bacterial responses were contaminant-specific: PE increased Chao1 richness from 1808 to 2579, while community composition differed among treatments (PERMANOVA, R² = 0.482, P = 0.001) and assembly shifted markedly under PE + DEHP and DEHP + Cu. Predicted microbial functions differed among treatments (R² = 0.525), with internal PE and Cu burdens significantly associated with KO profiles. Metabolomics identified 100, 66, and 124 candidate metabolites under PE, Cu, and DEHP, respectively, while Cu showed the clearest FDR-supported pathway enrichment. These findings reveal component-specific internal exposure linked to host, microbial, and metabolic responses.

title: Unsaturated constructed wetlands for the remediation of cylindrospermopsin and microcystin-LR
abstract: The increasing risk of cyanotoxin contamination of water resources can be mitigated using nature-based solutions. However, removal mechanisms remain insufficiently understood, particularly under unsaturated conditions. This study investigated the removal of cylindrospermopsin (CYN) and microcystin-LR (MC-LR) in mesocosm constructed wetlands (CW) operated in unsaturated mode. Vegetation (Juncus, Phragmites, unplanted), porous media (sand vs. gravel), season/loading conditions, and environmental drivers were assessed together with microbial community structure (16S rRNA gene metabarcoding) and cyanotoxin transformation product (TP) candidates. Planted systems, especially Juncus, achieved high cyanotoxin removal, MC-LR (up to 97%) and CYN (up to 90%), comparable to saturated systems despite shorter contact times. Associations between cyanotoxin attenuation, rhizosphere oxygenation, and prokaryotic biodiversity were found. Porous media had no statistically significant effect on cyanotoxin removal. The mlrA pathway was not consistently detected and most mlr-associated TPs were absent. Although these observations do not exclude involvement of the mlra pathway, they suggest that alternative and/or complementary degradation mechanisms may occur. Suspect screening identified nine tentatively annotated TP candidates, including five not previously reported in the peer-reviewed literature, more effectively attenuated in planted mesocosms. CW dimensions were estimated using the P-k-C⁎ model. Overall, this study highlights the potential importance of plant-microbe interactions for cyanotoxin removal.

title: Amphipods (Hyalella azteca) and zooplankton as sentinels of rare earth elements, uranium and thorium in a northern mining region contaminated with arsenic
abstract: Growing demand for green energy and new technologies is driving rare earth elements (REEs) mining, with implications on the bioavailability and accumulation of REEs and co-occurring radionuclides (U, Th) in aquatic organisms. We evaluated the amphipod Hyalella azteca and zooplankton as potential biomonitors for REEs, U, Th, and arsenic by sampling ten lakes in the historically arsenic-contaminated region of Yellowknife (NWT), near the Nechalacho REE mine. Lanthanum (La) concentrations were among the lowest reported in Canadian fresh waters (0.01-0.07 nmol L⁻¹). In zooplankton, La bioaccumulation was negatively influenced by protein-like dissolved organic matter and phosphate, U free ion concentrations best predicted U accumulation, and dissolved organic carbon was found to reduce Th accumulation. In H. azteca, littoral sediment La, U, and Th concentrations strongly predicted bioaccumulation, and aqueous carbonate complexation likely reduced U accumulation. Arsenate (As(V)) in surface water was an important predictor of La, U, and Th amphipod bioaccumulation. Even after EDTA washing, Fe strongly predicted La accumulation, suggesting an association beyond their surface adsorption. Key processes controlling the bioaccumulation pathways of La, U, Th, and As in this arsenic-contaminated region were summarized in a conceptual model, providing a risk assessment framework for REE mining in northern Canada.

title: Heavy metal content of plastic waste in agricultural ditches: Distinction and relation between exogenously adsorbed and endogenously added
abstract: Plastic waste in agricultural environments can act as a sink and a source of heavy metal contaminants. However, the relationship between plastic waste and heavy metals under actual environment conditions remains poorly understood. In this study, sediments and plastic waste were collected from two agricultural ditches in the Dongting Lake basin, China. Pb, Cd, Cr, Cu, and Zn concentrations were determined in ditch sediments, and surface-associated and intrinsic metal concentrations in plastic waste were investigated. Zn exhibited the highest concentration in exogenous plastic waste (231.76 ± 75.94 mg/kg), endogenous plastic waste (119.31 ± 56.04 mg/kg), and sediments (96.71 ± 25.25 mg/kg). This finding reflects the combined influence of environmental accumulation and metal additives within plastics. Overall, endogenous Pb, Cr, and Cu concentrations were 5.0, 13.9, and 4.8 times higher, respectively, than exogenous concentrations, suggesting that the potential release of these additive-derived metals warrants future monitoring and assessment. PE showed relatively higher endogenous metal concentrations. Correlation analysis indicated that the relationships between exogenous and endogenous metals varied across environmental conditions and polymer type, indicating that these factors affected the exogenous adsorption and endogenous release of heavy metals in plastics. This study provides field-based evidence from actual agricultural ditches and highlights the need for greater attention to interactions between plastic waste and heavy metals. It thus offers empirical support for managing combined plastic-heavy metal pollution in agricultural environments.

title: Reactive diffusion of selenium anions into clay-rocks: A sorption in batch and through-diffusion investigation
abstract: Selenium-79 is a critical radionuclide in the safety assessment of high-level radioactive waste in deep geological repositories in clay-rich formations, due to its long half-life and speciation. It exhibits three relevant oxidation states in anionic forms: selenate(+VI), selenite(+IV), and selenide(−II) whose mobility through clay-rocks needs to be evaluated. To this end, batch and diffusion experiments were performed in the French Callovo-oxfordian clay-rocks under anoxic conditions and at ultra-trace concentrations, using the 75 Se isotope. Our findings reveal that selenate is weakly retained and diffuses similarly to the inert anionic tracer 36 Cl − . In contrast, selenite exhibits strong retention in diffusion experiments conducted with and without the addition of hydrazine. The steep 75 Se rock profile and the 75 Se(+IV) activity evolution in solution were modeled using high distribution ratio values (1000−3300 L kg −1 ). The oxidation of selenide, HSe − species, into the precipitate Se(0) (s) was strongly delayed by its polymerization into polyselenides (Se n 2− ), with no 75 Se(0) (s) observed after 100 days of diffusion. Adding hydrazine to one of the diffusion cells slowed the polymerization rate of selenide, thus allowing more selenide to diffuse into the solid. Based on a simplified model, we proposed that the selenide diffusion would be similar to that of selenate and 36 Cl − .

title: Pesticide leaching in sandy and loamy soil—contrasting impact of polyethylene microplastic pollution and freeze–thaw events
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can alter pesticide migration in soils by modifying soil structure and influencing pesticide sorption and transport. Freeze–thaw cycles (FTCs), which are common in temperate regions, naturally change soil structure and may influence the environmental fate of both MPs and pesticides. We investigated a mixture of 20 pesticides with a broad range of physical-chemical properties in a factorial column experiment combining sandy and loamy soils, room-temperature and FTC treatments, and the presence or absence of 1% (w/w) polyethylene (PE) particles (63–100 μm). Transport was characterized by the pore volumes required to reach 5% and 50% of the nominal influent concentration (BV 5 and BV 50 ). FTCs reduced mean breakthrough volumes by approximately 15–35% in sandy soil and 40–85% in loamy soil, whereas PE addition generally increased breakthrough volumes by approximately 7–17% across treatments. Loamy soil showed greater pesticide retention at room temperature and a 1–2.5-fold stronger response to FTCs than sandy soil. Associations with organic-carbon partition coefficients ( K OC ) and water solubility ( S w ) indicated compound-dependent transport. Changes in soil physical properties and complementary experiments with selected triazines suggested possible physical and partitioning-related contributions, particularly in loamy soil, consistent with FTC-induced changes in soil structure and flow pathways.

title: Mechanism of in-situ calcium sulfate in the synergistic sulfidation–carbothermal reduction for efficient recovery of Cu, Pb, and Zn from copper smelting flue coated materials
abstract: Flue coated materials from copper smelting are hazardous wastes rich in Cu, Pb, and Zn, containing intrinsic CaSO 4 . Unlike processes relying mainly on externally added sulfur sources, this study evaluates whether intrinsic CaSO 4 can serve as an in-situ sulfur donor and slag-forming flux during sulfidation-carbothermal reduction. Thermodynamic calculations, in-situ XRD, and TG-MS were combined to investigate phase evolution and metal partitioning. CaSO 4 remained stable below about 900 ℃, was reduced to CaS mainly at 900-1050 °C, and participated in CaO formation and SO 2 release above about 1050 °C. Significant CO, CO 2 , SO 2 release occurred above 1000 ℃, defining a reaction-active window of 1050-1200 °C. The CaSO 4 /C ratio strongly influenced oxygen-sulfur potential. insufficient carbon left CaSO 4 undecomposed, an appropriate ratio favored Cu 2 S and FeS, and excess carbon promoted metallic alloying. The overall mechanism is supplying sulfur at low T, making slag at high T, and regulating oxygen-sulfur potential in the middle stage, which enables selective separation and recycling of Cu from Pb and Zn into matte and volatile phases, with efficiencies of 95.1 ± 0.9%, 92.2 ± 1.1%, and 90.1 ± 1.3%. The volatile Pb/Zn species and SO 2 generated require downstream capture and off-gas treatment, but the capture efficiency was not evaluated in this study.

title: Context-dependent effects of microplastics on soil available phosphorus: An AP-centered multilevel meta-analysis
abstract: Microplastics are increasingly recognized as modifiers of soil nutrient availability, but their effects on soil available phosphorus (AP) remain difficult to generalize across soil-plastic contexts. Building on broader P syntheses, this AP-centered multilevel meta-analysis addressed within-study dependence, missing variance information, and AP-specific heterogeneity. The full dataset contained 597 paired observations from 79 studies, with 546 complete-SD effect sizes from 75 studies used for primary inference. Microplastic exposure was associated with an average 11.8% decrease in soil AP (lnRR = -0.126, 95% CI: -0.199 to -0.053), and this negative mean effect remained stable across complementary robustness analyses. However, the wide prediction interval showed that AP depletion was not universal. Reported background pH, particle size, and polymer identity were the clearest heterogeneity axes. Depletion was strongest in acidic soils and under exposure to particles ≤ 100 μm, while polymer identity significantly structured AP responses and the binary biodegradability classification did not. Exposure-duration class and soil sampling location showed limited explanatory power. The evidence base was concentrated in Asia, especially China, and AP extraction methods were poorly reported. Overall, microplastics shifted average AP toward depletion, but this response is best interpreted as context dependent rather than universal.

title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the modulation of Co(II)-catalase interactions by polystyrene nanoplastics
abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) can interact with heavy metals and alter metal-protein interactions. However, their effects on Co(II)-catalase (CAT) interactions remain unclear. We integrated enzyme activity assays, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), multispectroscopic analyses, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to compare Co(II) alone with the PS-NPs-Co(II) system. Co(II) increased background-corrected apparent CAT activity at 0.5-0.8 mM, whereas PS-NPs generally attenuated this increase, significantly at 0.6 and 0.8 mM (p = 0.024 and 0.009). ITC yielded distinct apparent responses for Co(II) into CAT titration (fitted ΔH = -335 kJ mol -1 ) and titration of the filtrate from a directly prepared PS-NPs-Co(II) mixture into CAT (-14.9 kJ mol -1 ). These values reflect different titrants in 20 mM HEPES and do not isolate a single binding event. Spectroscopy showed changes in CAT secondary structure, aromatic-residue environments, and heme Soret responses, with a distinct heme response in the combined system. Simulations indicated fewer direct CAT-Co(II) contacts and greater heme-pocket solvent exposure in the PS-containing model. These findings suggest that PS-NPs may modify the local CAT-Co(II) environment and contribute to the observed activity differences under these cell-free conditions.

title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal inoculation as a potential approach for enhancing pollutant removal from tailwater in Acorus calamus constructed wetlands
abstract: The residual organic matter, nitrogen, phosphorus, and heavy metals (HMs) in the effluent from wastewater treatment plants pose persistent risks to the ecological environment. To enhance advanced treatment of synthetic tailwater, this study used CWs based on the symbiosis of Acorus calamus and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and investigated its pollutant removal efficiency and underlying mechanisms. The results showed that AMF inoculation significantly increased the removal rates of organic matter and total nitrogen by 11.35% and 16.62%, respectively, while TP removal showed a non-significant increasing trend (7.65%), respectively; reduced N₂O flux and peak emissions by 39.34% and 21.96%. Compared with the control group, AMF symbiotic treatment showed more positive changes: AMF-plant symbiosis significantly increased plant biomass and significantly enhanced plant HM content and accumulation (Cr, Ni, Pb, and Zn). Meanwhile, changes in microbial diversity and the relative abundance of microbial communities related to nitrogen and phosphorus cycling indirectly enhanced the removal of organic matter, nitrogen, and phosphorus in CWs. In addition, changes in the abundance of functional genes related to carbon metabolism and nitrogen transformation/reduction were consistent with organic matter and nitrogen removal and reduced N₂O/TN emissions. In summary, this study proposes that the AMF-plant symbiosis may coordinately enhance the advanced treatment performance of CWs for synthetic tailwater through plant-microbial community-functional gene interactions, thereby providing new insights for the application of plant-microbe symbiotic technology in advanced tailwater treatment.

title: Fate and persistence of emerging chemical contaminants after land application of biosolids: A screening-level risk assessment
abstract: The presence of emerging chemical contaminants embodied in wastewater treatment plant residuals represents a potential barrier to the continued land application of biosolids given concerns about diffuse and long-term contamination of agricultural lands. Their diverse physiochemical properties, and uncertain environmental fate and persistence constitute chemical contamination risk for the health of soils, especially due to accumulation after repeat applications. This study aimed to quantify the risk posed by 47 emerging contaminants from a range of sources (e.g., pharmaceuticals, personal care products, industrial chemicals, hormones and nitrosamines). Risk was characterized as a combination of persistence and ecotoxicological effect, using the half-life and the hazard quotient, respectively, as the key metrics. Chemicals identified to be persistent in the environment included several per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS), carbamazepine, galaxolide, tonalide, triclocarban and triclosan. Wastewater treatment plant operational and environmental conditions that resulted in faster degradation for particular chemicals have been identified, so practices to minimize their persistence could be implemented. This work has developed a framework for identification of chemicals likely to be highly persistent and thus accumulate following repeat biosolids application, facilitating prioritization of chemical concentration monitoring, targeted treatment, and quantification of repeat biosolids application frequency to minimize emerging contaminant accumulation.

title: Environmental effects of biodegradable microplastics in cadmium-contaminated soil and their regulation on cadmium bioavailability
abstract: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) residues in soil are becoming increasingly prevalent; however, their effects on cadmium (Cd) bioavailability and toxicity in contaminated soils remain poorly understood. A pot experiment was conducted to investigate the effects of four typical BMPs-polylactic acid (PLA), poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), polybutylene succinate (PBS), and polycaprolactone (PCL) on soil physicochemical properties, Cd speciation, pak choi growth, antioxidant responses, and rhizobacterial community structure in Cd-contaminated acidic soil. Results demonstrated that BMPs regulated Cd behavior through dual abiotic (pH, zeta potential, electrical conductivity) and biotic (microbial community restructuring) pathways, with effects highly dependent on BMPs type. PBAT elevated soil pH, increased negative zeta potential, reduced shoot Cd accumulation, alleviated oxidative stress, and enhanced bacterial diversity with enrichment of Cd-immobilising taxa. Conversely, PLA, PBS, and PCL decreased soil pH, increased Cd availability and plant Cd uptake, aggravated lipid peroxidation and leaf tissue damage, and inhibited antioxidant enzyme activity. PLA broadly suppressed soil enzyme activity, whereas PCL reduced bacterial richness and enriched Cd-mobilising taxa. These findings demonstrate that BMPs exert species-specific regulation on Cd fate through combined modifications of soil physicochemical properties and reshaping of functional microbial communities, highlighting the need for risk differentiation when introducing biodegradable plastics into metal-contaminated farmlands.

title: Hydrological processes significantly increase mercury-related ecological risk in karst paddy ecosystem: Evidence from mercury isotope
abstract: Mercury (Hg) transported by runoff poses potential ecological risks to aquatic ecosystem. However, its mechanism remains unclear. This study investigated a typical karst paddy ecosystem in southwestern China. By analyzing isotopic compositions of inorganic Hg (IHg) and methylmercury (MeHg) across different environmental matrices, we clarified the significant impact of hydrological processes on Hg migration and accumulation in paddy ecosystem. Rainfall-driven runoff transported Hg from hillslope soils into irrigation water, with hillslope soils-derived Hg accounting for 72.6% of the total Hg in irrigation water. Irrigation water subsequently contributed 47.6% of the IHg to pore water in paddy soil. Importantly, pore water served as the primary source of IHg in rice grain and also supplied the dominant source of bioavailable Hg for methylation in paddy soil, thereby facilitating MeHg accumulation in rice grain. These coupled Hg migration and transformation processes resulted in elevated Hg accumulation in rice grain. Therefore, the distinct geological and hydrological processes in karst regions can accelerate Hg migration and enhance Hg bioavailability in paddy ecosystem, thereby significantly increasing Hg loading and risk in these systems. This study provided new insights into Hg-related risks driven by natural processes in agricultural ecosystems and offered guidance for developing targeted mitigation strategies.

title: Divergent evolution of trace elements in groundwater-dependent lakes: Insights from multi-isotopic tracers, DOM molecular characteristics, and microbial evidence
abstract: Groundwater-dependent lakes are highly vulnerable to trace element (TE) accumulation, yet the mechanisms controlling TE occurrence in coupled lake-groundwater systems remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the occurrence, transport, and controlling mechanisms of TEs in a representative groundwater-dependent lake system. Concentrations are reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD; LW, n = 6; GW, n = 44). Lake water (LW) and groundwater (GW) exhibited distinct TE occurrence patterns, with significantly higher concentrations of V (89.50 ± 69.00 μg L⁻¹), Mo (32.40 ± 24.30 μg L⁻¹), and U (25.60 ± 20.60 μg L⁻¹) in LW, whereas Sc (3.78 ± 0.93 μg L⁻¹), Zn (11.95 ± 38.54 μg L⁻¹), and Ba (193.04 ± 94.58 μg L⁻¹) were significantly higher in GW (FDR-adjusted p 222 Rn) mass balance model estimated a mean lacustrine groundwater discharge rate of 22.2 mm d⁻¹ , demonstrating substantial groundwater inputs to the lakes and highlighting groundwater as an important hydrological pathway for the transport of dissolved TEs. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of TE evolution in groundwater-dependent lakes and improve predictions of TE accumulation and ecological risks under arid conditions.

title: Concentration-dependent impacts of ofloxacin on the mobilization-immobilization dynamics of geogenic arsenic in groundwater environment
abstract: Arsenic (As) behaviors in aquifers can be altered by exogenetic antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), which modifies evolution of originally geogenic As-contaminated groundwater while increasing environmental risk of ARGs. The roles of introduced antibiotics in As biogeochemical cycle in groundwater environments however remain elusive mechanistically. Using Shewanella oneidensis (S. oneidensis) as a model, this research elucidates the impacts of varying levels of antibiotic (e.g., ofloxacin) exposure on As fate during microbially-mediated reductive dissolution of host goethite. Under low-level ofloxacin exposure (≤1 μg/L), S. oneidensis restored secretion of riboflavin after a short period of stress adaptation. Conversely, high ofloxacin exposure (≥10 μg/L) consistently depleted aqueous riboflavin and weakened mineral-biomolecule interactions, restricting electron transfer and inhibiting goethite bioreduction. Contrasting changes in the abundances of ARGs (e.g., qnrA) and As efflux gene (e.g., arsB) indicate concentration-dependent reorganization of resistance-associated genetic potential under ofloxacin and As co-exposure, while aqueous As(III) accumulated despite declining arsB abundance. Therefore, the molecular mechanism underlying As migration differs depending upon antibiotic exposure levels. These findings provide novel insights into underestimated effects of concomitant antibiotics on As re-mobilization in geogenic contaminated groundwater.

title: Crude oil addition enhanced greenhouse gas production and altered microbial communities in tidal flat sediments under tidal cycling
abstract: Coastal wetlands are critical blue carbon sinks, yet their resilience to hydrocarbon intrusion remains poorly understood. We conducted a 240-day laboratory microcosm experiment simulating exposed, alternating, and flooded tidal regimes to investigate how crude oil addition affected CH 4 , CO 2 , and N 2 O production and microbial communities in tidal-flat sediments. Crude oil significantly increased CH 4 and CO 2 production under all tidal regimes (p 4 increase occurring in exposed sediments (3746.3 ± 525.4%). N 2 O production increased only under flooded conditions (45.2 ± 10.7%). The relative stimulation of CH 4 declined along the exposed-alternating-flooded gradient. Crude oil addition selectively reshaped bacterial communities, shifting them from oligotrophic and slow-growing (e.g., Nitrospirota, Nitrospinota) to copiotrophic and fast-growing types (e.g., Pseudomonadota, Planctomycetota), thereby enhancing bacterial diversity while leaving archaeal and fungal communities largely unchanged. Bacterial network complexity was positively associated with CH 4 and CO 2 production, whereas bacterial vulnerability was negatively associated with CH 4 production. No network property was significantly associated with N 2 O production. These findings show that tidal regime strongly shaped gas-specific responses to crude oil and highlight microbial restructuring as an important correlate of enhanced greenhouse-gas production in oil-impacted coastal sediments.

title: A phyllosphere bacterium Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11 mitigates cadmium toxicity in seagrass (Zostera marina) via a synergistic "exclusion–redox–repair" network
abstract: Heavy metal pollution, particularly cadmium (Cd), threatens coastal marine ecosystems and foundational species like the seagrass Zostera marina. Here, a multi-extremophilic phyllosphere bacterium, Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11, was isolated to investigate its protective mechanisms under acute Cd stress (500 μM). In vitro assays confirmed high Cd tolerance in S11 via extracellular adsorption and active efflux. In mesocosm experiments, S11 inoculation reduced root Cd accumulation by 38.3% and attenuated systemic oxidative stress by suppressing malondialdehyde and stabilizing glutathione peroxidase activity. Whole-genome sequencing revealed key efflux systems (czcD, cadD, zupT, and znuA) regulated by cadC and resD. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) showed that S11 upregulated host folate biosynthesis, vitamin B6 metabolism, and DNA base excision repair pathways. Integrated multi-omics further demonstrated a metabolic shift toward defensive diterpenes, flavonoids, and isoflavonoids. Overall, E. aurantiacum S11 establishes a synergistic "exclusion–redox–repair" network that enhances host resilience, offering a novel microbially assisted strategy for marine ecological restoration.

title: Oxidant-free aqueous arsenic removal over few-layer Ti3C2Tx MXene via coupled As(III) photooxidation and As(V) adsorption
abstract: Coupling arsenite oxidation with arsenate capture may reduce the need for separately dosed oxidants in water treatment, but the roles of the active phase and adsorption sites require careful evaluation. Here, Ti 3 C 2 T x -based nanosheets were prepared by NH 4 F-assisted electrochemical etching and tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH)-mediated delamination without directly adding HF. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 80.37 m 2 /g and expanded basal spacing. Batch experiments under simulated solar irradiation showed light-dependent arsenic transformation and As(V) uptake without an added chemical oxidant. Under simulated solar irradiation, the material achieved efficient oxidant-free arsenic removal through coupled As(III) photooxidation and As(V) adsorption, enabling nearly complete oxidation of 10 mg/L As(III) within 3 h and a high maximum As(V) adsorption capacity of 349.1 mg/g. The system also showed good environmental adaptability and reusability, maintaining over 85% arsenic removal efficiency across pH 3-9 in the presence of common coexisting ions, with negligible performance decay after four regeneration cycles.
