Mechanistic analysis reveals that the enlarged interlayer spacing and exposed terminal groups provide abundant binding sites for As(V), while the ultrathin Few-Layer structure and favorable interfacial charge transfer promote As(III) photooxidation. This work demonstrates an oxidant-free MXene-based strategy for efficient remediation of arsenic-contaminated water.

title: Multi-tributary seasonal patterns and exploratory source identification of potentially toxic elements in water and sediments: Ecological risks screening in a gold - mining river systems, Northern, Tanzania
abstract: Gold mining in Northern Tanzania raises concerns about potentially toxic elements in rivers draining into Lake Victoria. This study investigated seasonal and spatial distributions of As, U, Pb, Cd, Cu, and Zn in surface water and bed sediment from the Mara River, its tributaries, and the Mori River. 40 water and 42 sediment samples were collected during the 2024 rainy and dry seasons and analysed. Contamination and ecological-risk indices were calculated using Upper Continental Crust (UCC) and local-bedrock backgrounds, alongside sediment quality guidelines and exploratory multivariate analysis. At paired sampling locations, sediment concentrations of studied elements were significantly lower during the rainy season, whereas dissolved concentrations showed no significant seasonal differences. Sediment As and Cd accounted for most guideline exceedances, with 31.0% and 16.7% of samples exceeding Probable Effect Levels, primarily in mining-affected tributaries. Dissolved As and Pb exceeded WHO and Tanzanian guidelines in 17.5% and 15.0% of samples, respectively. Risk assessments were sensitive to background selection: Cd dominated under UCC, whereas As became more influential under local-bedrock backgrounds, although both approaches identified the same priority sites. Multivariate analysis revealed element covariation but did not resolve provenance. These findings establish a baseline-sensitive screening framework and prioritise sites for future monitoring.

title: Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles alleviate florfenicol-induced phytotoxicity in soybean seedling through multi-level regulation of photosynthesis, carbon metabolism, and nutrient homeostasis
abstract: The threat posed by antibiotic contamination to agricultural ecosystems requires effective alleviation strategies. This study characterized the multi-level regulatory network by which Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles (NPs) restore soybean carbon metabolism under florfenicol stress. In a pot experiment across three growth stages (VE, V1, V2), florfenicol suppressed photosynthetic systems, reducing chlorophyll content by 19-65%, Fv/Fm by 30-56%, and Rubisco activity by 31-36%. Fe₃O₄-NPs treatment (40-80 mg/kg) reversed these effects, increasing chlorophyll content (up to 88%), enhancing chlorophyll fluorescence parameters (Fv/Fm, Y(II), ETR), and reducing non-photochemical energy dissipation (Y(NO)). Mechanistically, Fe₃O₄-NPs up-regulated key genes involved in chlorophyll synthesis, photosystem II, Rubisco subunits, sucrose synthesis, and sugar transport; and restored Rubisco, sucrose phosphate synthase, sucrose synthase, and amylase activities. Metabolomic and KEGG analyses revealed enrichment of metabolites in pathways related to core carbon metabolism and defense-related signaling, with potential involvement of hormone signaling pathways in leaves. Fe₃O₄-NPs restored the accumulation of key nutrients-which serve as cofactors for Rubisco (Mg), glycolytic enzymes (K), electron transport (Cu, Fe), and antioxidant defense (Cu, Zn)-linking nutrient homeostasis to photosynthetic carbon assimilation and energy metabolism. These findings establish a multi-level regulatory framework for Fe₃O₄-NP-mediated alleviation of antibiotic stress, offering a potential strategy for safeguarding crop productivity in antibiotic-contaminated soils.

title: Phthalate and non-phthalate plasticizers co-occur in soils and reshape microbial carbon metabolism
abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs) are widely used plasticizers with well-documented ecological effects. The increasing use of non-phthalate plasticizers (NPAEs) as alternatives to PAEs has resulted in their co-occurrence in the environment, yet their co-contamination and microbial impacts in soils influenced by plastic production remain poorly understood. Here, a field survey around a plastic industrial area revealed that concentrations of PAEs (306-10,718 ng g -1 ) and NPAEs (20.3-380 ng g -1 ) in factory soils were an order of magnitude higher than those in nearby farmlands and villages. Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP, 17.6-9280 ng g -1 ) and acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC, 1.19-233 ng g -1 ) were the dominant PAE and NPAE compounds, respectively. A 28-day microcosm experiment examined their combined effects on soil bacterial communities and functions. DEHP contamination individually enriched aromatic degradation pathways (i.e., benzoate/styrene degradation), whereas DEHP-ATBC co-contamination inhibited the aromatic degradation pathway, potentially associated with altered microbial carbon-utilization preferences, with Sphingomonas as a key functional taxon. Co-contamination also suppressed core carbon metabolism (i.e., citrate cycle), and enriched the ribosome pathway, indicating a shift toward fast‑growing, metabolically streamlined taxa. These findings provide the first evidence that PAE-NPAE co-contamination reshapes microbial carbon metabolism and impairs aromatic compound degradation, underscoring the need for mixture-based risk assessment for plasticizers.

title: Spatial prediction of the soil−wheat cadmium bioconcentration factor with a knowledge-guided learning model
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) readily transfers from contaminated soils into wheat grain, posing dietary risks; however, predicting the spatial distribution of the bioconcentration factor (BCF) remains challenging due to interacting direct and indirect pathways. We developed a knowledge-guided learning model using structural equation modeling to quantify relationships governing BCF. These mechanistic insights guided Random Forest coupled with high-accuracy surface modeling for spatial prediction and informed management strategy evaluation through scenario simulations. The results showed that the BCF was jointly governed by direct soil buffering and Zn-Cd competitive uptake, and indirectly by industrial emissions and wind that degraded soil properties and increased soil Zn concentrations. Validated against a large field dataset from northern China, the model achieved R 2 of 0.44-0.84. Spatial predictions revealed a partial mismatch between soil Cd and BCF hotspots, with high-BCF zones occurring where neutral pH, moderate organic matter, and industrial emission-related deposition converged. Scenario simulations suggested that a combined strategy of source control and zinc fertilization could reduce the high-BCF area from 22.7% to 3.9% by 2050. We proposed a spatially differentiated zoning framework for targeted wheat production management. This knowledge-guided learning model provides a transferable methodology for precise control in heavy metal-contaminated agricultural regions.

title: Biocomposite based on alginate hydrosphere immobilized with Pseudomonas psychrotolerans for highly selective recovery of Ce-group rare earth elements from mine wastewater
abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) recovery from secondary resources urgently requires green and highly selective biosorbents to address supply shortages and mining pollution. Herein, a novel biocomposite PP/ALG was constructed by immobilizing the indigenous bacterium Pseudomonas psychrotolerans within alginate hydrospheres, enabling a specific adsorption preference for Ce-group REEs in mine wastewater, with adsorption efficiencies up to 90.37% and distribution coefficients (K d ) up to 9312.5 mL·g -1 , outperforming many other adsorbents. As well, the separation factor (SF) of Ce-group REEs for Tb and Yb groups were significantly higher than that between other groups, drastically exceeding 27. The REEs selectivity originates from three synergistic effects: (1) the larger ionic radius and lower charge density of Ce-group REEs favor stronger coordination with surface functional groups, (2) microbial extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are crucial in facilitating the adsorption process, and (3) metabolic-derived C-N and carboxyl/phosphate groups provide highly specific chelating sites for Ce-group. Overall, this work establishes a green, sustainable, and highly selective biorecovery strategy for REEs from hazardous mine wastewater, highlighting the critical role of indigenous bacteria and EPS in REEs separation.

title: Hazardous elements associated with UV-weathered polypropylene nanoplastics: Implications for elemental transport
abstract: Environmental nanoplastics can form through weathering-induced cracking and fragmentation, accompanied by surface oxidation and roughening that may alter their interactions with co-occurring contaminants. However, the operational association and redistribution of hazardous elements in the presence of UV-weathered polypropylene (PP) nanoplastics-and how this behavior differs from that of PP microplastics and mineral particles-remain poorly understood. Newly prepared and UV-weathered PP nanoplastics and microplastics, together with quartz sand, were exposed to a multielement standard solution containing hazardous elements (As, Be, Cd, Co, Cr, Ni, Pb, Se, and V) in a simplified, salt-free, pH-adjusted aqueous system (pH 8.1-8.3). Elemental masses in the floating, dissolved/filtrate, and settled fractions were quantified, and the Association and Transfer Index (ATI) was defined as the percentage of the total recovered elemental mass present in the operational floating fraction with plastics. The results showed that UV-weathered PP nanoplastics exhibited the highest mean ATI (86.8%), compared with newly prepared nanoplastics (36.1%), newly prepared microplastics (6.1%), and UV-weathered microplastics (3.5%). Under the applied experimental conditions, UV-weathered PP nanoplastics were associated with a pronounced redistribution of element-bearing phases toward the operational floating fraction. Meanwhile, TEM-EDS qualitatively demonstrated the co-occurrence of element-bearing phases with the analyzed UV-weathered PP nanoplastic material. The contrasting behavior among plastic sizes and weathering states suggests that these factors may influence the floating-versus-settled distribution of plastic-associated elements. Whether this redistribution translates into enhanced transport or prolonged retention in natural waters remains to be evaluated under environmentally relevant conditions.

title: 137Cs and natural radionuclides in Antarctic soil-vegetation systems on King George Island: Contrasting patterns in penguin-influenced and reference habitats
abstract: Fallout radionuclides are useful tracers of contaminant retention and redistribution in polar soil-vegetation systems. This study examined activities of 137 Cs, 40 K, total 210 Pb, 226 Ra, and 228 Ac, together with δ 15 N and δ 13 C, in soil, penguin guano, lichens, mosses, and vascular plants collected during four campaigns over two austral spring-summer periods on King George Island. Relatively high 137 Cs activities were observed in soil and Deschampsia antarctica in the penguin-influenced area, whereas Usnea antarctica showed low 137 Cs activity in both areas. Fresh penguin guano contained low 137 Cs activity (∼1 Bq kg -1 d.w.) and was not a direct high-activity source at sampling. D. antarctica showed consistently higher 137 Cs activity in the penguin-influenced area than at the reference site across matched campaigns, together with a higher median soil-to-vegetation transfer factor, providing the clearest site-related 137 Cs contrast among the analysed vegetation groups. U. antarctica showed the highest total 210 Pb activity, while 7 Be was detected in three lichen samples, a pattern compatible with atmospheric particle interception. Lower δ 15 N in U. antarctica was consistent with weaker ornithogenic nitrogen influence. Together, the contrasting radionuclide profiles indicated a stronger substrate-associated 137 Cs signal in D. antarctica, whereas the U. antarctica profile was more compatible with atmospheric particle interception.

title: Catalytic perchlorate reduction over supported Ru catalysts: Support effects and the origin of CeO2-induced activity enhancement
abstract: Catalytic hydrogenation over supported Ru catalysts offers an effective way for perchlorate (ClO 4 - ) decomposition in water to Cl - ; however, the role of catalyst supports in determining catalytic performance remains poorly understood. In this study, Ru catalysts supported on five oxide supports were evaluated for ClO 4 - reduction with H 2 . Among them, Ru/CeO 2 and Ru/ZrO 2 showed markedly higher activities than Ru/SiO 2 , Ru/Al 2 O 3 , and Ru/TiO 2 . The catalytic activity generally correlated with Ru dispersion and the electronic state of Ru. In particular, Ru/ZrO 2 contained highly dispersed Ru species and electron-rich Ru sites, both of which contributed to its high activity. In contrast, Ru/CeO 2 deviated from this trend. Kinetic analysis revealed that the exceptional activity of Ru/CeO 2 originated from enhanced activation of adsorbed ClO 4 - rather than from H 2 activation. Systematic variation of the CeO 2 source and pre-calcination temperature further showed that spectroscopic features associated with the local Ru-CeO 2 interfacial environment correlated with turnover frequency, whereas no single oxygen-defect descriptor alone accounted for the activity variation. These findings highlight the important role of the specific Ru-CeO 2 interfacial environment in promoting ClO 4 - activation.

title: Buoyancy-enabled direct lithium extraction from brines using waste-derived Li-Al LDH-coated cenospheres
abstract: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from salt-lake brines is challenged by the low concentration of Li + and abundant competing ions, as well as the difficulty of separating adsorbents after adsorption. Here, we develop a buoyancy-enabled adsorption strategy using a self-floating solid-bubble adsorbent (SBA) composed of fly ash cenospheres coated with Li-Al layered double hydroxide (LDH). The low-density cenosphere core provides buoyancy and mechanical support, while the Li-Al LDH shell supplies vacancy sites for selective Li + capture. The resulting SBA spontaneously floats at the brine-air interface, enabling interfacial Li + adsorption and direct surface recovery without packed-column operation or subsequent solid-liquid separation. In simulated and authentic Qarhan brines, SBA exhibited high Li + selectivity, with a Li + /Mg 2+ separation coefficient of 699.59 and a Li + uptake of 2.51 mg·g -1 in authentic brine. After 10 adsorption-desorption cycles, the Li + uptake remained 2.39 mg·g -1 , while 91.65% of the adsorbent remained afloat under dynamic disturbance. Mechanistic analysis indicates that Li + selectivity arises mainly from size-compatible insertion into LDH vacancies, whereas competing ions are constrained by hydration and size mismatch. This work demonstrates a waste-derived, buoyancy-enabled approach that integrates selective Li + capture with facile adsorbent recovery for lithium extraction from brines.

title: Arsenic induces hepatic lipid accumulation associated with DNA methylation alterations and oxidative stress in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma)
abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination is a global environmental concern, but its toxicity and mechanisms on marine organisms remain largely unknown. In this study, marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) were exposed to dietary arsenate (AsV) at 0, 100, and 1000 μg/g for 28 days, and primary hepatocyte cultures were established to investigate the underlying mechanisms. The results showed that AsV induced significant and dose‑dependent lipid accumulation both in vivo and in vitro, following the internal arsenic burden. The transcription of lipogenic genes was upregulated, and the transcription of lipolytic genes was downregulated after AsV exposure. AsV reduced the level of SAM, suppressed transcription of dnmt1 and tet3, and induced hypomethylation of the ppargc1b promoter. Correspondingly, AsV upregulated the transcription of ppargc1b, which might modulate downstream genes of the PPAR signaling pathway and impaired lipid metabolism. In addition, the redox cycle of arsenic triggered oxidative stress and endoplasmic reticulum stress. The ROS scavengers GSH and NAC significantly alleviated arsenic‑induced lipid accumulation and aberrant gene expression, whereas the ER stress PBA inhibitor showed no protective effect. Our results demonstrated that AsV induced lipid accumulation associated with DNA methylation alterations and oxidative stress, providing insights into arsenic lipotoxicity and ecological risk assessment in marine environments.

title: The dietary pathways of heavy metal accumulation in wild fish from the urbanized waterways of Pearl River Estuary at Guangzhou, China: Insights from fatty acid biomarkers
abstract: Diet critically influences heavy metal bioaccumulation in fish but their corresponding processes were rarely detailed. Given the severe heavy metal pollution in wild fish from heavily urbanized section of Pearl River Estuary in Guangzhou, this study integrated contamination surveys with fatty acid tracing to identify dietary pathways driving metal accumulation, with their impacts further evaluated through health risk assessment. Results showed that As and Pb exceeded maximum residue limits in some fish. 23 fatty acids were detected, which consisted of 40.39%, 37.11%, and 22.50% for MUFAs, SFAs, and PUFAs, respectively. Fish were classified into two groups via bi‑cluster analysis: a PUFA‑rich benthic feeding group accumulating As and Cd, and a SFA/MUFA‑rich pelagic feeding group accumulating other metals. Significant correlations between As, Cd and ω‑3 PUFAs suggested a dietary pathway from algae/detritus, while the rest metals positively correlated with most SFAs and MUFAs, indicating a dietary pathway from plankton/bacteria. Positive correlations of C17:0 and C17:1 with most metals suggested the predominance of bacterial pathways in enhancing metals accumulation, whereas the negative correlations of C18:1ω9 and C18:2ω6 with metals identified dietary pathways from phytoplankton and terrestrial detritus that mitigate metal accumulation. The higher hazard index (HI) of As highlighted its higher risk, especially for children, with nearly 80% of the HI derived from the algae/detritus pathway. Therefore, controlling the risk of fish should focus on the management of the benthic environment. This study demonstrated metals have distinct dietary pathways, and identifying high‑risk metal intake pathways is fundamental for strengthening pollution risk control.

title: Semi-dynamic Zn leaching from solidified/stabilized dredged soil under varying curing temperatures: Kinetics and mechanisms
abstract: Elevated curing temperatures accelerate hydration and promote matrix densification in cement-based solidification/stabilization (S/S), yet whether these benefits improve Zn retention across contrasting leachants remains unclear. Zn-contaminated slurry-like mud treated with an ordinary Portland cement-ground-granulated blast-furnace slag binder was cured at 20, 40, or 60 °C and subjected to accelerated semi-dynamic leaching in deionized water (DW; pH ∼7.0), sulfuric/nitric-acid simulated acid rain (SN; pH = 3.20), and acetic acid (AA; pH = 2.88). Results reveal a fundamental trade-off: elevated temperatures refined the pore structure and shifted Zn toward less labile fractions, but reduced alkaline buffering and lowered leachate pH under DW and SN. Under DW, heat curing suppressed Zn release by increasing resistance to diffusive transport through the hydrated matrix (D e ≈ 10 -18 -10 -17 m 2 s -1 ). Under AA, Zn release was dissolution-dominated at all temperatures; strong Ca-Zn coupling and 94-98% outer-layer Ca/Si depletion supported matrix decalcification and mobilization of matrix-associated Zn. Notably, under SN, earlier buffering depletion advanced the transition from diffusion-dominated to dissolution-dominated kinetics below an empirical leachate-pH transition point of ∼4.4. Near-zero Ca-Zn coupling and SEM-EDS/TG-DTG evidence supported preferential acid-labile Zn mobilization with localized near-surface decalcification. Maximum interval-mean Zn concentrations were 0.164-0.325 mg L -1 under SN and 4.418-6.456 mg L -1 under AA; concentrations under SN remained below the Chinese Class II groundwater Zn limit of 0.5 mg L -1 . These findings demonstrate that curing temperature shifts the balance between transport resistance and buffering capacity, providing a mechanistic basis for matching curing strategies to exposure chemistry in engineering design.

title: Copper valence dynamics link microbial redox functions to humification during composting
abstract: Organic-waste composting supports resource recovery, but microbial links between Cu transformation and humification remain insufficiently resolved. We combined XPS-Auger analysis, metagenomics, day-4 metatranscriptomics, and genome-resolved analysis to compare Cu(I), Cu(II), and mixed-valence treatments receiving equal Cu inputs with a control without added Cu (CK) during lignocellulosic composting. By day 30, surface Cu(I) proportions reached 55.63% and 59.04% in Cu(I) and mixed-valence treatments, respectively, whereas the Cu(II) treatment remained Cu(II)-dominated. On day 4, AA1 accounted for 1.331% of the exported CAZy expression total in CK and 2.085-2.931% in Cu treatments, alongside distinct substrate-transformation and redox profiles. Cu treatments showed higher day-4 transcript levels of carbohydrate-associated MAG204 and Cu-homeostasis-associated MAG674. The Cu(I) treatment had the greatest humic acid (HA) concentration gain (60.09 g kg⁻¹), whereas the mixed-valence treatment had the highest final HA concentration (122.45 g kg⁻¹). The findings support a Cu-valence-associated working model of redox-active humification; extracellular electron transfer remains to be verified by direct electrochemical measurements.

title: Suspended particulate matter enhances light responsive superoxide generation at aquatic biofilm interfaces via regulating matrix photoreactivity and electron transfer
abstract: Suspended particulate matter (SPM) is ubiquitous in shallow waters and frequently interact with aquatic biofilms, yet its role in regulating biofilm-derived superoxide (O 2 ·- ) generation remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that SPM enhances light-responsive O 2 ·- generation at submerged macrophyte biofilm interfaces via modulating electron supply, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) photoreactivity, and EPS-mediated electron transfer. During biofilm development, the maximum interfacial O 2 ·- production increased 2.36-fold as SPM concentration rose from 0 to 300 mg L -1 , reflecting enhanced biofilm biomass accumulation and elevated mass-normalized O 2 ·- production activity. SPM exposure intensified light-driven O 2 ·- generation from 323.22 ± 6.15-558.24 ± 37.46 nmol mg C -1 h -1 , and improved the electron-donating capacity from 2.11 ± 0.21-4.87 ± 0.49 μmol e - mg C -1 in intact biofilms. Isolated EPS exhibited a tighter correlation between electron-donating capacity and light-induced O 2 ·- generation. Further experiments involving electron donors, inhibitors and redox mediators confirmed that SPM incorporation facilitates EPS-mediated electron transfer to molecular oxygen, with a 2.04-fold response at 300 mg L -1 SPM under sufficient electron-donor supply. Collectively, our findings reveal a biofilm-dependent mechanism for SPM enhances O 2 ·- formation and highlight SPM as an overlooked regulator of biofilm interfacial O 2 ·- generation in shallow aquatic ecosystems.

title: Associations of particulate matter-associated microbial profiles with lung and intestinal microbiomes in healthy mice
abstract: Ambient air pollution has detrimental effects on human health. We investigated exposure-related differences and microbial overlap among PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes in mice exposed to PM₁, high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA)-filtered air, or clean air. PM₁ was characterized for soluble ions, metals, carbonaceous fractions, and oxidative potential, while gaseous pollutants data were obtained from air-quality monitoring stations. PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes were analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were quantified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Proteobacteria was the dominant phylum in PM₁. PM₁ contained diverse chemical constituents, including soluble ions, metals, and oxidative species. Lung microbial diversity remained largely unchanged, whereas the gut microbiome was significantly altered. Compared with control, the PM₁ group showed reduced Actinobacteriota and Bacteroidota, while Campylobacterota and Patescibacteria decreased in both HEPA and PM₁ groups. Verrucomicrobiota increased in the HEPA group, and Proteobacteria increased in the PM₁ group compared with both HEPA and control groups. Correlation analyses identified associations between lung and gut microbiomes, environmental variables, PM₁ characteristics, gaseous pollutants, and SCFAs. Eleven bacterial families and six genera overlapped among PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes in the PM₁ group. Overall, ambient air pollution was associated with gut dysbiosis in mice.

title: Iodine-induced local coordination reconstruction of Bi2MoO6 for superoxide-dominated photocatalytic degradation and mineralization of bisphenol A
abstract: Efficient photocatalytic degradation and mineralization of endocrine-disrupting pollutants require enhanced visible-light utilization, efficient charge separation, and controlled generation of reactive oxygen species. Herein, iodine-regulated Bi 2 MoO 6 was developed for visible-light-driven degradation of bisphenol A (BPA) through a superoxide radical (·O 2 - )-dominated pathway. Bi L 3 -edge EXAFS analysis reveals that iodine modulation does not yield metallic Bi or a simple Bi 2 O 3 -like phase, but rather generates a heterogeneous, distorted Bi-O coordination environment with multiple scattering paths, elongated Bi-O bonds, and enhanced local disorder. This local coordination reconstruction, coupled with oxygen-vacancy-related defect modulation, reshapes the electronic structure of Bi 2 MoO 6 , leading to enhanced visible-light absorption, improved charge separation, a more favorable conduction-band position, and strengthened O 2 adsorption/activation. The optimized iodine-regulated Bi 2 MoO 6 , denoted BMI-2, achieves approximately 99% BPA removal within 80 min and 60.17% TOC mineralization under visible light, while maintaining stable degradation performance over pH 5-9. Radical-trapping experiments, ESR spectroscopy, in situ FT-IR, HPLC-MS analysis, KPFM, and DFT calculations collectively confirm that BPA degradation proceeds predominantly through a ·O 2 - -mediated pathway involving isopropyl bridge cleavage, aromatic ring opening, and progressive oxidation. This work provides atomic-level insight into dopant-defect regulated oxygen activation and offers a rational strategy for designing ROS-selective photocatalysts for hazardous organic pollutant remediation.

title: Crystal facet engineering of Mn3O4 supported Ru catalysts for boosted photothermal propane oxidation: Synergy between metallic Ru0 and oxygen vacancies
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement remains a significant challenge, particularly for the deep oxidation of inert short-chain alkanes like propane. Herein, we report a facet-engineered Ru/Mn 3 O 4 catalyst where the exposure of Mn 3 O 4 {010} facets triggers a remarkable activity inversion compared to {110} facets upon light irradiation. Comprehensive analyses reveal a distinct facet-dependent metal-support interaction. On the {010} facet, pronounced interfacial charge transfer stabilizes a high proportion of metallic Ru 0 and reduces the oxygen vacancy formation energy to 1.84 eV. The resulting electronically coupled Ru/Mn 3 O 4 {010} interface thus combines electron-rich Ru 0 domains with a high density of oxygen vacancies; their synergy facilitates the cleavage of C-H bonds and accelerates the conversion from carboxylate intermediates to CO 2 by generating reactive ·O 2 - species. Consequently, the Ru/Mn 3 O 4 -D catalyst achieves a 90% propane conversion at 169 °C under full-spectrum irradiation, corresponding to a significantly lowered activation energy of 17.4 kJ/mol. Conversely, the {110} facet tends to anchor oxidized Ru species, leading to severe intermediate accumulation and inferior performance. This work not only elucidates the microscopic origin of facet-dependent influence in photothermal catalysis but also provides a feasible strategy for designing catalysts with optimized interfacial electronic structures.

title: Azelaic and pipecolic acids mitigate chromium toxicity in barley seedlings by maintaining redox and ion homeostasis and depriving Cr uptake
abstract: The roles of pipecolic (Pip) and azelaic (AzA) acids in mitigating Cr-induced injury in plants remain uninvestigated, rendering their role somewhat mysterious. Chromium reduced seedling growth, photosynthetic pigments, nutrient uptake, and relative water content, and triggered oxidative bursts relative to nonpolluted seedlings. AzA or Pip spraying reversed Cr toxicity on growth while decreasing Cr bioaccumulation. Under normal or Cr-pollution conditions, spraying Pip and AzA increased photosynthetic pigments, chlorophyll stability index, nutrient uptake, and seedling development relative to untreated seedlings in those conditions. Furthermore, AzA or Pip spraying preserves redox homeostasis by boosting antioxidant solutes and antioxidant enzyme activity over untreated seedlings. Spraying Pip to Cr-affected seedlings significantly increased dry mass of shoots (72.50%) and roots (36.36%), total phenols (219.04%), and total chlorophyll (32.66%) over those treated with water. This increase was linked to a great reduction in H 2 O 2 (31.22%), malondialdehyde (16.31%), membrane permeability (47.04%), and Cr uptake in shoots (39.08%) and roots (26.50%). Collectively, current outcomes highlight that Pip or AzA can mitigate Cr injury by strengthening antioxidant capacity, sustaining ion homeostasis, refining root structure, and reducing Cr bioaccumulation and translocation. Pip, as a novel molecule, may be favored over AzA for barley establishment in Cr-contaminated conditions.

title: Investigation of bubble dynamic evolution and evaporation micro-explosion characteristics of tire pyrolysis oil-diesel blended fuel droplets
abstract: Tire pyrolysis oil (TPO) has physicochemical properties similar to diesel and can be regarded as a promising alternative fuel for diesel engines. This study employed a suspended-droplet evaporation apparatus to capture the evaporation process of TPO-diesel-blended fuel droplets and investigated the effects of TPO blending ratio and initial droplet volume on the bubble nucleation mechanism and the micro-explosion mode transition. The results show that the evaporation process of the blended fuel droplets can be divided into three stages: fluctuation evaporation, intense micro-explosion, and stable evaporation. Surface pit nucleation is the primary bubble nucleation mode, while raft-interface nucleation serves as a secondary mechanism, together facilitating the initial formation of bubbles within the droplet. As the TPO blending ratio increases, the bubble nucleation mode changes from multi-point nucleation to single-point nucleation, the nucleation location shifts from the droplet surface toward the center, and the maximum micro-explosion intensity increases. The blended fuel with a 20% TPO exhibits the shortest droplet lifetime. Variations in the initial droplet size can not alter the bubble nucleation mode or micro-explosion mode, but can increase the degree of droplet expansion. Increasing the initial droplet size effectively enhanced the micro-explosion intensity, but had no significant effect on droplet lifetime.

title: Emerging contaminants in hospital wastewater: A critical review of characteristics, fate, risks, and treatment
abstract: Hospital wastewater (HWW) represents a critical source of environmental and public health concerns, particularly in the post-epidemic era marked by frequent infectious disease outbreaks. This review offers a comprehensive overview of the characteristics, fate, risks, and remediation strategies of emerging contaminants (ECs) in HWW. The characteristics and properties of typical ECs reported in HWW are systematically analyzed. Six major classes of pharmaceuticals and ten classes of antibiotics have been detected. Statistical analysis reveals that iodinated contrast media (ICMs) are detected at the highest concentrations (up to 1050 μg/L), whereas antibiotics show the highest detection frequencies. The occurrence of last-resort antibiotic resistance genes (LARGs) in HWW has also been frequently reported. Analysis of environmental fate shows that ECs are probably transformed via photolysis, hydrolysis, biotransformation, adsorption, and deposition. Ecotoxicological risk assessment indicates that the LC 50 for sensitive organisms occurs at HWW proportions of only 0.508%–6.1% (v/v) over exposure durations of 12–96 h. Particularly, the effectiveness of advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) is evaluated in real HWW treatment. The removal rates of COD, TOC, NH 3 -N, ARGs, and ECs (where reported) across electrochemical AOPs, photochemical AOPs, ozonation, and persulfate activation are statistically analyzed. Moreover, the performance, advantages, and limitations of various AOPs are critically compared to guide tailored HWW management. Pilot-scale devices have also been evaluated for real HWW treatment, demonstrating considerable promise for practical application. This review is expected to serve as a valuable reference for academic researchers and practicing engineers engaged in HWW treatment and environmental risk control.

title: Gut microbiota-derived 1H-Indole-3-propanoic acid deficiency mediates BPB-induced decidualization impairment via TLR4/NF-κB pathway
abstract: As an important alternative to bisphenol A (BPA), the reproductive toxicity of bisphenol B (BPB) has drawn increasing concern, but the mechanism by which BPB impairs uterine decidualization remains unclear. This study investigated whether early pregnancy BPB exposure impairs decidualization via the "gut microbiota-1H-Indole-3-propanoic acid (IPA)-Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor kappa-B (TLR4/NF-κB)" axis. Results showed that BPB inhibited embryo implantation, decidual cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and disrupted intestinal barrier integrity. 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics revealed that BPB induced gut dysbiosis (reduction in Lactobacillus) and decreased serum IPA, with IPA positively correlated with Lactobacillus abundance. Network pharmacology predicted that IPA targets were enriched in the TLR4/NF-κB pathway. Fecal microbiota transplantation confirmed that transferring BPB-exposed microbiota replicated decidualization impairment and IPA reduction. Exogenous IPA supplementation inhibited BPB-induced TLR4/NF-κB activation and inflammatory cytokine release, and rescued decidualization. The TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 partially restored decidualization function. In summary, early pregnancy BPB exposure reduces IPA-producing bacteria such as Lactobacillus, leading to decreased IPA, which subsequently activates the uterine TLR4/NF-κB pathway and impairs decidualization. Supplementation of IPA or TLR4 inhibition effectively rescues this impairment, providing a potential target for intervention in environmentally related reproductive disorders.

title: Widespread antibiotic resistance and multidrug resistance in Escherichia coli from surface waters near dairies and a calf ranch in Wisconsin: Implications for hotspot screening and multi-method monitoring
abstract: Although concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) are known sources of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), gaps remain regarding AMR dissemination to environments and monitoring methods. Impacts of large dairies and a calf ranch in Wisconsin on the environmental resistome were assessed at nine surface water sites near CAFOs and two nearby unimpaired sites. 1297 Escherichia coli (EC) isolates were tested against a suite of antibiotics by Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion. Up to 68% of EC isolates at dairy-impacted sites and 70% downstream of the calf ranch exhibited multidrug resistance (MDR), versus up to 8% at the unimpaired sites. Fecal indicator bacteria kits modified with antibiotics detected elevated extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing (ESBL) EC at the site exhibiting highest MDR, suggesting use as a screening tool. Metagenomic analysis showed elevated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), abundance, diversity, and human health risk scores at the calf ranch-impacted site. Follow-up sampling just upstream and downstream of the calf ranch showed dramatic increases in multiple measures, indicating calf ranches may warrant additional monitoring and elucidate more complex processes such horizontal gene transfer. Culture-based results revealed pronounced AMR hotspots and differences among sampling events only partially reflected by metagenomic analysis and a limited quantitative PCR (qPCR) panel, underscoring the importance of monitoring through complementary methods.

title: Effect of neonicotinoid insecticide exposure during early life on neurodevelopment: An integrated assessment via animal models and the TRAEC strategy
abstract: The potential neurodevelopmental risks of gestational neonicotinoid (NNIs) exposure have attracted increasing attention. Our previous population study revealed that prenatal thiamethoxam (THM) exposure affects offspring neurocognitive development, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, and systematic risk assessment and risk comparison of NNIs are still scarce. We systematically investigated the neurodevelopmental effects of early-life THM exposure by integrating an original animal model with the Targeted Risk Assessment of Environmental Chemicals (TRAEC) risk assessment framework. In the animal model, the results showed that prenatal exposure to 0.50 mg/kg bw/day THM induced anxiety-like behavior and cognitive impairment in mouse offspring, with evident hippocampal dentate gyrus damage in male offspring. KEGG analysis revealed that male offspring primarily involved pathways related to cellular structure and growth, while female offspring exhibited alterations in energy metabolism and oxidative stress. Based on multidimensional evidence using the TRAEC framework, early-life NNI exposure yielded a moderate neurodevelopmental risk score of 7.72, with THM (risk scores: 7.33) and thiacloprid (7.65) posing the highest risks. This study provides clues to the potential neurodevelopmental toxicity mechanisms of THM and characterized its environmental risk using the TRAEC framework, providing scientific evidence for policy formulation.

title: Systematic review on the toxicity of wildfire emitted particulate matter: State of science, knowledge gaps and way forward
abstract: The intensity and frequency of wildfires have increased worldwide. The health impact of wildfire emitted particulate matter (WFPM) has been considered an emerging field in air pollution research. This review presents the state of toxicological science related to WFPM for the 2005-2025 period. We found 46 peer-reviewed in vitro and in vivo studies, excluding clinical, epidemiological, and ecotoxicological studies. Environmental WFPM collected during active wildfires was used to model exposure in only 42% of in vitro and 27% of in vivo studies. Most in vitro studies investigate effects on the pulmonary system (50%) and on macrophages (17%), with all other biological systems corresponding to 33%. Mechanisms of toxicity focused mostly on inflammatory and stress response, and DNA damage/mutation. Inhalation studies evaluated lung (46%), cardiovascular (15%) and brain (15%) effects, with the remaining 24% addressing reproductive, genetic or immune effects. WFPM induced significant toxicity with distinct mechanisms as a function of concentration, particle-size, biomass type and burning conditions. Knowledge gaps included: lack of a comprehensive physicochemical characterization of WFPM to achieve robust structure-activity conclusions, use of realistic concentrations representing human exposure scenarios, chronic exposure studies, evaluation of systemic effects and toxicokinetic studies, potential synergistic effects with other anthropogenic air pollution sources.

title: Influence of ultraviolet/chlor(am)ine processes on the formation of toxicity and aromatic byproduct from the dipeptide tyrosyl-L-phenylalanine
abstract: Amino acids and peptides in wastewater are key precursors of highly toxic nitrogenous disinfection byproducts (N-DBPs) during chlor(am)ination. The UV/chlor(am)ine processes have been increasingly employed for toxicity control, yet their efficacy against peptide precursors remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the toxicity control of UV/chlor(am)ine on tyrosyl-L-phenylalanine (Tyr-Phe), its monomers (Phe, Tyr), and real secondary effluents. At a UV dose of 1200 mJ·cm -2 , 5 mg-Cl 2 ·L -1 disinfectant and 4 mg-C·L -1 precursor, UV/chlorine reduced the cytotoxicity and genotoxicity of Tyr-Phe by 75.7% and 82.8%, respectively (UV/chloramine: 55.5% and 64.4%). Total organic chlorine (TOCl) and Tyr-Phe-derived byproduct counts decreased by > 70% and > 30%, accompanied by a shift toward higher oxidation states and lower aromaticity. Four low molecular weight DBPs (trichloromethane, dichloroacetonitrile, trichloroacetaldehyde, and chloroacetone) and seven identified emerging aromatic DBPs were also significantly reduced. Similar trends were observed for Phe, Tyr, and real secondary effluents. Radical quenching coupled with TOCl measurements indicated that ·OH and ·Cl, individually or together, contribute to the suppression of DBP formation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that UV/chlor(am)ine effectively controls DBP formation and associated toxicity from aromatic peptides and their monomers in wastewater disinfection.

title: Earthworm-assisted enrichment of specific indigenous soil microbes for the preferential degradation of hexaconazole R-enantiomer
abstract: This study examined the influence of earthworm addition on the enantiomer-specific degradation of the chiral triazole fungicide hexaconazole, focusing on the associated functional bacterial communities in soil and earthworm casts. S-hexaconazole was preferentially degraded in soil, whereas R-hexaconazole strongly inhibited soil microbial activities. Earthworm addition preferentially accelerated R-hexaconazole degradation and eliminated its inhibitory effects. Two soil bacterial families, Sphingomonadaceae and Xanthomonadaceae, and two biodegradation genes, p450 and ppo, were associated with the preferential degradation of S-hexaconazole. Two bacterial strains, HEX1 and HEX2, which belong to Sphingomonadaceae and Xanthomonadaceae, respectively, degraded R-hexaconazole but preferentially degraded S-hexaconazole in pure culture. In the R-hexaconazole treatment, earthworms selectively increased the abundances of Sphingomonadaceae, Xanthomonadaceae, and ppo, with Xanthomonadaceae and ppo levels being 23.1% and 25.1% higher, respectively, than those in the S-hexaconazole treatment, thereby shifting the community-level degradation preference toward R-hexaconazole. Notably, similar patterns were observed in earthworm casts. Network and metagenomic binning analyses revealed that Sphingomonadaceae and Xanthomonadaceae were potential hosts of the p450 and ppo. These findings suggest that earthworms facilitate the enrichment of specific indigenous soil bacterial families (Sphingomonadaceae and Xanthomonadaceae) to accelerate the preferential degradation of R-hexaconazole, highlighting the potential of earthworms to mitigate the risks in chiral fungicide-contaminated soil.

title: Contrasting potential mediating roles of DOC and SOM in microplastic effects on soil heavy metals bioavailability: A meta-analysis and machine learning approach
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and heavy metals (HMs) often co-occur in soil, yet the role of soil organic matter (SOM) fractions in mediating the effects of MPs on HMs bioavailability remains unclear. Here, data from 52 studies were used to investigate whether dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and soil organic matter (SOM) serve as contrasting mediating pathways, by integrating meta-analysis, machine learning, and structural equation modeling (SEM). MPs increased DOC, SOM, and HMs bioavailability by 14.84%, 13.82%, and 5.21%, respectively. DOC changes positively correlated with HMs bioavailability, whereas SOM showed a U-shaped relationship. MPs size, time, and soil pH were identified as common drivers across all responses. Biodegradable MPs and higher water holding capacity promoted DOC increases and HMs mobilization, while higher MPs concentrations enhanced SOM accumulation and HMs immobilization. SEM supported DOC and SOM as two opposing mediating pathways: DOC exerted a positive mobilization effect, while SOM exerted a negative immobilization effect. Their dynamic balance may contribute to the net direction of HMs bioavailability. These findings reveal that MPs influence HMs bioavailability primarily through two contrasting OM pathways, rather than through direct MPs-metal interactions. Distinguishing DOC from SOM is therefore critical for assessing the ecological risks of MPs-HMs co-contamination in soil.

title: Tire-related additives distribution in roadside soils and uptake by native plants: Insights from laboratory and field studies
abstract: The toxicity of Tire and Road Wear Particles (TRWP) is mainly linked to organic additives and their transformation products. This study used a dual approach: controlled lab experiments on root uptake in clover, and paired soil-plant sampling from roadside environments, to assess contamination patterns and exposure routes. In soils spiked with 1% tire wear particles, clover roots absorbed tire-related additives and translocated them to leaves, with total concentrations of 15 additives reaching 621 ± 209 ng/g d.w. Roadside soils and plants were also significantly impacted, with concentrations declining exponentially with distance from the road-ranging from 72 to 0.7 ng/g d.w in soils and 777-73 ng/g d.w in plants between 1 m and 10 m. Notably, in pot experiments soil concentrations exceeded plant concentrations, whereas at roadside sites, plants showed much higher concentrations than soil. This contrast suggests that atmospheric deposition, rather than root uptake, is the dominant pathway by which tire-derived additives contaminate plants in real-world conditions. These findings offer key insights into the widespread occurrence of tire-derived compounds in terrestrial environments near roads, and underscore the need for further research to accurately assess the environmental and human health risks posed by this contamination.

title: Study on road performance, microstructural evolution, and environmental safety of red mud-modified reactive cold-mix asphalt mixtures
abstract: Slow early-strength development limits the application of cold-mix asphalt (CMA), while environmental challenges of red mud (RM) utilization remain unresolved. This study developed RM-modified reactive cold-mix asphalt mixtures (RCMA) using reactive liquid asphalt (RLA), an alkali activator, and water to integrate organic curing with inorganic activation. The effects of RM on mechanical performance, microstructure, and environmental stability were investigated through multi-age tests, X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and leaching tests. Results showed that 30% reactive diluent (RD) and 5% RLA achieved workability and early-age stability. Compared with limestone powder (LP), RM improved high-temperature stability, low-temperature cracking resistance, and moisture durability, with residual stability (RS) close to or above 100% after water immersion. RM incorporation promoted a denser organic-inorganic structure by introducing Si-, Al-, and Fe-bearing reactive components and enhancing interfacial bonding. Leaching tests under thermal, ambient, and freeze-thaw conditions confirmed that regulated metals remained below limits, although Ni showed higher sensitivity. Enhanced performance was attributed to synergistic effects of moisture-triggered polyurea network and RM-derived reaction-product-rich regions, improving interfacial transition zone (ITZ) densification, stress transfer, and contaminant retention. This study provides a low-energy approach for RM utilization in sustainable pavement engineering.

title: Component-specific effects shape shifts between synergism and antagonism in organophosphate ester mixtures
abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs) frequently co-occur in human exposure, yet their combined hazards cannot be reliably inferred from single-compound toxicity. How individual OPEs reshape non-additive effects across compositions and effect levels remains unclear. Here, we investigated interaction patterns and associated biological responses of representative OPE mixtures, including tributyl phosphate (TNBP), triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), and tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCIPP), using human keratinocytes as a dermal exposure model. Combination index (CI) analysis revealed composition- and effect-level-dependent interactions. Ternary mixtures exhibited distinct composition-dependent CI-Fa trajectories, with some compositions trending toward additivity at higher effect levels, whereas TPHP-rich mixtures showed progressively stronger synergism. Binary mixtures showed pair-dependent interactions, with TPHP-TDCIPP and TNBP-TDCIPP exhibiting contrasting interaction modes. At total nominal molar concentrations of 0.1, 1, and 10 μM for the 1:1:1 ternary mixture, co-exposure modestly increased HaCaT monolayer permeability, reaching statistical significance at 10 μM, and altered differentiation-related gene expression, revealing barrier-associated effects. Untargeted metabolomics of individual and mixture exposures further revealed distinct lipid remodeling patterns, including interaction-associated differences in glycerophospholipid responses. Collectively, OPE mixture hazards depend not only on individual toxicity but also on the capacity of specific components to modify combined effects, supporting improved mixture hazard characterization and prioritization of interaction-modifying contaminants.

title: Dynamic changes of chicken gut microbiota and resistome during enrofloxacin treatment against multidrug-resistant Salmonella based on metagenomics
abstract: Antibiotics are widely used to treat and prevent bacterial infections in human and animals. However, the impact of antibiotic dose on bacterial burden and diachronic changes and transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in gut bacterial infections remains unclear. Here, we used enrofloxacin (ENR) at sub-inhibitory (1 mg/kg b.w.), prophylactic (3.03 mg/kg b.w.), and therapeutic (10 mg/kg b.w.) doses to treat infections with Salmonella harboring plasmid pJX-4, with infected but untreated groups as controls. We found that subtherapeutic ENR may pose potential risks to the gut ecosystem. Specifically, sub-inhibitory ENR led to persistently high Salmonella and its carried resistance gene qnrS1 levels; under this dose condition, preliminary evidence suggested that intestinal Escherichia coli was a potential host for in vivo transfer of plasmid pJX-4. The prophylactic dose group showed significantly higher relative abundances of human bacterial pathogens and ARGs, especially during treatment. Furthermore, this group was enriched in genes related to oxidative stress, cellular signaling, and secretion systems, and these functional genes were primarily associated with ARGs. Overall, different ENR doses shaped distinct evolutionary trajectories of the gut microbiome and resistome. This study provides a theoretical basis for the rational use of antibiotics in treating bacterial infections.

title: Critical fine particles in road dust: oxidative potential, distribution, and driving factors
abstract: Urban road dust act as both a sink and a secondary source of airborne fine particles (FPs), yet the components that determine their oxidative potential (OP), a metric of particle-induced reactive oxygen species, remain poorly understood. Here, we combined acellular OP measurements using the dithiothreitol assay with single particle ICP time-of-flight mass spectrometry to analyze FPs from Shanghai road dust. Samples collected in 2013 and 2022, spanning a period of major energy and emission transitions in China. The OP of road dust FPs decreased by approximately 28% between 2013 and 2022, significantly in industrial areas but not in traffic areas. Among all measured particle components, Fe-rich FPs associated with toxic metals (e.g., Cr, Zn, and Pb) emerged as the strongest correlates of OP. Notably, magnetite-rich FPs, a proxy for such Fe-rich toxic carriers, accounted for only 7.0% of the FP mass in selected dust samples but contributed 29%-68% of OP, highlighting their disproportionate oxidative activity. Variable importance analysis for Fe-rich FPs associated with toxic metals showed that the highest ranked factors shifted from industrial-related factors in 2013 to traffic-related factors in 2022. Our findings suggest that traffic-related emissions warrant particular attention in future mitigation strategies.

title: From Disinfectants to Endocrine Disruptors: Unveiling the Inhibitory Potential of Oxygenated Benzalkonium Analogues on Gonadal 3β-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenases via Enzyme Kinetics Analysis and Computational Simulations
Coupled evolution of sedimentary environment and groundwater flow systems drives groundwater arsenic heterogeneity in the Yangtze River Basin
abstract: In the alluvial-lacustrine Jianghan Plain (JHP), widespread but heterogeneous arsenic(As) contamination in groundwater is closely related to the evolution of the groundwater flow system (GFS) since the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) under progressively changing climatic conditions. Approximately 72% of groundwater samples in As hotspots exceeded the WHO (World Health Organization) guideline of 10 μg/L, with concentrations up to 2620 μg/L. However, the role of GFS evolution as a key driver of As enrichment has received limited attention. Through systematic integration of basin sedimentology, paleohydrogeology, and the modern hydrogeochemical environment, this study established a macro-scale theoretical framework linking "sedimentary evolution-GFS driving-geochemical field formation" in the JHP. Paleoclimate-controlled sedimentary environment significantly influenced both GFS evolution and As-rich groundwater development since the LGM. Deep incision of the ancient Yangtze River channel during the LGM created a strong potential sink and promoted an upward discharge pattern of multi-hierarchical GFSs. Rapid burial of weathered As-rich minerals during the late deglaciation period (LDP) provided a material source. The formation of an overlying clay layer during the Holocene warm period (HWP) maintained reducing conditions in the underlying aquifer. Collectively, these processes formed the origin of As-rich groundwater. Additionally, the hierarchically nested GFS pattern characterized by a gradually sluggish flow and upward discharge, drives the continuous convergence of As-rich groundwater toward regional discharge areas, contributing to the stable occurrence and heterogeneous distribution of As. This conceptual model elucidated the control mechanisms of As-rich groundwater in alluvial-lacustrine plains, supporting effective utilization and sustainable management of regional groundwater.

title: Beyond sulfites: Integrating sulfonated derivatives into food safety
abstract: Existing safety frameworks, focused narrowly on free and reversibly bound sulfite residues, fail to account for the persistent sulfonated derivatives formed during the sulfite treatment of food. While previous research identified these derivatives as chemical markers of sulfite treatment, these efforts rarely progressed beyond preliminary discovery. Critically, this foundational work lacked a systematic evaluation of their chemical and toxicological properties, and its insights have not been translated into regulatory practice. Drawing on preliminary evidence, this perspective argues for a paradigm shift in sulfite risk monitoring by expanding the scope beyond free and reversibly bound sulfite to include these persistent irreversibly bound sulfonated derivatives. To achieve this goal, we propose a foundational scientific framework that systematically characterizes key sulfonated derivatives, evaluates their toxicity, and develops robust analytical methods. We call upon researchers, industry stakeholders, and regulatory bodies to build on this foundation together to establish globally harmonized detection methods and safety thresholds. This collaboration is essential for developing updated, evidence-based regulations for food surveillance, ultimately ensuring stronger consumer protection.

title: Combined nitrate and oxygen dosing restores phosphorus retention and suppresses sulfide without mobilizing legacy sediment metals in a eutrophic urban lake
abstract: Lake Schäfersee (Berlin, Germany), a eutrophic urban lake with a regularly anoxic, sulfidic hypolimnion and metal-contaminated sediments, has been treated since 2017 by hypolimnetic dosing of calcium nitrate (Ca(NO 3 ) 2 ) and oxygen-saturated water. We monitored inorganic nutrients, dissolved organic carbon, sulfide, (semi)metals, and the sediment microbial community. Ca(NO 3 ) 2 additions produced transient NO 3 -N peaks confined to the hypolimnion, and concentrations in the epilimnion stayed <4.5 mg L -1 . Bottom-water redox potential turned positive after dosing. Relative to untreated years, hypolimnetic O 2 increased, while H 2 S fell by 8 2 %, PO 4 -P by 87%, and NH 4 -N by 72%; pore-water DOC declined by a third within 14 days of dosing. Despite cadmium, chromium, copper, lead and zinc exceeding sediment quality guidelines, no sustained mobilization to the water body occurred, lead stayed below the drinking-water limit. Sediment community composition followed seasonal bottom-water oxygenation rather than treatment status, and methanogenic Methanothrix declined. Microcystis was present in the sediment, but neither the mcyA gene nor microcystin-LR was detected in the water column. Combined Ca(NO 3 ) 2 and oxygenated water improved water quality without mobilizing legacy metals or promoting toxigenic cyanobacteria, offering a potential alternative to dredging or aluminum and lanthanum dosing where nitrogen, metal, and cyanobacterial dynamics are monitored.

title: Sulfamethoxazole in the environment: Occurrence, fate, risks, and remediation strategies
abstract: The extensive use of antibiotics in human and veterinary medicine has led to their widespread occurrence in the environment, raising concerns about pseudo-persistence, ecological effects, and their contribution to antimicrobial resistance. Sulfamethoxazole (SMX) is one of the most common sulfonamides and is an environmentally relevant contaminant. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the environmental behavior and management of SMX, integrating its occurrence, fate, transformation, associated risks, regulatory frameworks, and remediation strategies, while identifying remaining knowledge gaps. The reported concentrations of SMX in aqueous matrices range from ng/L to µg/L and in solid matrices with levels reaching up to 0.18, 12.7, and 0.63 mg/kg in soils, manure, and sewage sludge, respectively. SMX exhibits a low solid-liquid distribution coefficient, suggesting high mobility and the potential for environmental transport, leaching, and plant uptake, with concentrations in plant roots reaching up to 13.8 mg/kg under highly contaminated conditions. Despite the relatively low potential of SMX for bioaccumulation, continuous input may lead to chronic exposure and thus ecotoxicological effects and the development of antimicrobial resistance. Transformation products, recent regulatory advances, and remediation strategies are also reviewed, focusing on the limitations of treatment approaches, including incomplete mineralization and by-product formation. Hybrid treatment systems are proposed as a promising solution to overcome these limitations, but further validation is required to assess their scalability, sustainability, and efficiency under realistic conditions. The review concludes by highlighting the need for integrated monitoring, risk-based regulation, and sustainable remediation strategies to mitigate environmental and health concerns associated with SMX pollution.

title: Sublethal lambda-cyhalothrin suppresses reproductive hormone secretion through NCX3-mediated calcium depletion in male Chrysoperla sinica
abstract: Chemical insecticides can persist at sublethal concentrations after field application, posing reproductive risks to natural enemies. However, the mechanisms underlying insecticide-induced male reproductive toxicity remain poorly defined. Here, sublethal lambda-cyhalothrin (λ-Cy) exposure during the second larval instar severely impaired male reproduction in the lacewing Chrysoperla sinica, causing testicular enlargement, disordered spermatogenesis, accessory-gland atrophy, and reduced sperm production. Consequently, mating treated males with untreated females decreased female fecundity and egg hatchability by 42.9% and 35.0%, respectively. Mechanistically, λ-Cy induced acute larval Ca 2 + overload, upregulating the Na + /Ca 2+ exchanger NCX3. Compensatory NCX3 overexpression drove excessive Ca 2+ extrusion, leading to Ca 2+ depletion in the corpora allata and testes during pupal and adult stages. This imbalance suppressed juvenile hormone and 20-hydroxyecdysone biosynthesis via Ca 2+ -CREB signaling. RNA interference, pharmacological assays, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and electrophoretic mobility shift assays validated this cascade. RNAi CsMet or CsEcR phenocopied λ-Cy-induced reproductive defects. These findings identify NCX3-mediated Ca 2+ depletion as a key mechanism of pyrethroid-induced endocrine disruption and male reproductive toxicity.

title: Slow Mn(II) oxidation by chloramine under various conditions: Implication for controlling Mn deposition in drinking water distribution systems
abstract: Chloramine (NH 2 Cl) has been observed to result in substantially lower MnO x deposits in drinking water pipes compared to chlorine, yet the underlying chemical mechanisms and its applicability under various water conditions remain unclear. Here, by integrating thermodynamic analysis with batch experiments, we demonstrated that Mn(II) oxidation by NH 2 Cl was intrinsically slow under various drinking water conditions. Thermodynamic calculations showed that both the absolute Gibbs free energy change and overall redox potential for Mn(II) oxidation by NH 2 Cl were substantially lower than those for free chlorine, fundamentally limiting the driving force of Mn(II) oxidation. Kinetic experiments showed that the homogeneous oxidation of Mn(II) by NH 2 Cl (1, 4, and 8 mg/L) proceeded very slowly. Notably, Mn(II) adsorption-oxidation experiments revealed that although MnO x could adsorb Mn(II), it exhibited no significant catalytic capacity for Mn(II) oxidation by NH 2 Cl, as confirmed by SEM images showing no further MnO x growth on the particle surface. XPS showed that Mn(III) dominated in chloramine-formed MnO x , whereas Mn(IV) dominated in chlorine-formed MnO x . Moreover, Cu(II), Pb(II), and elevated pH, which can promote Mn(II) oxidation by free chlorine, were ineffective in NH 2 Cl systems. These findings demonstrated that Mn(II) oxidation by NH 2 Cl was kinetically slow under varying water quality and pipe conditions, supporting chloramination for MnO x deposit control even in drinking water distribution systems containing existing MnO x deposits or metal pipe surfaces.

title: O,N,O-tridentate chelation directs Mn(II)/periodate activation toward Mn(V)=O formation and selective micropollutant oxidation
abstract: Ligand coordination has emerged as an effective strategy for steering Mn(II)-mediated periodate (PI) activation toward the formation of high-valent manganese-oxo species for micropollutant degradation, yet the influence of N/O donor-site arrangement on catalytic reactivity remains poorly understood. Herein, the relationship between N/O donor-site arrangement and Mn(II)/PI reactivity toward organic pollutants was elucidated using structurally distinct ligands. Among the tested ligands, 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid with an ortho-flanked pincer-like O,N,O-tridentate coordination motif exhibited the highest catalytic performance, outperforming ligands with alternative N/O donor-site configurations by 1.2-11.3-fold. This reactivity trend indicated a close association between N/O donor-site arrangement and catalytic performance within the examined ligand series. Mn(V)=O was suggested as a plausible high-valent Mn-oxo species involved in the nonradical oxidation pathway. Density functional theory calculations provided electronic-structure and thermodynamic support for the role of O,N,O chelation in modulating the electronic structure of the Mn center, promoting I-O bond polarization in the precursor complex, and favoring the proposed formation of Mn(V)=O. An ortho-chelation score was further proposed as an empirical descriptor of position-dependent reactivity within the examined ligand series. These results highlight the favorable association of the ortho-flanked O,N,O coordination motif with Mn(II)/PI activation and provide insight into ligand-assisted selective oxidation systems for water treatment.

title: Reproductive and F1 developmental alterations following parental fluorochemical exposure in zebrafish: Insights from steroidogenesis-related biomarkers
abstract: Regulatory shifts on legacy PFAS have accelerated the use of fluorinated alternatives or precursor, yet their reproductive safety remains uncertain due to persistence, bioaccumulation, and maternal transfer potential. Using a zebrafish parental exposure model, we investigated whether 28-day sublethal OBS, Et-PFOA, or PFOSA exposure disrupts steroidogenesis-centered endocrine homeostasis and affects F 1 offspring. Although hormone measurements were derived from mixed-sex blood pools, parental exposure increased circulating testosterone (T) from 27 to 41-83 nmol·L -1 and elevated estradiol (E 2 ) to 25-68 ng·L -1 , resulting in T/E 2 imbalance. PFOSA produced the strongest reproductive phenotype, increasing early vitellogenic oocytes from approximately 34-62%, decreasing late or mature oocytes from approximately 50-26%, and reducing fecundity from approximately 230-130 eggs per spawning. Ovarian metabolomics at the acute-toxicity-normalized nominal concentrations showed that OBS, Et-PFOA, and PFOSA markedly altered steroidogenesis-related pathways. These changes were supported by dysregulation of ovarian steroidogenesis-related genes. sPLS integration identified steroid-related ovarian metabolites associated with parental reproductive endpoints, while matched F 0 -F 1 analyses further suggested potential links between parental ovarian steroid metabolism and offspring developmental and behavioral phenotypes. Collectively, these findings identify ovarian steroid-related metabolites as candidate indicators of parental reproductive impairment and F 1 phenotypic variation.

title: MOSAIC-Age: Initial binding states and shared ageing trajectories establish a method-compatible predictive baseline for soil metal ageing
abstract: Sequential-extraction and longitudinal studies document soil metal ageing, but differences in protocols, matrices and exposure histories limit cross-study assessment. MOSAIC-Age maps exact analytical protocols to method-compatible domains, equally weights independent experimental programs, and reconstructs shared reference trajectories anchored to the earliest measured state. Evidence spans 70 model-development and 23 registered holdout papers. P1 core training comprises six programs and 86 compositional states. Whole-program validation of 64 post-anchor states yielded RMSE 1.072 and 79.0% directional agreement. Two independent holdout programs yielded RMSE 0.654; ten external endpoints in a Cd/As research-family stratum yielded RMSE 0.275. In an agricultural-wastewater wetland experiment, predictions across 32 non-baseline states correlated with observations (r = 0.837), with RMSE 0.439 and 84.4% directional agreement. Treatment ordering was retained across eight 60 d endpoints (Spearman ρ = 0.738). Prediction intervals were assessed by coverage, width and proper scoring. Incorporating measured 60 d states improved 120 d forecasts over initial-anchor forecasts; persistence comparisons attributed improvement primarily to intermediate observations. The anchored baseline provides a shared temporal reference for state comparisons, while exposure and process observations identify local departures. MOSAIC-Age converts dispersed fractionation evidence into a computable, updatable baseline for relative mobility/activity screening and targeted monitoring, with uncertainty and applicability feedback.

title: Engineering of magnetic peroxidase-like heterojunction nanozymes from homogeneous iron precursor by surface-initiated encapsulation for self-calibration colorimetric/fluorescence dual-mode analysis of Hg2 + ion in foods
abstract: The engineering of multi-modal optical sensors with improved detection accuracy is still a hot topic. Herein, the homologous heterostructured nanozyme with enhanced peroxidase (POD)-like activity was prepared by surface-initiated encapsulation of porphyrin-based metal-organic frameworks on magnetic ferroferric oxide (Fe 3 O 4 @TCPP-Fe) for self-calibration colorimetric/fluorescence dual-mode detection of Hg 2+ in foods. The TCPP-Fe can be in-situ surface-initiated formed via coordination reactions between TCPP and Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ released from Fe 3 O 4 . The "electron bridge" effect of Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ accelerates electron transfer between Fe 3 O 4 and TCPP-Fe, thereby significantly enhancing POD-like activities of Fe 3 O 4 @TCPP-Fe. The colorimetric/fluorescence dual-mode method for determination of Hg 2+ was developed based on strong oxidability of reactive oxygen species, specific recognition of aptamer, optical properties of o-phenylenediamine, and separation/enrichment effect of magnetism. The limits of detection (LOD) and limits of quantification (LOQ) were 0.02 μg/L, 0.08 μg/L, and 0.01 μg/L, 0.04 μg/L for colorimetric and fluorescence modes, respectively. In addition, the detection accuracy was further confirmed by self-calibration process between colorimetric and fluorescence modes in complex food samples. It provides a novel strategy in enhancing POD-like activity for overcoming limitations of single-mode method in complex samples.

title: Chiral antibiotics amplify the phage-associated antibiotic resistome in salinized soil
abstract: Anthropogenic global change is intensifying antibiotic pollution and soil salinization, yet how salinity shapes bacteria-phage interactions to drive the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) under chiral antibiotic pressure remains poorly understood. Using viral metagenomic analyses and laboratory validation, we show that salinity amplifies the enrichment of total and high-risk ARGs along gradients of racemic ofloxacin and its S-enantiomer levofloxacin, concomitant with the parallel accumulation of mobile genetic elements and virulence factors. High-concentration antibiotic treatment in saline soils selected for stress-tolerant, fast-growing antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARBs) carrying abundant prophages and diverse defense systems, thereby promoting tight ARB-phage interactions. Under these dual extreme stresses, lysogenic phages were enriched, enhancing their carriage of ARGs, auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) that bolster host survival, and antidefense genes via a "piggyback-the-winner" strategy, thereby increasing ARG dissemination potential. Notably, high-concentration levofloxacin exerted stronger selective pressure than ofloxacin, increasing virus-to-host ratios and phage-associated ARG accumulation, as supported by incubation assays. Collectively, our findings support a mechanistic framework in which soil salinization interacts with chiral antibiotic exposure, particularly levofloxacin, to increase phage-associated ARG dissemination potential. This highlights a long-underappreciated, Anthropocene-driven pathway intensifying environmental resistance risks and posing new challenges for the One Health framework.

title: A multifunctional Ce(IV)-based coagulant with integrated oxidation and adsorption for efficient removal of diverse arsenic species
abstract: Arsenic contamination is widespread in groundwater and surface water, with species including As(V), As(III), and organic arsenic. This study developed a Ce(IV)-based coagulant, CAN, with dual adsorption and oxidation capabilities for arsenic removal. For organic arsenic, CAN outperformed PAC in removing p-arsanilic acid (p-ASA) and disodium methylarsonate (DSMA); for roxarsone (ROX), CAN achieved > 99% removal at only 1/8 of the PAC dosage. The large ionic radius and high coordination number of Ce(IV) enable stronger binding to organic arsenic ligands via inner-sphere As-O-Ce complexation, overcoming steric hindrance that limits Al(III). For As(III), Ce(IV) exhibits oxidation-adsorption-coagulation synergy, converting As(III) to As(V) and immobilizing it in situ. To further optimize As(III) removal, pre-hydrolyzed CAN B (B>0) was synthesized; with pre-ozonation, it reached > 96% efficiency and residual Ce of 0.006-0.024 mg/L, due to flower-like nanocrystal clusters. CAN hydrolysates are mainly Ce 4 and Ce 6 species, forming large flocs (D 50 > 160-200 μm) and a loose, porous cake layer in the coagulation-ultrafiltration, sustaining ∼70% membrane flux (J/J₀). In real groundwater, CAN resisted competing ions and maintained high removal. Overall, the combined oxidation, adsorption, and coagulation functions of Ce(IV) salts broaden their applications and provide new strategies for treating water containing heavy metal oxyanions.

title: Modelling hazardous mineral fibres – Do we just need more data?
abstract: Spatial exposure modelling for hazardous mineral fibres is constrained by sparse, biased datasets and poorly understood exposure pathways. This study applies six regression frameworks (OLS, ridge, LASSO, geographically weighted regression (GWR), random forest, and XGBoost) to two contrasting datasets: airborne asbestos in El Dorado Hills, California (n = 238) and mordenite in Ngakuru, New Zealand (n = 22). Performance was assessed using cross-validated R² and RMSE, with predictor importance scored across methods. In El Dorado Hills, cross-validated performance was moderate (R² = 0.25–0.36), with tree-based ensembles performing best; activity surfaces, canopy cover, and disturbance proximity were dominant predictors. In Ngakuru, penalised linear models performed strongest (R² = 0.83–0.87), driven by rock sample concentration and soil type, though high in-sample fit indicates overfitting risk given the small sample size. GWR was unstable, producing negative cross-validated R² in El Dorado Hills and in Ngakuru fixed-predictor models. Model complexity did not improve predictive performance at either site; source geology, land use, and land cover formed a transferable predictor framework, though dominant predictors differed by site. These findings indicate that targeted sampling and in-situ predictor measurement will advance exposure modelling for hazardous mineral fibres more than increased model complexity.

title: pH dependence of zinc and copper chemical forms in waste incineration fly ash treated with sulfuric acid
abstract: Acidic treatment can enable secondary use of hazardous municipal solid waste incineration fly ash, but its effects on the speciation and mobility of potentially toxic metals remain incompletely understood. This study systematically investigates the pH-dependent solid-phase speciation of Zn and Cu during sulphuric acid-treatment across pH 3-12 at L/S ∼3, using an ash mixture representative of ash generated in Scandinavia. Zn and Cu speciation was characterised using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XANES, EXAFS), complemented by XRD, SEM-EDS, ICP-MS, and leaching tests. Despite both elements being partly present in stable phases that resisted leaching even at pH 4, Zn and Cu speciation showed clear pH-dependence, which was more pronounced for Zn, likely because a larger fraction of Cu was present in refractory phases. The refractory phases identified were Cu/Zn in iron oxides and Zn in silicates. At pH 7-11, Zn occurred also in sulphate- and hydroxide-containing phases, and adsorbed to ferrihydrite, and Cu in sulphate-, carbonate-, hydroxide-containing phases. Below pH 5.5, Zn was dominated by alkali chlorides and Cu pure chlorides. Using a novel approach to analyse the ash XANES spectra, we show how acid treatment alters Zn and Cu speciation. The results provide a basis for future studies of long-term stability.

title: Calcium restricts cadmium accumulation in rice by competing for iron plaque adsorption sites
abstract: Calcium (Ca) amendments are widely used to restrict cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice; however, the mechanisms governing competitive adsorption between Ca and Cd in iron plaque (IP) of rice roots remain poorly understood. Here, hydroponic and adsorption experiments using detached roots and goethite (Gt), a simulant for IP, were conducted to investigate these interactions. Results showed that exogenous Ca did not affect IP formation but decreased Cd concentrations in IP, roots, and shoots by 21%-28%, 11%-25%, and 17%-27%, respectively. Detached-root adsorption experiments showed that Ca reduced Cd adsorption in IP by 70% when the Ca: Cd ratio reached 20, with root Cd uptake declining by 50% compared with the Ca-free treatment. Gt experiments introduced competitive mechanisms through a dual-pathway model. First, Ca adsorption shifted the point of zero charge of Gt towards higher pH, weakening electrostatic attraction for Cd. Second, spectroscopic evidence supported that Ca bound to surface hydroxyl groups (Fe-OH) through ligand exchange to form inner-sphere complexes (Fe-O-Ca), competitively occupying surface binding sites. This study not only revealed molecular-scale mechanisms of Ca/Cd competition in roots IP, but also provided new insight into quantitatively estimating Ca detoxification when optimizing Ca compound strategies in Cd-contaminated paddy soils beyond pH effects.

title: Ferrous iron fertilizer triggers a time-dependent switch in PFAS bioavailability via soil organic matter remodeling
