abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent and pervasive in agricultural soils. Ferrous iron [Fe(Ⅱ)] fertilizers are applied to alleviate crop Fe-deficient. However, whether and how Fe fertilization dynamically alters PFAS fate in soil remains unknown. Using an emerging PFAS alternative 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate (6:2 Cl-PFESA) as a model compound, we revealed a time-dependent trade-off in its soil bioavailability after Fe(Ⅱ) addition. Within five days, high-dose Fe(Ⅱ) triggered substantial reactive oxygen species production, which preferentially mineralized the water-soluble soil organic matter (SOM), including chromophoric dissolved organic matter and aromatic components. This process released the SOM-associated 6:2 Cl-PFESA and transiently increased its bioavailability, as confirmed by dialysis tests. Upon prolonged aging, Fe(Ⅱ) stimulated the activity of Pseudomonadota microbes, driving the neo-formation of protein- and polysaccharide-like organic matter and the transformation of SOM into stable well-crystallized mineral-associated organic carbon. These newly formed binding domains sequestered 6:2 Cl-PFESA, overriding the initial mobilization and substantially reducing its bioavailability. Although amorphous Fe oxides adsorbed 6:2 Cl-PFESA, their contribution declined during mineral recrystallization. Instead, Fe(Ⅱ)-mediated SOM compositional remodeling governed PFAS bioavailability, highlighting strategic Fe(Ⅱ) fertilization with adequate aging as a promising approach to mitigate PFAS accumulation in agricultural soils.

title: From waste to resource: A plasma-flocculation synergistic strategy for flonicamid removal and upcycling of residues into electrocatalysts
abstract: Treating fluorinated pesticide wastewater poses dual challenges: efficient decontamination and sustainable management of the generated solid waste. Here, we propose a plasma-assisted flocculation system that simultaneously removes flonicamid (FLO) and upcycles the Cu-containing flocculation residue into a high-performance electrocatalyst for the nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). By leveraging polyacrylamide (PAM) to promote pollutant-associated aggregation and create localized reaction domains, this strategy enhances interactions between FLO and plasma-generated reactive species, achieving > 95% FLO removal. Mechanistic analyses support a synergistic coupling between PAM-mediated aggregation and plasma oxidation. The recovered solid residue is directly converted into a CuO x -C catalyst rich in mixed-valence Cu 0 /Cu + /Cu 2+ sites and oxygen vacancies. This catalyst delivers an exceptional NH 3 yield of 44.53 mg·h -1 ·mg cat -1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 92.19% at -0.6 V vs. RHE. Residual liquid intermediates are deeply mineralized via anodic oxidation. In-situ spectroscopies further reveal a sequential deoxygenation-hydrogenation pathway for NO 3 RR, and a 2500 mL continuous-flow system further demonstrates the feasibility of operation at an increased treatment volume. This work integrates pollutant degradation with resource recovery, providing a sustainable "waste-to-catalyst" paradigm for pesticide wastewater valorization.

title: Organic nitrogen substitution stabilizes antimony in paddy bulk soil but mobilizes it in the rhizosphere
abstract: Rhizosphere processes strongly regulate antimony (Sb) bioavailability and root uptake in paddy soils, but whether organic nitrogen substitution induces divergent Sb transformation pathways across rhizosphere remains unclear. Here, by separating bulk soil, rhizosphere soil, and root iron plaque, we identified a soil-rhizosphere-plaque continuum that determines Sb mobilization, retention, and root uptake under organic nitrogen substitution. Organic nitrogen substitution exerted contrasting, rhizosphere-dependent effects on bioavailable Sb fractions, including non-specifically adsorbed Sb and specifically adsorbed Sb. These fractions decreased in bulk soil by 5.07-26.79% via humic acid complexation and sulfide precipitation, but increased in the rhizosphere by up to 31.45% through competitive adsorption by root-derived low-molecular-weight organic acids, phosphate, and dissolved organic matter. At the root surface, organic nitrogen substitution markedly promoted iron plaque formation by 32.41-75.63%, with amorphous iron (hydr)oxides dominating Sb retention and accounting for 86.31-89.08% of plaque-associated Sb. Iron plaque significantly reduced shoot Sb content by intercepting rhizosphere-mobilized Sb, leading to a 24.48-41.02% decrease in shoot Sb content. Finally, we propose a compartment-specific mechanism of Sb fate in which organic nitrogen substitution drives bulk-soil stabilization, rhizosphere mobilization, and root-surface interception of Sb, supporting organic nitrogen management as a strategy to mitigate rice Sb accumulation and sustain rice growth. SYNOPSIS: By distinguishing the rhizosphere from bulk soil, this study reveals that organic nitrogen substitution creates opposing effects on antimony bioavailability across soil compartments, while root iron plaque limits antimony uptake by rice. These findings advance our understanding of antimony cycling in paddy soils and inform safer rice production strategies.

title: Magnesium promotes aluminum tolerance in apple by regulating cell wall remodeling through the MdMYB78–MdHCT/MdXTH2 transcriptional module
abstract: Soil acidification-induced aluminum (Al) toxicity severely restricts apple growth and development, threatening apple production and potentially human health. Magnesium (Mg) supplementation can alleviate Al toxicity in plants, but the underlying physiological and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, increasing the Mg supply from 0.3 to 3 mM reduced root Al accumulation and increased root dry weight and root length in M26 apple rootstock seedlings exposed to Al stress (1.5 mM). Elemental analysis showed that approximately 60% of the accumulated Al was localized in the root cell wall, with hemicellulose 1 (HC1) exhibiting a greater Al-binding capacity than other cell wall components. Mg supplementation under Al stress reduced the cell wall hemicellulose (HC) and lignin contents, thereby decreasing cell wall thickness and Al accumulation. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified MdHCT and MdXTH2 as key genes involved in Mg-mediated Al tolerance. Overexpression of MdHCT and MdXTH2 negatively and positively regulate Al tolerance in apple seedlings, respectively, by modulating cell wall modification. Transcription factor analysis identified the MYB family member MdMYB78, which directly binds the ACCAAC motif in promoters of MdHCT and MdXTH2, activating and repressing their transcription, respectively. Transgenic validation results indicate that MdMYB78 negatively regulates Al tolerance in apple seedlings. Collectively, these findings establish MdMYB78 as a key regulator of Mg-enhanced Al tolerance in apple seedlings by coordinately regulating MdHCT and MdXTH2 to remodel the root cell wall and alter its Al-binding capacity. Mg-mediated cell wall remodeling provides a potential strategy for mitigating Al toxicity in acidified soils.

title: Dual-mode colorimetric and photothermal detection of thiram using a smartphone-integrated platform with an Fe-doped ZIF-8-derived nanozyme
abstract: The extensive use of the fungicide thiram in agriculture poses health risks, necessitating sensitive on-site monitoring. Conventional detection methods often rely on costly and unstable biological recognition elements, while many nanozyme-based strategies still depend on complex cascade reactions involving natural enzymes. Herein, we report a robust, enzyme-free dual-mode sensing platform based on Fe-doped ZIF-8 derived nanozyme (Zn-NC/Fe). Through systematic optimization of iron doping, the optimized Zn-NC/Fe 5% nanozyme exhibits superior peroxidase-like activity with low Michaelis constants, attributed to abundant Fe-N x active sites. Thiram specifically passivates these sites via Fe-S coordination, enabling direct inhibition-based detection. Using TMB as substrate, we constructed a colorimetric sensor and a complementary photothermal sensor based on oxTMB's near-infrared light-to-heat conversion. To enable field use, the nanozyme was encapsulated in sodium alginate hydrogel microspheres and integrated with smartphone-assisted RGB readout, achieving an LOD of 11.25 μM and linear range from 20 to 1000 μM. The platform was successfully validated in environmental water and fruit juice samples with recoveries of 95.6-108.2%. Elliptic Joint Confidence Region analysis further confirmed the statistical accuracy of the three modes. This work provides a stable, cost-effective, and user-friendly toolkit for thiram monitoring, advancing food safety applications.

title: Tissue-specific microplastic burdens in humans: An intra-individual mapping of 18 tissue types
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their tissue-specific distribution within individuals remains poorly characterized. We analyzed 165 samples from 18 tissue types collected from ten donors, including two newborns, using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) and Laser Direct Infrared (LDIR) imaging for chemical quantification and morphological characterization, respectively. MPs were detected in all donors and tissues, with substantial inter-individual and tissue-specific variation. MP burdens in the two neonatal donors fell within the range observed across the adult donors. MP accumulation was tissue-specific, with lipid-rich tissues (adipose and brain) and highly perfused endocrine/metabolic organs (adrenal, liver, thyroid) harboring the highest burdens, whereas blood contained the lowest MP levels. Polyethylene (PE), polyamide 66 (PA66), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) accounted for > 90% of the 11 MP types quantified by Py-GC/MS. LDIR analysis showed that MPs were predominantly small (66.06% within 20-40 μm) and moderately rounded, although particles > 150 μm were also detected across tissues. These findings provide a systematic map of human MP distribution, demonstrating heterogeneous tissue accumulation and providing a understanding for the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of MPs and associated their health risks.

title: Upcycling spent ternary lithium-ion batteries into enlarged covalency manganese-based Fenton-like catalysts for efficient emerging contaminants removal
abstract: Growing deployment of ternary Mn-rich lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for electric vehicles generates large amounts of spent ternary Mn-rich LIBs. However, traditional recycling processes face limited economic benefit because of the high-content but low-value Mn. Upcycling Mn from them into Fenton-like catalysts is a promising strategy, but their activity is limited by the thermodynamic constraints of Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) redox cycling. Herein, we proposed an upcycling process to convert them into Mn-based Fenton-like catalysts (MnNiCoO x -LIBs) for efficient emerging contaminants removal by peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Co-doping with strong-electronegativity Ni/Co from spent ternary Mn-rich LIBs enlarges Mn-O covalency in MnNiCoO x -LIBs, strengthening PMS adsorption and breaking the thermodynamic limitation of Mn(IV)/Mn(III) redox cycling by PMS. As expected, the Fenton-like activity for bisphenol A removal of MnNiCoO x -LIBs is 3.3 times that of MnO x prepared from commercial oxalates. It exhibits excellent anti-interference ability, long-term stability (over 800 min), and universality for multiple emerging contaminants. Life cycle assessment confirms that MnNiCoO x -LIBs shows superior environmental sustainability and cost-effectiveness. Notably, multiple spent ternary Mn-rich LIBs can be upcycled into MnNiCoO x -LIBs that exhibit lower synthetic cost and better Fenton-like activity than multiple reported catalysts. This work provides a promising approach for emerging contaminants removal and sustainable recycling of spent ternary Mn-rich LIBs.

title: Alteration of simulant UK nuclear waste glass in a low temperature natural environment: the Ballidon glass burial field experiment
abstract: Non-active UK nuclear waste glass surrogates, representative of vitrified highly active liquor (HAL) from Magnox and oxide fuel reprocessing, were buried in a mildly alkaline, undersaturated, near-surface environment at Ballidon, UK. Following 16-18 years, alteration layers were large (40-55 µm) on simulant 'Blend' glasses, made from a mixture of Magnox and oxide HAL, but smaller (10 µm) on glasses made from simulated Magnox HAL. Short term laboratory experiments showed that Magnox glass had a lower initial dissolution rate in deionised water when compared to Blend glasses. Analysis of alteration layers revealed distinct zones of varying composition and morphology; silicon rich nearest the glass, layered Fe, Al, Si and Zr in the centre, and a Ca/P/lanthanide rich layer nearest the surface. Outer layers were mostly amorphous and comprised glass-derived lanthanides, environment-derived calcium, and phosphate derived from both the glass and environment. Availability of P may have been enhanced through exchange of sorbed phosphate with dissolved silicic acid from the glass. Nanocrystals, tentatively identified as the hydrated lanthanide phosphate phase churchite, were detected at the silica-phosphate interface. Results provide insight into alteration layer evolution in a natural open system and how radioactive fission products and actinides may be retained within alteration layers.

title: Secondary Organic Aerosol from Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Modulates Glioma Proliferation
A fluorine-centered framework for energy-normalized evaluation of PFAS destruction technologies
abstract: Destructive treatment is increasingly recognized as an important long-term strategy for managing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) because it targets irreversible carbon-fluorine (C-F) bond cleavage rather than contaminant transfer or parent-compound disappearance alone. However, comparison of destructive processes remains challenging because defluorination performance and energy demand are not consistently integrated within a common evaluation framework. To address this gap, this study develops an energy-normalized, fluorine-centered framework based on energy-normalized defluorination extent (ENDE) and energy-normalized fluoride production (EFP), which represent fractional defluorination and absolute fluoride production per unit energy input, respectively. Application of the framework to a curated multi-technology dataset of laboratory-scale aqueous PFAS destruction systems revealed substantial variability in energy-normalized defluorination performance. In photocatalytic systems, parent-compound degradation exceeded a median of 99% for several catalyst families, yet ENDE and EFP varied widely. Across technology classes represented in the dataset and at a common 50% defluorination endpoint, electrochemical systems and UV-based advanced reduction processes exhibited higher median ENDE 50 and EFP 50 values under the reported operating and energy boundaries. Overall, the framework provides a descriptive and diagnostic basis for evaluating energy-normalized C-F bond cleavage across reported PFAS destruction systems and identifying opportunities to improve defluorination performance.

title: Facilitating the sequential conversion of *NOx intermediates by tandem catalyst and electrolyte engineering for high ammonia selectivity from electrochemical nitrate reduction
abstract: Efficient electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia (eNO 3 RA) requires the continuous conversion of surface-bound nitrate reduction intermediates, especially at low nitrate concentrations. We construct a tandem catalyst by electrodeposition of NiO x on the Cu x O nanowires to promote the sequential conversion of *NO 2 to *NO, and then a superior performance with 95.89% nitrate conversion and 95.83% ammonia selectivity is achieved for 1 mM nitrate. In situ Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations confirm that the NiO x promotes the conversion of *NO 2 to *NO by lowering the corresponding free energy barrier from 0.85 to 0.59 eV. Additionally, the enrichment of potassium ions in the electric double layer can alleviate the electrostatic repulsion at the electrode-electrolyte interface, which facilitates the accumulation of nitrate and stimulates the eNO 3 RA at a low concentration of nitrate. Our results provide a deep insight into the eNO 3 RA pathways at low concentrations and may facilitate their application towards dilute nitrate waste streams.

title: Fluorinated donor-acceptor polymers blended with solid-state ionic liquids for highly sensitive and selective detection of volatile organic compounds
abstract: Solid-state ionic liquids (SILs), comprising cations with long-alkyl chains and anions containing fluorine atoms, have become essential for achieving electrochemical doping of π-conjugated polymers (π-CPs), as the formation of polarons is stabilized by the presence of fluorinated anions under applied bias. Nevertheless, phase separation on the scale of a few hundred nanometers between the polymers and SILs limits efficient doping and hinders intermolecular charge transport. In this study, we present a molecular design approach that incorporates electron-withdrawing fluorine atoms into the isoindigo unit of benzodithiophene-isoindigo (BI) copolymers. This targeted fluorination optimizes the surface energy of the polymer, facilitating the development of well-organized fibrillar nanostructures with improved order and connectivity when mixed with SILs. The optimized morphology enhances the migration of fluorinated anions from the SIL, which in turn promotes efficient electrochemical doping within the fluorinated BI matrix. Additionally, the electrochemical doping process is modulated by alcohol-based gases, yielding chemiresistors with outstanding gas selectivity. Of particular note, the fluorinated BI:SIL chemiresistor demonstrated an impressive response to 1-butanol, reaching a resistance change (ΔR/R₀) of 85.28% at 500 ppm and a limit of detection (LOD) of 513.6 ppb. These results underscore the potential of fluorinated π-CP/SIL blends to serve as adaptable platforms for scalable, selective, and environmentally sustainable organic sensing applications.

title: Adsorption/desorption processes using palygorskite clay mineral for table olive fermentation brine treatment and phenols recovery
abstract: Table olive fermentation brine (TOFB) is an acidic, organic-rich agro-industrial effluent containing elevated concentrations of phenolic compounds that pose significant environmental risks due to their toxicity and resistance to biodegradation. Nevertheless, these compounds constitute valuable bioactive molecules exhibiting antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study investigates TOFB treatment via adsorption onto palygorskite (Pal), emphasizing simultaneous pollutant removal, recovery of phenolic constituents (TPC) and Pal reusability. Raw Pal exhibited a characteristic fibrous morphology, high specific surface area (233 m²/g), and mesoporous structure, as confirmed by SEM and N₂ physisorption analyses. Adsorption performance was evaluated through batch and continuous-flow experiments under varying operational conditions. In batch systems, decreasing the initial phenolic concentration from 5200 to 40 mg/L increased removal efficiency from 58.5% to 88.3%, while increasing Pal dosage from 2.5 to 100 g/L enhanced removal from 50.6% to 75.6%. Continuous-flow operation achieved 37.5% TPC removal, with column saturation occurring after approximately 20 h. Equilibrium and kinetic analyses indicated that adsorption followed the Freundlich isotherm, whereas fixed-bed performance was adequately described by the Clark model. Desorption experiments enabled phenolic recovery up to 76% using water and a 50% (v/v) ethanol-water solution, with UHPLC-MS/MS-DAD confirming tyrosol and hydroxytyrosol among recovered compounds. Thermal regeneration did not affect the removal efficiency at the initial reusability cycle. However, it was found that the removal efficiency decreased to 30% of the initial capacity at the third time of reusability. Structural evolution throughout adsorption-desorption-regeneration cycles was evaluated using XRD and XPS analysis, supporting an integrated and sustainable TOFB management strategy aligned with circular economy principles.

title: Exposure to Emerging and Legacy PFAS and Risks of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Liver Fibrosis in Adults Living Near a Semiconductor Science Park

Exogenous granular activated carbon (GAC) promotes the biogenic oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite and the degradation of pollutants: Insights from extracellular superoxide radical generation, key enzyme activities and transcriptomic analysis
Molecular impairment-guided ecotoxicity assessment: Insights from copper and pH stress in zebrafish
abstract: Copper (Cu) toxicity is governed by the redox transition of Cu(II) to Cu(I), yet its temporal dynamics and modulation by water chemistry remain poorly understood. This study developed an omics-driven toxicokinetic framework evaluating Cu toxicity in zebrafish gills across varying pH levels. By interrogating the expression kinetics of key redox-switch genes (steap family/fdx1), we identified a 9-h molecular peak window serving as a highly sensitive signature for incipient toxicity, preceding macroscopic phenotypic shifts. A relatively high-dose of Cu (30 μg/L) advanced steap2/4 peaks to 6 h, indicating STEAP capacity-constrained reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(I). Fluorescent quantification of gill Cu(I) accumulation displayed no significant differences. Nonetheless, transcriptomic profiling established a condition-dependent hierarchical pathway impairment: necroptosis > ferroptosis > apoptosis > inflammatory > immune > stress response > oxidative stress response. Acidic regimes uniquely triggered necroptosis and profound metabolic dysfunction. Interaction with a Cu(I)-specific chelator abolished cell necrosis and reversed global transcriptional phenotypes, validating that intracellular Cu(I) trafficking drives systemic damage. This dual-analytical framework, coupling a "Cu toxic molecular switch" with a "gradation of injury pathways", to some extent, provides a temporally resolved predictive tool and offers a robust mechanistic foundation for risk assessment of metals in dynamic aquatic ecosystems.

title: Deep learning-driven fine-grained classification and traceability of illicit pollution sources in urban stormwater networks using 3D-EEM images
abstract: Illicit wastewater discharge into stormwater pipes poses a severe ecological risk to receiving waters, yet conventional parallel factor analysis lacks the requisite precision to distinguish spectrally overlapping domestic wastewaters (e.g., office buildings, hotels) due to their intricate composition and overlapping spectral features. This study introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework integrating three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy with a hybrid Swin Transformer-ResNet architecture. Through systematic comparison of eight convolutional neural network architectures and subsequent optimization, the refined model delivers superior classification performance with 98.21% accuracy. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping reveals that the model focuses on diagnostically relevant spectral regions (Ex/Em ≈ 225-375/300-475 nm), suggesting potential for reducing the EEM scanning range, although instrument-level benefits require further validation. Within the studied region, the framework generalizes to complex multi-source mixtures without retraining, achieving exact, partial, and type match accuracies of 79.59%, 88.89%, and 98.41%, respectively. T-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding highlights overlapping category pairs, such as Convenience store and Supermarket, indicating cases requiring additional field verification. This work establishes a robust intelligent screening and progressive tracing tool for narrowing pollution sources in drainage networks, reducing blind field investigation and enabling precision rehabilitation of illicit connections to mitigate hazardous contaminant loads to aquatic ecosystems.

title: Multi-scale soil heavy metal risk zoning in a typical industrial agglomeration area based on atmosphere–soil coupled risk assessment framework: Integrating pollutant discharge permit data and soil monitoring data
Defect engineering of zero-valent iron promotes interfacial electron transfer for efficient Fenton-like activation at low catalyst dosage
abstract: Zero-valent iron (ZVI)-activated persulfate systems are limited by sluggish Fe cycling and rapid surface passivation, resulting in inefficient electron utilization and excessive reagent consumption. Here, we develop a NaCl-assisted ball milling strategy to construct a defect-rich ZVI interface (Cl-D-ZVI) with enhanced electron transfer capability. NaCl-assisted ball milling induces local structural disorder and coordination reconstruction at the ZVI interface, facilitating interfacial electron transfer and Fe redox transformation. Cl-D-ZVI enables efficient persulfate activation at a low catalyst dosage (20 mg·L -1 ), exhibiting consistently higher degradation activity than conventionally ball-milled ZVI. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the defective interface reduces the solid-liquid electron transfer barrier and facilitates Fe redox transformation, thereby promoting the concurrent formation of ·OH and Fe(Ⅳ)=O species. Continuous-flow filtration demonstrates sustained reactivity under different water matrices, while life-cycle assessment indicates reduced environmental impacts of the developed system. This study provides a scalable defect-engineering strategy for improving electron utilization and advancing sustainable iron-based advanced oxidation processes.

title: Divergent aging patterns of polylactic acid (PLA) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) plastic sheets and their differential associations with soil carbon stability
abstract: Plastic pollution is a growing concern. Plastic particles undergo aging that changes their properties and ecological impacts, yet how different polymers age in natural settings and relate to soil carbon cycling remains unclear. We conducted a nine-month in situ experiment to compare the aging of biodegradable PLA (polylactic acid) and conventional PVC (polyvinyl chloride) sheets and to assess their associations with soil microbial communities, enzymes, and organic carbon fractions. PLA surfaces developed hydrolysis‑induced cracks and fragmentation, whereas PVC showed oxidative roughening. These aging patterns were associated with divergent functional potential of plastisphere microbial communities. PLA‑associated soils had higher β-glucosidase and peroxidase activities, together with a trend toward higher labile carbon (FPOC) indicators than PVC‑associated soils. Mineral‑associated organic carbon (MAOC) did not differ between treatments, but MAOC proportion was negatively correlated with bulk density only under PLA. Because our study lacked an unamended control, our conclusions are limited to PLA-PVC comparisons. Our findings show that the two polymers differ in aging pathways, microbial associations, and associations with labile carbon turnover that vary with soil physical properties, suggesting that the environmental implications of biodegradable plastics cannot be assumed from their label alone.

title: Diesel breakthrough resistance of soil-bentonite backfills via capillary barrier effect
abstract: Diesel contamination at petrochemical sites poses a critical threat to groundwater security and public health. Soil-bentonite backfills are widely used as vertical barriers in contaminated sites, yet their long-term containment performance against diesel is strongly influenced by the pore structure and the resultant capillary resistance. This study evaluated the diesel retention capacity of sand-bentonite (S d B) versus silt-bentonite (S t B) through long-term flexible-wall permeation tests under incremental permeation pressures (10, 20, and 30 kPa). Diesel breakthrough behavior and capillary entry pressure threshold were analyzed. The underlying mechanisms were further elucidated. The results revealed three key findings: (1) S t B exhibited excellent retardation capacity under all tested pressures (10-30 kPa), maintaining extremely low daily flow rates ( d B experienced rapid diesel breakthrough at 20 and 30 kPa, with daily flow rates exceeding 25 mL/d within a short period; (2) The capillary entry pressure threshold of S d B was less than 10 kPa, while that of S t B ranged from 20 to 30 kPa, indicating a significantly higher capillary resistance for S t B; (3) S t B had much finer pores concentrated at 0.05-0.39 μm (0.28-2.13 μm for S d B), corresponding to the denser pore structure. Consistent with the Young-Laplace equation, smaller pore throats produced higher capillary entry pressures. Consequently, S t B had higher capillary entry pressure and superior long-term diesel containment. These findings underscored the promising application of fines-rich soil‑bentonite backfills against organic non-aqueous phase liquids at petrochemical sites, and provide practical guidance for the design of geoenvironmental containment systems.

title: Exposure to polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics elicits renal injury with limited compensation and associated intestinal alterations: A time-resolved multi-omics study
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) are emerging contaminants of toxicological concern. However, the temporal progression of PET-NPs-induced renal injury during repeated oral exposure remains poorly understood. Male C57BL/6 J mice received PET-NPs at 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 14, 28, or 56 days to characterize time-dependent nephrotoxicity and intestinal alterations. Fluorescence imaging detected gastrointestinal signals at all time points and a time-dependent increase in renal fluorescence following administration of Nile red-labeled PET-NPs. PET-NPs exposure was associated with impaired intestinal barrier integrity and altered gut microbial composition. Renal assessments revealed functional impairment, tubular injury, inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, and lipid peroxidation. Integrated renal transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified alterations in inflammatory signaling, redox homeostasis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid metabolism. Mean TUNEL positivity was numerically highest at 28 days and remained elevated relative to controls at 56 days. At 56 days, tubular injury, renal dysfunction, and inflammation persisted alongside increased Ki-67 positivity. Although the renal Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant axis was activated, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and renal injury indicated insufficient antioxidant compensation. Repeated oral PET-NPs exposure elicited time-dependent nephrotoxicity characterized by inflammatory-redox-lipid metabolic remodeling and constrained antioxidant compensation. These findings provide a time-resolved multi-omics framework for assessing PET-NPs-associated renal hazards following repeated oral exposure.

title: Insights into heavy metal accumulation and chemical speciation in Huixian Karst Wetland, China: Depositional history, mercury isotope tracing and environmental risk assessment
abstract: Heavy metal (HM) contamination in wetland sediments has attracted increasing attention because of its persistence and potential ecological impacts. In this study, HMs including Cd, Pb, Zn, Ni, As, and Hg in the surface and core sediments of the Huixian Karst Wetland were investigated in terms of the contamination characteristics, ecological risks, depositional history and possible sources for the first time. The mean concentrations of six metals exceeded their respective background values, with Cd, Pb, and Hg showing high enrichment in Zone 2. Based on the Nemerow Integrated Pollution Index (averaging 3.55), the sediments exhibit a severe level of overall contamination. Sequential extraction revealed that while most HMs predominantly remained in the residual fraction, anthropogenic disturbances increased their reducible and acid-exchangeable forms. Notably, according to the risk assessment code, Pb and Hg exhibited high bioavailability-with highly mobile fractions accounting for approximately 67.34% and 59.95%, respectively-thereby posing significant ecological risks. The depositional history (1925-2020) revealed distinct temporal variations in HM accumulation corresponding to historical and socioeconomic developments, including wartime activities, economic reforms, and industrial expansion. Furthermore, mercury isotope compositions (negative δ 202 Hg values and a significant Δ 199 Hg-Δ 201 Hg relationship) suggested possible anthropogenic contributions to sediment Hg, potentially linked to industrial activities.

title: Soil-to-Rice Transfer of Cs, Sr and Other Elements in Tropical Agricultural Soils of Eastern India: Influence of Soil Properties on Plant Uptake
Scale matching between polyethylene microplastics and soil pores drives nonlinear greenhouse gas emission responses in karst soils
abstract: A laboratory microcosm experiment evaluated the effects of polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) with different particle sizes on the physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, pore structure, bacterial community, and greenhouse gas emissions of karst soil. The effects of PE-MPs on greenhouse gas emissions were nonlinear and depended on the match between microplastic particle size and soil pore scale. Small-sized particles (10-25 μm) may have filled micropores, induced localized anaerobic microsites, and increased microbial attachment interfaces, potentially enhancing CO 2 and N 2 O emissions. Large-sized particles (900-1150 μm) promoted CO 2 emissions, potentially by altering soil pore structure and improving aeration. Medium-sized particles (260-300 μm), being close to the characteristic pore size of the soil, may have caused limited disturbance to pore connectivity and microbial habitats and had no significant effect on either gas. Further analyses indicated that the effects of PE-MPs on greenhouse gas emissions were unlikely to result from direct mineralization, decomposition, or chemical release. Instead, PE-MPs may have indirectly affected greenhouse gas emissions by altering soil physical structure, reshaping bacterial community composition, regulating nitrogen forms, and changing enzyme activities. Small-sized particles exhibited the highest short-term integrated warming effect, followed by large-sized particles, whereas medium-sized particles showed the lowest effect.

title: PMF Resolved Source Identification & Health Risk Assessment of Trace-elements in Airborne Particulate Matter (PM10) from South-Asian Megacity
abstract: To mitigate the adverse effects of airborne particulate matter, it is crucial to comprehend its composition, size distribution and corresponding emission inventories. In this study, we investigated the sources of trace elements in PM10 from the Faisalabad metropolitan area, situated in the Indo-Gangetic Plain. We employed ICP-OES for the analysis of trace elements. The average PM10 concentration was 517 ± 206 µgm -3 , exceeding safety levels established by Pak-EPA (150 μgm -3 ), US-EPA (150 μgm -3 ), and WHO (50 μgm -3 ). Notably, higher concentrations were observed in summer than in autumn and winter. On average, elemental concentrations followed the order: Fe > Al > Si > Zn > Cu > Pb > Cd > Sn > B > Se > Ni > Co > Mn > Cr > Mo > Sb > Ba > V > As > Zr. The PMF model predicted seven major sources for elemental contents, including metal works, vehicular exhaust and non-exhaust emissions, burning of fossil fuels in industries, municipal waste incineration, and industrial mixed dust. Furthermore, a health risk assessment revealed that the Cumulative Carcinogenic Risk (CCR) for adults (1.22 ×10⁻³) and children (5.05 ×10⁻⁴) exceeded the WHO/USEPA upper limit (1 ×10⁻⁴) by factors of 12.2 and 5.05 respectively.

title: Novel neonicotinoid flupyradifurone exhibits sublethal toxicity to natural enemies ladybeetles Propylea japonica by disturbing multi-level metabolic systems
abstract: Flupyradifurone, a novel neonicotinoid insecticide widely used against sap-sucking pests, has poorly characterized sublethal effects on non-target natural enemies. We assessed sublethal effects of 0.5 and 3 mg/L flupyradifurone on Propylea japonica using biological, biochemical, transcriptomic, and metabolomic assays. Flupyradifurone significantly prolonged larval development and reduced adult body weight and fecundity, without affecting survival, pupation, or emergence. Enzyme activities (GST, POD and AChE) and nutritional substance contents (glycogen and free fatty acids) generally decreased at 12 and 24 h. However, CarE activity and total protein content showed no significant changes at 24 h. Transcriptomics analysis identified 1798 and 1607 differentially expressed genes, enriched in xenobiotic metabolism, immunity, and nutrient metabolism. Key genes GST, UGT, Duox, and TPS were significantly downregulated, whereas GLD was significantly upregulated, and Lys and FASN were significantly induced only at the low concentration. RNAi silencing of GST, UGT, Duox, TPS, and GLD increased ladybeetles susceptibility to flupyradifurone. Metabolomics analysis identified 483 and 508 differentially accumulated metabolites, with disruptions in glutathione, amino acid, and lipid metabolism. Thus, flupyradifurone suppresses detoxification and immunity, depletes energy reserves, and inhibits development and reproduction in P. japonica, highlighting the need to incorporate sublethal effects into ecological risk assessments.

title: Hydrochemical differentiation and heavy metal migration along karst fracture-conduit runoff paths in an acid mine drainage-affected watershed
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) from karst sulfide mines threatens regional groundwater security, yet water-rock-pollutant coupling across heterogeneous runoff media remains poorly understood. Using hydrogeological, hydrochemical and isotopic data, we examined four water types-tailings-pond water (M-type), fracture-spring and conduit water (S-type, G-type) and surface river water (R-type)-along fracture-conduit runoff zones in an AMD-affected karst watershed during the August 2024 wet season. All waters were circumneutral to weakly alkaline, carbonate-neutralized AMD-affected waters, not acidic leachate. Isotopes (δ²H-H₂O, δ¹⁸O-H₂O, δ³⁴S-SO₄ and δ¹⁸O-SO₄) and hydrochemistry showed that M water was dominated by sulfuric-acid dissolution, S-type water by mixed carbonic-sulfuric-acid dissolution, R-type water by coexisting multi-acid dissolution and G-type water by carbonic-acid dissolution. S-type water showed stronger apparent bidirectional AMD buffering than R/G-type water, although dilution and immobilization could not be distinguished. Isotope patterns were consistent with preferential bacterial sulfate reduction (BSR) in fractures, one of several interpretations pending microbiological verification. Sulfide oxidation elevated dissolved metals in M-type water; dilution reduced them downstream in R-type water. S-type water likely attenuated metals through carbonate buffering and weakly reducing conditions, with a possible unverified BSR contribution; G-type water buffered mainly through carbonate dissolution. These findings support karst AMD prevention and control.

title: Depolymerization of polyurethane by Cladosporium sp. CP25 via two thermotolerant cutinases with distinct catalytic properties
abstract: Polyurethanes (PU) are extensively used in industrial products, but their end-of-life recycling has been a long-standing research challenge due to the intrinsic structural stability. PU depolymerization by biological enzymes represents a feasible strategy with promising attention. However, examples of robust depolymerization enzymes are lacking despite extensive research scale-up to a laboratory-relevant level. Here, we reported two cutinases CpLCut1 and CpLCut2 derived from Cladosporium sp. CP25 that demonstrated thermotolerant properties and efficient depolymerization of polyester-PU materials. After 21-days incubation at 25 °C, CP25 degraded up to 72% of commercial PU foam, as supported by changes in foam structure and the detection of degradation products. CpLCut1 and CpLCut2 possessed significant ability to hydrolyze PU into adipic acid by ester bond cleavage. Notably, CpLCut2 exhibited remarkable thermal stability, retaining 93% of its initial activity after incubation at 55 °C for 12 h, which could be attributed to the enhanced conformational stability and more persistent enzyme-substrate interactions from molecular dynamics simulations. Molecular docking, along with product distribution, elucidated a special substrate-binding mode of CpLCut1 and CpLCut2 with a plastic substrate analogue. Overall, our results expand the repertoire of PU-degrading cutinases, and provide promising enzyme candidates for future end-of-life recycling of PU waste.

title: Effects of cabin heating and cooling on ammonia emissions from hybrid electric vehicles under extreme ambient temperatures
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is an unregulated by-product from NO X reduction over three-way catalysts (TWCs), yet how hybrid vehicle NH 3 emissions respond to cabin thermal demand remains poorly defined. Four China VI gasoline hybrid passenger vehicles were tested on the Worldwide harmonized Light vehicles Test Cycle (WLTC) at -7, 23, and 40 °C. Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC)-off tests were carried out at all temperatures, with heating-on and cooling-on tests conducted at -7 °C and 40 °C, respectively. Cycle-averaged NH 3 , CO, and NO X emission factors were analysed using second-by-second emissions, engine speed, lambda, coolant and catalyst temperatures, and battery state of charge (SOC). With HVAC off, all vehicles produced higher NH 3 , CO, and NO X at -7 °C than at 23 °C, while the 40 °C response was vehicle-specific. Heating at -7 °C increased NH 3 emissions for three vehicles and reduced emissions for one; cooling at 40 °C raised NH 3 of one vehicle approximately fivefold and cut that of another by nearly 50%. Transient results show high NH 3 coincides with intense, frequent reducing events under active catalyst conditions. HVAC modulates emissions via vehicle-specific energy management, engine engagement and engine-catalyst timing.

title: Cross-media partitioning, sources, and health risks of phthalate esters in campus indoor air and PM2.5
abstract: Campus environments present functionally heterogeneous indoor settings for multiphase phthalate esters (PAEs) exposure. Here, paired gas-phase and PM 2.5 samples were collected from classrooms, dormitories, canteens, and courier stations at a university campus in Hebei Province, China, during spring and summer 2025. Fifteen PAEs were quantitatively analyzed to identify how microenvironmental functions and cross-medium distributions jointly regulate PAEs source characteristics, gas-particle partitioning, source contributions, and health-risk prioritization. Total PAE concentrations ranged from 1.11 × 10 2 to 1.53 × 10 3 ng m -3 in air and from 3.14 × 10 1 to 2.94 × 10 2 ng m -3 in PM 2.5 . Seasonal variation was characterized by a summer shift of lower-molecular-weight PAEs toward the gas phase, accompanied by compound- and microenvironment-specific changes in particle-bound PAEs. Gas-particle partitioning varied with K OA with low-K OA PAEs preferentially occurring in the gas phase and high-K OA PAEs showing greater particle association, while the dynamic partitioning framework better described the measured behavior than the instantaneous-equilibrium model. Source apportionment indicated phase- and season-dependent potential source patterns associated mainly with plasticized products, building/decorative materials, and daily-use products. The health risk assessment indicated that ingestion of PM 2.5 -bound PAEs was the dominant exposure pathway, and bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate was the main contributor to carcinogenic risk. Toxicological Priority Index ranking further identified dibutyl phthalate and diisobutyl phthalate as priority compounds for cross-media control. This study demonstrates that paired measurements of the gas phase and PM 2.5 enable more precise identification of phase-specific pollution sources, exposure pathways, and priority control pollutants across distinct indoor scenarios on campus.

title: Spatial organisation of microplastics in road runoff across an urban network
abstract: Road runoff is a major pathway by which microplastics are transported from urban surfaces to aquatic ecosystems, yet the spatial scales over which measurements represent road networks remain unresolved. This constrains source attribution, monitoring design and urban emission inventories. Using high-resolution µFTIR imaging, we quantified microplastic abundance, particle-size distribution and polymer composition in runoff across an interconnected urban road network following a rainfall mobilisation event, characterising twenty-one polymer types across four particle-size fractions. Concentrations spanned more than an order of magnitude (18-544 particles L⁻¹), varying sharply even between road only 114 m apart. Compositional dissimilarity showed no significant relationship with inter-site distance, instead revealing a mosaic of locally distinct polymer assemblages, with significantly greater heterogeneity in the urban core. Cellulose acetate, polyurethane, polymethyl-methacrylate and polypropylene dominated, reflecting diverse sources. In contrast, 25-50 µm particles consistently dominated, accounting for ∼84% of particles, indicating a common fine-particle transport signature despite pronounced spatial variability in polymer composition. These reveal for the first time, that fine-scale spatial heterogeneity, rather than geographic distance, is the defining characteristic of microplastic distributions in road runoff. Resolving this is therefore fundamental to establishing the representativeness of urban microplastic measurements, without which risk assessments remain inherently uncertain.

title: Honoring the Scientific Legacy of Dr Joseph J Pignatello
Fate and risk of natural and synthetic estrogens in a feed-manure-soil-vegetable system
From dense packing to porous layered POMOFs for ultra-efficient seawater uranium extraction
abstract: Efficient and selective uranium extraction from seawater (UES) is crucial for nuclear fuel sustainability but is challenged by low concentration, complex matrix, and biofouling. Here, we construct two POMOFs with distinct architectures: a dense D-W 10 -MOF and a porous layered P-W 10 -MOF. Taking advantage of the precise O···O distance (4.17 Å) matching uranyl bidentate coordination, open porous framework, and enhanced mass transfer, P-W 10 -MOF achieves a record-breaking Langmuir-fitted theoretical maximum uranium adsorption capacity (q max ) of 3197.5 mg·g⁻¹ in simulated seawater adsorption tests, along with outstanding selectivity (U/V ≈ 10 3 ) and cycling stability. By contrast, D-W 10 -MOF delivers a substantially lower q max of 961.5 mg·g⁻¹ due to hindered access to coordination sites. XAFS, XPS and DFT results confirm an equatorial U-O coordination number of 5.0 ± 0.4, consisting of three O donors from the W 10 cluster and two bidentate carbonate O donors. P-W 10 -MOF also exhibits strong antibacterial activity, and a preliminary life cycle assessment guides green synthesis. This work provides a paradigm for designing high-performance uranium adsorbents by clarifying the geometric structure and framework structure of the components.

title: Humic acid and related natural-organic-matter interfaces as sinks, carriers and mediators for persistent and recalcitrant organic contaminants: Mechanisms and endpoint-specific evidence
abstract: Humic acid (HA) is commonly viewed as an immobilizing sorbent, yet HA-associated organic matter can also mobilize contaminants or alter their transformation. This critical review evaluates when HA functions as a sink, carrier, or mediator for PAHs, pesticides and phenols, PFAS, and halogenated persistent organic pollutants. Evidence is distinguished among isolated HA/FA, operational natural humic fractions, bulk dissolved organic matter, native or mineral-associated organic matter, and model/comparator systems. We link hydrophobic partitioning, π-π interactions, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic forces, cation bridging, and quinone-mediated electron transfer to measurable fate endpoints. pH, ions, hydrodynamics, redox conditions, light, and biological activity can shift HA conformation, aggregation, mineral association, transport, and reactivity. Consequently, lower freely dissolved concentrations may coexist with greater colloid-associated flux, while parent loss may occur without mineralization or lower toxicity. We define sink, carrier, and mediator behavior from retention, transport, and product-resolved transformation, respectively, with exposure evaluated downstream. Event-scale evidence indicates contaminant redistribution during rainfall, freeze-thaw, and resuspension, although direct HA-specific data remain limited. An endpoint-specific assessment should integrate freely dissolved concentration, phase-resolved mass flux, products, mineralization, NER stability, and biological exposure within defined materials, media, comparators, and timescales, rather than a single removal metric.

title: Old meets new: How emerging contaminants reshape the environmental behavior of legacy contaminants in soils—interaction mechanisms, remediation reassessment, and the regulatory role of soil organic matter
abstract: Microplastics, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and antibiotics coexist in soils with legacy metal(loid)s, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and pesticides. These mixtures can alter contaminant fate, microbial selection, and remediation performance, but direct soil evidence remains uneven. This review synthesizes studies mainly from 2015 to 2025, earlier work, and selected early-online papers through June 2026. Soil evidence supports microplastic interactions with metals and PAHs; PFAS-metal evidence remains limited, mainly to retention. Antibiotic-metal evidence primarily concerns resistance co-selection rather than altered metal fate. We organize candidate processes into overlapping diagnostic tiers (physical co-location, interfacial chemical coupling, and biologically mediated feedback) and appraise evidence by study design, environmental relevance, mechanistic support, and risk of bias. A comparative map specifies required observations, alternative explanations, endpoint direction, and direct-evidence confidence. Concentration addition, independent action, and the combination index apply only to commensurable toxicological dose-response endpoints; transport, speciation, accumulation, and resistance require factorial or response-surface analyses. HIX, SUVA254, and PARAFAC components remain conditional dissolved organic matter proxies requiring method controls and independent validation. We classify remediation conclusions as direct mixture evidence, transferred single-contaminant principles, or author recommendations. The synthesis separates established findings from provisional interpretations.

title: Enhanced As(V) removal by a Zr-doped β-FeOOH functionalized PTFE membrane: Interfacial structure, selectivity, and ligand exchange
abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination poses a critical threat to water safety, yet efficient removal of As(V) remains challenging due to the lack of robust adsorbents with high selectivity and stability. Herein, a Zr-doped β-FeOOH-functionalized PTFE membrane (Zr/β-FeOOH-PDA/PEI-M) has been reported and fabricated via in situ mineralization on a PDA/PEI interlayer. By optimizing the Fe-to-Zr molar ratio to 3:2, an unprecedented balance between abundant Zr-O active sites and the preservation of β-FeOOH lattice integrity was achieved, as evidenced by multi-scale characterization. The optimized membrane delivers a remarkable As(V) removal efficiency of 97% with an adsorption capacity (Q e ) of 442.01 mg/m 2 in cross-flow filtration, outperforming most state-of-the-art materials. Notably, it exhibits exceptional tolerance to coexisting ions (Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , Cl - , SO 4 2- , CO 3 2- , PO 4 3- ) and natural organic matter, maintaining > 80% removal in real Pearl River water and meeting discharge standards. Mechanistically, we reveal a diffusion-ligand exchange-inner-sphere complexation pathway in which Zr 4+ enhances Lewis acidity and coordination affinity, while Fe-O sites play an auxiliary role, collectively accounting for the superior selectivity. This work not only provides a scalable, high-performance membrane for As(V) remediation but also offers insights into the rational design of Zr-based adsorbents for capturing toxic oxyanions.

title: Corrigendum to “Rainfall-driven electron acceptors loss constrain natural attenuation of petroleum hydrocarbons and development of a rainfall-responsive biostimulation strategy” [J Hazardou Mater 516 (2026) 143091]
Synergistic drivers of microbial carbon, nitrogen fixation and phosphorus mobilization in mining soils by integrating machine learning with causal analysis
abstract: Microbial carbon (C), nitrogen (N) fixation, and phosphorus (P) mobilization are key processes in ecosystem nutrient cycling. However, the key environmental factors driving these microbial functions in heavy metal-contaminated soils of mining areas remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed machine learning and causal analysis models to systematically identify the primary environmental drivers governing the relative abundances of key functional genes associated with C, N fixation and P mobilization in 48 metal mining areas across China. The results revealed that Fe, C/N ratio, and soil pH exert dominant controls on microbial functional genes. Among them, Fe was identified as a shared environmental driver across all functional groups, while C/N balance and soil pH exhibited consistent direct or indirect regulatory effects on microbial functional potential. Furthermore, machine learning-based threshold analysis revealed distinct ecological regulation windows in which microbial functional potential remained at relatively high levels, including Fe contents of 9-30%, C/N ratios of 20.47-50.62, and soil pH values of 5.8-6.30. This study elucidates the key environmental factors shaping microbial functions in mining-affected ecosystems and provides quantitative insights to support precision regulation in ecological restoration of contaminated soils.

title: Machine learning identifies drivers behind the emergence of actinobacteria as novel odor contributors in stratified reservoirs
From environmental gradients to putative intrinsic resistance: Deciphering the soil resistome across Mongolian Plateau grasslands
abstract: Soils are important reservoirs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet the ecological differentiation and host associations of grassland resistomes remain poorly understood. We investigated topsoil resistomes across desert steppe, typical steppe, and meadow steppe of the Mongolian Plateau using short- and long-read metagenomics. The resistome comprised 28 ARG types and 819 subtypes, dominated by rifamycin, vancomycin, and multidrug resistance genes. ARG abundance increased from desert steppe to meadow steppe. Soil pH, total organic carbon, total nitrogen, and climatic variables were strongly associated with resistome turnover, whereas grazing showed weaker associations. Mobile genetic element (MGE) abundance correlated positively with ARG abundance, but only 3.37% of ARG-carrying contigs contained detectable MGEs. An operational multi-indicator framework distinguished putative intrinsic and putative acquired ARGs with contrasting host and environmental associations. Both fractions were dominated by Actinomycetota, although Pseudomonadota contributed relatively more to putative acquired ARGs. Putative intrinsic ARGs were associated mainly with nutrient-related soil variables, whereas putative acquired ARGs showed stronger climatic and edaphic associations. Long-read assemblies markedly reduced the unclassified fraction. Among 195 ARG-carrying metagenome-assembled genomes, 65.6% represented reference-poor or previously uncultured lineages. These findings reveal spatially structured and heterogeneous grassland resistomes linked to ARG composition, host affiliation, and genomic context.

title: Distribution patterns of PFASs in intertidal sediments and the effects on reductive dehalogenating bacteria: A nationwide study in China
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are of great concern because of their environmental persistence. The intertidal zone sequesters various halogenated organic pollutants (HOPs) in sediments. Microbial reductive dehalogenation is crucial for HOPs detoxification. However, the nationwide distribution characteristics of PFASs in intertidal sediments and their impact on reductive dehalogenators (RDGs) remain poorly understood. We investigated PFAS distribution profiles in 128 intertidal sediments across China and analyzed their impact on potential RDGs. Sedimentary PFAS concentrations ranged 0.049-2.58 ng/g, with legacy PFASs being dominant. Amplicon sequencing and Spearman rank correlation analysis revealed positive correlation between total organic halogens and relative abundance and/or α-diversity of Anaerolineae and Desulfobacterota (p < 0.05), whereas no correlation was observed for Dehalococcoidia. Despite low ecological risks, Cl-PFESAs showed significant negative correlations with their relative abundance and α-diversity. Cl-PFESAs negatively correlated with abundance of the module associated with elemental cycles (p < 0.05), rather than those linked to organohalide utilization in the co-occurrence network. Microbial cultivation and metagenomic analysis reinforced the crucial role of Desulfobacterota and Anaerolineae in intertidal microbial dehalogenation and the negligible effect of 6:2 Cl-PFESA (0.1 mg/L) on reductive dehalogenating activity. This study provides critical insights into bioremediation strategies for HOPs in intertidal zones co-contaminated with PFASs.

title: Silver nanodot embedded waste PET nanofibres for efficient multifunctional air filter
abstract: This study focuses on conversion of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into ultrafine nanofibres with silver nanodots (AgND) (diameter 3.49 ± 0.94 nm) embedded within via electrospinning. Ultrafine PET (diameter 74 ± 15 nm) or PET-AgND (diameter 68 ± 17.4 nm) nanofibre-based membranes (basis weight 0.5 ± 0.02 g/m 2 , thickness 20 ± 1.4 μm), sandwiched between two spun-bond nonwoven layers, achieved a remarkable particle filtration efficiency (PFE) of 99.24-99.93% against 10-1000 nm particles, while maintaining pressure drop (ΔP) of 13 Pa at a face velocity of 5 cm/s. Such 3-ply filters demonstrated PFE > 99.5% against 350 nm particles with ΔP between 13-27 Pa over 28 consecutive filtration cycles. The PET-AgND membranes also demonstrated antibacterial efficacy of 99.78 ± 0.18% against Escherichia coli and 99.92 ± 0.02% against Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Washability assessments showed reduction of PFE from 99.7% to 57.6% with increment in pressure drop from 13 to 79 Pa, from unwashed till 9 washing-drying trials. The 3-ply filters also exhibited significant air permeability (64.4 ± 0.25 cm 3 /cm 2 -s), water vapor transmission rate (82.45 ± 2.7 g 3 /m 2 -h) coupled with prominent UV protection (79.5%). This study highlights a sustainable route for converting waste PET into high-performance, multifunctional, filter media.

title: Synthesis, characterisation, and chemical durability of UK uranium Butex high-level waste glasses
abstract: Two inactive simulant glass wasteforms were developed to incorporate a unique blend of high-level waste calcine from Butex, Magnox, and ThORP fuel reprocessing at a ratio of 50: 37.5: 12.5, with a total waste loading of 32 wt%. The glasses differed compositionally: one used the traditional Mixed Windscale (MW) borosilicate base glass (Butex MW), the other a CaZn-modified borosilicate base glass (Butex CaZn). Glasses were characterised by Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy, X-ray Diffraction, and X-ray Absorption Near Edge Spectroscopy, the latter confirming that U is incorporated as the uranyl (U⁶⁺) moiety in both glasses. Dissolution kinetics were evaluated using the Product Consistency Test-B (PCT-B) in UHQ water at 40 °C for 110 d, under both oxic and anoxic conditions. No significant differences were observed in the dissolution behaviour of the main glass elements (B, Si, Na, Li) between either glass composition or atmosphere. Both glasses followed typical borosilicate dissolution behaviour: a rapid initial rate (∼10⁻³ g m⁻² d⁻¹, 1-35 d), transitioning to a slower residual rate (∼10⁻⁵ g m⁻² d⁻¹, 35-110 d) - up to 16 times lower than Magnox/ThORP-only blends, attributed to reduced Mg content from the Butex component. Uranium release rates were similarly low (∼10⁻⁵ g m⁻² d⁻¹), indicating that Butex calcine addition improves durability in short-term accelerated testing. Minor differences between oxic and anoxic experiments were attributed to CO₂-driven pH changes, which affected Al solubility. Enhanced U release under oxic conditions was linked to U⁶⁺ complexation with bicarbonate ions, offering novel preliminary insight into Butex glass behaviour in (bi)carbonate-rich groundwater.

title: Abundance and characterization of microplastics in milk and dairy milk products with a special emphasis on possible health risk assessment: A global systematic review
abstract: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in food products has attracted widespread global attention because of concerns about their potential adverse effects on human health. This study synthesises published data on MPs in milk and dairy products, incorporates a comparative analysis across multiple countries and assesses potential health risks from MPs exposure through dairy consumption. In addition, methodological heterogeneity among the included studies was quantitatively evaluated by examining the effects of analytical techniques, minimum particle-size detection thresholds, and digestion protocols on the reported MP concentrations. The findings demonstrated that MPs concentrations in milk and dairy products ranged from 6 particles/L to approximately 20,200 particles/L. Methodological heterogeneity analysis demonstrated that analytical sensitivity and digestion protocols significantly contributed to inter-study variability, whereas differences among the principal analytical techniques were not statistically significant. Morphological characterisation revealed that fibers and fragments were the dominant forms in the milk matrices. An exposure assessment indicated that children are the most vulnerable population group for infant milk powder (827.75 particles/kg) and human breast milk (1828.92 particles/L) exposure. The MPs contamination factor (MCF) values across all countries and milk and dairy milk matrices predominantly fell within Category IV, corresponding to a very high contamination level classification. However, in packaged milk, countries such as Mexico and Ecuador were categorised within a comparatively lower, yet still significant contamination level. Notably, the microplastic load index (MPLI) values were highest in infant milk powder, followed by those in breast milk and packaged milk. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of MPs occurrence, methodological heterogeneity, contamination severity, and dietary exposure through milk and dairy products, thereby providing evidence to support policymakers, food safety authorities, and public health initiatives aimed at reducing MPs contamination. Furthermore, the findings align with global sustainability goals, particularly SDG 2 (Zero hunger), SDG 3 (Good health and well-being), SDG 12 (Responsible consumption and production), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

title: Layer cellulose-based sandwich sponge with directionally aligned channels for rapid removal of polystyrene nanoplastics and TBBPA
abstract: Nanoplastics can adsorb organic pollutants and facilitate their transport in water environments, thereby increasing potential risks to ecosystems and human health. However, most porous adsorbents have an even structure, making it difficult to combine rapid pollutant capture with stable retention. Herein, a layer cellulose-based sandwich (PCP) sponge with directionally aligned channels was fabricated through directional freezing and chemical cross-linking of cellulose fibers with chitosan and polyvinyl alcohol. The aligned porous channels promote solution transport, while chitosan provides positively charged sites favorable for capturing polystyrene (PS) nanoplastics. The layered architecture integrates macropore-mediated transport, interfacial adsorption, and physical interception within a single material. PCP sponge removed up to 99.88% of 100 nm PS nanoplastics within 10 min at room temperature. In coexistence experiments, an apparent tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) removal efficiency of more than 80% was also observed. After 10 adsorption-desorption cycles, the removal efficiency of PS still remains above 94.85%, and the pore structure remains intact under acidic, saline, and repeated cycling conditions. This study proposes a sustainable strategy for raw materials, which convert biomass resources into high-performance multifunctional adsorbents, providing a promising solution for the simultaneous removal of nanoplastics and coexisting organic pollutants from complex water environments.

title: Ultrasensitive and selective rGO QDs modified flower-like Bi2S3/Bi2O3 heterostructures for room-temperature trace NO2 detection
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a ubiquitous ambient pollutant, and chronic exposure to NO 2 , even at relatively low concentrations, has been associated with sustained adverse effects on multiple organ systems. Bismuth sulfide offers a promising platform for room-temperature gas sensing, yet its practical use is curtailed by poor charge-transfer efficiency and sparse interfacial active sites. In this study, reduced graphene oxide quantum dots (rGO QDs) modified Bi 2 S 3 /Bi 2 O 3 composites with abundant p-n heterojunctions were fabricated and used for NO 2 detection. The effects of annealing temperature and the amount of rGO on sensor performance were investigated, revealing optimal results for 0.5 wt% rGO modified Bi 2 S 3 annealed at 150℃ (rGO 0.5 -Bi 2 S 3 /Bi 2 O 3 -2). The rGO 0.5 -Bi 2 S 3 /Bi 2 O 3 -2 sensor exhibited a high response of 36.95 toward 500 ppb NO 2 at room temperature (RT). Experimental results demonstrated theoretical and experimental detection limits (LODs) of 0.6 ppb and 50 ppb for NO 2 respectively, as well as excellent selectivity, anti-interference ability, good repeatability, and long-term stability. By combining band structure alignments analysis with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the mechanism underlying the enhanced NO 2 detection performance was elucidated, revealing a synergistic effect of the heterojunction interface modulation between components and rGO-promoted charge transfer.

title: Evaluation and genomic characterization of endosulfan-degrading Streptomyces spp. isolated from a tropical environment
abstract: Endosulfan was banned worldwide under the Stockholm Convention in 2011, generating large amounts of waste to be disposed of and sporadic reports on its illegal usage. Microorganism-assisted treatment can be a cost-effective and environmentally friendly strategy to remove this chemical. Screening of bacteria from tropical agricultural sources heavily treated with endosulfan enabled us to isolate two Streptomyces spp. with ability to degrade α- and β-endosulfan isomers via hydrolytic pathway within 20 days of incubation in both sulfur-free medium (SFM) and carbon-free medium (CFM), producing endosulfan diol as metabolite. During the 20-day incubation in SFM, strain S12 degraded 99% (α) and 93% (β) of the isomers, while 68% (α) and 80% (β) were degraded in CFM. A similar tendency was observed for strain S9, with 96% (α) and 92% (β) degradation in SFM, compared to 40% (α) and 70% (β) degradation in CFM. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis identified endosulfan diol as a single metabolite in both strains. Based on genome and RNA-Seq analyses, homologous genes of known endosulfan degradative genes, esd and ese , were found in both genomes; however, their expression levels were negligible or not induced in SFM supplemented with endosulfan, suggesting that these genes are not involved in endosulfan degradation. In contrast, other genes that were highly expressed and showed different expressions in SFM- and CFM-containing endosulfan were discovered, implying that novel genes may be involved in endosulfan metabolism. This report provides evidence of newly isolated Streptomyces species and their potential to transform endosulfan into endosulfan diol.

title: Amplifying the invisible: Liquid crystal–hydrogel microcavities decode trace Hg ions and aflatoxin B1
abstract: Chinese herbal medicines (CHMs) have been applied to the prevention and treatment of numerous diseases. Ensuring the safety and pharmacological efficacy of CHMs demands precise detection of trace heavy metal ions and toxins, especially Hg and aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). However, due to subtle chemical signals, current technologies still make it challenging to monitor these quality parameters in a highly sensitive manner. Herein, we introduced a liquid crystal whispering gallery mode microresonator formed by encapsulating liquid crystal droplets in a hydrogel microcavity for monitoring analyte interactions. By employing an aptamer-target assay within the hydrogel, interfacial liquid crystal molecule reorientations and strong light-matter interactions in an optical microresonator can amplify signals. The tuning of resonance wavelength can be converted to improve monitoring of interaction processes. With narrow resonance linewidth, the limit of detection can reach 3.58 nM (Hg²⁺) and 101 fg/ml (aflatoxin B1). This method has been applied to detect the targets in real herbs (relative errors ranging from -2.931-5.572% compared with gold-standard methods) and demonstrated batch-to-batch heterogeneity in herbal analyte content. Further applications in various Chinese herbs evaluation demonstrated the applicability of this method supporting its potential for herbal safety assessment.

title: Agricultural impacts reshape the distribution and future potential health risks of soil heavy metals across global wheat-growing regions under interactive climate–socioeconomic influences
abstract: Soil heavy metal(loid) pollution poses a critical threat to ecosystem health and sustainability. However, it remains unclear whether agricultural activities have systematically altered their distribution across global wheat-growing regions. Here, we collected paired soil samples from cropland and adjacent non-cropland sites across global wheat-growing regions on six continents to evaluate concentration differences and potential drivers for six heavy metal(loid)s-arsenic (As), nickel (Ni), cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), antimony (Sb), and chromium (Cr). We found clear element-specific patterns: Ni was enriched in high-input agricultural regions, whereas Pb and Cr were more concentrated in non-croplands. These differences varied by region. Using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), we identified fertilization intensity, moisture conditions, and socioeconomic development as key nonlinear predictors. Projections under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios suggest that by 2100, these concentration differences may either reverse or intensify, with their spatial evolution accompanied by shifts in potential non-carcinogenic health across cropland soils. Our findings show that agricultural land use is closely associated with spatial patterns of soil heavy metals across global wheat-growing regions and highlight land-use differentials as valuable early indicators of pollution risk, particularly in major wheat-producing regions.

title: Construction and application of a mouth level exposure assessment system for harmful constituents in cigarette and heated tobacco products
abstract: Smokers' actual exposure to harmful constituents is critical for assessing tobacco product health risks. This study established a mouth level exposure (MLE) method using nicotine and solanesol as filter markers to evaluate constituent exposure among Chinese users of regular cigarettes (RC), slim cigarettes (SC), and heated tobacco products (HTP). Twenty-eight constituents, including HTP-specific propylene glycol, glycerol, chloropropanols, and glycidol, were selected. In RC and SC, nicotine and solanesol perform differently across constituents, requiring constituent-specific marker selection. Filter nicotine is superior for HTPs, predicting all constituents (R² ≥ 0.86). The equations differ among product types (P < 0.0001) and are not interchangeable. Relative to RC users, SC users show 20%-50% lower daily MLE for most constituents. HTP users exhibite the lowest constituent exposure, with formaldehyde, crotonaldehyde, acrolein, phenol, and HCN daily MLE reduced by over 90% relative to RC. This reduction primarily reflects lower constituent release from HTPs. HTP-specific constituents are first quantified, with daily exposures of propylene glycol 20.9 ± 12.7 mg, 3-MCPD 93.9 ± 57.0 μg, and glycidol 46.3 ± 28.0 μg, warranting attention to potential health risks. The developed MLE equations provide a tool for comparative risk assessment and regulatory evaluation based on actual exposure.

title: The tolerance differences and response mechanisms of the main submerged plants in Erhai Lake to the environmental concentration of atrazine stress
abstract: To investigate whether pesticide residues in the area near farmlands of Erhai Lake affect the growth of submerged plants in Erhai Lake, this study combined field investigations with 56-day outdoor simulation experiments to assess the differences in the effects and tolerance mechanisms of atrazine at environmental concentrations in Erhai Lake on four submerged plants: Ottelia acuminata, Potamogeton wrightii, Hydrilla verticillata, and Ceratophyllum demersum. The results showed that: ①Exposuring to atrazine at level of ≤ 35 ng/L caused no visible injury under the tested conditions. Under the stress of 75 and 125 ng/L atrazine, the plants Ottelia acuminata and Hydrilla verticillata showed observable growth differences. The metabolic level of Potamogeton wrightii had shown latent damage. The Ceratophyllum demersum had the best growth. ②The Fv/Fm values of the four plants were all inhibited, which are the most sensitive physiological indicators. ③Combining the weighting of photosynthetic factors with the metabolic results, the comprehensive tolerance of the four plants to atrazine was ranked as follows: Ceratophyllum demersum > Potamogeton wrightii > Hydrilla verticillata > Ottelia acuminata. Long-term exposure to high concentrations of atrazine may selectively inhibits the growth of submerged plants of sensitive species, thereby affecting the community structure of submerged plants in the lake.

title: Tire-derived 6PPD-quinone promotes conjugative gene transfer through respiratory bioenergetic perturbation
abstract: Tire-derived N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q) is transported by roadway runoff into urban waters, yet its sublethal effects on microbial gene exchange remain poorly resolved. Here, 5 μg/L 6PPD-Q increased the transconjugant fraction from 0.25% to 0.65% in a lake-water enriched biofilm community and enhanced plasmid transfer in a defined donor-recipient system. Relative to its parent compound 6PPD, 6PPD-Q more strongly altered oxidative phosphorylation, ATP/ADP ratios, and NAD + /NADH balance. Molecular simulations indicated membrane partitioning and predicted quinone-site interactions resembling those of ubiquinone analogues, while cyclic voltammetry and partial growth rescue of a ubiB-deficient strain supported quinone-associated redox activity. 6PPD-Q also increased succinate dehydrogenase activity, oxygen consumption, membrane potential, and ATP/ADP ratios. Respiratory-chain and bioenergetic inhibitors attenuated both these responses and the transfer enhancement, linking the phenotype to cellular energy metabolism. Extracellular filament-like structures, migration responses, and appendage-related transcription changed concurrently, although the structures could not be assigned to a specific pilus system. These results support respiratory bioenergetic perturbation as an upstream contributor to 6PPD-Q-enhanced conjugation and identify microbial gene exchange as a water-quality endpoint relevant to tire-contaminated runoff and receiving waters.

title: Detoxification-associated polyvinyl chloride micro- and nanoplastics clearance and liver metabolomic responses in mice
abstract: Aged PVC (A-PVC) exhibits distinct surface chemistry from original PVC that may result in different toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic behaviors, yet relevant evidence remains limited. This study investigated the tissue distribution, excretion kinetics and liver metabolic responses of PVC and its debris A-PVC in C57BL/6J mice following acute oral exposure. Py-GC/QTOF measurement revealed that both particles rapidly accumulated in major organs of liver, spleen, heart and lung, and that the particle burdens in the measured organs declined substantially by 72 h, which was further verified by the multiple imaging analysis. Although histopathological and biochemical alterations gradually attenuated during recovery, small A-PVC elicited more severe acute biological responses, whereas large original PVC produced relatively sustained toxic effects characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation and endocrine disruption. These findings highlight aging-associated alterations in the kinetic behavior of PVC MNPs. Notably, the organ specific clearance patterns of 300-1300 nm aged PVC are consistent with a hypothesized non-biliary intestinal excretion pathway, which warrants further verification.

title: Cascading effects of nano-biochar mitigate antibiotic resistance via phage–host interactions in the soil–crop ecosystem
abstract: Controlling the spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in agroecosystems is central to One Health, yet whether nano-biochar-amended organic fertilizers can mitigate phage-mediated ARG dissemination along the fertilizer-soil-crop continuum remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 120 viral metagenomes to examine how biochar-amended organic fertilizers modulate ARG dynamics, phage-associated functions, and phage-host interactions across the fertilizer-soil-lettuce continuum.
