The lettuce phyllosphere served as a key endpoint for ARG accumulation, exhibiting 4.1-4.9 times the total ARG abundance and 56.8-66.3% higher phage-encoded ARG abundance compared with rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere soils. Source-tracking analysis indicated that manure and soil inputs accounted for 50.8-57.0% of phyllosphere ARGs, while 111 manure-associated viral populations were shared with the phyllosphere at the viral cluster level. Notably, nano-biochar-amended vermicompost exerted a cascading mitigation effect, reducing manure- and soil-derived ARG inputs to the phyllosphere by 20.4-21.6% and manure-associated viral sharing by 51.6%. Meanwhile, nano-biochar-amended vermicompost reduced lysogenic phage-host interactions, phage-encoded ARGs, and auxiliary metabolic genes associated with antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which may contribute to reduced phage-associated ARG dissemination potential. Consequently, total ARG abundance in the phyllosphere decreased by 68.9-76.3%, while lettuce biomass increased by 54.1-61.5%. This work suggests that nano-biochar-amended vermicompost may mitigate antibiotic resistance risks and enhance crop productivity partly by attenuating phage-associated ARG dissemination across the fertilizer-soil-crop continuum, highlighting its potential for One Health-oriented resistance-risk control in agricultural production.

title: Simultaneous nutrient and PAH removal from municipal secondary effluent in pilot-scale open algal raceway ponds: Effects of hydraulic retention time and multi-trophic microbial succession
abstract: Algal raceway ponds (ARPs) are considered one of the most promising technologies for the advanced treatment of wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluents. In this study, three parallel pilot-scale open ARPs, each assigned to one hydraulic retention time (HRT, 2, 3, or 4 d), were continuously operated for 52 d to assess nutrient and PAH removal, PAH partitioning, and microbial community succession. The 3-d system provided the most favorable observed balance between pond biomass accumulation and pollutant removal, with the highest mean pond biomass concentration (704 mg L -1 (dw)) and mean removal efficiencies of 86.52%, 95.18%, 67.74%, 91.81%, and 73.68% for TN, TP, NH 4 + -N, NO 3 - -N, and Σ 16 PAH, respectively. Daily biomass harvesting was highest at 2 d (14.9 g m -2 d -1 (dw)). At the 3-d HRT, the mean removal efficiencies of low-molecular-weight (LMW) and high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs were 74.39% and 69.61%, respectively. Distinct microbial assemblages developed in the ARPs, with Golenkinia predominating among microalgal genera, Pseudomonadota among bacterial phyla, and Cercozoa among protozoan phyla. Exploratory association analyses revealed that LMW-PAH removal showed positive directional relationships with OD 680 and microalgal diversity, whereas HMW-PAH removal showed predominantly negative relationships with physiological, nutrient-removal, and community indicators. Phase-distribution analysis further showed that HMW-PAHs were enriched in harvested biomass and that logK d increased with logK ow . Aqueous BaP-equivalent concentrations were lower in the effluents than in the influent, and incremental lifetime cancer risk estimates for harvested biomass were below 10 -6 under the specified adult incidental-ingestion scenario. These findings support the engineering application of open ARP systems for advanced treatment of WWTP effluent.

title: From manure to fertilizer in minutes: Radical induced humification and decontamination
abstract: Global livestock/poultry manure output (approximately 13 billion tons/year) poses a major sustainability challenge. Conventional recycling via composting and anaerobic digestion after solid-liquid separation is slow (20-60 d) and inefficient at removing pollutants (i.e. pathogens, antibiotics, and heavy metals). This study develops a minute-scale, one-step process using microwave and FeSO₄ to activate persulfate, generating radicals that rapidly convert chicken manure into a fertilizer rich in fulvic-like acids (41.7 wt% on a dry-product basis) and nutrients, including K (a primary nutrient) and Fe (a micronutrient). It simultaneously inactivates culturable bacteria, achieves approximately 99% removal of the parent antibiotics, reduces the combined acid-extractable and reducible fractions of Cd, Cu, and As by approximately 90%, and reduces odors (>97%). Carbon and nitrogen losses, calculated on an absolute-mass basis, were 15.6% and 12.6%, respectively. In a 21-day pot experiment, the fertilizer increased the fresh biomass of pak choi seedlings by 214.3% compared with the unamended soil control (Blank), while increasing soil total potassium and available nitrogen and potassium. This process shows cost (201 RMB/t wet CMPFM) advantage compared with composting, offering an efficient green alternative for manure recycling and circular agriculture.

title: Biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics pose greater field nitrous oxide emission risks than conventional polyethylene by reshaping microbial production-reduction pathways in a wheat-maize rotation system
abstract: Microplastic contamination in agroecosystems is increasing, yet the field-scale effects of biodegradable microplastics on soil nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions remain unclear. We conducted a wheat-maize rotation field experiment to compare conventional polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) at three application levels. Measurements included N 2 O fluxes, soil physicochemical properties, N-transformation enzyme activities, potential nitrification and denitrification rates, functional gene abundances, N 2 O/(N 2 O+N 2 ) product ratios, 15N-18O-based N 2 O production pathways. Two-way ANOVA showed that microplastic type was the most consistent determinant of key responses, whereas concentration and interaction effects varied among indicators and seasons. PE-MPs caused weak and variable changes in soil N cycling and cumulative N 2 O emissions. In contrast, PLA-MPs increased cumulative N 2 O emissions by 38.9-61.1%, increased dissolved organic carbon, lowered pH, suppressed ammonia monooxygenase activity and nitrification, and stimulated nitrite reductase activity, potential denitrification, and nirK/nirS abundances. Increased N 2 O/(N 2 O+N 2 ) and (nirK+nirS)/nosZ ratios indicated a stronger imbalance between N 2 O production and nosZ-mediated reduction. Dual-isotope tracing further showed that microplastics reduced nitrifier nitrification and shifted N 2 O production toward nitrifier denitrification, coupled nitrification-denitrification, and heterotrophic denitrification, with the strongest shift under PLA-MPs. These results demonstrate PLA-MPs pose greater N 2 O emission risks than PE-MPs, biodegradability does not necessarily imply environmental safety.

title: Tailored nanofiltration membrane for enhanced performance by surface modification using zwitterionic piperazine
abstract: Nanofiltration (NF) membranes are indispensable for removing hazardous contaminants such as dyes and salts from industrial wastewater, yet their performance is often bottlenecked by the inherent permeability-selectivity trade-off and membrane fouling. Zwitterionic surface modification offers a means to overcome these limitations by promoting hydrophilicity and introducing charge-mediated transport. Here we synthesized a pre-formed zwitterionic piperazine (ZW-PIP) via a one-pot ring-opening of piperazine with 1,3-propanesultone, and directly grafted it onto polyamide films through residual acyl chloride groups. Combined low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF NMR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations demonstrated that the grafted zwitterionic moieties stabilized a hydration layer and facilitated water and chloride-ion diffusion (>90%), while sterically excluding sulfate. The resulting membrane exhibited a pure water permeance of 29.2 L∙m -2 ∙h -1 ∙bar -1 . Crucially, this enhanced permeability was achieved while maintaining the exceptional salt-rejection performance for Na 2 SO 4 (>97.0%). This high selectivity persisted even under challenging conditions of elevated salt concentration (8.0 g/L) and operating pressure (8.0 bar). The membrane exhibited robust rejection of various dyes (>96%), sustained stability, and potent antifouling (BSA, FRR 89%) and antibacterial (>99.97%) properties. Collectively, this work offers a mechanistic basis for designing zwitterionic NF membranes with high permeability, selectivity, and fouling resistance for treating complex hazardous wastewater.

title: Abnormal electron-donation-dependent sulfite activation in the Mn(II)-nitrilotriacetic acid system: QSAR and mechanistic insights
abstract: In advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), electron-rich contaminants are generally susceptible to oxidation by reactive species. Herein, an unusual substrate-selective degradation was observed in sulfite (Na 2 SO 3 ) based AOPs with the Mn(II)-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) complex. The strong electron-rich phenolics were hardly degraded, whereas electron-deficient phenols were efficiently removed. An asymmetric volcano-shaped correlation between the degradation rates and Hammett constants σ + was established via quantitative structure-activity relationship analysis and can be expanded to antibiotics and dyes with anodic peak potential as a descriptor. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that electron-rich phenolics complex with Mn(II)-NTA, suppressing O 2 -driven Mn(III)-NTA formation and thus limiting Mn(V)-NTA accumulation, with a slow radical chain reaction for Na 2 SO 3 oxidation. In contrast, electron-deficient substrates promote Mn(III)-NTA generation, fast Na 2 SO 3 oxidation and transformation to peroxymonosulfate (PMS), and subsequent Mn(V)-NTA formation. Consequently, radical pathways participate in the degradation of electron-rich pollutants, whereas Mn(V)-NTA governs the oxidation of electron-deficient ones. The low-cost Na 2 SO 3 system shows comparable or superior performance to PMS-based systems for electron-deficient pollutants, highlighting its economic viability. These findings underscore the importance of pollutant-catalyst interactions in AOPs and provide mechanistic insights for targeted contaminant remediation.

title: Molecular insight of U-As-Cd synergistic mineralization and metabolic responses mediated by Brevundimonas spp.
The C-terminal fragment of COL1A1 protects mammalian testicular BTB integrity by competitively inhibiting Cd-induced activation of the TGFβ-SMAD2/3-MMP9 pathway
abstract: Cadmium (Cd), a heavy metal pollutant, impairs male reproductive health by disrupting the blood-testis barrier (BTB) and inducing testicular injury in mammals. Collagen type I alpha 1 chain (COL1A1) and its bioactive fragments are essential for maintaining BTB integrity and seminiferous tubule structure. However, whether COL1A1 and its bioactive fragments can modulate Cd-induced BTB injury remains largely unknown. In this study, proteomic analysis showed that downregulated proteins including COL1A1 were mainly enriched in collagen-containing extracellular matrix pathway in boars with low quality semen. COL1A1 generates an approximately 25 kDa bioactive fragment termed C1158/59. Overexpression of C1158/59 in primary mouse Sertoli cells and testes mitigated Cd-induced BTB damage by restoring the expression and localization of BTB-associated proteins, as well as the organization of F-actin and α-tubulin cytoskeletons in Sertoli cells. Mechanistically, C1158/59 competitively inhibited the binding of latent TGFβ to ITGB1, suppressing Cd-induced activation of the TGFβ-SMAD2/3 signaling pathway and subsequent MMP9 upregulation, ultimately preventing BTB structural degradation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate a critical protective role of the COL1A1-derived fragment C1158/59 against Cd-induced structural and functional impairment of the testicular BTB, providing new insights into the regulatory functions of bioactive fragments in preserving BTB structural integrity against environmental toxicant-induced testicular injury.

title: Engineering FAST-PETase with enhanced catalytic efficiency and acidic adaptability for sustainable PET waste recycling
abstract: This study presented a comprehensive protein engineering strategy to enhance the catalytic efficiency and environmental adaptability of FAST-PETase for PET plastic degradation. Through systematic site-directed mutagenesis of key basic residues (Arg84, Arg117, and Lys227) surrounding the active site, we identified R84D as the optimal single mutant, exhibiting 2.1-fold higher activity than FAST-PETase. Iterative saturation mutagenesis at 19 targeted positions yielded the quadruple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q, demonstrating superior kinetic parameters: 3.3-fold higher catalytic efficiency (k cat /K m = 10.8 L·mmol -1 ·min -1 ) and significantly improved substrate affinity (K m = 72.6 mM) at acidic conditions. Structural characterization revealed this mutant's optimized active site geometry, featuring enhanced hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. It exhibited broad pH adaptability (maintaining >80% activity at pH 7.59.0) with a 0.5-unit acidic shift in optimal pH (7.5 vs wild-type's 8.0), while retaining thermal stability up to 50°C. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the mutant's enhanced structural rigidity, with 3050% lower RMSD values compared to FAST-PETase. When tested in a two-module reactor system, the quintuple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q/S239V enabled efficient PET conversion to TPA, achieving a space-time conversion rate of 3.51 g·(L·h) -1 . These results demonstrated its practical potential for industrial application. It established an effective framework for engineering plastic-degrading enzymes with enhanced performance under industrially relevant conditions.

title: Econazole prevents the conjugative transfer of plasmid-borne last-line antibiotic resistance genes
Spatial distribution and microbial degradation potential of microplastics and nanoplastics along a 134-year proglacial chronosequence
abstract: Glacier retreat increasingly exposes proglacial soils to micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) pollution, yet long-term MNP dynamics and associated microbial plastic-degradation potential remain unclear. Along a 134-year chronosequence at Hailuogou Glacier, we combined µ-FTIR, Py-GC/MS, and metagenomics to characterize MNP pollution, ecological risk, and microbial degradation potential. MP abundance followed a non-linear trajectory, peaking at 270 items kg⁻¹ at 66 yr, whereas NP abundance increased from 1.54 to 4.17 mg kg⁻¹ . MPs were dominated by PA, PE, PET, and Rayon, while NPs shifted from PMMA to PE dominance (>78%) in mature soils. Ecological risk was non-monotonic and polymer-dependent: MP-associated PERI reached Level IV at 66 yr, whereas NP-associated PERI peaked at 94 yr despite increasing NP mass. This decoupling suggested that risk was strongly influenced by polymer-composition turnover rather than abundance or mass alone. Gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential increased during succession through enrichment of plastic-degradation-related genes. PLS-PM identified a sequence of positive associations linking glacier retreat age, soil development, MNP pollution, and microbial plastic-degradation potential. Random Forest analysis further highlighted retreat age and Ca among the leading predictors of degradation-gene abundance. These findings provide insights into MNP risk and gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential in rapidly deglaciating high-altitude ecosystems.

title: Salinity-Associated Shifts in DOM-Cu(II) Binding Along a Coastal Wetland Gradient: Molecular Weight Dependence and Implications for Metal-Risk Assessment
Fe(III)-mediated sulfide mineralization preserves and reactivates sulfur-derived reductive capacity in autotrophic Cr(VI) bioremediation
abstract: Sulfur-based autotrophic bioreduction is effective for Cr(VI)-contaminated groundwater remediation, yet the fate of sulfur-derived reducing equivalents after Cr(VI) depletion remains unclear. Continued sulfur disproportionation generates biogenic sulfide that constitutes a secondary pollutant and an irreversible loss of reductive capacity. Here we show that Fe 2 O 3 supplementation (0.2-0.8 g/L) intercepts this loss pathway by sequestering post-reduction sulfide as reactive Fe-S minerals. After Cr(VI) exhaustion, sulfide produced from sulfur disproportionation was immobilized predominantly as FeS, with minor FeS 2 , as confirmed by XANES and EXAFS analyses. Electron-balance calculations showed that the otherwise mobile sulfide-derived reducing equivalents were largely retained in these reactive solids, and the resulting FeS reduced Cr(VI) more efficiently than elemental sulfur, indicating that mineral-preserved reductive capacity remains accessible for subsequent contaminant removal. Also, Fe 2 O 3 accelerated autotrophic Cr(VI) bioreduction, with the pseudo-first-order rate constant 5.3 times that of the Fe-free control. This acceleration was driven by enhanced cell viability, electron transport activity, and cytochrome c, rather than by community restructuring or redirected electron allocation between Cr(VI) reduction and carbon metabolism. These results recast Fe(III) from a kinetic enhancer of electron transfer into a mineralogical sink that preserves reduction potential across the full cycle, coupling sulfide control with electron conservation in sulfur-driven remediation.

title: Erratum to “Function of pre-sulfation: Boosting sulfur resistance of nanocrystal PtO2/KL-NY catalyst in benzene oxidation reaction” [J. Hazardous Mater. 494 (2025) 138626]
Sonic hedgehog pathway activation mitigates the anti-neurogenic effects of Bisphenol-A in the rat brain hippocampus
Microplastics amplify Cr(VI)-mediated RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer through coupled interfacial, oxidative, and metabolic regulation
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can accumulate heavy metals and influence plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance gene (ARGs) transfer, yet the regulatory mechanisms under metal-associated MP exposure remain poorly understood. Here, a polystyrene microplastic-Cr(VI) composite (PSMPs@Cr) was established to investigate RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer by integrating physicochemical characterization, physiological measurements, transcriptomic analysis, and multivariable modeling. PSMPs@Cr exhibited a non-monotonic effect on conjugative transfer, with the highest conjugative transfer frequency (9.4 × 10 -2 ) observed at 20 ppm Cr loading, representing a 4.75-fold increase compared with the control. Cr adsorption reconstructed the MP interface by modifying surface charge, wettability, morphology, and colloidal stability, which was accompanied by altered bacterial adhesion behavior. Meanwhile, PSMPs@Cr exposure induced coordinated changes in ROS accumulation, antioxidant responses, ATP production, membrane-associated functions, and energy metabolism. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed treatment-dependent regulation of oxidative stress, membrane transport, cellular communication, and metabolic pathways. Random forest-SHAP analysis identified zeta potential, CAT activity, ATP, and ROS as relatively important variables associated with CTF variation. Overall, PSMPs@Cr-associated ARGs transfer was linked to coupled interfacial, redox, and energetic processes rather than a single regulatory pathway, providing new insights into how microplastic-metal interactions influence plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer under complex contaminant exposure scenarios.

title: Tracing sediment organic matter sources in a tributary of the Three Gorges Reservoir via stable isotopes (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) under anthropogenic influences
abstract: As major reservoirs of organic matter (OM), sediments are substantially influenced by anthropogenic activities, yet their effects on OM sources remain unclear. Surface sediments from the Yulin River, a tributary of the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR), were analyzed for δ 13 C, δ 15 N, TOC, TN and C/N in 2019 and 2023 during stable impounding (SIP) and discharge (SDP) periods of TGR. Across the sampled sites, TOC and TN tended to be higher at the upstream sites than at the downstream site, indicating dam-induced sediment trapping and enhanced autochthonous production. From 2019-2023, δ 13 C shifted from -26.54‰ to -21.41‰, and δ 15 N increased from 2.51‰ to 6.15‰, reflecting a transition from soil dominance toward increased sewage and C4 plant contributions. MixSIAR showed soil contribution decreased (66.11%→58.70%), while sewage (2.83%→5.51%), phytoplankton (5.21%→6.65%), and C4 plants (18.93%→24.51%) increased over the four-year. Hydrological regulation further modulated source dynamics: SIP favored ¹ ³C-depleted algal OM, whereas SDP enhanced terrestrial and 15 N-enriched sewage inputs. These findings indicate that dam operation, urbanization and sewage discharge substantially altered sedimentary OM composition, with stable isotope signatures proving effective in tracing anthropogenic impacts on riverine carbon and nitrogen dynamics.

title: Glyphosate exposure alters the faecal corticosterone metabolite profile in a lizard: Validation and application of an enzyme immunoassay in Podarcis bocagei
abstract: Glyphosate, the active ingredient of world’s most widely used herbicide RoundupTM, has attracted attention due to its impact on non-target organisms. Recent studies highlight the effects of glyphosate and glyphosate-based herbicides on the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis of vertebrates. Nevertheless, previous studies utilised dosages higher than toxicological reference values (TRVs) suggested by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), or formulations of glyphosate, not allowing for clear distinctions of the effects of glyphosate itself. Moreover, its impact on the HPA axis was assessed using blood samples, a technique inappropriate for small animals and for assessing long-term chronic effects. Here we tackled those caveats by analyzing faecal corticosterone metabolites (FCMs) of the wall lizard Podarcis bocagei to detect glyphosate-induced effects on the HPA axis. This species provides a promising animal model as reptiles are prevalent in agricultural fields treated with herbicides, reptile-specific TRVs are still lacking, and only five studies have validated immunoassays for measuring FCMs in reptiles. Here we validated the 5α-pregnane-3ß,11ß,21-triol-20-one enzyme immunoassay. We detected a glyphosate-induced moderate increase in FCM levels during the exposure phase, while exposed animals of both sexes displayed an altered mass-depended FCM profile. Our results indicate that glyphosate likely impacts the energy mobilization and management of lizards, at the expense of maintenance, growth and reproduction. Our outcomes support the need for reptile-specific TRVs and the consideration of reptiles in EFSA's risk assessment for glyphosate. In methodological terms, FCM analysis can serve as an effective non-invasive tool to estimate the chronic impacts of glyphosate in animal species.

title: National-scale evaluation of groundwater fluoride in Ethiopia using spatially buffered machine learning
abstract: Excess groundwater fluoride (F⁻) is a public health concern in the East African Rift, yet sparse, clustered observations limit reliable national inference. This study developed a leakage-controlled framework to classify groundwater fluoride exceedance above the WHO guideline of 1.5 mg/L, separating well-level prediction from national spatial transferability. A dataset of 1567 observations, including 567 exceedances, was evaluated using five-fold buffered spatial cross-validation with a 75-km train-test exclusion radius. The hydrochemical Extra Trees model (HYD_ET) achieved the strongest well-level performance, with Macro-F1 = 0.830, balanced accuracy = 0.817, MCC = 0.671, ROC-AUC = 0.910, PR-AUC = 0.859, and Brier score = 0.116. In contrast, the environmental-only Random Forest showed negligible geographic transferability (Macro-F1 = 0.495; balanced accuracy = 0.501), while Gaussian indicator kriging achieved Macro-F1 = 0.594. Applicability-domain analysis identified 8.23% of observations outside the model domain. Because no continuous model demonstrated adequate transferability, no wall-to-wall national F⁻-risk surface was retained. Instead, 48.43%, 18.84%, and 32.73% of 10-km grid cells had stronger, moderate, and weaker monitoring support, respectively. This evaluation spans heterogeneous hydrogeological and environmental settings under uneven monitoring across Ethiopia. The results show that strong well-level prediction does not imply reliable national extrapolation and supports groundwater monitoring and data collection.

title: Structural Dependence of Pharmaceutical Transformation and Toxicity Evolution During Water Oxidation and Disinfection
Arsenite-associated attenuation of daptomycin-induced inhibition in Clostridium butyricum under co-exposure conditions
abstract: The metalloid arsenic may co-occur with antibiotics in anaerobic environments, yet microbial responses to their combined stress remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how arsenite (As(III)) alters the response of Clostridium butyricum CXL-1 using phenotypic, physiological, and transcriptomic analyses. Individually, As(III) and daptomycin inhibited bacterial growth and fermentative metabolism in a dose-dependent manner, with an As(III) IC50 of 120 mg/L and complete growth inhibition at 5 mg/L daptomycin. Under co-exposure, increasing daptomycin concentrations at fixed As(III) progressively inhibited fermentative metabolism, whereas increasing As(III) concentrations at fixed daptomycin increased final biomass despite slower substrate utilization. Relative to daptomycin alone, As(III) co-exposure produced a higher ATP index, lowered reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and the NADH/NAD + ratio, and reduced lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) leakage. Transcriptomic analysis under co-exposure revealed upregulation of the arsenic resistance operon (ars), mepA_6, and genes for thiamine biosynthesis, sulfur transport, and glutathione biosynthesis, and downregulation of phosphotransferase system and pentose phosphate pathway genes. At the relatively high laboratory As(III) concentrations tested, co-exposure was associated with attenuated daptomycin-induced inhibition, slower carbon utilization, a higher ATP index, improved redox balance, and membrane integrity. This study reveals a previously underexplored influence of arsenic exposure on bacterial responses to antibiotics under anaerobic conditions.

title: Stepwise sulfation roasting for co-recovery of Li and F/Al as AlF3 from spent aluminum electrolyte: in-situ phase evolution and atomic-scale migration
abstract: Spent aluminum electrolyte (SAE) from aluminum smelting is both a hazardous fluoride waste and a valuable Li/F resource. The current Al 2 (SO 4 ) 3 roasting process of recycling SAE focuses solely on either AlF 3 recovery or Li extraction, leading to incomplete F/Li/Al resource utilization. Mechanistic understandings of roasting reaction remain at the static thermodynamics and macroscopic level. Herein, we propose a stepwise roasting-leaching closed-loop recovery process. Primary sulfation roasting-water leaching converts SAE into AlF 3 with 98.5% Li leached, and the crude AlF 3 is purified to 95.20% purity via Na 2 CO 3 conversion. The F and Al in the leachate were recovered as aluminum hydroxyfluoride, followed by NH 4 HF 2 roasting to recycle AlF 3 and entrained Li, boosting the overall Li and F recovery to 97.09% and 98.23% respectively. In-situ thermal behavior indicated that the melting point of the system decreased initially and then increased during roasting due to stepwise phase-evolution, and local melting occurred at 477 ℃, rather than the reported pure solid-solid reaction. First-principles calculation further revealed the atomic migration priority of the roasting reaction (F > Na > O > Al > S). Techno-economic and environmental analysis shows a profit of CNY 8382.1 /t-SAE and a net abatement of 0.92 t CO 2 eq/t-SAE.

title: Electron-Enriched Ir Centers at Ir-O-W Interfaces Enable O2-Tolerant CO-Assisted NO Reduction
Co-inoculation of indigenous cyanobacteria and fungi effectively immobilizes heavy metals in molybdenum tailings by forming biocrusts: Exploration of potential immobilization mechanisms
abstract: Nutrient deficiency and heavy metal (HM) toxicity represent major obstacles to the ecological restoration of tailings ponds. However, as "ecological engineers" in extreme environments, biological crusts (BCs) play a significant role in the restoration of degraded habitats. In this study, the molybdenum tailings were inoculated with the indigenous cyanobacteria and fungi isolated from a tailings pond to construct BCs in a pot experiment. Both single cyanobacteria inoculation and co-inoculation of cyanobacteria and fungi formed moss BCs after an 80-day cultivation. Compared with single inoculation, co-inoculation significantly increased the BCs thickness and chlorophyll a content by 16.16∼17.47% and 10.17∼26.29%, respectively. BCs effectively reduced the bioavailability of Cd, Cu, Mo, and Zn in tailings, while substantially enriching these HMs. EPS chelation, biosorption by moss and microorganisms, and clay mineral adsorption in BCs were synergistically involved in HM immobilization. Additionally, BCs significantly improved tailings properties, and BCs growth, organic carbon, exopolysaccharide, microbial biomass carbon, and available potassium were key influencing factors in reducing HM bioavailability. These results demonstrated the feasibility of rapidly constructing BCs via co-inoculation of functional microorganisms onto tailings and provided a low-cost, eco-friendly, and sustainable new strategy for ecological restoration and HM pollution mitigation of tailings ponds.

title: Sixteen-year changes in hazardous metal(loid)s in urban topsoils: Land-use-specific enrichment and PM₁₀-based human health risk
abstract: Urban topsoils are persistent reservoirs of hazardous metal(loid)s, yet reassessments rarely integrate censoring-aware statistics, geochemical enrichment and updated exposure modelling. We reassessed 137 topsoils collected in 2001 and 94 in 2017 across Urban, Industrial and Garden land uses in Alcalá de Henares, Spain. Eleven elements were compared temporally using left-censored methods with false-discovery-rate correction; Hg was retained as a 2017 descriptive endpoint because of poor historical comparability and high censoring. Urban Pb declined by 43.3%, whereas Be, Cr, Mn, Tl and V showed FDR-robust shifts towards higher 2017 acid-recoverable concentrations; because the digestion workflows differed between campaigns, the magnitude of these increases cannot be attributed exclusively to environmental accumulation. Sn showed a significant distributional shift, while the apparent 16.4% Cd decline was not robust to conservative analytical-threshold sensitivity. Industrial soils likewise showed higher 2017 acid-recoverable concentrations of As, Cr, Mn, Tl, V and Zn. Integrated enrichment was lowest in Urban soils and highest at the four sampled Garden locations; because the 2017 Garden subset comprised only n = 4, these metrics are interpreted as site-specific screening indicators rather than municipality-wide Garden estimates. Using updated U.S. EPA toxicity parameters and the historical-comparability assumption Cr(VI) = total Cr/6, 2017 hazard indices were 1.214 for Urban children, 0.156 for Urban adults, 0.0997 for Industrial workers, 2.173 for children at the sampled Garden locations and 0.278 for Garden adults. Cancer risks ranged from 4.13 × 10⁻⁵ to 2.16 × 10⁻⁴, with As dominating both non-cancer and cancer risk. From 2001-2017, Urban-child HI increased from 0.949 to 1.214, crossing the screening benchmark of 1. Excluding inferred Cr(VI) did not change this or any other qualitative receptor-level interpretation. Alcalá topsoils therefore show divergent contaminant trajectories, with declining legacy Urban Pb coexisting with higher 2017 acid-recoverable multi-element signatures and persistent child-exposure screening priorities.

title: Analysis and Prediction of Tissue-Specific Bioconcentration Factors of Organophosphate Esters in Silver Salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch) Using Machine Learning
Zearalenone hepatotoxicity in an agro-environmental context: Proteomics-anchored systems toxicology and hyperoside-associated stabilization
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA), a thermally stable Fusarium mycotoxin, is frequently detected in cereals and feed-related matrices. In agricultural systems, contaminated feed exposes livestock directly, while mycotoxins or metabolites may re-enter the environment via manure handling and land application. However, how ZEA perturbs hepatic systems at the network level remains unclear. We combined network toxicology, label-free porcine liver proteomics, porcine-to-human orthology mapping, and molecular docking with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The analysis used a stage-oriented disease-module framework encompassing DILI-like injury, MAFLD, fibrosis, and HCC-related contexts. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted hepatotoxic liability for ZEA and its major metabolites. Across modules, enrichment implicated lipid and xenobiotic metabolism, redox regulation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular stress. Proteomics revealed broad remodeling of metabolic and antioxidant networks after ZEA exposure, while hyperoside (HYP) co-exposure shifted part of these alterations toward the control pattern. After orthology mapping, HYP-attenuated proteins converged on candidate hubs within human disease modules. Docking and 100 ns MD simulations suggested more stable HYP binding than ZEA at representative hubs, including glutathione reductase (GSR), mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 (MAPK3), and sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1). These findings provide a systems-level basis for interpreting ZEA-associated hepatotoxicity in feed-linked agricultural settings and identify candidate signatures for monitoring and mitigation.

title: Unraveling the influence of Fe2O3 and CaO on phase transformation of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances during sewage sludge pyrolysis
abstract: Understanding the phase transformation behavior of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) during the thermal treatment of lime-conditioned or iron-treated sludge is crucial for environmental risk evaluation. However, to date, no studies have explicitly evaluated PFAS degradation during the pyrolysis of sewage sludge. Herein, we report the investigation of the roles of CaO and Fe 2 O 3 in promoting PFAS degradation in sewage sludge during low-temperature pyrolysis at 300°C and 500°C. Analyses via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicated physical interactions between Fe-containing surface sites and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Fe 2 O 3 facilitates PFAS volatilization and/or transformation into fluorinated intermediates rather than mineralization, whereas PFAS undergo mineralization in the presence of CaO. Nontarget liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry analyses of leachates from Fe 2 O 3 -treated sludge biochar and gas-trapped samples revealed the presence of PFOA and fluorinated intermediates, such as 1-hydro-pentadecafluoroheptane, indicating partial degradation rather than mineralization. In contrast, no newly enriched intermediate compounds were observed in CaO-treated samples, probably owing to the increased stabilization of fluorinated species within the solid matrix. Leaching tests of the resulting biochar demonstrated that acidic conditions highly promote the release of PFOA and perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) compared with neutral and alkaline conditions. PFBS leaching was strongly influenced by pH, whereas PFOA release was highly time dependent, highlighting compound-specific leaching behavior and potential environmental risks associated with post-pyrolysis biochar application. This study provides key insights for future research for optimizing pyrolysis conditions and additive selection to minimize secondary PFAS release.

title: Removal and stabilization of PFAS and As(V) co-contamination in soils by fluorine-functionalized biochar
abstract: The prevalent PFAS and heavy metals (such as arsenic) co-contaminated soils, resulting from industrial activities, present a considerable remediation challenge as conventional single-function materials are often ineffective. In this study, a fluorine-iron dual-functionalized biochar (FMBC) was prepared via a magnetite impregnation-fluorosilane grafting strategy, which integrates multiple binding modes: grafted perfluoroalkyl chains provide hydrophobic and F-F interaction zones for capturing PFAS tails; loaded Fe oxides offer positively charged electrostatic and coordinative sites to attract the anionic headgroups of PFAS, while simultaneously capturing As(V) through electrostatic attraction, coprecipitation, and complexation. 1:10FMBC exhibited a higher PFOS sorption (75.91 mg/g) compared to raw biochar (0.63 mg/g), achieving 99.9%, 95.3%, and 65.7% removal for PFOS, PFOA, and PFHxS, showing notable chemical stability, and maintaining efficient PFAS-As(V) removal across various water matrices. DFT calculations reveal that synergy of F-F interactions and electrostatic attraction governs the chain-length-dependent sorption of PFAS. In column tests with co-contaminated soils, 1.0 wt% 1:10FMBC was estimated to reduce the cumulative release of PFAS and As(V) over 20 years by 75.8-99.4% and 31.8-82.9%, suggesting competitive performance among reported amendments. This work validates that the design of multifunctional biochar is an effective pathway for stabilizing PFAS-As(V) co-contaminated soils, offering a technological option for field-scale remediation.

title: Molecular-Level Decoding of Gallium Geochemical Cycling: From Coal Sequestration to Soil Humic Acid Effects via Fluorescent Carbon Dot Tracking
Multi-scale analysis of the selective depression mechanism of lactobionic acid on albite and its flotation separation from quartz
abstract: In this study, lactobionic acid (C 12 H 22 O 12 , LA) was employed as a depressant to investigate its performance and underlying mechanism in the flotation separation of albite from quartz using the Fe 3 + /sodium oleate (NaOL) system. Flotation tests indicate that under the optimal conditions (pH=5, Fe 3+ /NaOL (1:10, 165 mg/L, and LA=7.5 mg/L), the recovery difference between albite and quartz reaches as high as 76.03 %age points, and a high-quality concentrate with an Al 2 O 3 grade of 10.10% and recovery of 95.57% is obtained from a 1:1 mixed ore. A comprehensive suite of multi-dimensional characterization techniques, including surface wettability, zeta potential, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, was employed to gain in-depth insights into the selective depression mechanism of LA. Mechanistic studies reveal that the polyhydroxyl structure of LA plays a pivotal role in its selectivity: the oxygen atoms of the hydroxyl groups preferentially form stable chemical bonds with the Al 3+ sites on the albite surface via metal complexation, while a portion of the hydroxyl groups concurrently engage in hydrogen bonding with siloxane bonds. This dual interaction, dominated by chemical coordination and supplemented by hydrogen bonding, constructs a hydrophilic barrier on the albite surface, effectively hindering the adsorption of the collector sodium oleate.

title: Site-specific ecological risk assessment of a historically contaminated site: Integrating environmental DNA and species sensitivity distributions for multi-trophic soil communities
Combined salicylic and jasmonic acids enhance cd tolerance and accumulation in Sedum alfredii
abstract: Salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) individually improve Cd responses in the hyperaccumulator Sedum alfredii, but whether their combined application provides additional benefits and how these relate to Cd accumulation remain unclear. We compared SA, JA and their combination in an independent hydroponic experiment integrating physiological, hormonal, transcriptomic, metabolomic, thiol and subcellular Cd analyses. Compared with Cd alone, co-treatment increased fresh biomass by 62.9%, total chlorophyll by 99.3%, net photosynthetic rate by 75.0% and shoot Cd concentration by 80.0%, while reducing malondialdehyde by 27.5%. Among Cd-containing treatments, SA × JA interactions were significant for photosynthetic parameters and selected antioxidant and hormone indicators. Although net photosynthetic rate exceeded that under either hormone alone, its increase was smaller than the sum of the single-hormone increases. Glutathione and phytochelatins increased without a detectable interaction. Co-treatment increased Cd concentrations in cell-wall and soluble fractions, alongside changes in signaling, redox metabolism, lipid-related metabolites and metal transport-related gene expression. At the tested concentrations, combined SA and JA improved growth and photosynthesis despite higher shoot Cd concentration, without uniformly greater-than-additive responses. Increased thiols and Cd recovery in cell-wall and soluble fractions suggest that Cd binding and partitioning may contribute to reduced injury.

title: From PN23 to PN10: Unraveling the operating-condition dependence of particle number emissions from heavy-duty diesel vehicles
abstract: Current particle number (PN) regulations for heavy-duty diesel vehicles (HDDVs) count particles above 23 nm, potentially missing sub-23 nm emissions. Euro VII lowers this boundary to 10 nm, and China VII development considers this transition. One China VI HDDV and three China VII prototypes were tested under start, temperature, and payload conditions. The analysis combined second-by-second high-emission episodes (HEEs), size distributions, and explainable machine learning. At 25 °C, cold-start PN10 emission factors (EFs) were 3.97 × 10 10 -8.79 × 10 11 #/kWh, or 1.15-15.4 times hot-start values. Sub-23 nm particles represented 64%-76% of hot-start PN10 versus 16%-54% under cold starts; the 10-23 nm spectral fraction increased from 26.7% to 50.7%. Low temperature increased the relative sub-23 nm contribution, whereas full payload increased total PN, demonstrating that relative and absolute PN10-23 changes were asynchronous. HEE#3 required a sub-23 nm contribution above 50% and PN10 above the test 75th percentile. It occupied 19.1%-22.5% of cycle duration but contributed 85.9%-89.3% of PN10-23. RF and LightGBM achieved receiver operating characteristic area-under-the-curve values of 0.833-0.924. Fuel rate (FR), engine speed (ES), exhaust temperature (ET), and vehicle speed (VS) were principal predictors. Overall, PN10 provides condition-dependent sub-23 nm information that cannot be derived from PN23 using a fixed conversion factor.

title: Human-relevant hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid exposure drives neuronal senescence via KDM6A-mediated CDC42 K27 demethylation
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA, also known as HFPO-DA) is an emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) alternative increasingly detected in the environment, raising concerns about its potential long-term health effects. Neuronal senescence is a critical hallmark of brain aging and has been implicated in age-related neurodegeneration. However, whether chronic exposure to HFPO-DA promotes neuronal senescence and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrates that HFPO-DA exposure robustly induces neuronal senescence with subtype specificity ( Camk2d⁺ and Sgcz⁺ subpopulations expansion, Dock10⁺ subpopulation depletion), convergently disrupting neuronal homeostasis and accelerating neurodegeneration. KDM6A is identified as a key protein activated by HFPO-DA exposure, whereas Kdm6a deletion ( Kdm6a fl/fl , Emx1-Cre ) significantly alleviates HFPO-DA-induced neuronal senescence. Mechanistically, KDM6A-mediated demethylation of CDC42 constitutes a critical event driving neuronal senescence. Kdm6a deficiency increase CDC42 K27 dimethylation, reduces CDC42 activation, and alleviates neuronal senescence. Taken together, these findings identify KDM6A-mediated CDC42 demethylation as a critical mechanism that drives neuronal senescence in response to environmental stress. Inhibition of KDM6A emerges as a potential strategy to counteract age-related neurodegeneration.

title: Ammonia emissions from range-extended electric vehicles under coupled temperature-HVAC conditions
abstract: Ambient temperature and cabin heating or cooling jointly affect engine operation and ammonia (NH 3 ) emissions from range-extended electric vehicles (EREVs). Two China 6 EREVs were tested in a climatic chamber over an RDE-derived aggressive chassis-dynamometer profile under three coupled temperature-HVAC conditions: 0 °C with heating on, 23 °C with HVAC off, and 40 °C with cooling on. Each condition was repeated three times. Reported trip-level NH 3 emission factors ranged from 15.31 to 17.98 mg/km for SHEV 1 and from 2.65 to 4.69 mg/km for SHEV 2. The coupled conditions affected emission timing and phase distribution more strongly than trip-level factors. Both vehicles had higher urban NH 3 factors at 0 and 40 °C than at 23 °C, coinciding with earlier or prolonged engine operation. Later engine intervention at 23 °C shifted emissions toward rural or motorway operation. SHEV 1 showed large NH 3 peaks during rich motorway operation at 40 °C; SHEV 2 emitted less NH 3 but exhibited isolated pollutant events and high catalyst-temperature signals. These observations support coordinated energy-management and aftertreatment control for the tested vehicles.

title: Influence of material properties and environmental factors on VOC emission characteristics from automotive paint sludge
abstract: Automotive paint sludge is a hazardous waste with significant volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. Effective source control requires understanding how material properties and environmental factors govern key mass-transfer parameters: initial emittable concentration (C m,0 ), diffusion coefficient (D m ), and partition coefficient (K m ). This study couples a finite diffusion model and nonlinear optimization with chamber experiments on oil-based paint sludge to evaluate effects of temperature, humidity, air exchange rate, VOC type, porosity, moisture, and solid matrix. Temperature dominates: increasing temperature raises C m,0 and D m but lowers K m , and correlating K m with temperature yields apparent desorption activation energies (E d ). Although relative humidity induces minor non-monotonic fluctuations via competitive water adsorption and air exchange rate slightly alters surface convection, their standardized sensitivities are two orders of magnitude below temperature's, rendering their net impacts engineering-wise negligible. Low-molecular-weight, nonpolar VOCs have low E d and desorb rapidly, whereas hydrogen bonding hinders polar alcohols. D m increases with porosity via a power law, suggesting compaction for mitigation. Moisture forms water films that reduce C m,0 and D m but increase K m , and inorganic scaffolds exhibit higher adsorption potentials than organic matrices. These findings provide strategies for predicting and mitigating VOC emissions from hazardous wastes.

title: Environmental constraints reveal condition-dependent advantages of a defined benzene-degrading consortium
Pyrite-promoted hydrothermal upcycling of polyvinyl chloride waste: Deep dechlorination, enhanced graphitization, and heterogeneous Fenton catalysis
abstract: Green dechlorination and high-value conversion of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) waste are critical challenges in plastic pollution control and resource recycling. This work presents a pyrite (Py)-enhanced one-step hydrothermal strategy that utilizes the reducing ability and Lewis acidity of Py to synergistically promote deep dechlorination and catalytic carbonization of PVC, thereby preparing an efficient heterogeneous Fenton catalyst. The Py-PVC system achieved a dechlorination efficiency of 99.90% at 240°C for 6 h, 15.72% higher than that of the control system without Py. Fe 2+ donated electrons to facilitate C-Cl bond cleavage, thereby forming the C=C bond; while lattice sulfur contributed to Fe 2+ regeneration. Subsequently, driven by Fe 2+ / 3+ catalysis, the dechlorinated polyene intermediates formed highly graphitized hydrochar. The resulting composite showed excellent heterogeneous Fenton activity, removing 99.2% of bisphenol A within 10 min and facilitating the activation leaching of 84.75% of uranium within 180 min. As an electron shuttle, the graphite-carbon structure not only facilitated the transfer of electrons from Py to recalcitrant organochlorines during the hydrothermal process but also promoted the Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycle during the advanced oxidation process. This work elucidates the synergistic mechanism of Py-assisted PVC hydrothermal dechlorination and catalytic carbonization, offering perspectives on the green upgrading of chlorinated plastics.

title: Hazard evolution in liquid dinitrogen tetroxide-isopropanol cleaning systems: thermal runaway and gas release
abstract: Liquid dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄, NTO) can pose severe hazards when contacting incompatible cleaning agents. A vessel rupture accident involving NTO and an isopropanol-containing cleaning agent was investigated using accident reconstruction, chemical analysis, online Raman monitoring, calorimetry and field validation. Temperature-pressure records supported chemically driven thermal runaway. Blank tests showed vigorous gas evolution but limited heat accumulation during NTO hydrolysis and neutralization. HPLC/HPLC-MS supported acetone formation and tentative assignments to isonitrosoacetone, nitrolic-acid- and isoxazoline-type products. Raman monitoring revealed attenuation of NTO-related bands and transient spectral features tentatively associated with oxime/N-OH and cyano-containing species, while quantum-chemical calculations assessed the proposed nitrile-oxide-mediated pathway. Gas analysis tentatively indicated N₂O and carbon oxides without establishing their formation pathways. DSC revealed exothermic decomposition at approximately 60-90°C under the tested conditions, while ARC demonstrated rapid self-heating and pressure rise. Comparative experiments showed greater runaway severity at lower initial temperatures, consistent with liquid NTO retention and enhanced liquid-liquid contact. Higher temperatures reduced heat accumulation under the tested conditions but promoted volatilization, while toxic-gas release remained a concern. These findings highlight thermal runaway and gas-release hazards, with secondary decomposition of unstable intermediates as a possible contributor, and inform safer residual oxidizer cleaning and off-gas management.

Characterization of physical and chemical properties controlling the transport of 129I and 99Tc in ultra-high-performance grout
abstract: Ultra-high-performance grout (UHPG) was evaluated as an engineered barrier for encapsulating solid waste generated during nuclear waste processing. The objective of this study was to measure geochemical, hydrological, and physical properties related to 129 I and 99 Tc transport through UHPG. 99 Tc and 129 I are key health-risk drivers associated with near-subsurface nuclear disposal facilities. To provide context, a second flowable Baseline grout currently used in nuclear waste disposal facilities was also characterized. Compressive strength and bulk density were appreciably greater in the UHPG (120.5 MPa and 2.2 g/cm 3 , respectively) than the Baseline grout (8.4 MPa and 1.5 g/cm 3 ). UHPG had appreciably lower porosity (0.15 cm 3 /cm 3 ) and hydraulic conductivity ( K = 5.8 ×10 −14 cm/sec) than the Baseline grout (porosity = 0.32 cm 3 /cm 3 ; K = 9.4 ×10 −7 cm/sec). Desorption partitioning experiments indicated that both grouts had similar 129 I partitioning coefficients (C Solid /C Liquid ; K d ), of ∼100 (moles/g)/(moles/mL) and had similar aqueous iodine speciation: I - > > IO 3 - > organo-I. 99 Tc aqueous concentrations appeared to be controlled by solubility (7 ×10 −8 mol/L) in the UHPG, likely because slag in the UHPG formulation produced a reducing environment that converted the highly mobile aqueous TcO 4 - to a much less mobile Tc(IV) solid species, TcO 4 · n H 2 O. 129 I and 99 Tc observed diffusivity ( D obs ) were 6 and 7 orders of magnitude less, respectively, in the UHPG than in the Baseline grout. These tests provide multiple lines of evidence indicating that UHPG possesses excellent characteristics for encapsulating 99 Tc and 129 I waste.

Microplastics in a large Brazilian bay: Multispecies bivalve approach reveals an association with population density
abstract: Microplastic contamination is pervasive across aquatic ecosystems, including protected coastal environments. Todos os Santos Bay, the second-largest bay in Brazil, encompasses 1385 km² within a multiple-use marine protected area and supports over three million inhabitants, major port activities, petrochemical industries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs. Here, we assessed microplastic contamination using three filter-feeding bivalve species as sentinels, and evaluated its associations with population density, human modification, socioeconomic deprivation, and distance to river discharges using Crassostrea sp., the only species sampled at all 16 sites. A total of 834 microplastics were detected, with average concentrations of 3.21, 2.88, and 2.36 particles g-1 in clams, oysters, and mussels, respectively. These concentrations exceeded the literature-based Brazilian average for bivalves (2.06 particles g-1), indicating comparatively elevated contamination levels in Todos os Santos Bay. Microplastic contamination was widespread across Todos os Santos Bay despite all sampling sites being located within a multiple-use protected area. No consistent overall differences in microplastic concentrations were detected among species; however, a significant Species × Site interaction indicated that interspecific differences varied across sampling sites. Fibers, small and transparent particles predominated, whereas anthropogenic cellulose accounted for 56.8% of the spectroscopically characterized subset. Population density received the strongest statistical support among the evaluated socio-environmental predictors and was positively associated with microplastic concentrations in oysters. This spatial association highlights the importance of reducing land-based microplastic inputs in densely populated coastal areas through improved wastewater treatment, urban drainage, and solid waste management.

Seasonal variation in the spatial distribution, community assembly, and associated factors of antibiotic resistance genes in tropical drinking water reservoirs of Hainan, China
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have been widely investigated in temperate and subtropical reservoirs but remain poorly understood in tropical drinking-water reservoirs. We sampled four drinking-water reservoirs in Hainan during both winter and summer, integrating physicochemical, heavy-metal, and metagenomic data to investigate the diversity, spatiotemporal patterns, and assembly of ARGs, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and microbial communities. ARG composition and community structure differed significantly by season and reservoir. Contig-based analysis identified ARG–MGE arrangements in diverse putative hosts; sul1 and qacEdelta1 co-occurred with integrases and transposases, demonstrating MGE co-localization. Null-model analysis indicated reservoir-specific ARG assembly in winter but predominantly stochastic assembly in summer, whereas microbial community assembly was deterministic in both seasons. Mantel and Spearman analyses showed seasonal variation in ARG relationships: stronger correlations with environmental factors in winter and more positive correlations with MGEs in summer. Summer co-occurrence networks were larger and more connected, with more positive ARG–MGE–microbial genus associations. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) showed positive MGE–ARG associations in both seasons, whereas microbial community composition was negatively associated with ARGs only in winter. These results characterize seasonal ARG variation and its associations with microbial communities and MGEs in tropical reservoirs, providing a baseline for monitoring regional drinking-water sources.

Corrigendum to “Fermi-level pinning and internal electric field engineering in S-scheme titanium dioxide/bismuth molybdate for fast mineralization of gaseous formaldehyde” [J Hazard Mater 514 (2026) 142655]
Simultaneous cesium desorption and surfactant degradation from montmorillonite by coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation
abstract: Remediation of cesium-contaminated clay minerals is difficult because Cs + is strongly retained within collapsed interlayer spaces. Cationic surfactants can promote Cs + release, but residual surfactant creates a secondary pollution risk requiring post-treatment. Here, a coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation (CDI-EO) system using a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode and activated carbon cathode was developed for one-step Cs + desorption and in situ surfactant degradation from Cs-saturated montmorillonite (0.95 mmol g -1 , 85% of cation exchange capacity, CEC). Electrochemical degradation of dodecyltrimethylammonium bromide (DTAB) was first optimised in a static electrolytic cell, reaching ~96% degradation at 150 mA cm -2 after 12 h for a DTAB loading of 0.5 × CEC. These conditions (150 mA cm -2 , 0.4 M Na 2 SO 4 , pH 7) were then applied in a recirculating flow-by CDI cell at 20 mL min -1 . Within 6 h, DTAB degradation reached 84–89% and Cs + desorption up to ~89%, with maximum Cs + release within 1 h due to surfactant-induced interlayer expansion and electric-field-driven ion extraction. XRD showed interlayer contraction to 1.22–1.25 nm after treatment, confirming effective surfactant removal from the clay structure. Over five consecutive cycles, Cs + desorption remained ~70% and surfactant degradation exceeded 80%, demonstrating sustained treatment performance. Electrical energy consumption was 129–140 kWh kg -1 clay for the dilute laboratory batches studied, and the electrosorption capacity of the unmodified AC cathode is identified as the bottleneck for net Cs⁺ capture. The integrated CDI-EO process therefore provides a simplified single-step route for radionuclide-contaminated clay remediation, simultaneously combining decontamination and surfactant removal while avoiding a separate post-treatment stage for disposal.

title: Mechanisms of organic pollutant removal and residual carbon evolution from pharmaceutical waste salts via molten bubble-enhanced oxidation
Pangolin scales as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for environmental and rescue-associated chemical exposures in endangered wildlife
abstract: ABSTRACT Pangolins are among the world's most trafficked and endangered mammals, yet their exposure to emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) remains largely uncharacterized. Their keratinous scales represent an untapped matrix for potentially non-invasive biomonitoring. This study developed and validated a modified QuEChERS-based extraction coupled with liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-QTOF/MS) for suspect screening and targeted quantification of EOCs in pangolin scales. The workflow was applied to scales collected from 18 deceased wild Formosan pangolins ( Manis pentadactyla pentadactyla ) with and without documented rescue histories. A total of 57 EOCs spanning six chemical classes were tentatively identified, reflecting environmental contamination and rescue-associated pharmaceutical exposure. Eight EOCs were further selected and confirmed as targets. The method achieved recoveries of 70–120%, relative standard deviations ≤20%, and method detection limits ranging from 0.1 to 2.0 µg kg −1 . Target EOC concentrations spanned nearly four orders of magnitude, from 0.84 µg kg −1 (isoxaflutole) to 15,400 µg kg −1 (enrofloxacin). Compositional and quantitative EOC patterns showed substantial inter-individual variation and rescue-associated pharmaceutical signatures. This study provides the first report of multiple EOC residues in pangolin scales, supporting their further evaluation as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for wildlife conservation across the family Manidae .
